The record’s summary, whole

The 4.0.0 release plan addresses issues filed by this repository and by adopters. The original 2026-10-12 scope covered 26 issues against CodeFlow 3.0.0 and 3.1.0. The combined scope covers codeflow ci verdicts that depend on how a range is spelled, planning and exemption pull requests that cannot be classified, guards that miss commands, writers and history reads that can be redirected in a local clone, CodeFlow's own pushes using a personal credential, managed CI steps an adopter must edit by hand, a landing mode, tests that touch an enclosing repository, and one post-release evaluation. This epic fixes or settles each of them for the 4.0.0 release, which the operator renumbered from 3.2.0 on 2026-10-28 (Version relabel amendment below).

Done means

each task below has landed on integration/EPC-022-the-3-2-0-milestone-fixes with its cross-lineage review, the integrated body passes the full gate and the journey below on the installed candidate, and its pull request to main is ready for a human merge.

The record’s summary, whole

Five feature requests from adopters in October 2026 ask CodeFlow to change its defaults rather than fix a defect: a define-once gate with a tracked exemption register (issue 274), strict typing and linting by default with an explicit opt-out (275), a repository that holds only what it needs long term (279), a local run of the managed secret scan and dependency audit (252), per-project account profiles with limit-aware seat routing (234), and the supervisor and separate-account layers of lane isolation (286, items 2 and 3; item 1 is TSK-437 in 4.0.0). The operator placed them on 2026-10-22 in one separate epic, smaller than EPC-022, sized by issue 280's guidance; this epic is that placement.

Done means

each task has landed on this epic's line with its cross-lineage review, the integrated body passes the full gate and the journeys below on the installed candidate, and its pull request to main is ready for a human merge.

The record’s summary, whole

Issue 272 asked for an orchestrator follow-up ledger: every handed-over item logged, checked and closed on proof. The operator shaped it on 2026-10-22 into project-level working state that CodeFlow owns for any orchestrating model, and an independent Codex review of the design (sound with changes, 22 findings, 14 high) settled its contracts: the coordination ledger, a clone-local single event log with follow-ups (FU-NNN, codeflow follow) and lanes (LN-NNN, codeflow lane), the coordinator as lead role, hooks on every harness, and the rules and skills that adopt them (ADR-0086). It is its own small epic, sized by issue 280's guidance, and it targets 3.2.0 as the operator placed issue 272 there. It lands on its own integration line, integration/EPC-025-the-coordination-ledger-follow-ups-and-lanes, cut from the EPC-022 line, because the epic-line binding (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:880-917) requires a task's epic to equal the line's epic, so an EPC-025 task cannot bind to the EPC-022 line (found at the first EPC-025 push on 2026-10-23; amended the same day, a reversible primary decision). The closing step: once its four tasks have landed and the epic's criteria are proven on its own installed candidate, the EPC-025 line merges into the EPC-022 line through one reviewed pull request, gated once as a candidate there, before the 3.2.0 pull request to main; that pull request describes both epics' outcomes, and the operator merges it. Amended 2026-10-24: codeflow ci lands an integration/ head only on the default branch, so each merge of this line into the EPC-022 line is carried by an EPC-022 task branch that merges it (the first is TSK-1000), and the operator chose that day to merge the line once now, with TSK-422 landed, so the 3.2.0 pull request can open.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Original plan (Planning notes)/An update is previewed read-only before anything is written

An update is previewed read-only before anything is written

TSK-247todo

After this merges, an agent in an adopting project can run `codeflow update --plan` against the live repository.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an agent in an adopting project can run `codeflow update --plan` against the live repository, see every file's predicted action, the citations and overrides the update makes stale and the paths only a person can write, with nothing on disk changed.

Context

Fixes the preview portion of #74. An adopter who has tailored CodeFlow needs the whole update in view before it lands: which files change and how, which project rules and docs cite managed lines that move, which new defaults the project overrides, which skill mirrors have drifted apart, and which paths the agent's session cannot write so a person must. Today the only preview is one file's decide (crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/update.rs:141), --diff writes its report after applying, and a sandboxed run that cannot write .claude/ stops part way with the manifest unwritten. An adopter on 3.1.1 reported on 2026-10-13 that an agent now has no preview route at all: exporting the tree to a scratch copy is refused by the guard, so the preview has to run against the live repository without writing.

This task adds a read-only codeflow update --plan [FILE] produced by the same steps as the apply (one write sink, so the plan cannot drift from the apply), a cross-reference scan of project-owned text for citations of managed lines that move, a write preflight shared by plan and apply, the policy report for every changed default the project overrides, and a mirror-pair comparison. The plan separates the files an agent may resolve from the files only a person may change, so the agent prepares the first set and hands the person a short list for the second. It reads bases as SPC-015 defines them (TSK-1087).

History: allocated as a standalone task on 2026-10-06 (its branch task/TSK-247-update-plan never landed); joined this epic on 2026-10-30 when the operator's version decision brought the read-only update plan into 4.0.0. Two criteria moved out on 2026-10-30 and their ids are retired, never reused: AC-5 (whole-file drift in doctor, which read the recorded shipped hash that the baseline replacement removes) is TSK-1087 AC-7, and AC-7 (the procedure file, [scaffold] ignore in the adoption guide and the skew warning naming the procedure) is TSK-1088 AC-1, AC-3 and AC-5; this task's skew warning names --plan only, under AC-9. Non-goals: generating one skill tree from the other (an ADR-sized change, a recorded follow-up in the epic), embedding changelog entries or ADRs (the plan links each release), and a doctor cross-reference check.

Outcome
The 4.0.0 milestone fixes EPC-022

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Original plan (Planning notes)/codeflow ci gives one verdict for a range however it is spelled

codeflow ci gives one verdict for a range however it is spelled

TSK-275complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

codeflow ci gives different work.acceptance_binding verdicts for one range when --base is a ref name or the commit id that ref points at (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/141), and an explicit --head takes its branch context from the checkout without saying so (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/130). After a sync merge of main into an integration line, both lead the tool to recommend reopening tasks already reviewed on main. At v3.1.0, crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:471-477 takes the acceptance target only from a named base, and crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/acceptance.rs:276-281 picks the frozen or amendable mode from it. This task resolves base, head and branch context once, before any rule runs, and makes the output say where each came from. The two issues share one cause and one code path, so they are one task. Non-goal: attribution of commits that follow a merge (issue 69).

Amended 2026-10-13 for https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/165: run locally without --base, the range base falls back to the policy's protected branches (origin/main) even when --branch names a branch that targets an integration line, so the range covers the whole line's divergence from main and reports criteria changes the line received as the branch's own (detect_range in crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs, the terminal fallback). The branch's declared target is already readable: a task branch's integration_target (declared_work_target), a planning branch that names its epic, and an integration/* line, whose target is the default branch. Same resolution step, so the same task: the base is chosen from the declared target before the protected fallback, and the output says which rule chose it.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Test integrity amendment (2026-10-17)/A planning amendment can update the project's document index

A planning amendment can update the project's document index

TSK-276complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

An epic amendment that adds a planning home cannot also add that home's row to the project's documentation map. classify::amendment_path (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/classify.rs:257-281 at v3.1.0) admits records, plans and non-product files under docs/, but not a root index such as DOC-INDEX.md, so the range loses the planning class and fails work.criteria_frozen (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/136). The docs/research/ half of https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/83 was fixed by PR 61 (TSK-229, ADR-0078); its index half and its request that the refusal name the admitted path set remain. The two issues are the same gap, so they are one task. This task lets a project declare its document index files in policy, admits them into a planning amendment, and makes the refusal name the path and the admitted set. Product globs keep precedence, so docs/portal/ stays out by design. Non-goal: a general configurable planning-path list (issue 83 option 1); one declared index is the narrower change and covers both reports.

Outcome

Context

Since PR 26 the secret scan reads exemptions from the trusted base commit, so an integration line that carries a reviewed false positive needs a small exemption pull request into main first. That pull request has no class codeflow ci accepts (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/139): with Task: TSK-NNN it fails work.stable_planning_anchor on a dependency that is complete only on the line, and with Task: EPC-NNN amendment_path (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/classify.rs:257 at v3.1.0) refuses the hidden .gitleaksignore. The operator then merges over a red required check. This task adds one narrow class for a range whose only changed path is the secret-scan ignore file the managed CI reads (.gitleaksignore). Non-goal: admitting the ignore file into the planning class, which would let any planning PR carry an exemption.

Context

A project that must remove personal or customer names from a completed record has no sanctioned route when a non-planning commit followed the record's landing on its line (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/134). PR 111 (TSK-253, ADR-0080) lets a completed standalone task's criteria text be corrected, but the acceptance block and an acceptance_superseded block cannot be redacted, and the waiver that the work.acceptance_binding message names has no documented field or format (a grep of docs/ and cf-method finds none). This task adds a record-only redaction route that keeps every result, the reviewed commit and the review provenance and records a digest of the replaced text, and documents the waiver. Non-goal: changing a criterion's meaning or result, which stays a reopen.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Original plan (Planning notes)/Policy keys have one placement rule and a check

Policy keys have one placement rule and a check

TSK-280complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

No written rule or check says where a new policy key goes, so agents ship keys in the policy template, where an adopter's older pinned binary can meet them and fail closed (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/118). Since 3.0.0, git.pr_summary lives only in the schema and the code default, with a per-key note (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/policy_schema.rs:392-393); git.claim_remotes was first added to the template and then removed; two replays on 2026-10-08 put a key in the template again. This task writes one rule where a contributor adding a key reads, ties it to the two-step upgrade in docs/adoption.md, and adds a check that holds it. TSK-276 adds a key and follows this rule, so it lands after this task.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Original plan (Planning notes)/CodeFlow's own pushes use a configured non-personal credential

CodeFlow's own pushes use a configured non-personal credential

TSK-291todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

CodeFlow's own pushes (the registry reservation from task new, epic new and adr new, work claim, epic new --integration, ids sync) use whatever git credential is ambient (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/151). A project that requires agent pushes to come from a bot or GitHub App identity had to inject a credential helper per command through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT and its keys. Since 3.1.0 git-guard refuses that route under git.hook_integrity (the issue comment), and repository or worktree writes of credential.*.helper are refused too, so an agent's reservation goes out under the operator's personal credential; the adopter has stopped agent CodeFlow pushes. This task gives a first-class setting that CodeFlow applies to its own pushes only, reports it in doctor, and can refuse an agent push when no non-personal credential is configured. A credential helper runs a program (credential.helper=!cmd), so where the setting is read from and who may change it is a security boundary; the design settles it first. It is first in the 4.0.0 build order because an adopter is blocked on it.

Amended 2026-10-13 for the adopter's comment of that day on issue 151: on 3.1.1 the per-command route is still refused, and the 3.1.1 notes' upgrade step (a repository-scope helper set after an empty value) omits credential.useHttpPath. A helper that answers for one repository only never sees the path unless credential.useHttpPath=true is also set, so git gets no credential and, with the empty reset, has no fallback. When CodeFlow applies the helper per call, it passes useHttpPath with it, or the design note says why that is not needed.

With git.test_gate_on_push at block, a commit that fails the push set can still be pushed: edit a tracked file without committing and push again, and the pre-push hook skips the tree checks with a note (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/156, reproduced 2026-10-12). crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs runs validate --docs and the quick targets only when the checkout is clean, complete and at the pushed commit (push_set.rs:184, tracked_tree_clean at :1725); every other ref gets the PUSH_TREE_UNCHECKED note, never a violation, whatever the level. The existing CLI tests in crates/codeflow-cli/tests/hooks_cli.rs expect success on the unchecked dirty-tree and other-ref paths.

This task makes the gate fail closed for the whole class, not only the dirty-file spelling: at block, a pushed ref whose tree the hook cannot check (dirty tracked files, a ref other than HEAD, several refs in one push, a sparse or incomplete checkout, a submodule whose checkout differs from the pushed gitlink) is either checked on the pushed commit in a temporary checkout or refused with the clean-checkout remedy. The builder chooses between the two and records the choice and its cost in the PR; the Codex triage of 2026-10-13 (triage-codex-02.md, "Patch contents and release order") names both. Lower levels keep the note, honestly worded. The documented caveat that untracked files can influence a working-tree test (push_set.rs:11) stays and is tested.

The destination-held exception is limited to advertised branch history: tag pushes run no push set and cannot establish this exemption. A clean, complete checkout at the pushed commit still runs the tree checks first (AC-4).

Operator record: kept first in 3.2.0 rather than in a 3.1.2 patch (SETTLED_DISSENT of 2026-10-13 in the workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md), because hosted CI reruns the same checks on every pull request and they are required on protected branches. Non-goal: changing which checks the push set holds.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Gate efficiency amendment (2026-10-17)/An unanswered default-branch lookup is reported as a network failure

An unanswered default-branch lookup is reported as a network failure

TSK-305complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

codeflow ci and the pre-push hook ask the destination for its default branch with one git ls-remote --symref call and a fixed 10-second deadline (crates/codeflow-core/src/git/remote_query.rs:15, ls_remote at :28, no retry). When the destination answers slowly, the push is refused (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/161). The failure is wrapped at crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/release_line.rs:182-187 and reported by scope_refusal in crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/acceptance.rs:223 and by the record check in crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/work_records.rs:142.

Two parts of the report differ in age. The message the issue quotes, with a sanctioned line that points at a planning PR, is the older text: at main 4226a9408, scope_refusal already says "repair the destination or policy named above, then rerun codeflow ci" (acceptance.rs:227). The defect that remains in the current source is the classification: a destination failure is still reported under a lifecycle rule (work.criteria_frozen through FROZEN_RULE, and work.records) rather than under a rule of its own, and its remedy does not name the network.

Failing closed is right and stays: an unanswered destination never lets a range through unjudged, and a stale local default is never trusted. This task distinguishes the causes (a timeout, an authentication failure, a malformed advertisement, and a destination with no usable default branch) and reports each once under its own rule with a remedy that names the network or the remote. One shared lookup owns the query and its bounded retry sequence: a first-attempt success makes one network attempt; a timeout gets a bounded number of extra attempts with a short backoff, whether they end in success or exhaustion; the other causes are not retried. The lookup's final answer, or its final error, is cached and shared: pre-push passes it to its child checks (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs:354-360, --advertisement-stdin), and no child check or additional pushed ref queries the destination again. Scope per the Codex triage of 2026-10-13 (triage-codex-01.md, the paragraph on issue 161). Non-goal: a configurable deadline.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Original plan (Planning notes)/A line's newer task version wins over a copy main inherited

A line's newer task version wins over a copy main inherited

TSK-306complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Pre-push refuses a task branch on an integration line when main holds an older version of the task record that the line itself held and later amended (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/176). With main and the line diverged, judge in crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/landing.rs (from :442) finds no judged point that is newer than every other (:458-475), falls to agreed (:523-559), and refuses whenever the held criteria signatures differ. It never asks whether one point's version was inherited and then replaced on the other point's line. The issue states the search backwards: judge looks for a point that descends from every other point, not for their common ancestor. The current refusal is intended: held_versions_that_differ_still_give_no_answer (landing.rs:1354) builds this shape and expects unknown authority, so this task changes that test and settles the inheritance rule. 3.1.1's issue 153 fix (TSK-295) left this case unresolved; it did not cause it.

The fix adapts the inherited-supersession reasoning the recovered-record path already has (recovered from :562, inherited at :633, and its merge-resolution handling near :668, which tells choosing an old version apart from inheriting it unchanged) to held records, and keeps refusing competing introductions, ambiguous identities, unreadable history and overlays. Copying the helper alone does not supply every safeguard of its current caller. The issue's suggested rule, dropping a version whose bytes appear somewhere in the other point's history, is not used: main may revert to v1, reintroduce v1 independently or resolve a merge to v1 after the line chose v2, and equal bytes do not make those decisions stale (triage-codex-02.md, "The stale-record refusal"). This is a core acceptance rule, never a project setting.

Recovery first. Merging current main into the line makes main an ancestor of the line tip, so a task range based on the new tip has a newest judged point (landing.rs:458-475) and takes the line's criteria without agreed. That recovery is proved through the installed hooks before any code, and the result is written in this record. If it fails through the installed gates and no other sanctioned recovery exists, the operator decides whether this fix moves to 3.1.2 (workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md, triage of 2026-10-13). Merging main into the task branch alone, while the judged line base stays old, is not the same recovery, and dropping --policy-from or --commits-from is not a workaround.

Design note, 2026-10-14

Written before any code, at the EPC-022 line tip 1e6e29e93 (landing.rs line numbers below are at that revision). It settles the held-version inheritance rule, the cases, the AC-1 recovery procedure and the change to the existing test. The AC-1 result is appended to this record as a dated "Recovery proof" note when the procedure is run, before the first code commit; nothing below reports a run. Revised the same day after the Codex design review (target/review-design-TSK-306-codex-01.md): the recovery procedure's judged points and its setup route are corrected (F1, F2), and the three fix-now clarifications are taken (fixture interleaving, the stricter recovered path, the AC-5 and AC-6 output). Revised again after the build found F4 (target/review-design-TSK-306-codex-03.md, target/build-TSK-306.md): the rule now compares introductions with introductions, never with a tip, so a version one point restored after seeing the other's stays a competing decision; the rule paragraph, the walk-through table and the recovered consequence below are the revised text. Revised a third time on 2026-10-15 after the security review's SEC-306-01 (target/security-review-TSK-306-01.md): introductions are traced by criteria signature, not by blob; the definitions, the introduction paragraph, the blob-or-signature decision and the non-criteria row of the walk-through table are the revised text.

The shape. main planned T at v1; the line forked from that commit and amended T to v2; main moved on without touching T. The pre-push judges the task branch at two points: the line tip (the range base) and the main tip (--policy-from).

Neither point descends from the other, so judge finds no newest point (landing.rs:458-475) and asks agreed (:523-559), which compares only the criteria signatures the points hold now and refuses at :550. held_versions_that_differ_still_give_no_answer (:1354) builds this exact shape and expects the refusal.

The inheritance rule for held records (decision, revised for F4). Definitions first. For a held judged point P, s(P) is the criteria signature of the record P holds for T (CriteriaList::signature, the one the criteria freeze compares), and I(P) is the set of commits in P's history that introduce s(P): a commit holds a record with s(P) while some parent holds no record of T or one with another signature, or it has no parent. A merge that resolves a conflict between two signatures therefore introduces the one it keeps, whatever its bytes, and a merge whose parents all hold s(P) introduces nothing. I(P) is read by the shared walk over P's whole history and is unreadable, which refuses, on an overlay, a shallow cut, a held doubt, a second uid, or when it comes back empty. The refusal messages still name each point's blob, which identifies the record it holds.

The predicate, for two held points P and Q whose criteria signatures differ:

> P yields to Q if and only if every commit in I(P) is a proper > ancestor of every commit in I(Q).

Read: Q's version was decided, every time it was decided, after every decision for P's version, so P's version is the older on every line that holds either, and P's tip holds it unchanged since. The relation is asymmetric (mutual yielding would need c before d and d before c) and needs no point order. Among the held points, every point that yields to some other held point with a different signature is dropped; the points left must share one criteria signature, and the record of the point left (the newest of them when more than one agree) is the authority; otherwise no answer, naming each point and its blob (AC-5). The same predicate replaces inherited on the recovered path (:590-608, :633-704), so the spec states one rule.

What this tells apart, and why the first rule could not: the first rule compared I(P) with the other point's tip ("every introduction of P's version is an ancestor of Q"). A tip is reached by everything the point merged, so when main merged the commit B that introduced the line's v2 and then restored v1, every introduction of v2 was an ancestor of main's tip and the rule dropped the line's own decision as if it were an inherited copy, leaving main's restoration as the authority, which AC-3 forbids (F4, the two failing tests). Introductions are decisions and tips are not. Comparing with I(Q) instead, the restoration fails on both sides: main's v1 has an introduction (the restoring commit R) that precedes no introduction of v2, so main does not yield; and v1's first introduction A precedes B, so the line's v2 does not yield either, because v1 was not decided wholly after v2. Both decisions stay, and the answer is unknown. In the positive case main's v1 has the one introduction A, which precedes B, and v2's introduction B precedes nothing of v1, so only main yields. The two conditions AC-2 names are this predicate read from each side: every introduction of v1 precedes the line's v2 (main yields), and the line replaced v1 with v2 after holding it (v2's introductions descend from v1's, which is the same ancestry read the other way). A version a point introduced after it saw the other's is a competing decision, never a stale copy, whatever its bytes.

An introduction is a decision for a signature: a commit introduces it when it holds it and at least one parent holds no record of T or another signature. A merge whose sides held different signatures introduces the one it keeps, as a merge naming the record's path against the automatic remerge did under the blob reading; a merge whose sides held the same signature, with any text, introduces nothing.

On the recovered path (revised 2026-10-15 for SEC-306-04 and the Codex review's F2, target/security-review-TSK-306-02.md, target/review-TSK-306-codex-05.md): when two holders hold different criteria, one supersedes the other only by criteria-signature introductions, exactly as on the held path. Status and epic never erase an earlier introduction of a competing signature: tracing the tuple of criteria, status and epic let a restore of S that also changed the epic or status drop S's first introduction A, so the line's V yielded where AC-3 requires no answer. Status and epic only order holders whose criteria agree (same_version), where the walk traces the tuple, so a line's completed version still supersedes a stale line's planned one with the same criteria (the control at landing.rs near :1426 and TSK-295's expectations).

The introductions of a version are a property of one task's history, so the run's cache of them is keyed by the task's full identity (id, uid and own file) as well as the holder and the version, and a cached refusal is kept per task too (SEC-306-03, Codex F1): one task's proof never answers for another task with the same criteria.

What identifies a version in the walk: blob or signature (decision, revised for SEC-306-01). Two options were open.

OptionIntroduction of a versionEffect on main's copy after the fork
A, by blobA commit holds the record's blob while no parent does; inherited as writtenAny edit to T on main, criteria or not, is a new introduction, so main's copy competes and the push is refused
B, by criteria signatureA commit holds a record with the signature while some parent holds none or another signatureA non-criteria edit on main (description, status) is no introduction; a revert or reintroduction of v1's criteria still is

Chosen: B. The first revision chose A as the conservative side, and the security review showed it is not (SEC-306-01, medium, confirmed). The competition is between criteria signatures, but A traced the exact blob a point holds. When the line merged main and resolved T's conflict to its own criteria with one changed description byte, that merge became the only commit holding the line's blob, so I(line) was {M'} instead of {B, M'}. main's concurrent amendment A' precedes M', so main yielded and the line's criteria won, which AC-3 forbids ("resolution on the line" row). A revert on main to v1's criteria with fresh bytes defeated the "revert" row the same way: I(main) lost the base commit A. Traced by signature, the line's earlier decision B stays in I(line) and A stays in I(main), so both rows refuse whatever the resolution's text. The signature is the existing CriteriaList::signature, the one the freeze compares, so what competes and what is traced are the same thing. A resolution that changes the record's text but not its criteria is no new decision about its criteria, and a merge between different signatures introduces the one it keeps without reading the remerge. Renames are not an issue: the walk reads T by identity at each commit, whatever its path.

Effect on a non-criteria edit: an edit on main that keeps v1's criteria (a description or status change) is no introduction of v1, so main still holds the criteria the line replaced and yields; the line's v2 is the authority. Under A it refused; the test a_noncriteria_record_edit_on_main_does_not_compete now asserts the new answer in both point orders. Held points with equal criteria and other status or epic already agreed before this task, so status and epic still decide nothing between held points. AC-4 still holds: an independent reintroduction of v1's criteria, with any bytes, is a new introduction of that signature.

The pre-filter stays as it is: the inheritance test runs only when the held signatures differ, the condition that refuses today. Held versions with equal criteria and other status or epic still agree, as agreed returns today.

Why the issue's byte-match rule is rejected. The issue proposes dropping a point's version when an equal version (same blob, or the same signature) appears in the other point's history at an ancestor of that point. In the issue's shape that gives the right answer, and it gives the wrong one in three others, each of which the introduction rule refuses:

main after the forkByte ruleIntroduction rule
merges the line (takes v2 clean), then reverts T to v1v1's bytes are at A, an ancestor of the line tip: v1 dropped, v2 winsthe revert introduces v1 at a commit the line tip does not descend from: no answer
deletes T, then adds v1's bytes againsame: v1 droppedthe re-add is an introduction outside the line's history: no answer
merges the line and resolves T to v1 against the remergesame: v1 droppedthe resolution introduces v1 at the merge (the line's parent holds v2): no answer

In each, main made a newer decision for v1 after the line chose v2, and equal bytes do not make that decision stale. Dropping it would let the line's criteria win over a reviewed decision on main, which is the "unreviewed criteria win" risk the triage named (triage-codex-02, "The stale-record refusal"). The introduction rule asks where a version was decided, never only whether its bytes occur.

Safeguards inherited does not carry on its own. In recovered, the walk that finds each line's holder (first_holder, :710-748) has already refused a shallow boundary (:730), a held doubt (:736) and a second uid (:740) before inherited reads the same history, and recovered refuses an overlay first (:579). inherited itself reads held_at(...).records and ignores doubt, never checks self.boundary, and does not collect uids (:642-648). Called from agreed without those, it would trust an overlaid, cut or ambiguous history. The design therefore moves the introduction walk into one helper, introductions, that both callers use and that refuses on all four: overlay before any read, the shallow boundary and a held doubt at each commit, and a second uid across the walk (two_uids). inherited is replaced by the yields predicate above for both callers: recovered compares each holder's introductions with the other holder's introductions, no longer with the other holder's commit (:699, graph_descendant_of(newer, commit)), which differs only where a line restored a version after another line's decision, the F4 shape in a deleted-record history, and there it now refuses. recovered keeps its other answers wherever its own guards already fired (the next paragraph names where it does not); its tests (:1202, :1375, TSK-295's) stay and must stay green, and a recovered test the predicate breaks is a record and code conflict to bring back here, never to patch around. Coordination with TSK-287: the ancestry and parent reads in this walk and in judge (:462, which reads ancestry without an overlay check today) go through the guarded reader when TSK-287 lands first; when this task lands first, the new helper is one site in TSK-287's sweep, with its overlay and boundary checks already in place.

One consequence is stated rather than assumed away: recovered does not keep exactly today's behaviour. first_holder returns at the first holder it meets (:743) and the next walk hides that holder's ancestry (:582-588), so the commits below a holder were never validated before inherited read them; with the shared walk, a doubt, a shallow cut or a second uid below a holder refuses recovered where it answered before. That is stricter in the direction the module's proof-of-absence rule already takes (a Planned answer needs a complete, readable history), and it is covered: the recovered-path tests (:1202, :1375) stay, and one new test plants a doubt below the first holder on a line and asserts the refusal.

Controls that do not change: points ordered by ancestry keep the newest point's version (:476); held versions with one signature and other status or epic still agree; a point that no longer holds T is still judged by recovered against the held signature, so a deletion on main after the fork still refuses (a deletion is a decision; the absent case keeps its test at :1375); the issue 153 case (:1327) is unchanged; and the recovered-path control :1202 walks the same way (the stale line's planned version, introduced at the plan commit, precedes the completed version's introduction on main, so the stale line yields and the completed version stays the authority).

The refusal message (AC-5) and the authority output (AC-6). The competing-version message keeps its first clause, which three tests assert on ("different versions"), and names each held point with its version: "the judged points hold different versions of this task, and none of them is newer than the others: <point> holds <blob>, <point> holds <blob>", with ids shortened to nine characters as the module's other messages do. judge sees only ids; the codeflow ci range line already says which id is the base and which --policy-from names, so the adopter can tell which point is main's. The uncertainty refusals keep context too: their reasons already name the commit or path (shallow cut :410-412, unreadable file :262-264, second uid at a point :286-289, unparsed file :297-299, two uids in a walk :938-943), and the shared walk prefixes them with the judged point and blob whose history it was reading ("reading the history of <point> (<blob>): <reason>") when it has them, and names the unreadability plainly when it has none.

AC-6 needs output the code does not print today: frozen_criteria passes equal criteria silently (acceptance.rs:2261), so the range line and the --policy-from line (ci.rs:1570) alone would not show which version was selected. The build adds one codeflow ci note line per task record the range changes, on pass and on refusal, naming the selected held version by judged point and blob and, when the inheritance rule dropped a point, that point as holding an older version. It prints through the existing note channel (ci/acceptance.rs:86), separately from the policy-authority line, so the journey output names the line's version as the authority and --policy-from as the candidate, as AC-6 asks.

The recovery procedure (AC-1), through the installed hooks. Two phases: fixture preparation, which advances the protected main only by its sanctioned route, and the actions under test, which run through the installed pre-merge-commit and pre-push hooks with no override, hook edit or policy change. A failure in the preparation is a setup failure, reported as such and never as the recovery's; a failure under test is the recovery's. The binary is the line tip's build (cargo build -p codeflow-cli in this worktree, then CODEFLOW_HOOK_BINARY at its target/debug/codeflow), because it carries the 3.1.1 fix the issue was reported against and the hook report prints its revision; the host's installed binary is 3.1.0 (codeflow 3.1.0 source=698cc878), which predates issue 153's fix and would be the wrong witness. The note records codeflow --version in full.

Preparation, not under test:

  1. git init -b main the preparation repository P (with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null); codeflow init --full --yes there makes the scaffold commit, the one sanctioned commit before the gates arm, and wires the hooks. From here on main in P takes commits only through codeflow integrate <branch> --into main, the documented landing route with no remote (docs/adoption.md, "With no remote, codeflow integrate replaces the pull request"); a direct commit or push on main is blocked by the installed policy (git_hook.rs:121, :1013; bootstrap grace ends with the first commit, policy.rs:835-866) and is not attempted. Call the scaffold commit S and create the line there at once: git branch integration/EPC-001-line main. The allocator refuses a task whose integration target does not resolve to a local or remote-tracking branch (allocate.rs:368), so the line ref must exist before T is allocated; Codex's live run of the earlier ordering stopped at exactly that refusal (target/recovery-TSK-306.log, exit 1). codeflow epic new --integration would cut the same ref under the epic's own slug; the explicit branch keeps the name this note uses.
  2. In a worktree on plan/t-v1 from main: codeflow epic new "Recovery outcome", then codeflow task new --epic EPC-001 --into integration/EPC-001-line "Recovery task" (T, at project-management/tasks/TSK-001.md); give the epic and T one criterion each, T's being v1; commit; codeflow integrate plan/t-v1 --into main; call the result A1. Then move the line forward to A1 with a normal fast-forward merge from a linked worktree on the line: git merge --ff-only main. No merge commit is made and the line is not protected, so no hook is asked to allow anything. The line's history is now S, A1, and the divergence still forks at A1.
  3. An unrelated file on feat/unrelated; codeflow integrate feat/unrelated --into main; call the result N. main holds v1 at N.
  4. In a linked worktree on the line, amend T to v2 on plan/t-v2 as a planning amendment naming EPC-001 and merge it into the line with git merge --no-ff (the pre-merge-commit hook allows a merge into a non-protected line); call the line tip L. main and the line now diverge.
  5. The destination: git init --bare origin.git, then git -C origin.git fetch <P> main:main, a fetch into the bare destination and never a push, as the TSK-145 journey seeds its destination (acceptance_journey.rs:664-675); git remote add origin in P and git fetch origin. Push the line with git push -u origin integration/EPC-001-line through the pre-push hook (a line's first push has no old tip, so the hook reports a best-effort check; record it). If the operator prefers a push for main, the adoption doc's empty-remote step (docs/adoption.md, step 7) is a human's action with the human override, never the agent's; the fetch route needs no override.

Record codeflow --version, S, A1, N, L and the destination's main. Preparation and the actions under test stay separate: nothing in steps 1 to 5 is evidence about the recovery, and nothing in steps 6 to 9 is repeated to repair a setup.

Under test, through the installed hooks:

  1. Reproduce: task/TSK-001-x from L changes a non-criteria line of T; git push -u origin task/TSK-001-x. Expected: work.criteria_frozen with the issue's message. Record the exit code and the message; this is the fail-before for AC-6's fixture too.
  2. Recovery, the line sync: in the worktree on the line, git merge --no-ff origin/main with the message Merge origin/main into integration/EPC-001-line (this repository's own precedent is 4a16a43d6 on the EPC-022 line), then git push origin integration/EPC-001-line; call the merge M. A two-parent merge is not a direct commit (line_adoption.rs:194). The three-way merge keeps the line's v2, because main's side of T is unchanged since A1. Record whether the whole push passed and any rule that refused.
  3. On the task branch, git merge origin/integration/EPC-001-line (the declared target's tip is the base the hook passes, push_set.rs:1324-1337), then git push; call the head H'. Expected: pass, with no work.criteria_frozen. Record the exit code, the range line and the --policy-from line.
  4. Observation, the task-only merge: on a second task branch from L, git merge origin/main, then push, before or without step 7; call the head H''. Record the actual verdict and any refusing rule.

The judged points each push reaches, from judged_points (acceptance.rs:1640-1660): a criteria base the head reaches is moved to the own-history list and is no longer a judged point.

Two corrections follow from the table. First, the recovery never reaches agreed: the Description's "newest judged point" sentence describes the one-point case, where main's tip sits in the branch's own history, not a choice between two unordered points; the fix (AC-2) is exercised only by the reproduction shape and by AC-6's journey after the fix, a task branch pushed from the unchanged base. Second, the task-only merge is not refused by the criteria freeze, as the Description and the triage expected: main's tip leaves the judged set the same way. Whether that push passes as a whole is the observation step 9 records. It is still not the recovery: the line stays diverged, so every later task branch meets the refusal again, and the task's range L..H'' carries main's commits into the line's review and landing as the task's own work. The line sync, steps 7 and 8, stays the recovery this record proves, and no range selection is changed to fit either expectation.

The note states each revision (the destination's main, L, M, H', H'') and summarizes the output. If step 7 or 8 fails through the installed gates, the 2026-10-14 decision in the workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md (no 3.1.2) means the failure changes this task's build order and the adopter guidance, not the release; the operator decides the guidance.

What changes in held_versions_that_differ_still_give_no_answer (:1354). Its shape is the positive case, so it cannot keep its expectation. The test is rebuilt in two: a renamed positive test (for example a_version_the_line_replaced_does_not_compete) on the same shape, run in both point orders like :1333, asserting Authority::Held with v2's signature; and held_versions_that_differ_still_give_no_answer itself, kept under its name on the concurrent-amendment shape (main amends T to another criterion, the line to v2), asserting Authority::Unknown whose reason contains "different versions" and both point ids. Its doc comment says why the first shape no longer refuses. The diverged helper applies every main step before every line step (:1278-1286), so it cannot build the revert and merge-resolution shapes, where main merges the line's v2 before the line advances again; those tests use an ordered sequence of (branch, step) pairs, a new helper that takes one or explicit git in the test, with a step for a clean --no-ff merge of a named branch and one for a merge that resolves the record to the current branch's version against the remerge, and each asserts that neither tip is an ancestor of the other before judging, so the unordered case is proved rather than assumed. The shallow, graft and replace cases reuse codeflow_fixture::clone(...).depth(n) (:1173) and plant .git/info/grafts or git replace on a clone of the positive shape.

Truth written once. The parenthetical in SPC-013's criteria-authority requirement (near line 611, "a line's version is older only when that line inherited it unchanged ...") is rewritten to the predicate: a version is older than another only when every commit that introduced it precedes every commit that introduced the other, and the same rule decides between versions the judged points hold and between lines of a history the points no longer hold, so the spec states one rule for both paths. The release fragment is a patch entry: a false refusal removed; competing versions still refused.

Design review, 2026-10-14

The revised preparation resolves F1, F2 and F3, and the installed-hook recovery passed. Implementation tests then exposed F4: the symmetric inheritance rule drops the line's v2 after main merges it and deliberately returns to v1, but AC-3 requires no answer. The revised predicate at e85a3a508 compares introductions on both sides and resolves F4; the fourth design review approves it. Implementation resumes with all recovered-path expectations retained.

Preparation stopped before the issue reproduction or any recovery action. The scratch repository was initialized with installed hooks, and EPC-001 was allocated in a linked planning worktree. Task allocation then refused:

The binary was built from unchanged product code in this worktree: codeflow 3.1.1 source=a1cf984c5b6e4f8e9d96018ed9c38faee7129220 dirty=false, hook input digest e7dd481aa2743faa158f4e0bf110427abae0d1f5a697155877fddedbde32269c. Recovery proof, 2026-10-14

The line-sync recovery passed through the installed hooks before any product code changed. The original diverged task push failed with work.criteria_frozen; both the line sync and the subsequent task push passed. The separate task-only merge observation passed too.

The unchanged product was built with cargo build -p codeflow-cli in this worktree, using its target/ and TMPDIR=/private/tmp/cf306. Implementation conflict, 2026-10-14

Implementing the design's symmetric rule fails its own revert and merge-resolution cases. Main reaches B, the line's v2 introduction, after merging it. A later unrelated line commit keeps the tips unordered. The rule therefore drops the line's v2 as inherited from main's history, while main's deliberate new introduction of v1 keeps main from being dropped. Main becomes the authority, but AC-3 requires no answer.

cargo test -p codeflow-core --lib workgraph::landing reported 22 passed and 3 failed. The material failures are a_revert_to_the_inherited_bytes_still_competes and a_merge_resolution_to_the_inherited_bytes_still_competes. Both assert unordered tips before judging. The third failure is a control-fixture error: replacing an absent epic field makes no change to commit. It is not evidence about the rule and remains to be fixed.

The positive inherited-version unit test failed before the implementation and passed after. The corresponding CLI test failed before; its post-fix run remains unverified. Evidence is in target/test-landing-TSK-306.log and target/review-design-TSK-306-codex-03.md. The tested code diff is preserved, uncommitted, in the worktree and target/design-conflict-TSK-306.patch (SHA-256 42164c7d037a966a29e18090110eb239a06c626c4ad09aaa19a0dfc60fe312e2).

The build brief requires stopping on a record/code conflict. The design must distinguish unchanged inheritance from the deliberate return to an older version without dropping the other held version. No criterion was weakened and no product code was committed. Final gates and the draft PR remained pending that correction; the recovery proof above remains valid. The revised design at e85a3a508 and review 04 now resolve this conflict.

A misshapen acceptance file is refused by name

TSK-307complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

codeflow task status <id> complete --acceptance <file> refuses a file whose YAML has no top-level acceptance: key with "a complete record needs an acceptance block in its Closeout", which names the task record and reads as a problem with it (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/175). The command reads the file verbatim and inserts it (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/new.rs:733), and the lifecycle check then finds no block (NO_BLOCK, crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/lifecycle.rs:894). The option's help (new.rs:96) says "the YAML between the fences", which starts with acceptance:, but the template comment lists the fields, not the key. This task parses the file before inserting it and refuses a file without the top-level key with a message that names the file and the key. It does not wrap the fields silently: the refusal is explicit, so a lane learns the shape once. Non-goal: changing the acceptance block's fields.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Original plan (Planning notes)/The acceptance binding counts a landed line adoption

The acceptance binding counts a landed line adoption

TSK-308complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

After a task's landing merge, any non-merge commit on the line's first-parent chain that changes a non-planning path refuses that task's acceptance binding (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:1079-1140, the message at :1137). Since 3.1.0 an epic records a reviewed direct commit in line_adoptions (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/line_adoption.rs:1-10), and the pull request classifier reads it; the binding does not. So an adopted direct commit, such as an owner's .gitleaksignore change on an epic line, still refuses the binding of every task landed before it (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/167, part E). This task is the narrow defect of issue 167; the issue's other parts are the adopter feature epic's work (design task T1 of the adopter design approved on 2026-10-13).

The binding consumes the verified result of line_adoption::check_range, errors included, so an adoption the line check proves counts like a merge for that binding, and a forged entry on a branch, an unreadable history or a changed acceptance block stays refused. bind_completion (acceptance.rs:341) also gains a public structured result (the reviewed commit, the landing merge, the span head and the completion tail), which the adopter feature epic's carry task reads (design foundation F7). The adopter's case is declared fixed only after a reproduction with a valid, landed entry (triage-codex-01.md, the issue 167 row). Non-goal: the record-hygiene checks and guidance of issue 167 parts A to D.

TSK-309complete

The whole outcome and context, from the record

not recorded

Context

codeflow update writes the binary's own version into scaffold_version unconditionally (crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/update.rs:371-373), so an update run by a binary older than the project's pin lowers the pin and rewrites managed files with the older binary's assets, while the [scaffold_sha256] table may still name the newer release. codeflow update --pin already refuses a lower version (crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/release_pin.rs:418, "the pin only rises"), and version_skew_warning only warns (crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/version.rs:33-43). Found by the adopter feature design of 2026-10-13 (section 9, approved by the operator), which homes the fix in this epic; the adopter epic's install-on-clone task relies on a pin that never falls. This task makes update refuse, before it writes anything, when the binary is older than the project's scaffold_version, naming both versions and the remedy. The fix binds binaries that carry it; an older released binary still behaves as before, which the release note states. Non-goal: a codeflow ci check on a pull request that lowers the pin.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/The program report shows every record on every fetched line

The program report shows every record on every fetched line

TSK-311todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

An adopter with many integration lines has no generated answer to "where does the program stand": codeflow status reads the working tree only (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/status.rs:7-17), and work next judges a record only on its own target's tip (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/readiness.rs:633-657) (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/166). This task adds codeflow report program [--json] [--host] [--strict] [--epic] [--line], a read-only report over every fetched ref that says, for each epic and task, which copy is the truth and whether every other copy is the same version, behind, ahead or divergent. It builds the two foundations the rest of EPC-023 reads (design section 3):

  • F1, the cross-ref record reader: one snapshot of ref names to object ids; parsed fields per distinct blob; the last-change commit per record path per distinct tip; full ref names as identity, with a label; unreadable records kept in totals as unreadable; a duplicate id with a different uid is a conflict row. It extends the ids inventory (crates/codeflow-core/src/ids/inventory.rs).
  • F2, home and currency. A task's home is its integration_target as its copies on the trusted remote's default branch and integration lines declare it; disagreement, or two lines matching an epic, is unknown. An epic's home is its unique line, else the default branch. The home copy is the truth. The last-change commit of a record on a ref is the newest commit on that ref's first-parent chain whose blob differs from its first parent's or, for a merge, from either parent's; a merge whose result and both parents agree is no change. Each other copy carries agreement (equal, differs), currency (equal is same; for differs, with H the home's last change and C the copy's: behind when C is reachable from the home tip, else ahead when H is reachable from the copy's tip, else divergent; unknown when the home is unfetched or ambiguous or the history read refuses) and placement (home, elsewhere, off home only, planned on default, branch only).

Each row carries, for every epic and task on every fetched ref: the home, the status at home, each other copy with its agreement, currency and placement, the derived readiness (as work next derives it at the home, crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/readiness.rs) and the branches that hold it. Rollups are by epic and by line, and per epic the estimate against the actual where recorded outcomes exist (crates/codeflow-core/src/estimate/outcomes/). A fact the report cannot supply is an explicit incomplete-data field: readiness is unknown when the home is unknown or unfetched, and the estimate-against-actual fields are unavailable when an epic has no outcomes, never zero and never omitted.

Authority comes only from copies in the trusted remote's namespace (the remote landed_policy selects) on the default branch and integration/* lines; local branches, other remotes and forks are shown and never choose a home. The report never fetches and prints its snapshot time; filters filter output only; --host adds pull request facts, else unknown. Class and lane grouping is TSK-314. Non-goal: any check or verdict; this is a report.

Amended 2026-10-22 on the move to EPC-022, for issue 280 item 2: each line row also carries the drift facts TSK-420's reader derives (commits behind the protected target, the last sync event and its date, the creation state (known from evidence, or unknown with the oldest divergent commit labelled), the oldest unlanded task's age, and the flag against the project's sync interval), read through that reader, never recomputed. The per-stream view of open epics the issue's comment asks for is not in this report: streams are clone-local coordination ledger state (EPC-025), which a record-only report never reads; codeflow coord status (TSK-440) shows it, and a tracked stream home would be TSK-313's vocabulary (4.1.0) if the operator wants it here. Deferred, named.

Context

pre-commit's only name rule is is_env_file (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/scan.rs:190-203), and nothing refuses a secret-by-nature name deep in the tree or a change under a path a project protects (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/174). This task adds the path gate (design foundation F5) under decisions 7 and 12:

  • Keys: git.path_policy (a level, block by default); git.blocked_names (a string, or {pattern, except_under, reason}); git.protected_paths ({prefix, allow: [{path, reason}]}).
  • Patterns: without /, a glob on the final component; with /, a component sequence at any depth; a protected_paths prefix is root-anchored on component boundaries; except_under and allow are root-anchored and normalized; a root entry is a whole-rule waiver that doctor names.
  • Comparison: patterns, paths and the built-in exemption list are all NFC-normalized and folded with one fixed ASCII fold; a trailing dot or space, ., .., an empty or non-UTF-8 component, or a backslash refuses; git objects only.
  • Links and gitlinks: a symlink is a hit when its path is a hit or its normalized target is absolute, holds .., or lands in a blocked name or protected prefix; a gitlink is an addition at its path; neither is followed.
  • Walk: the commits base..head introduces; a non-merge commit by its parent diff; a merge by its remerge diff, so inherited parent content is not introduced; an octopus or unreadable merge refuses; add-then-delete refuses.
  • Change kinds: blocked names refuse additions, renames into, content and type changes, and allow deletion with a history note; protected prefixes refuse every kind; pre-commit judges the same kinds over staged changes.
  • Where: pre-commit reading landed policy (refuse when unreadable; the stricter of landed and worktree when both read; the no-remote and unborn cases of landed_policy.rs:58-72 kept); ci from the target's policy. Exceptions come only from the target's policy; no actor, branch, slug or body text discharges a path. Denials union; except_under and allow intersect, through a typed composition API this task adds beside landed_policy::stricter (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/landed_policy.rs). Until 2026-10-18 TSK-320 was to add that API; with this task moved to 3.2.0 and TSK-320 in 4.1.0, this task adds it for its own keys and TSK-320 extends it.
  • The gate never judges its own inputs: .codeflow/policy.json, .codeflow/project.toml, .codeflow/bootstrap.sh, .codeflow/bootstrap.ps1, .codeflow/ci-setup.sh, .codeflow/git-hooks/*, .github/workflows/codeflow-policy.yml, .github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml and every .gitignore are outside the four new rules whatever the policy says, compared with the same normalization and fold. Other CodeFlow or host rules may still refuse them (decision 12).
  • is_env_file and the content secret scan stay on git.secret_scan; git.path_policy: off removes only the new gate.
  • Shipped default names (decision 7): the .env family; *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, *.jks, *.keystore; id_rsa*, id_dsa*, id_ecdsa*, id_ed25519*; .netrc, .pgpass; *.tfstate, *.tfstate.*; kubeconfig; the sequences .kube/config and .aws/credentials; application_default_credentials.json.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Release scope amendment (2026-10-18)/Ignored and oversized files are judged by the default branch's size and ignore rules

Ignored and oversized files are judged by the default branch's size and ignore rules

TSK-323complete

After this merges, an adopter is warned about ignored files and files larger than 1 MiB.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an adopter is warned about ignored files and files larger than 1 MiB, and a new scaffold refuses files larger than 10 MiB with the routes to admit them, all judged by the default branch's policy.

Context

The second step of https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/174, on TSK-322's path gate: a file the project's own ignore rules exclude, or a file over a size limit, can still be committed. This task adds two keys, read at the policy authority, the default branch at one SHA (TSK-1077), never the working tree or a pull request's base:

  • git.ignored_files ({level, allow: [{path, reason}]}, default level warn): the authority's .gitignore files through a gitignore matcher; a tracked file is still tested; a .gitignore edit in the range admits nothing.
  • git.max_file_bytes ({limit, except_under}): on by default; a new or changed file larger than 1 MiB warns; in a new scaffold, a new or changed file larger than 10 MiB is refused; an updated project gets report lines only, for both thresholds, until it opts in; an explicit limit or except_under in the authority's policy replaces the default.

Both honour TSK-322's built-in exemption and its normalization. The matcher needs the ignore crate or an equivalent, a new dependency, so a tier-3 decision is recorded before any code (Cargo.toml:36 holds unicode-normalization; ignore is not yet a dependency). Non-goal: a type rule beyond the name patterns TSK-322 already gives.

A refused file has three admission routes: (1) Git LFS, since the gate sizes the blob git holds, which for an LFS-tracked path is the pointer, so it passes with no policy change; (2) a limit or except_under change in the policy on main through a reviewed pull request; (3) from 4.2.0, a per-path admitted row in TSK-424's register. A single-file exception does not exist in 4.0.0 beyond naming the file's directory under except_under. Legitimate large cases (model weights, datasets and fixtures, media, vendored binaries, installers) belong in Git LFS, or in a release asset or package registry the repository references by digest.

Amended 2026-10-29 by the content policy amendment (issue #279, design revision 5, decision 8, taken by the operator that day with the admission routes stated). Until then this record said both keys were off by default and read at the base revision, with ignored_files at level off. Reasons for the change: two keys that are off protect nobody on the day they ship (decision 8 (b)), and the default branch is the only policy authority (TSK-1077, decision 5). This task stays a feature on this line by the operator's placement of 2026-10-18 and is not relabelled.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Test integrity amendment (2026-10-17)/A fresh clone installs the pinned binary and wires the hooks

A fresh clone installs the pinned binary and wires the hooks

TSK-324todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

A fresh clone carries the hook shims and policy but not the binary, git wires nothing on clone, and the shims' repair line points at the releases/latest installer, which can install a version newer than the project pins (https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/issues/170). This task ships one managed setup step under decisions 13, 14, 16 and 17:

  • Managed files .codeflow/bootstrap.sh and .codeflow/bootstrap.ps1 at every tier, integrity paths through TSK-325.
  • Inputs: only scaffold_version and [scaffold_sha256] from the committed .codeflow/project.toml, by a strict line pattern, checked by is_version and is_digest before any URL, path or shell word; the TOML is never sourced. Origin: the https GitHub releases host compiled in, no environment override, file:// refused, redirects only to https.
  • Verification: the archive must match the table's digest and the release's sha256.sum; a missing table, entry or match installs nothing, so a maintainer with a binary lands codeflow update --pin <version> first (decision 13).
  • Install: download and extract privately with a lock; refuse traversing, absolute, link or unexpected entries; keep the verified binary in ~/.codeflow/versions/<version>-<archive digest>/codeflow with its own SHA-256 recorded beside it; place it in the installer directory the releases/latest installer uses, named in the output, when no codeflow is there, when the one there is older, or when it has this pin's version with a different hash. A newer one stays (ahead of pin); the shared binary is never downgraded by any flag (decision 16).
  • Under CI: the script exits early, before any download, install or wiring, printing "skipped: nothing installed or verified; the managed CI installer owns installation", exit 0. It runs neither codeflow setup nor a doctor check.
  • Completion outside CI: exactly one of verified (the codeflow on the launching PATH hashes to the recorded digest; exit 0), installed (exit 0), ahead of pin (exit 0), or a refusal (non-zero). After verified, installed or ahead of pin only, it runs codeflow setup, codeflow doctor --check hooks and codeflow doctor --check policy-source; after a refusal it wires nothing.
  • codeflow setup: sets core.hooksPath to the shim path only when unset, as init does; leaves a detected hook manager alone and prints its integration; records git_hooks; writes nothing else; arms, never disarms; no download, no update.
  • In-session selection of the hook binary is a fixed refusal (Violation::always_blocking, decision 17): an assignment of CODEFLOW_HOOK_BINARY (leading, export, env, declare); a git command whose process would run with a PATH under which codeflow resolves to a different file than under the launching PATH, judged from a leading assignment, an earlier export, declare -x or assignment-only segment, a plain declare, typeset or readonly of an already-exported PATH, and a prefix on a wrapper (sh -c, bash -c, the other shells git-guard unwraps, env, xargs, command) whose body expands to git, taking reassignments in order and each wrapper's and sourced file's scope; the same words in a direct script operand of sh, bash, zsh, dash, ksh, ash or pwsh or a file read by source, . or pwsh dot-source, tokenized one level; an unreadable or non-UTF-8 operand refuses. A PATH value the guard cannot resolve (an unresolved expansion) is never treated as an unchanged resolution: it refuses, or is recorded as a stated parser limit. An assignment that leaves the resolution unchanged is allowed; the binary's own export to its git children is untouched. The development route is the environment that launches the session.
  • ci compares .codeflow/bootstrap.sh, .codeflow/bootstrap.ps1 and .codeflow/git-hooks/* with the judging binary's embedded copies, or the target's bytes when unchanged; equal to neither blocks whatever the level (decision 14).
  • Never: the script runs update or init; a hook or guard runs the script; a missing binary admits anything while the hooks are loaded.

The sample adopter repository of TSK-303 (EPC-023, 4.1.0) can serve this task's fresh-clone journey.

Widened on 2026-10-18 (EPC-022 amendment, PR 255) by the primary under the operator's rule that every security gap belongs in 3.2.0: every file under .github/workflows/ is refused, not only the policy workflow. Today only .github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml is protected (git_guard.rs:3706, and the Edit(/.github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml) deny). Reproduced on the line at 236e9d08b with that tree's built hooks, the payloads judged and never run: a native Write to codeflow-policy.yml, release.yml or a new other.yml passes edit-guard; printf x > .github/workflows/release.yml, tee, and mv x.yml .github/workflows/new.yml or mv .github/workflows/release.yml /tmp/r.yml pass git-guard and exec-guard; python3 tool.py .github/workflows/release.yml and python3 -c "open('.github/workflows/release.yml','w')" pass exec-guard, which refuses the same argument naming codeflow-ci.yml. So the .github/workflows/codeflow-policy.yml entry becomes .github/workflows/, which also covers the existing codeflow-ci.yml entry. Git commands that check out, switch to, merge, rebase onto or pull a branch carrying workflow changes keep their current verdict: the workflow change was made and reviewed elsewhere, and a person's edit outside the session still commits. Adopter effect: agents in an adopter's session can no longer write any workflow file; workflow changes become a person's act, as they already are for codeflow-ci.yml.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Original plan (Planning notes)/Guards judge git operands and environment supplied as data

Guards judge git operands and environment supplied as data

TSK-326todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Both guards can be handed a git ref, a remote, a program or an environment assignment that comes from data they cannot read, and they allow it. The TSK-283 security review (PR 195, target/security-review-TSK-283-03.md in its worktree) confirmed these on the installed 3.1.0 build and on the TSK-283 head, with git-guard and exec-guard both allowing:

The guards resolve a value only when its text is in the command. A variable set from a command substitution, read or any other file or process data has no text to resolve, so the push, alias, transport and release decisions see an empty or unknown operand and pass. Severity: high. Branch protection and the pre-push hook still stop a push to a protected ref, so this is a missing in-session guard and not a way past the remote floor.

The remedy: a variable assigned from a command substitution, read or other data, and every xargs, -I or {} operand, is unresolved wherever it reaches a git ref, a remote operand, an environment assignment or a program position. The guard refuses, naming the rule and the sanctioned path (assign the value in the command, or run the command without data-supplied operands), before the push, alias, transport and release decisions. The same task closes a second, low gap found in the TSK-283 round 4 review (target/security-review-TSK-283-04.md): a bracket-arithmetic ref such as git push origin HEAD:v$[2] passes git-guard on 3.1.0 and on the TSK-283 head when v2 is protected, while $((2)) is refused. It has the same cause, an operand the guard does not resolve as the shell will, and it lives in the same ref-operand resolution, so it is one criterion here and not a task of its own (the sizing rule in .codeflow/rules/workflow-discipline.md "Planning" splits only for separate shippable value, a pinned contract, an operator decision, size or a risk boundary, and none applies: it is digits only and cannot spell main).

Non-goals: judging the content of a data file, and weakening the deterministic floor, which stays pre-push and branch protection. The policy reference must say that configuration or refs supplied as data through variables or xargs are not judged except by this refusal (the docs nit of the TSK-283 round 3 review).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Gate efficiency amendment (2026-10-17)/The pre-push destination query is isolated from local configuration and transport

The pre-push destination query is isolated from local configuration and transport

TSK-327todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

The pre-push hook asks the destination which branches and tags it holds (ls-remote) and uses the answer for three decisions: whether a pushed branch's tree is exempt from the tree checks, where the range base for the push set starts, and which policy authority the destination has. TSK-304 (PR 191) made the tree checks fail closed and hardened that query against rewritten destinations given on the command line, but its reviews left three inputs open. The TSK-304 record (Follow-ups, and follow_ups in its acceptance block) and its security review rounds 1 to 3 name them, with owner EPC-022 and revisit "before 3.2.0 ships":

  • An on-disk url.<x>.insteadOf setting in the repository, global or system configuration can redirect the hook's ls-remote to another repository. The answer then decides the exemption, the range base and the destination authority for a push that goes elsewhere. This predates TSK-304.
  • The range-base commands in crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs (merge-base and rev-list --boundary) read the commit-graph file, grafts and replace refs at TSK-304's head. TSK-287 owns this fix, and this task does not redo it. At TSK-287's reviewed commit 0cc98b23f (PR 194 now at 8bb7a22ef), its AC-1 covers forged commit-graphs and disabled subprocess commit-graph reads, and its AC-2 covers range bases (push_set.rs:1644 and :1659 guard both git entry points; history.rs:308 disables commit-graph reads). TSK-327 keeps the dependency so that invariant holds once TSK-304's push set and TSK-287 are combined, and it names a range-base path only if a concrete reproduction shows one that survives both.
  • The destination query's ssh transport comes from the pushing environment. batch_ssh_command in crates/codeflow-core/src/git/remote_query.rs honours an inherited GIT_SSH_COMMAND and reads core.sshCommand with a plain git command (security review round 3, finding L2). The transport is the push's own, so the answer is no less trustworthy than the push, but the hook then depends on state the rest of the query isolates. The source rates the finding low and likely, advisory, and recommends only moving the core.sshCommand read to judging_command. This task asks for more: the query's transport selection follows a stated rule over all three selectors (below). The same function also falls back to GIT_SSH (remote_query.rs:210 at TSK-304's head), and an inherited GIT_SSH_COMMAND masks core.sshCommand (:185), so a fix to one selector alone would leave another executable.

This task isolates the query: it runs with the configuration, transport and history inputs the hook chooses, and a setting it cannot isolate is reported as "cannot verify" and handled as an unchecked destination under TSK-304's rule (refuse at block). Hosted CI on the pushed commit stays the authority; this closes the local floor. Non-goal: changing which checks the push set holds, or reading the destination without network access.

The present close test is reliable under host load

TSK-328complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

present_cli::close_ignores_other_processes_with_unreadable_command_lines (crates/codeflow-cli/tests/present_cli.rs) failed once in the TSK-283 essential run 6558afd8 (target/s2-essential-9f-present-failed.log in the TSK-283 worktree) and passed alone and in its suite. The failure was present close refusing with "browser process group exists without its verifiable leader" (crates/codeflow-present/src/browser.rs, the macOS process_identity path). The test registers a stand-in browser (sh -c 'sleep 120 & wait' in its own process group), drops it, which kills the group and waits only for the leader, and then runs present close. The close treats a missing leader as gone only when the rest of the group is also gone within LEADERLESS_GROUP_EXIT_WAIT, two seconds. On macOS a group member that has exited but is not yet reaped still answers the signal probe (process_group_holds_only_exited_members can tell only on Linux), so the killed sleep member can outlast the wait while the host is busy.

That cause is a hypothesis: the failure was seen once, in a full gate run beside other work. The task confirms or refutes it, then makes the test reliable. The sibling test show_after_the_browser_exited_ignores_unreadable_command_lines builds the same fixture and gets the same check. Non-goal: lengthening a product timeout only to hide the race. If the cause is a product race (a leaderless group that is gone a moment later), the fix may be in browser.rs; if it is the fixture, the fix is the test.
