The model evaluation gate target waits for the binary it runs

TSK-329complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

The model-eval-kit gate target can start before the binary it runs exists, and its result then depends on scheduling. In the full gate on candidate dd1188c5e (batch 2, gate run 7ba19750-cf8d-4043-a25e-a89ff2299411 under /Users/sathya/.codeflow/gate-runs/7a134ea9c2ea8c39/), model-eval-kit failed with a FileNotFoundError for target/release/codeflow in test_closeout_inventory_matches_real_local_worktrees (evals/model-artifacts/test_eval_kit.py:8513, calling eval_kit.configure_closeout_inventory, which runs the binary at assets/base/agents/skills/cf-evaluate-model/scripts/eval_kit.py:3043). release-automation passed in the same run. The test builds the path from CARGO_TARGET_DIR or target, plus release/codeflow (test_eval_kit.py:8509). .codeflow/test-config.json declares model-eval-kit with no requires, and it runs in both the essential and the full mode (.codeflow/test-config.json:282), so nothing orders it after a producer of that binary in either mode. It passed in batch 1 and in a targeted rerun only because a binary was already there.

No target in the gate is shown to build target/release/codeflow. The archived run gives release-automation the debug binary (CODEFLOW_BIN ending in target/debug/codeflow, from the declared codeflow-bin target, .codeflow/test-config.json:114; scripts/test_release.py:33 and its fallback build at :39 to :51), so the pass of release-automation proves neither that the release binary existed nor an ordering. The release-profile test targets are full-only (read-benchmark at :460, prose-exhaustive at :476), and present-binary-delta builds under its own target/binary-delta-* directory. The inventory test states no release-profile requirement. The builder chooses the producer path and records why:

  • use the existing codeflow-bin contract, which the archived manifest already supplies to model-eval-kit as CODEFLOW_BIN, add codeflow-bin to the target's requires, and have the test take its binary from CODEFLOW_BIN before any path under target/; or
  • if a release-profile binary is necessary, say why, and name an explicit producer target, declared in requires, that is available in both modes. A test that builds its own binary is not an option, because the producer must be a declared prerequisite that runs before the consumer.

Adding requires: [release-automation] is not a repair, because that target does not build the release binary.

The outcome is that model-eval-kit succeeds in each supported gate mode, with only its declared prerequisites, from an empty artifact directory, whatever order the scheduler picks. Non-goals: changing what the evaluation kit tests, or switching the gate to serial execution.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Test integrity amendment (2026-10-17)/Hooks stay usable while a CodeFlow settings file has merge conflicts

Hooks stay usable while a CodeFlow settings file has merge conflicts

TSK-330todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

When .codeflow/project.toml holds merge conflict markers, every CodeFlow hook refuses every command, so an adopter's agent cannot take part in resolving the conflict. Reproduced on 2026-10-16 with the installed 3.1.0 build in a scratch repository: after a merge left tier conflicted in project.toml, codeflow hook git-guard, exec-guard and edit-guard each exited 2 with cannot parse project settings: invalid key for git status, git checkout --theirs .codeflow/project.toml, git merge --abort, plain ls and an Edit of an unrelated README.md. After git merge --abort, run outside the session, the same ls passed. A conflicted .codeflow/policy.json locks the session out the same way (cannot parse policy ... key must be a string, reproduced the same day), so this task covers both settings files the hooks parse.

The refusal comes from read_project_toml (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/policy.rs:955), reached through policy_armed and effective_armed (policy.rs:866, :931) on every Policy::load_effective call, and from the landed policy path (hooks/landed_policy.rs:164, :180) and project_tier (hooks/guidance.rs:342). Failing closed on an unreadable settings file is right in general. The defect is that a conflict the adopter is resolving leaves no sanctioned path inside the session.

The outcome is that a conflict in either settings file can be resolved or abandoned from the session, while every guard gives the verdict the ordinary effective policy gives.

Conflict recovery only replaces a local settings read that would otherwise fail. It never changes which policy is the authority:

  • The authority stays what landed_policy.rs selects: the default branch at the fetched remote, resolved to one SHA (TSK-1077, ADR-0091), with no line, task record or working copy supplying policy, and HEAD only where the no-tracking rule already uses it. Amended 2026-10-31: earlier text composed the default branch with a declared integration line by stricter; TSK-1077 removes that composition, so this task no longer requires it. Protected refs, root-branch selection and every level are chosen the same way, as is any enrolled baseline that TSK-320 composes later.
  • Where a hook reads the local file (the policy_armed read, policy.rs:931; the local comparison in finish, landed_policy.rs:178 to :180; project_tier, guidance.rs:342), the unreadable working copy is replaced by the copy committed at HEAD, read as git data, for that input only, with one note naming the file. Where a read can be dropped instead (for example, policy_armed is ignored once a commit exists, policy.rs:856), the builder may drop it and record why.
  • Recovery starts only on unmerged index entries for the path (stages 1 to 3). Conflict marker text alone is not evidence: a file that does not parse with no unmerged entry refuses as today.
  • An authority that cannot be read is never replaced by defaults: the hook refuses, naming the source.

Hook integrity is unchanged: a Bash write to a settings file is refused as today.

Non-goals: accepting a settings file that is unreadable for any reason other than an unresolved conflict (that still refuses, naming the file), and changing what any guard refuses once the file parses.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Test integrity amendment (2026-10-17)/Essential gate runs are serialized like full runs

Essential gate runs are serialized like full runs

TSK-331complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

codeflow test takes the machine gate lock only in full mode: guard_gate returns before the lock for any other mode (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/test.rs:198), and the lock itself is full-gate.lock under the CodeFlow home and under the git common directory (crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/gate_guard.rs:54, :215). Essential runs from several worktrees on one machine therefore overlap, with each other and with a full gate, and their targets time each other out, the failure TSK-134 fixed for full runs. In this repository, essential runs the workspace tests, clippy and docs (15 essential targets in .codeflow/test-config.json).

The outcome is that on one machine an essential or full run never overlaps another essential or full run: the second run refuses at once, naming the holder, its mode and its directory. As amended on 2026-10-17, a quick run's light targets are unaffected and its heavy targets follow the same lock.

Decisions recorded here:

  • One shared lock. Essential takes the same lock files as full; there is no second lock and no per-mode policy table. The protection sought is one heavy gate at a time, and essential beside full times out just as two full runs do. Keeping the files also means a 3.1 binary running a full gate and this build running an essential one still exclude each other, and the shipped sandbox presets already allow ~/.codeflow/locks. The file keeps the name full-gate.lock; the docs say it serves both modes.
  • Refuse, do not queue. The second run refuses as a second full gate does today, with the holder's mode added to the message. Waiting is not added here.
  • The lock follows the heavy work, not only the mode. --mode essential and --mode full take it for the whole run. Amended 2026-10-17 after the Codex review of PR 226 (finding F5): a quick run takes it only for its heavy targets. A target is heavy when the test config declares it heavy; in a project whose config defines no quick targets, where quick runs the essential targets (crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/gate.rs:735), every target counts as heavy unless declared light. Light quick targets run without the lock, beside any gate. This repository declares its heavy quick targets (workspace clippy at least). The pre-push gate runs quick through run_gate_exact (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_hook.rs:1280) and follows the same rule; its ref, range, authority and checked-out-tree checks are unchanged.
  • Waiting is bounded. A heavy quick target that meets a held lock waits up to a bound the repository config sets, default zero, then refuses naming the holder; the run reports which light targets ran.
  • Direct heavy work. The engine cannot see a cargo command run directly. A sanctioned wrapper runs a direct heavy command under the same lock and cleans up its process group (provisional name codeflow reserve -- <command>; the builder settles the shape), and this repository's contract says heavy direct Cargo work uses it while another worktree may be gating.

Non-goals: an unbounded queue, and any fixed worker cap for adopters.

Amended 2026-10-17 by the gate efficiency amendment of EPC-022, from the gate speed discovery of that day (ranked change 5). The lock keeps a second heavy gate off the machine, but one gate still contends with itself: execution.max_parallel is 3 and counts target processes, not the workers inside them, so Cargo builds, clippy, nextest and the shell oracle (up to eight workers of its own, crates/codeflow-cli/tests/prose_oracle.rs) each size themselves to the whole machine. rust-build, codeflow-bin and rust-clippy reported Cargo lock waits in all three inspected recent essential runs. The task therefore also gives heavy targets inside one gate one worker budget and stops this repository's Cargo producers waiting on each other (AC-8 and AC-9). The budget starts as a setting of this repository (about eight workers on the 10-CPU reference host, two left for the host); an engine change to the runner is made only if configuration cannot express it, and the reason is stated. No fixed cap is added for adopters. Over-serializing also costs time, so the change is adopted only on measured elapsed time. Widened 2026-10-22 by the EPC-022 amendment of that day for issue #276: a project where several agent sessions push from separate worktrees saw two quick sets overlap and fail targets that pass alone (the quick suites run 420 to 456 s against a 600 s limit and are undeclared, so AC-2 leaves them light), and the pgrep check agents used before pushing is a race. AC-12 lets the project make undeclared quick targets heavy and bounds the pre-push wait with the holder named; AC-13 makes the holder record readable. The lock decision (one lock, refuse by default, bounded wait by setting) is unchanged.

Folded in by the amendment of 2026-10-18: the unit test testing::gate_guard::r22_regressions::r22_invalid_group_record_cannot_be_reclaimed in crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/gate_guard.rs failed one of three module reruns in TSK-305's essential run at 269f520bc. This task changes the same lock code, so it finds the cause and makes the test reliable (AC-11) rather than a separate task.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Original scope (no introducing section)/A docs portal workflow lease whose owner has exited is reclaimed at once

A docs portal workflow lease whose owner has exited is reclaimed at once

TSK-332complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

The docs portal's check, build, dev and preview scripts hold one workflow lease, .portal/workflow.lock (docs-portal/scripts/publication.mjs:19, withWorkflowLease). The lease records only a token and two times (publication.mjs:34). A contender treats it as live while its heartbeat is younger than WORKFLOW_LEASE_MAX_AGE_MS, four hours (publication.mjs:16, :50), although the owner writes a heartbeat every 30 seconds (publication.mjs:66 to :73). So a portal run that is killed (a timed-out gate target, a closed terminal, kill -9) leaves a lease that refuses every check and build with "portal build/check workflow already in progress" for up to four hours, and nothing checks whether its owner still runs. The same file ships to adopters as assets/docs-portal/starter/scripts/publication.mjs, byte-identical today.

The lease owner is the workflow, not only its coordinating process. The workflow holds the lease while it spawns the adapter, Astro and evidence children (docs-portal/scripts/workflow.mjs:12, :31 to :36). The signal-aware lifecycle stops those children on SIGINT and SIGTERM (docs-portal/scripts/child-lifecycle.mjs), but SIGKILL of the coordinator runs no cleanup, so a child can outlive it and keep writing dist, generated content or caches. A dead coordinator therefore does not prove the workflow has stopped writing.

The outcome is that a lease whose whole workflow has stopped (the coordinator and every writer it started) is reclaimed at once, with a message naming the dead owner, while a live coordinator or a live writer still blocks. The lease records its owner: the coordinator's process id and host, plus whatever the builder needs against process id reuse (such as a process start time), and either the writers it starts or a mechanism that proves no writer can outlive the coordinator (for example a process group the contender can check, or children that exit with their parent). The builder chooses and records which. A contender on the same host checks the coordinator and its writers before applying the age rule. Where liveness of the coordinator or of any writer cannot be decided (another host, a lease written by an older version without an owner, a permission error on the check), the four-hour rule stays. A reused process id reads as live, which blocks; that is the safe direction.

Non-goals: the publication lease (PUBLICATION_LEASE_MAX_AGE_MS, publication.mjs:15) and changing the four-hour age for leases whose owner cannot be checked.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Test integrity amendment (2026-10-17)/Version pins compare with one parser everywhere

Version pins compare with one parser everywhere

TSK-333complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

TSK-309 (PR https://github.com/sathyassn/codeflow/pull/207, not yet landed) replaces the loose version parse in crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/version.rs with a strict one that returns nothing for a version that is not MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional prerelease and build, and guards init and update with it (check_write_version). Its review (finding N2, tracked on PR 207) found that two other paths still differ:

  • is_older now falls back to plain string order when either side does not parse, where the line's version (version.rs:9 to :31) read missing or non-numeric parts as 0. A hand-edited pin such as 3.10 or 10.0 therefore compares differently after TSK-309 in the two other callers: update --pin refusing a lower pin (crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/release_pin.rs:418) and doctor's lowered-pin warning (crates/codeflow-core/src/doctor/ci_pin.rs:258). For example, "10.0" < "9.0" as strings.
  • pin_release (release_pin.rs:397) accepts any value that passes the looser is_version (release_pin.rs:342, checked at :403) and writes it to scaffold_version (:463). So update --pin can write a pin that TSK-309's guard then refuses for every later init and update as not parseable.

The outcome is that every comparison of versions and every writer of a pin uses the one parser TSK-309 adds, and no caller compares an unparseable version as a string: pin_release refuses a version the parser rejects before it fetches or writes anything; the lower-pin check and doctor's pin comparison report an unparseable pin by name instead of comparing it; the skew warning (version.rs:38) stays quiet or names the unparseable pin, the builder chooses which and records why. The comparison API makes the unparseable case explicit (for example a result the caller must handle) so a new caller cannot reintroduce a string order.

Non-goals: version handling in scripts/release.py, the installers' format check (the strict form is a subset of what they read, so they keep accepting every pin this task allows), and TSK-309's own criteria.

Scope added after the whole-unit review (2026-10-22): the codeflow_older shell function in the three shipped CI templates (assets/base/ci/ci-generic.sh, .gitlab-ci.yml, bitbucket-pipelines.yml) ordered pins with awk arithmetic and whole-string prerelease comparison, so it disagreed with the parser on rc.2 against rc.10, on +build metadata and on very large numbers. It now implements the parser's precedence rules and refuses an unparseable version (exit 2), and a test runs it against is_older over one table. Doctor's ci-perimeter pin check also validates every pin it reads before any success report.

Issue: #180. This is related to proposal A by security boundary, but its root is the matcher, not a missing store entry. It deserves separate regression evidence.

security/interpreter.rs:101 passes the raw word into matches_extended_glob at :132. security/pattern.rs:19 turns into .* but keeps the following slash. Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Original plan (Planning notes)/Policy and release verdicts run only the default branch's code

Policy and release verdicts run only the default branch's code

TSK-336todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issues: #204 and #202. These share the hosted workflow trust boundary, although credential persistence and check-name reuse are separate mechanisms. One workflow-hardening unit can cover both.

assets/base/ci/codeflow-policy.yml:57 fixes the job name to commit standards; :71 checks out the PR base SHA; :74 installs the target-pinned binary. :219 runs CI only on PR events while :238 runs the registry check under the same job name on other events. No inspected step classifies the base's protection before selecting the required name. Current automation profiles come from the judging policy in crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:1687; the older target_profiles function named by the issue is not present in ci/adopter.rs at this revision.

The five shipped checkout steps lack persist-credentials: false: codeflow-ci.yml:49, :197, :333, :795 and codeflow-policy.yml:69. Workflow permissions are read-only (codeflow-ci.yml:36, codeflow-policy.yml:62). This constrains the token's impact but does not justify handing it to later code.

Also owned here: SEC-03 from the confirm review of PR 231 (TSK-292) on 2026-10-18. A pull request's secret scan runs the head's own copy of the workflow, so the head can change the scan that judges it. It shares this task's workflow trust boundary: the scan, like the policy verdict, must come from trusted authority (AC-1). Named here by the amendment of 2026-10-18, with acceptance in AC-6. The same amendment gives this task SEC-06 (AC-7) and SEC-07 (AC-8) from the PR 231 follow-ups. SEC-05 (low: legacy-fingerprint advice still covers a clean two-parent merge amended to add content) is advice only and suppresses no finding; disposition: tracked once here, revisit when this task edits the legacy-fingerprint advice, where the fix is to require a remerge CONFLICT header naming the path.

Outcome: Only a fully checked range judged by trusted authority can produce the required policy verdict, and later repository code receives no persisted checkout token.

Source inspection is from the accepted triage at c5c6f6f671d2bf67a77113c656b3be446fb0bea1; runtime reproductions remain implementation evidence.

Amended 2026-10-29 by the content policy amendment (issue #279, design revision 5, unit U1; decisions 1, 3, 4 and 6 taken by the operator that day). Outcome, amended: both hosted policy jobs run only the default branch's code at one SHA; every required policy, secret-scan and release-impact check is produced only by that code; and on the default branch only by an identity the agent cannot hold, a dedicated GitHub App (Mode A), with Mode B's permission floor kept beneath it. The reasons:

  • A check bound to a job name under the Actions app id (15368) can be produced by any workflow in the repository, and a skipped same-named job counts as success (design D-3, high). Six required names on main are pinned only to 15368 today (live ruleset 24379074, read 2026-10-29 18:43Z).
  • Both hosted jobs build or install, read policy and run scripts from the pull request's base (assets/base/ci/codeflow-policy.yml:69-76; repo .github/workflows/codeflow-policy.yml:73-76, :87-90, :183; crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:1971-1994), so a line, which agents update, judges every pull request into it (D-4). "Protected integration targets remain usable" is withdrawn from AC-1.
  • The secret scan is the pull request's own workflow (assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml:343-470; repo :855), and this repository's release impact job builds the head (.github/workflows/codeflow-release.yml:28-58) (D-5, high).

The design in short:

  • Verdict jobs in the policy workflow (pull_request_target, the default branch's file) run for every pull request whatever its target, never reference the environment, and are named trusted: commit standards, trusted: secret scan and, in this repository, trusted: release impact. The head-run secret scan job and this repository's head-built release impact job are removed in the same change, and registry-only runs get their own name, so the old names have no producer.
  • One authority job, only for pull_request_target into the default branch, is the only job that references environment: codeflow-authority; it mints an App installation token inside the one step that creates the authority: commit standards, authority: secret scan and authority: release impact check runs on the head SHA. Ruleset B (TSK-1080) pins those names to the App's id. Without the App (Mode B, the floor), the final step lists check runs and statuses of the trusted names and fails closed.
  • Pull requests into lines get no App check; ruleset C (TSK-1080, strict) requires the trusted: names pinned to 15368.
  • Enablement order: this task reaches main through the line's reviewed pull request under today's rules; from that merge until the operator runs remote protect and retires rulesets 24379074 and 25435656, every pull request into main and the lines is unmergeable (fail closed, by design). The operator's Mode A steps are listed in TSK-1080.

Widened 2026-10-30 after the Grok whole-diff review of PR 396 (review-PR396-grok-01.md, high, CWE-345). Merge admission, ci-reuse.py admit (scripts/ci-reuse.py:182-207, called from this repository's .github/workflows/codeflow-policy.yml:171-185), accepts the newest codeflow-ci pull_request run at the head by event, head SHA, pull request number and workflow path, and by the conclusions of the jobs named codeflow gates and windows; it never checks what those jobs ran. A pull_request run executes the head's own codeflow-ci.yml, so a head that replaces it with trivially green jobs of those two names is admitted. This is on main today, where both names are also required directly and pinned only to the Actions app (ruleset 24379074); PR 396 did not widen it, since admission only adds refusals there. The design above still has the trusted and authority verdicts call admit, so it does not close this alone.

AC-14 closes it with the standard split between trusted CI definition and untrusted code under test. The gates verdict that admission reads comes from the default branch's codeflow-ci.yml at the authority SHA (AC-1), with the scripts and configuration that decide which tests run and how a job concludes (the set AC-13's Findings names, such as the partition and reuse scripts) read from that SHA too. The head's code, Rust and scaffold included, is the candidate those jobs build and test, as codeflow-ci.yml:110-127 builds it today, so an ordinary product change is still admitted. The run gets a read-only token and no secret or environment, since it executes head code. A head's own copy of the workflow or of those inputs never decides admission, and neither does a line's copy: equality with an integration base is not authority. A pull request that changes the workflow or those inputs is judged by the default branch's copy and reaches main by the operator's merge (Mode A), as AC-11 already states for the policy workflow.

Track once, from the same review (a nit): the adopter workflow chooses essential or full on a pull request from the head's own .codeflow/test-config.json (assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml:175-178), so a head can lighten its own gate. Revisit with AC-14, which reads the same head-controlled inputs.

Split on 2026-11-01. The whole-PR review of PR 479 graded this task Very Hard (9: S2 2, S6 1, S7 1, C 2, X 1, R 2), and a Very Hard task is split before claim. This task keeps the foundation, the default branch's code judging every pull request, and four new tasks take the other outcomes, with their criteria moved and not copied:

PieceOutcomeCriteria moved from this record
TSK-336 (this task)policy and release verdicts run only the default branch's codekeeps AC-13, AC-1, AC-2, AC-3 (narrowed), AC-5 (narrowed), AC-9 (narrowed), AC-11
TSK-1175checkout credentials are unavailable to repository codeAC-4; AC-5's per-surface part

  • acceptance.rs:2940 assigns a task range all its changes. Its origin becomes the range head at :2953 unless the amendable-line path applies. task_landing at :1058 and the refusal at :1152 can therefore treat a sync merge as the landing of imported main completions and blame later product work on them. This covers #181's 2026-10-17 comment as well as its earlier differing-shared-file comment.
  • recovered_completion at :1427 handles Landed::Unjudged at :1475 by retaining earlier criteria. This explains #218 after a valid pre-landing reopen on the task's home.

TSK-318 explicitly excludes merges (TSK-318.md:53) and its AC-1 rejects them (:67). None closes this group as written.

Folded in by the amendment of 2026-10-18: issue #240. A task branch on an integration line merges the protected target twice (the task must land with that merge). codeflow ci over the task's range then reports 42 blocks, none naming the task: 29 work.acceptance_binding blocks attribute a later target commit (one that edits .codeflow/policy.json) to every target task whose completion arrived with the first merge; 7 blame files that differ between line and target; 5 work.criteria_frozen blocks report the target's own criteria changes as the branch's; 2 concern a task the target reopened. Any non-merge commit on the branch that edits a file a target task's reviewed commit touched is refused as "changes <file> after the landing merge", even an unrelated runbook (34 more blocks). With a PR body, work.classification adds "a task PR may add only its own standalone task record" for records that arrived from the target. The pre-push hook gives the same blocks with different wording. Same family as #181: the importing range is judged as if it landed the imported completions.

Outcome: A completion imported unchanged from its proven home is judged at its accepted home landing, while changes introduced by the receiving line remain accountable to that line.

Source inspection is from the accepted triage at c5c6f6f671d2bf67a77113c656b3be446fb0bea1; runtime reproductions remain implementation evidence.

Desktop work stays in its own session worktree

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

not recorded

Context

Issue 219 reports that a Claude Code desktop session can create another worktree but its native isolation hook refuses edits there. CodeFlow's rules allow harness-managed folders, yet do not explain that a second unit needs a separate desktop session. The shared recovery command can also create a nested worktree when followed from a linked checkout.

Source evidence at cdfb4964829976bf87a61e544af196801c6eff94:

  • assets/base/rules/worktrees.md:8 permits a harness-managed folder but does not name the desktop session boundary or anchor .worktrees/<slug> to the canonical root.
  • crates/codeflow-core/src/root_checkout.rs:41 supplies the relative git worktree add .worktrees/<slug> -b <branch> recovery command. Its default locations already include .claude/worktrees at line 72; the defect is not a missing allowed location.
  • assets/base/claude/skills/cf-delegate/SKILL.md:123 scopes delegate edits to a worktree but does not explain desktop session cards.
  • assets/base/settings/default.json:14 begins the permission preset; all three shipped presets omit permissions.additionalDirectories. crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/settings_merge.rs:567 already merges incoming permission entries, so any qualified addition should use that existing ownership mechanism.
  • .agents/skills/cf-ship/references/pr-evidence.md:123 already puts gate evidence in the CodeFlow home's gate-runs directory. The issue's general local notes need a documented desktop-access route; they do not justify moving that established evidence store.

The native desktop refusals and repeated symlink prompts are reported by the issue and have not been reproduced in this planning session. The task qualifies a usable desktop route before shipping permission advice. It preserves the app's isolation hook, root-checkout protection and existing evidence stores. A broad grant to sibling worktrees is not an isolation repair. The proposed universal .dev/ layout and automatic grants are not accepted defaults merely because the issue suggests them.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Original plan (Planning notes)/Own-task criteria use the judged head in every checkout

Own-task criteria use the judged head in every checkout

TSK-350todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

The same judged task head shall receive the same own-task criteria verdict from main, detached and task checkouts. Issue 221 is a small follow-up to TSK-275, whose reviewed completion in PR 206 must retain its verified criteria. This task builds on that landed range context.

Criteria classification still resolves the branch's task from checkout records. At cdfb4964829976bf87a61e544af196801c6eff94, crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/acceptance.rs:257, :269 and :286 call task_id_from_branch; crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:899 uses visible_task_ids, whose directory walk starts at line 907. A checkout without the task record therefore loses own-task authority for the same judged head. The existing task_id_from_branch_at at line 1132 reads the named commit's records; reuse the head-based mechanism with the judging context's policy and guarded history rules. PR 206 at 8aa0748c3230f7eb44caa88ba5fcf5a0d7561c97 still has the checkout-based calls at lines 267, 279 and 296. This is a remaining invocation-context gap, distinct from TSK-339's imported completion origin. Native reproduction remains implementation evidence.

The task stays separate from TSK-339 because it fixes branch-to-task identity during criteria classification; TSK-339 preserves accepted completion origins across merged lines. Each has an independently verifiable outcome and a different regression matrix.

Widened 2026-10-26 for issue #304 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). Pre-push codeflow ci refused a lease-guarded force push of a task branch with work.criteria_frozen, because refs/remotes/origin/<branch>, the old head the push replaces, records a completion of the task outside the range (Landing::Elsewhere, crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/landing.rs). That completion never landed; it is the state the push removes. A remote-tracking ref is checkout state, so under this task's outcome (the verdict depends on the judged head and explicit authorities) it must not make the landing unknowable. The ref is identified by the pre-push input for the destination, never by a branch name.

Widened 2026-10-27 for issue #354, item 4 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). After a task branch was rebuilt with identical content, both a local codeflow ci and the pre-push hook refused with work.criteria_frozen: "origin/task/... records a completion of this task outside this range". That completion existed only on the task's own remote branch, never on the target; the adopter had to delete the remote branch, which closed the pull request. The pre-push half is AC-4's case. The local codeflow ci half has no push input to name the replaced ref, so AC-5 covers it with the same rule: the ref is the remote-tracking ref of the branch the run judges, never a ref found by name pattern.

Widened 2026-10-28 for issue #380 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). A task on an integration line changes its own criteria in its own PR, which cf-plan step 5 allows. codeflow ci --into <line> reports a note; the pre-push hook blocks the same range with work.criteria_frozen ("the judged points hold different versions of this task, and none of them is newer than the others"), because it adds --policy-from <tip> --commits-from <from> for the default target (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs:307-314) and main's copy of the task then joins the judged points (RecordStore::agreed, crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/landing.rs:522-545): --policy-from becomes names.candidate (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:611) and joins RunBases (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:4144); --commits-from selects the commit checks and adds no criteria point. Planning reproduced it on the line tip 654935d52 with a scratch CLI fixture (not committed): main and the line hold versions of the task that neither history contains (the line cut before main amended its copy, or the task planned separately on each), the branch is cut from the line and changes its own AC-1. Plain codeflow ci --base <line> --into=<line> gives the note; the same call with the hook's --policy-from <main> --commits-from <main>, with or without --baseline-from and --into, blocks; with the line's tip as --policy-from and --commits-from it gives the note. When main is an ancestor of the line, or only moves on with unrelated commits, both give the note. The adopter's workaround is a separate planning PR per affected task.

This conflicts with landed rules. EPC-022 AC-16 and SPC-013 R-52 make concurrent amendments at unordered judged points give no answer, and TSK-306's test competing_held_versions_name_the_points_and_blobs (crates/codeflow-cli/tests/acceptance_cli.rs:4742) checks that refusal with main as the hook's authority. So #380 needs a bounded exception to those rules, not a reading of them.

Proposed rule (the bounded exception), which AC-7 tests before any code:

  • Scope: only a range whose head carries the task's own criteria change, whose --into target is an integration line the destination confirms, where that line is the integration_target the task's record declares both at the line's tip and at the judged head, and where the line passes the existing trusted-line binding (epic_line_binding, crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:883): the epic exists in the trusted anchor records, is not cancelled or archived, and a task of that epic there names this exact line. Both entry points apply the same binding: an explicit CLI --into, which today skips declared-target eligibility (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/context.rs:41), earns the exception only after that check. Any other range, including one with no --into, keeps today's rule.
  • Criteria points (the proposed selection): for that task's own change, the criteria points are the line's tip and the range base. Today acceptance derives its points from the range anchor and the run bases, and an explicit --into adds no point of its own; plain codeflow ci --into <line> gives a note only because it passes no --policy-from. The default branch's tip passed as --policy-from would no longer be a criteria point for that task. Concurrent amendments among the points that remain still give no answer (R-52 unchanged there).
  • Kept from main: --policy-from stays the policy authority and --commits-from the commit-history authority, so main's stricter policy still judges every commit commits_from selects (push_set.rs:433), including history already on the line. A fix that passes the line tip for both flags is out of bounds.
  • Completion history: every point, main and the line's history included, still counts for whether the task's completion landed elsewhere (R-52's completion test, R-60, R-119, the reopen freeze, and AC-4 and AC-5's replaced-ref rule).
  • Where main's copy meets the line's today: when the line merges main before its landing pull request, Git merges the two copies of the record. Overlapping edits conflict and a person resolves them; edits on different lines merge without notice. The line-to-main pull request is an epic line range (Criteria::Amendable, crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/acceptance.rs:318), which skips the frozen-criteria comparison (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:4171), so no automatic check surfaces competing copies there; only that pull request's reviewer and the operator's merge do. AC-16 and R-52 give no automatic guarantee at that landing.
  • Added enforcement at the line landing (AC-9), in the scope the operator decides: a line-to-main range that merges a task record whose criteria main and the line each amended since their common version reports the two versions and the one the merge kept. Proposed level: a note, since the line carries legitimate amendments; the alternative is a block until a planning amendment reconciles them.

Decision owner: this moves a criteria-authority boundary, which cf-method/references/autonomy.md reserves to the operator. The operator decides the whole: the exception (AC-6 with its binding), the added enforcement at the line landing (AC-9) and its level (note or block). The builder writes no AC-6 or AC-9 code until that approval is recorded in this task's Closeout notes or a planning amendment. If AC-7's findings contradict the rule (a case where main's copy must stay a criteria point, or a protection the rule would weaken), the builder records them and the rule, AC-6, AC-8, AC-9, EPC-022 AC-16 and the R-52 deliverable change through a planning amendment before any code.

Amended 2026-11-01 (planning amendment): the operator approved the AC-6 exception with its binding, and AC-9 at note level, on 2026-10-28 at 15:12. Source: the workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md entry for 2026-10-28 (15:12), "Issue #380: TSK-350's AC-6 exception is approved and AC-9 reports at note level." The builder may now write the AC-6 and AC-9 code.

TSK-306's record, acceptance and tests stay as they are: its tests run without a confirmed --into binding, so the exception does not reach them, and AC-8 requires them to pass unchanged. Amended 2026-10-30: the #420 widening below changes the fixtures of two of them, with the reason it gives; AC-8 and AC-11 say which.

Widened 2026-10-30 for issue #420 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, by an adopter). A task branch edits only the Description and an amendment note outside the criteria of another task's record, TSK-X, whose criteria differ between main and the line, with neither copy an ancestor of the other. The pre-push hook and codeflow ci with --policy-from <main> refuse with work.criteria_frozen ("the judged points hold different versions of this task, and none of them is newer than the others"); the same change judged as the line's landing range passes. The cause: frozen_criteria (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:3059) sends every changed task record through the judged-points authority (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/landing.rs:455-490, refusal in agreed at :538-545), even when the range leaves that record's criteria as the range base holds them. It sits in this task because it is the same judged-points path that AC-6 changes for a task's own record, reached through the same pre-push call; one writer changes it. The rule admits no criteria change, so it needs no operator decision: a record whose criteria signature (CriteriaList::signature, record_text.rs:280, amendment notes and tags included) is the same at the head as at the range base is not judged against the points; any other record is judged as today. Equality with one judged point alone, such as main's tip, never skips the check.

Widened 2026-10-31 for issue #454: judging an own task's criteria must place a record version from main that the line amended, and not fail closed with work.criteria_frozen when main is not an ancestor of the line; the PR 453 sync of main into the line is the workaround.

This changes two of TSK-306's tests, which today refuse a Description-only edit: competing_held_versions_name_the_points_and_blobs (crates/codeflow-cli/tests/acceptance_cli.rs:4705, refusal asserted at :4757) and the two-task test beside it (:4839, :4849). Their branches append "A description note." without touching the criteria, which is #420's shape, so after this change they would pass. Each keeps testing the competing-authority refusal by having its branch change one AC word of the competing record; the Description-only shape becomes AC-10's passing case. Their names, the R-52 refusal they pin and every other assertion stay. For a record whose criteria the range leaves unchanged, the criteria authority note may still print as information (tests such as acceptance_cli.rs:4745 assert it); only the refusal is skipped.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Gate efficiency amendment (2026-10-17)/Gate selection uses proven candidate evidence against the task's line

Gate selection uses proven candidate evidence against the task's line

TSK-352complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: the gate speed discovery of 2026-10-17 (Codex peer report, ranked change 1, at line head eaf2ed04e932186cdd26dc4a7e5740cc553acee3) and the operator's request of the same day to make the verification gates fast without losing assurance. Amended after the Codex review of PR 226 (finding F1).

Today a run with no --since selects every eligible target (crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/delivery.rs, select, the "no proven comparison base" branch). Of 239 retained run records, 139 gave that reason and 100 were --only runs, so no unrestricted run has used change-based selection. Two further gaps stop it working even with --since: green_base needs a passed, clean, complete run at the exact base revision with the exact config digest, and only an unrestricted full run is ever recorded complete (testing/gate.rs, the complete computation). So a landed merge whose tree equals the gated candidate's tree never counts, because its revision differs. The run record's tree field is a digest of the tracked snapshot, not a Git tree id, so it cannot be compared with git rev-parse <base>^{tree}. A matching tree and config digest also say nothing about the tools, platform, environment, test membership or producer outputs a check depended on.

Outcome: quick and essential codeflow test runs, and the pre-push quick run, select against the task's declared line by default and skip a target only when recorded evidence covers the exact check that would run now. Full mode compares only with explicit --since; without it every target runs for non-selective landing evidence (security F1). Every unproven case runs and names its reason.

This task owns the evidence foundation that TSK-355 (result reuse) builds on.

Decisions recorded here:

  • Default base. The merge base of HEAD with the declared integration target of the task being worked on, read from the task record's integration_target (or the branch's work metadata). It is never guessed as main, never the previous commit, and never a mutable branch name used as evidence identity. An explicit --since stays authoritative and --all stays available.
  • Input classes. Each target declares an input class in the test config: content (it reads only declared files), or history, remote, time or external (it reads Git history, a remote, the clock, a vulnerability database or another outside source). A target with no declared class is unclassified. Only a content target can ever be skipped; every other class, and every unclassified target, runs.
  • Per-target evidence. The run record stores, for each executed target: its mode and exact command, the Git tree id, the digests of its declared inputs before and after it ran, the identities of the tools it declares (for example the rustc, cargo, nextest, node and python versions), the platform and architecture, evidence for the environment variables it declares as relevant (below), its test membership digest where it has one, and its producers' output digests. Missing evidence of any kind means the target runs.
  • Environment evidence never stores raw values. Amended after the Codex confirmation review of PR 226 (finding F6). Equality evidence is kept apart from displayable data. Only metadata the config marks as audited non-secret (for example a platform or locale name) may be stored as a value. Every other declared environment input is stored as an opaque keyed fingerprint (a keyed hash under a key held outside the repository and the run record, so the record cannot be used to test a guessed value), never as its value. An environment dependency marked sensitive with no safe fingerprint available, or one that is undeclared or unclassified, makes the target ineligible for selection and reuse: it runs. Sensitive and fingerprint values are redacted from gate-owned output and reports. Audited non-secret and unclassified values remain unchanged in output; equality evidence never stores raw values.
  • Coverage of the check. A target is skipped only when the qualifying run executed the same command in the same mode with matching evidence, or when the config declares a coverage relation between two commands (for example that full's rust-coverage runs the membership of essential's rust-workspace) and a test proves that relation. A full run is not assumed to cover quick-only or essential-only commands.
  • Qualifying run. A passed, clean, complete full run whose recorded Git tree equals the base's tree and whose config digest is current, and in which each credited target's inputs were unchanged during its own run.
  • The landing candidate. Selection never applies to a landing candidate's gate: the primary runs it with --all, and a run with any skipped or reused target is never recorded complete, so the candidate always executes every target.
  • Pre-push. The pre-push quick gate uses the same selection. Its ref, range, authority, release preflight and checked-out-tree protections (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs, and run_push_targets in crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_hook.rs) are unchanged and always run.

Non-goals: declaring this repository's target inputs and classes (TSK-353), reusing a prior target result (TSK-355), and any change to what a complete full gate runs. Product surface: adopter-facing engine (CAP-004 test gate, the test config schema) and the pre-push hook path.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Gate efficiency amendment (2026-10-17)/Repository gate targets declare the inputs they read

Repository gate targets declare the inputs they read

TSK-353todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: the gate speed discovery of 2026-10-17, ranked change 1 and its section "Input declarations still select most work".

Once TSK-352 gives selection a proven base, this repository's own config still selects almost everything. In .codeflow/test-config.json, execution.run_everything lists crates/, assets/, .codeflow/ and .github/, so any Rust or scaffold edit selects every eligible target. Of the targets, 5 of 7 quick, 10 of 16 essential and 20 of 26 full have an empty narrow, which select always keeps (crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/delivery.rs). A records or docs change therefore still runs the workspace suite, clippy and the build targets. In recent passing essential runs the workspace target alone took 28.89 and 31.02 target minutes of 49.19 and 54.00.

Outcome: each target in this repository declares the inputs it really reads, so a records-only or docs-only change runs only the checks that read those paths, while docs, release fragments, managed instructions and Rust changes still run every relevant check. The landing candidate's full gate stays complete and unchanged. Under row A below this narrowing takes effect; under row B the declarations are written and tested against a trusted base in unit tests, every requested target still runs with the reason, and the narrowed runs are deferred.

Credit rows (TSK-1044 settles which one holds; every criterion below that narrows, skips, reuses or recommends --since is checked against both):

RowWhenRequired behavior
Athe operator adopted a protected recorder in TSK-1044the positive journeys: selection narrows, skips and reuse happen only from attested executions
Bno protected recorderevery requested target runs and the reason is reported; no output recommends --since where it cannot narrow; positive narrowing, skip and reuse journeys are marked deferred in the epic's planning notes

Rules for the declarations (each target also gets the input class that TSK-352 defines; a target whose reads cannot be audited stays unclassified and always runs):

  • A declaration is justified by what the target actually reads. Input ownership cannot be inferred from file extensions: the update no-op test reads .codeflow/, every manifest destination and the shipped assets (crates/codeflow-core/tests/repository_update_noop.rs), and Rust tests that read real repository docs or records need their own mapped inputs.
  • A managed-instruction or scaffold edit is product input, not prose.
  • Unknown, deleted and renamed paths keep the conservative fallback.
  • The guard, hook and policy suites are never narrowed away from a change to hooks, guards, policy, security tables or the files they protect.
  • Docs keep the portal check AGENTS.md requires, not an assumed equivalent.

Plan amendment of 2026-10-23 (process cuts, TSK-449 to TSK-452): this task is the one owner of input declarations for this repository. That includes input_class = content on targets whose reads are fully audited, a run_everything narrowed to build inputs, and the skip of those targets on an unchanged tree. A skip is granted only from complete matching check identity (command, tools, environment, membership and producer outputs) recorded by a qualifying execution; unproven cases run. Targets that read docs or records (for example docs-validation) keep running when those paths change. TSK-449 declares no inputs.

Non-goals: engine changes (TSK-352 owns selection), result reuse (TSK-355) and the full gate's membership. Product surface: this repository's gate config only; no shipped default changes.

Outcome

Source: the gate speed discovery of 2026-10-17, ranked change 2 and its section "Rust execution and the slow tests".

Before this task, the essential rust-workspace target ran cargo test --workspace --quiet (.codeflow/test-config.json). Cargo ran test binaries one after another, so the slowest binary of each crate sets the pace: in run f5c9303a-23be-48b4-9908-8b9be010d034 the target spent 1,689.67 of 1,733.18 seconds inside 99 libtest result blocks. A simple longest-first model of the retained JUnit gives an upper planning clue of about half the elapsed time at 10 workers; it is not a measurement.

Under the 2026-10-17 decision builders no longer run essential, so this target now runs only when the primary, a reviewer or a pipeline asks for essential. Such a run uses the same runner, isolation and serial groups as the full gate, so the two modes cannot disagree about a test because of the runner. The speed comparison is deferred under AC-4's amendment.

Outcome: essential Rust verification runs under nextest with an explicit doctest step, with exactly the same test membership as today.

Non-goals: filtering or moving slow tests (TSK-356), the coverage threshold, and any change to shipped Rust defaults for adopters. Product surface: this repository's gate config and nextest profile only.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Gate efficiency amendment (2026-10-17)/Unchanged deterministic gate results are reused while push protections stay live

Unchanged deterministic gate results are reused while push protections stay live

TSK-355todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: the gate speed discovery of 2026-10-17, ranked change 3 and its section "Exact reuse and changed-input selection are different". Amended after the Codex review of PR 226 (finding F3 and a minor on producer outputs).

The same checks run again on inputs already proven. In the retained records, sixteen groups of clean passing runs repeated the same snapshot, config, mode and selection, fifteen of them quick runs. Two quick runs at dec65cb133e4 and d37e55ed86be share Git tree 14956b9f5b20400ff7d1f802db432877ca1efb38 and cost 2.18 and 1.72 target minutes; quick repeats usually cost 1 to 3 target minutes and one cost 10.53 with build waits. The pre-push hook calls run_gate_exact(root, "quick") with no reuse (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_hook.rs, run_push_targets).

Outcome: in an explicit gate run, a target whose evidence matches an execution attested through TSK-1044's trust mechanism reuses that result and names the run that executed it, while a push still runs no test-config target (TSK-449), every push protection still runs live and a landing candidate's gate still executes everything. If TSK-1044 lands with no protected recorder, reuse from local records is not enabled: every requested target executes with the reason, and the reuse scope returns to the epic's planning notes as deferred, never to credit from writable records. (Amended 2026-10-28 after the PR 378 review: since TSK-449 the push runs no test-config target, and reuse depends on TSK-1044.)

Credit rows (TSK-1044 settles which one holds; every criterion below that narrows, skips, reuses or recommends --since is checked against both):

RowWhenRequired behavior
Athe operator adopted a protected recorder in TSK-1044the positive journeys: selection narrows, skips and reuse happen only from attested executions
Bno protected recorderevery requested target runs and the reason is reported; no output recommends --since where it cannot narrow; positive narrowing, skip and reuse journeys are marked deferred in the epic's planning notes

This task builds on the input classes and per-target evidence TSK-352 adds; it does not define a second key.

Decisions recorded here:

  • Two kinds of completeness. A *completed target execution* is one target that ran to its end in some run: its exit status was recorded, it was not interrupted, cancelled or timed out, it passed, its declared inputs were unchanged from its start to its end, and every output it declares exists with a recorded digest. A *complete gate* is today's run-level complete: an unrestricted full run with no skipped target. Reuse needs the first and never produces the second.
  • What may be reused. A completed target execution from any run (quick, essential, full or --only), whether or not that run was a complete gate, may be reused when its content class and its evidence (TSK-352: mode and command, tools, platform, relevant environment, membership, producer outputs and inputs) match the current check. A target of any other class or with any missing evidence executes. Environment equality uses TSK-352's one contract (audited non-secret metadata as values, opaque keyed fingerprints otherwise, fail closed when neither is safe); this task adds no other encoding and never stores or prints a raw environment value.
  • Producer outputs. A consumer is reused only when each producer's output exists now and matches its recorded digest; a missing or corrupt output makes the producer execute and the consumer re-evaluate.
  • Provenance. A reused result names the run that executed it; a result reused again keeps naming that original run, never an intermediate one.
  • Never certification. A run that reuses any target is never recorded complete. A landing candidate's gate runs with --all and executes every target (TSK-352).
  • Push protections. The pre-push ref, range, authority, release preflight and checked-out-tree checks are never reused. The repository's config decides which targets qualify; unknown means no.

Non-goals: hosted CI reuse (TSK-359), and any compiler cache (not adopted; TSK-357 records the verdict). Product surface: adopter-facing engine (CAP-004 run records and the gate runner) and the pre-push hook path.

Outcome

Context

Source: the gate speed discovery of 2026-10-17 (ranked change 6), and the primary's build-speed research of the same day (scratchpad build-speed-research.md, read-only, nothing built), which replaced the planned sccache pilot with this task by the primary's decision of 2026-10-17.

Where the time goes, from 32 passing essential runs in 6 worktrees:

  • The essential Rust test step is 79 to 98 percent serial test-binary execution (94 to 100 binaries); its wall time ranged from 1,183 to 2,650 seconds. TSK-354 moves it to nextest.
  • Warm compile steps take 35 to 133 seconds (rust-build 35 to 96, rust-clippy 41 to 133), with outliers of 480 to 600 seconds under contention. Clippy waited on the build directory lock in 7 of 18 sampled runs; TSK-331 AC-9 gives clippy its own target directory.
  • Disk: one worktree's target/debug holds 56 GB (30 GB incremental, 26 GB deps with 453,923 .o files); worktree target directories total about 260 GB. On macOS the default split-debuginfo = "unpacked" leaves debug info in object files.
  • The debug codeflow binary is 75.6 MB (release 18.2 MB), and the tests launch it thousands of times (123 CARGO_BIN_EXE_codeflow uses, 282 Command::new in tests) with unoptimized dependencies. The first launch of a freshly linked binary took 1.06 seconds (one sample), then 0.01.
  • crates/codeflow-cli/build.rs reruns on changes under crates, assets, docs, project-management, .agents, .claude and more, and emits three rustc-env values; whether that recompiles all 52 CLI integration test targets after a docs-only edit is unverified.

Outcome: Rust build profiles and test layout cut disk use and build and test time without any new tool, each change kept only if its measurement meets its criterion.

In order:

  1. Do first: debug info. [profile.dev] debug = "line-tables-only" for workspace crates, [profile.dev.package."*"] debug = false for dependencies, and an opt-in [profile.debugging] (inherits = "dev", debug = true) for debugger sessions. Cargo PR 17518 proposes the same default upstream.
  2. Pilot: optimized dependencies in dev. [profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 1, measured on test wall time, since the tests spawn the debug binary thousands of times. The repository already does this for sha2.
  3. Pilot: fewer integration test binaries. Consolidate the 77 integration test files (52 in codeflow-cli, 24 in codeflow-core, 1 in codeflow-present) into a few binaries per crate, codeflow-core first, updating nextest filters that name binaries (binary(present_cli), binary(init_e2e), binary(test_gate_cli)) and any CI references.
  4. Check: the build-script cascade. Whether a docs-only edit rebuilds the CLI binary and all 52 CLI test targets. If it does, the fix touches the embedded-identity design and is a separate decision; this task records the finding.
  5. Measure only: macOS XProtect first-launch scanning. How much it adds per fresh binary and per test run. Exempting a terminal or agent host from XProtect weakens a system security control; that is the operator's decision, and this task only measures and reports.

Not adopted now, with the research verdict recorded: a compiler cache. sccache's Rust cache key includes the working directory, so hits across worktrees at different paths are unproven; it cannot cache incremental, bin or proc-macro crates; and compile time is a minor share of the gate. Revisit event: compile time becomes a material share of gate time after TSK-354 and this task land. kache is not considered (created 2026-02-15, one author with most commits). Shared target or build directories, other linkers, Cranelift and the parallel frontend stay out, as the research explains.

Non-goals: sharing any target or build directory between worktrees, installing any tool, changing the hook binary's embedded identity, and any XProtect setting. Product surface: this repository's Cargo.toml profiles, test layout and gate config; no shipped default changes.

Context

Source: the hosted-red diagnosis of 2026-10-17 ("Main merge impact and the process gap") and the operator's direction of the same day, relayed by the primary, to close that gap.

At eaf2ed04e, this repository's .github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml ran its Linux and Windows gate jobs on a pull request only when the base is main or master: the if: of gates, gates-coverage, gates-coverage-report, gates-verdict, windows-build, windows-tests, windows, windows-release-journey, windows-journeys and windows-verdict (lines 102, 283, 364, 416, 455, 513, 571, 621, 638 and 680 at eaf2ed04e). A task pull request into integration/ therefore landed with those jobs skipped, and its first Linux and Windows result arrived after landing. PRs 209 and 210 show this: their rollups mark every Linux and Windows job SKIPPED, they merged at 17:27 UTC on 2026-10-17, and their pushes added new failures to a line that had been red since 2026-10-12. The shipped template (assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml) has no such restriction; the restriction is this repository's own.

Outcome: a pull request into an integration line gets hosted Linux and Windows verdicts before it lands, once it is ready for review. A draft skips the expensive gates and runs security jobs plus verdicts that report the missing gates.

Cost, from one failed-run sample (run 39053855357 on 2026-10-17, which failed): 157.25 summed job minutes (55.58 Linux, 101.67 Windows), 30m42s from run start to its last update, of which about 16m14s passed before the first job started and 14m27s was job execution; a fan-out of 19 jobs at once (12 Windows partitions, 5 gate parts, 2 coverage shards). A green run and queueing will differ; AC-4 measures this task's own run. The repository is public, so standard GitHub-hosted runner minutes are not billed. The real costs are the account's concurrent job slots, which every workflow shares, the queueing that causes for other runs, and the wait per ready push. At this line's recent rate (17 merged pull requests from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-17) that is a few extra runs a day; a new push to a ready pull request cancels its run in progress (the workflow's concurrency group). Until TSK-359 lands, the push that lands each pull request runs the jobs again.

The operator decided on 2026-10-17 that a GitHub ruleset shall require the hosted codeflow gates and windows checks on integration/, applied once TSK-377 has made the line green. The primary prepares the ruleset and shows its exact content before applying it; this task carries that as AC-6. (Historical; superseded on 2026-10-18: the operator applies the ruleset, as the Deliverables and Execution contract below state.)

Non-goals: changing the shipped template, the secret scan, canary and security review jobs, and broader hosted reuse (TSK-359). Reuse association checks found in review are repaired here because integration pull request runs expose them. Product surface: this repository's CI and its integration-line ruleset.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Gate efficiency amendment (2026-10-17)/An integration push reuses the hosted verdict of an identical pull request tree

An integration push reuses the hosted verdict of an identical pull request tree

TSK-359todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: the gate speed discovery of 2026-10-17, ranked change 7, and scripts/ci-reuse.py. Amended after the Codex review of PR 226 (finding F2).

A push to main already reuses a pull request run's verdict when the pushed merge commit has exactly the tree of the pull request head and the conditions in scripts/ci-reuse.py hold (one merged pull request, ancestry, unchanged cache inputs, the present part's apt cache, and a fully successful pull request run). The operator approved that reuse on 2026-10-11 for main, and on 2026-10-17 extended it to integration lines.

The existing lookup has a provenance gap that matters once several lines reuse: it picks the newest successful run by head SHA, event and workflow path (scripts/ci-reuse.py near lines 116 to 144). It does not bind that run to the merged pull request's number, its base line and base commit, or the merge tree the run actually tested. Counterexample: head H contains line A's tip; a pull request for H into A lands with tree H; a newer successful run for the same H into line B tested merge(H, B), which holds changes absent from H; the lookup can pick that run and certify A's push. A retargeted pull request creates the same ambiguity, and a workflow file changed at the same path is not distinguished.

Once TSK-358 runs the gate jobs on ready pull requests into integration lines, the push that lands such a pull request runs the same jobs a second time on the same tree.

Outcome: a line push, and a main push, reuse a hosted verdict only from the run that tested exactly the merged pull request into exactly that destination, on the exact pushed tree, under the same workflow content and job contract; anything unproven runs the jobs.

The task starts with evidence: it first finds at least one real pair after TSK-358 lands (a ready pull request run and the landing push run on one tree) and records both runs and their timings. If no pair exists, because landings change the tree (for example a merge of a moved line), the task records that and closes without a change.

Decisions recorded here:

  • Extend scripts/ci-reuse.py; do not add a second mechanism. The stronger binding applies to main pushes as well as line pushes.
  • The pull request run records, in its own job output or artifact, the Git tree id of the merge it tested and the base commit it merged with. Reuse reads those from the run itself, never from text the pull request controls.
  • The secret scan, gitleaks canary, security review and CodeQL never reuse.
  • The required job set is read from the pushed workflow's verdict jobs, so jobs added later (for example by PR 224's hosted policy and native platform tasks) join the contract instead of being frozen out.

Non-goals: reusing local results as hosted evidence, changing the shipped template, and the cache-priming design. Product surface: this repository's CI only.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Gate efficiency amendment (2026-10-17)/The repository contract states builder evidence and the hosted green landing rule

The repository contract states builder evidence and the hosted green landing rule

TSK-360complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: the operator's request of 2026-10-17 to make the gates fast while the right checks run locally and in hosted CI, the decisions taken on it the same day, and the hosted-red diagnosis of 2026-10-17. Amended after the Codex review of PR 226 (finding F4 and a minor on the builder rule).

Two rules this repository works by are not written where builders and the primary read them:

  • Builder evidence. Builders no longer run routine whole essential or full gates. Their evidence is targeted tests plus the quick gate (the pre-push quick run counts for the same tree), as the managed block of AGENTS.md already states in its "build" row; one full gate runs on each landing candidate. Targeted checks that exist only in a heavier mode (codeflow test --mode essential --only <target> and the like, as .codeflow/rules/workflow-discipline.md already requires) and measurement trials a task authorizes stay allowed. The project section of AGENTS.md still asks for codeflow test --mode essential on every crates/ change.
  • Hosted green before the next landing. The line was red on hosted Linux and Windows from 2026-10-12 while later pull requests landed.

The hosted landing rule, as written by this task:

  • Ordinary landings on an integration line wait until the line's current tip has green codeflow gates and windows verdicts.
  • Recovery exception: while the tip is red or lacks evidence, the only landings allowed are the repair of the failure and work needed to produce the evidence (for example a workflow fix without which the jobs cannot run). After such a landing, ordinary landings still wait for green verdicts on the new tip.
  • Pending (a run still in progress) is not green: wait for it.
  • Cancelled, skipped (other than a reuse that names a green run, TSK-359), and missing (no run for the tip) are not green: start or rerun the run.
  • Stale (a green verdict for an earlier tip) is not evidence for the current tip.
  • A failure shown to come from runner infrastructure is rerun, never read as a pass; a failure shown to be unrelated to the next landing still blocks it until repaired, under the recovery exception.
  • Once TSK-358 lands, a pull request into a line also needs its own green codeflow gates and windows verdicts at the exact head that lands; TSK-358 updates that sentence when it lands.

The managed block between the codeflow markers is maintained by codeflow update, and the files under .codeflow/rules/ are managed scaffold destinations, so both rules go in the project section of AGENTS.md, below the markers.

Authority: the operator decided on 2026-10-17 that hosted gates run on ready pull requests and that a line lands only on hosted green, from the request to make sure the right checks run locally and in CI. Protection: no landing without Linux and Windows evidence, and no landing on top of an unproven or failed hosted run. Cost: a check of the line's latest hosted run before each landing, and a wait while a run is in progress (about 31 minutes from run start to finish in the failed-run sample of 2026-10-17).

Non-goals: the managed block, shipped rules, and the shipped pipeline default (TSK-370). Product surface: this repository's contract only.

Source: the Claude Fable 5.1 test integrity audit of 2026-10-17, finding F1, at eaf2ed04e932186cdd26dc4a7e5740cc553acee3.

Two shipped security policy keys are parsed, defaulted, shipped and documented as controls, and no code reads them:

  • security.sandbox_retry (default allowlist) and security.sandbox_retry_allow (assets/base/policy.json:62), described at docs/policy-reference.md:88 and :89. The shipped entry carries literal placeholder digests ("<sha256 at qualification>"). The schema validates only program (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/policy_schema.rs near line 1333). TSK-174 is cancelled. docs/policy-reference.md:598 discloses that these keys are not read yet.

An adopter who sets block gets nothing, on a security surface.

Decision (the primary's default, 2026-10-17): remove the claimed behaviour. The keys stop being documented as controls, a policy that still sets them gets a clear "not supported, has no effect" message naming the key, the shipped template and default policy drop them, and codeflow update migrates an adopter's managed copy. Implementing either control remains a separate future decision. A key that a project still carries must not break its hooks: the message warns, and codeflow doctor reports it; it never silently passes as a control.

A reader contract test makes this class of defect fail the build: every policy key the schema accepts and the reference documents has a module that reads it, or is listed as refused or unsupported.

Product surface: adopter-facing engine (policy load, schema, doctor), scaffold (assets/base/policy.json) and docs.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Test integrity amendment (2026-10-17)/A substituted hook binary cannot pass a hook silently

A substituted hook binary cannot pass a hook silently

TSK-364todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: both test integrity audits of 2026-10-17 at eaf2ed04e932186cdd26dc4a7e5740cc553acee3 (Codex medium finding on hook dispatch; Fable finding F2 and probes 1 and 3; Fable minor M6). Amended after the Codex review of PR 228 (finding R1) with the primary's decision of 2026-10-17.

Every installed git hook shim (assets/base/git-hooks/*, installed under .codeflow/git-hooks/) runs CODEFLOW_HOOK_BINARY when it names an executable file, checks only that it prints hooks 3 to git-hook capabilities, and then takes its verdict (pre-commit:7 to :24). An executable that prints that line and exits 0 disables the commit-time secret scan, the commit format check and the pre-push gate. The code calls the variable "a dispatch hint, not authentication" (crates/codeflow-core/src/git/mod.rs:21); tests cover only a missing or non-executable path (crates/codeflow-cli/tests/hooks_cli.rs:7256). No test presents an impostor that answers the handshake. The secret scan is the gate that is never relaxed (.codeflow/rules/git-rules.md).

Two related local overrides are honoured without a record: CODEFLOW_INTEGRATE_TOKEN is accepted when non-empty (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/mod.rs:37), and no test sets it empty, so weakening that check to "set" survives; and CODEFLOW_HUMAN_OVERRIDE=1. Neither use is written to the ledger.

Split with TSK-324 (EPC-022 since 2026-10-18): TSK-324 AC-5 makes the guard refuse an in-session assignment of CODEFLOW_HOOK_BINARY and a PATH that changes which codeflow resolves, and TSK-324 records the verified binary's digest under ~/.codeflow/versions/. This task depends on TSK-324 and covers what happens when the variable is set anyway, from the launching environment.

Decision (the primary's, 2026-10-17): an impostor is refused, never admitted with reduced assurance. The shim dispatches only to a binary whose identity CodeFlow has established, for example the binary CodeFlow installed and recorded with its digest; a substituted binary that answers the handshake is refused through every entry point. A legitimate development binary (this repository's hook and policy tasks run the worktree's own build) is admitted only through an explicit trusted route that records its digest outside an agent session; the ADR names that route. No choice that relaxes the secret floor is left to the builder.

Outcome: the trust contract of a designated hook binary is written down, an impostor is refused at every entry point with the repository unchanged, a legitimate designated binary still works through the trusted route, and override and integrate-token use is visible.

Product surface: adopter-facing scaffold (the shims) and engine (hooks, ledger).
