Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Release scope amendment (2026-10-18)/The guards judge every script interpreter the way they judge python and node

The guards judge every script interpreter the way they judge python and node

TSK-378todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: the security review of PR 239 (TSK-373) on 2026-10-18, marked "must fix before 3.2.0 ships". Severity high. It is unreleased TSK-302 work, so 4.0.0 would otherwise ship the gap.

The interpreter family list (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/outward.rs:1220-1236, interpreter_family) knows only python, node, nodejs, perl and ruby. A script run through another launcher passes both guards with an enforcement path as its argument:

  • deno run -A tool.ts .claude/settings.json
  • bun tool.ts .claude/settings.json
  • npx tsx tool.ts .claude/settings.json
  • uv run tool.py .worktrees/w/.git

uv run python tool.py ... is already refused, because the guard reaches python. The fix either adds these families (deno, bun, tsx and ts-node through npx and pnpm dlx, uv run and uvx with a script operand), or treats an unknown program followed by a script-like operand as an interpreter. The builder chooses and records the reason; the outcome is the same either way.

Outcome: a script run through deno, bun, tsx or uv gets the same verdict as the same script run through python or node.

Non-goal: modelling what each runtime's script does; the guard judges the operands, as it does for python and node.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

Widened on 2026-10-20 (EPC-022 amendment) by the primary under the operator's rule that every security gap belongs in 3.2.0, with finding P-2 of the cf-security-reviewer round 1 review of PR 264 (TSK-380) at c03b082dc, severity high, likely, pre-existing on base and head (.worktrees/tsk-380/target/review-TSK-380-security-01.md). GNU parallel runs the Perl inside a {= perl =} replacement string for each input, so a template word is interpreter code the guards never judge: parallel foo '{= system("touch ".$ENV{HOME}."/.zs"."hrc") =}' ::: x passes exec-guard on both binaries, and the same shape can name an enforcement path in a system or open call the template builds at run time. Today the guards read the commands parallel builds from its template and ::: inputs (docs/policy-reference.md, the closed rule; crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:4980, parallel_violation, and crates/codeflow-core/src/security/unresolved.rs:872), and a template word in braces is read as a replacement string, never as Perl. The widening: a {= ... =} replacement string (a --rpl defined replacement string holding Perl, and the --plus forms, included) is judged as perl -e code in addition to every check the line already gets: no existing refusal is removed, and no line refused today is allowed. So exec-guard, which judges perl -e 'open(F, ">", ".claude/settings.json")' as git.hook_integrity and perl -e 'system("touch $ENV{HOME}/.zshrc")' as security.shell_startup today, refuses the same text inside a replacement string for the same reason; git-guard keeps every refusal it gives those lines today (it names .claude/settings.json on the line, and reads a {= =} string as a glob it will not inspect past 4096 entries), and perl -e verdicts stay as they are on both hooks. Grok 4.7's round 3 review of PR 268 judged every line on the tree at d55b752ad (target/review-PR268-grok-03.md, the seven-row table) and is the base for the evidence below. Before the Perl judgment can be the verdict the test sees, the deletion reader has to model --plus and --rpl as input options (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/deletion.rs:4404, input_options_unproven, from judge_parallel at :4430), which today refuse any parallel --plus or --rpl line on exec-guard as an unmodelled option under security.dangerous_commands. A replacement string the guard cannot read refuses as cannot-verify, naming it, on a line that names a protected path or where one is reachable. The P-2 line itself builds its path from pieces at run time ($ENV{HOME}."/.zs"."hrc") and names no protected target on the line: that is the existing piece-assembly residual (docs/policy-reference.md, "Every harness": a path assembled by a program from pieces is kept as an allowed regression; the operator decision of 2026-10-15), which perl -e of the same text is allowed under today, and this widening does not narrow it: the P-2 parallel line stays allowed on exec-guard and stays refused by git-guard's current glob reading of the {= =} string, and perl -e of the piece text stays allowed on both hooks. What the widening closes is that the replacement string was not judged at all. parallel was not installed on the reviewer's host, so the behaviour was read from the GNU parallel manual and its {= =} documentation, and the builder confirms it with GNU parallel in a scratch fixture before the tests are written.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Release scope amendment (2026-10-18)/Repository and worktree discovery cannot unprotect enforcement files

Repository and worktree discovery cannot unprotect enforcement files

TSK-379complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Sources: SEC-377-5 from the security confirm of PR 246 (TSK-377) on 2026-10-18, and Grok's review of PR 246 at a3de25c80, findings F2, F3 and F6 (.worktrees/fix-hosted-red-5/target/review-TSK-377-grok-01.md in the codeflow checkout, outside the repository). Severity high. All are pre-existing on 3.1.x. PR 246 cites this task as their owner.

Protection follows the repository the guards discover from the working directory, not the repository that holds the target. Four ways to move or hide that discovery make another checkout's enforcement files writable:

  • Nested repository or non-repository cwd (SEC-377-5, F6). After git init sub, with the cwd in sub, printf x > ../.claude/settings.json passes git-guard, and native writes of <repo>/.claude/settings.json and <repo>/.git/hooks/pre-commit pass edit-guard (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/edit_guard.rs:241-290). A submodule gitfile cwd does the same. From a directory outside any repository the Write and the interpreter argument also pass.
  • core.worktree (F2). git config core.worktree <decoy>, or the same through --file .git/config, is allowed by both guards. core.worktree is not in SAFE_CONFIG (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/git.rs:46-101), and a local write with no file resolver drops the finding (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:8516-8532, :9060-9092). Afterwards both checkouts' enforcement files are writable.
  • mv then git worktree prune (F3). A plain mv of a registered worktree directory followed by git worktree prune unregisters a live checkout, and its .claude/settings.json becomes writable from the main checkout.
  • Registration that disagrees with its checkout. When a worktree is moved by hand, every guard fails closed and git worktree repair is refused under hook integrity. The remedy text does not name the person's route (git worktree repair run outside the harness). Folded here from the Fable confirm of PR 246, because this task changes the same messages.

Outcome: an enforcement file of any repository that encloses the target, or of the session's project, is refused whatever directory the command starts in, and no git or shell command can move, hide or unregister a checkout to drop that protection.

Reach, defined once here: a target is judged against every repository that encloses it (its work tree; for a linked worktree, also its common directory and main checkout) and against the session's project repository with its registered worktrees. So an absolute-path write into another repository's enforcement files, from inside this repository or from outside any, is refused the same way as a write into this one. Refuse writes of core.worktree (and the other keys that move a work tree) under git.hook_integrity. Refuse a shell move of a registered worktree directory. Protect every directory under the configured worktree locations whose .git gitfile names this repository's git directory, registered or not, so a checkout hidden by a move and a prune is still protected when it returns. The guard decides from on-disk state only, never from a memory of earlier commands.

Non-goal: a path that no repository encloses, other than the session project's files; the harness settings folders in the home directory are TSK-395. TSK-396 was cancelled on 2026-10-18 because this definition covers its case.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md, 2026-10-18 operator decision). The coordinator widened SEC-377-5 into this task on 2026-10-18.

A search pattern given to rg or grep is never read as a write target

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Context

Issue: #242. A read-only search is refused as a shell-startup write. rg --files | rg '/CHANGELOG.md$' gets "rg takes /CHANGELOG.md$, which the guard cannot resolve, and its directory is /" under security.shell_startup (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/startup.rs:2740-2750). The argument is a search pattern, and the command writes nothing. The adopter's workaround is to avoid searching. The same reading applies to grep patterns.

Outcome: a search tool's pattern argument is never read as a path it writes, and a read-only search is never classed as a shell-startup write.

The pattern operand is the first operand of rg, grep, egrep, fgrep, git grep and ag when no -e, -f or --regexp supplies it, and every -e or --regexp value. Paths those tools write stay judged: rg --pre <program>, grep has none, and an output redirect is judged as any redirect.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Release scope amendment (2026-10-18)/An amendment note under a criterion keeps its closing journey tag

An amendment note under a criterion keeps its closing journey tag

TSK-382complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue: #199. R-50 counts a (journey) tag only where it opens or closes a criterion. CodeFlow's own amendment practice adds an indented sub-bullet under a criterion ("- Amended <date> ..."). The checker reads the sub-bullet as part of the criterion, so a criterion whose head line ends with (journey) stops counting once amended (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:2190-2210). The effect spreads: work.journey_criterion then blocks every adopter-facing task, including one that serves the epic's journey criterion. The workaround is to move the tag to the start. This repository deferred the issue on 2026-10-17; the operator's release rule of 2026-10-18 brings it into 3.2.0 because it blocks work.

Outcome: an amendment note (a dash sub-bullet whose first word is exactly Amended or Moved and whose next word is a YYYY-MM-DD date) and its wrapped continuation are left out of tag reading, while every other sub-bullet stays criterion text, so a closing tag on the head line counts, and a refusal names the hiding sub-bullet or note when a tag is still unreadable.

The rule must keep substantive continuation lines of a criterion (wrapped text) part of the criterion, and keep direct and served journey semantics unchanged. The serves and (after release) tags follow the same rule.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

A project can run a gate target in its own split job without weakening the gate

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue: #203. The managed gates job in assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml runs codeflow test --strict over every target in .codeflow/test-config.json. A project cannot keep a target out of that job, so a target that needs its own runner shape (the reporter's browser target, sharded in its own workflow with codeflow test --only) makes the managed job fail or time out. The only route inside the project is to edit the managed workflow, which codeflow update overwrites. Deferred on 2026-10-17; the operator's rule of 2026-10-18 brings it into 3.2.0 because it forces an adopter workaround.

Outcome: a project can declare that a target runs in its own CI job; the managed job leaves it out, and the gate counts as complete only when a green, current run of that target from the split jobs is present.

Constraints carried from the 2026-10-17 deferral: every shard binds to the same revision and configuration; missing, failed or stale evidence is refused; required checks are kept; globally disabling the target is not a green result. ci_skip keeps its current meaning.

The edge to TSK-355 is real: split-job evidence is recorded target execution evidence, which TSK-355 defines and reuses.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

Widened 2026-10-27 for issue #352, item 3 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). An adopter's managed gate job ran five targets in series on the 2-vCPU ubuntu-24.04 runner in 23 min 54 s; running two targets at once in one job starved the CPU and one hit its 900 s limit. The adopter split the gate into a matrix of shards, each codeflow test --strict --only <targets> on its own runner, with one aggregate job keeping the required codeflow gates name and a unit test against shard drift, and measured 10 min 26 s. This task's outcome (a target runs in its own job and the gate is complete only with every split result green and current) already covers it; AC-5 and AC-6 ask the managed workflow to generate the shards from the test config, so the list cannot drift. The issue's items 1 and 2 (cancel superseded runs, skip a proven repeat) are TSK-1026.

The set is selected by a rule (a whole-repository scan under a time bound), so a new scan joins without a hand edit where the harness allows.

Not adopter-facing: this repository's gate config and contract only.

Issues: #223 and #225, two field reports from one adopter that ran a coordinator, six lanes and many Codex and Grok seats on one machine for a day. In each case CodeFlow already had the guidance, or nearly, but the managed AGENTS.md map or cf-method autonomy guidance never pointed a session at it, so the operator repeated it in chat.

From #223 (the map):

  • seat tabs: the cleanup row covers branches, build output and worktrees, not Herdr seat tabs (cf-herdr "Cleanup" has the rule);
  • standing operator rules: no row says where a rule the operator gives in chat is recorded (standing_reviews in .codeflow/model-selection.json, policy or a config key, else one project line);
  • standing reviews: the review and PR rows do not name the reviews codeflow models resolve owes for the touched areas;
  • pre-handoff checks: the status row does not say to check live state (remote ref, PR, checks) before handing the operator a command.

From #225 (autonomy guidance):

  • a peer seat's command prompt inside its brief's scope is the host's to answer and record; anything outside goes to the operator;
  • a classifier refusal with no stated rule of an in-scope verification command is distinct from a policy guard that names the operator; the sanctioned next step is stated, including a host-run route the operator turns on once in config;
  • operator delegations have a recorded home, and the autonomy rows read "the operator, or the delegate the project records";
  • shared machine resources: the host orders the gate queue and can ask lanes to defer heavy runs;
  • message budgets: batch one digest per lane rather than stall on a count;
  • a stuck-lane sweep before each status report.

Outcome: a session in an adopting project finds, from the managed map and the autonomy guidance, what to do in each of these multi-session cases without the operator repeating it.

Non-goals: new commands or checks (the doctor seat count and ci standing-review comparison suggested in #223 item 3, and a queue-aware gate lock from #225 item 4, beyond what TSK-331 delivers); each stays a separate request. Adding a standing approval or setting is a proposal to the operator under "Only the operator adds process", not a rule this task grants.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 under the operator's release decision of that day (workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

A lookup helper that keeps stderr open costs one timeout, not three

TSK-389todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: TSK-305 review finding L-3 (2026-10-16). A process the local configuration starts during the default-branch lookup (an ssh command, a credential helper) that keeps stderr open turns a good lookup into three timeouts and leaves orphan processes. It fails closed, but it still holds every push for three timeouts, so it blocks work.

Outcome: a lookup whose answer has arrived is not held by a helper that keeps stderr open, and no helper outlives the lookup.

The builder chooses between not piping stderr past the main process's exit and a short bounded read after exit, and records why.

The macOS case lookup stays fast in a crowded directory

TSK-392todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: found while landing PR 235 (2026-10-17). The macOS case normalizer (edit_guard::normalize_case) reads the parent directory listing for every path component, so a crowded temp directory made the interpreter suite take 2025 seconds. TSK-386 removes the leak that crowded it; a guard that slows with directory size remains a cost for adopters with large directories.

Outcome: a case-insensitive path lookup on macOS costs about the same in a directory of 50,000 entries as in one of 50.

Measurement basis, fixed before implementation: the reference host is a macOS arm64 workstation of this repository's workspace; the workload is 1,000 lookups of a three-component path whose last parent holds 50 entries, then 50,000 entries; the threshold is a median 50,000-entry lookup no more than twice the 50-entry median. TSK-386 removes the leak that crowded the temp directory; this task first measures the residual after TSK-386 on that workload, and the result decides whether code changes.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Release scope amendment (2026-10-18)/The exec guard adds a strict rule where the sandbox is absent or loosened

The exec guard adds a strict rule where the sandbox is absent or loosened

TSK-397complete

After this merges, the strict text rule applies in every session by default.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, the strict text rule applies in every session by default, and an operator can choose the line's rule for a project by landing `security.text_guard: relaxed` on its protected refs. No command the line refuses is allowed, except a line made only of bare `cd`, `pushd` and `popd` builtins under relaxed, which writes nothing. The change is breaking (4.0.0): `codeflow doctor --check sandbox` shows the rule in force.

Context

Source: PR 239 (TSK-373) final confirm, 2026-10-18. cd src && python3 tool.py .. from the checkout root is refused, because the guard's directory set keeps the starting directory after a cd (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/outward.rs, DirSet::change).

History of the outcome:

  • 2026-10-25 (operator): narrowing after cd cannot be made sound against shell state the guard cannot see, so cd src && python3 tool.py .. stays refused. The PR 331 reviews found 14 text-bypass classes.
  • 2026-10-27 (operator, option D): every stop in launcher traversal keeps its words judged, with a non-executing allowlist.
  • 2026-10-28 (operator, narrowed option (c)): the allowlist and its shadowing analysis are removed. The text guard has two outcomes, selected from the harness configuration the host can read. The specification is design note D revision 4.1, Part A (target/tsk-397-design-D.md in the TSK-397 worktree; checks: Codex 01 to 03, Fable 01 to 04).
  • 2026-10-29 (operator, option 2): selecting the outcome from the harness configuration is removed. A trigger list (rounds 15 to 16) and then an attestation (rounds 17 to 18) each missed a layer or key that let a weaker configuration select the relaxed rule, so the feature could not be made sound. The strict rule is the default; the relaxed rule is the operator's choice in landed policy.

The two outcomes:

  • Strict, the default, adds the strict branch, PR 331's rule with every name-based exemption removed. It applies to every call unless the operator chose relaxed.
  • Relaxed is the line's rule. It applies when security.text_guard is relaxed in every policy the hook reads at the remote-tracking refs as last fetched: the call's repository (its remote's default branch, the one policy authority since TSK-1077) and, for a Claude Code call, the session's project. A working copy, a local branch or tag, a remote HEAD outside the remote, a ref file that is a symbolic link and a repository without a remote stay strict. The guard verifies no sandbox under relaxed. A recognized marked retry (dangerouslyDisableSandbox), and every call on native Windows, stay strict under relaxed.
  • The strict rule's own refusals always block, under security.text_guard; git.hook_integrity sets the level of the line's findings only (security review round 1, SEC01-1).

Doctor and the hook decide through the same function (sandbox_state::reasons). Doctor prints text rule: strict with its reason, or text rule: relaxed by operator choice, not verified with the ref it was read from. codeflow init and codeflow update never write the key.

The strict outcome keeps every relaxed finding. Neither outcome allows what the line refuses, except the H-3 class below, which relaxed allows and strict refuses. A replay of the historical corpus is the test.

Hardening in both outcomes:

  • a NUL byte refuses (H-1);
  • the headless xargs reader no longer guesses a bare optional-value option or a BSD option (H-2);
  • a line made only of bare cd, pushd and popd builtins no longer takes the startup write judgement (H-3, issue 342);
  • the enforcement paths are explicit sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite entries in the presets (H-4);
  • ~/.codeflow/authority/ is a protected directory, reserved for the 4.1.0 qualification records (H-5).

codeflow doctor --check sandbox names the rule in force and why (H-6). Non-goals for 4.0.0: qualification, receipts, capability relaxation and the other Part C units, which are planned for 4.1.0.

Limits, each as it is on the line today unless noted:

  • An unread program (a script file, code the guard does not read) can write an enforcement file or read a secret wherever no kernel deny holds. The strict branch narrows the text-visible paths and contains nothing.
  • Under relaxed, the guard trusts the OS sandbox the project configures and does not check it. An unsandboxed retry the harness does not mark (a Codex seat has no field) follows the relaxed rule; TSK-1052 fails closed there for a command that runs code after a same-line write (EPC-022, filed by PR 390).
  • Doctor's state-root check reads Claude write grants only; Codex and Grok grants are not computed, and doctor does not claim the state root is unwritable.
  • An awk inline program that writes an enforcement path passes the exec guard (git-guard refuses it); it is the unread-program residual above, to be tracked once.
  • Debug builds honour CODEFLOW_TEST_CLAUDE_MANAGED_DIR, which moves the managed settings layer doctor reads; release builds ignore it.
  • The Monitor tool is outside the hook matcher (4.1.0, TSK-1058).
  • Policy authority under refs/remotes/origin/* and packed-refs is writable by a direct file write (4.1.0, TSK-1057). A relaxed value written there by a session, or a stale relaxed ref before the next fetch, would be read as landed; the same gap applies to every policy key. Security review round 1 (SEC01-2) narrowed the read to plain refs inside the remote's namespace with no symbolic-link ref files; it does not authenticate them.
  • A file a repository configuration include names is read by libgit2 with a blocking read and is not checked. A fifo named only by an include stalls that read until the guard's own deadline (TSK-1082, merged from the line on 2026-10-30) refuses with exit 2 after 20 seconds; the stall never allows the command (docs/policy-reference.md, repository discovery). The repository's own config and config.worktree files, the policy and the project settings are checked first (SEC01-3).
  • Neither rule sees the environment a command inherits (PATH, HOME, Codex's shell_environment_policy, secret-bearing variables); Fable F3-1's attestation finding is moot, this residual is not.
  • In a linked worktree, protection of the shared .git's hooks, config and config.worktree is unverified (4.1.0, TSK-1054).
  • Codex nested secret files and .envrc, and Grok's launch-time globs, are recorded gaps of those profiles.

Follow-ups (for the closeout follow_ups): the Part C units of design D, planned for 4.1.0 in EPC-023 by PR 391. They are TSK-1054 (qualification record), TSK-1055 (capability relaxation), TSK-1056 (administrator policy), TSK-1057 (authenticated policy authority), TSK-1058 (Monitor matcher), TSK-1059 (trusted host-state operations) and TSK-1060 (Codex managed requirements). A relaxed rule tied to verified containment, in place of the operator's unverified choice, belongs to TSK-1054. Failing closed in the unknown-containment cases is tracked as TSK-1052 (EPC-022). Deferred: setting security.text_guard: relaxed in CodeFlow's own .codeflow/policy.json (the operator's choice of 2026-10-29) waits until 4.0.0 publishes. Reason: a new key enters the installed policy only after the release that introduced it has published (docs/policy-reference.md, "Where a new key goes", held by policy_key_placement), and the hosted policy check judges the head with the base's binary, which does not know the key; the coordinator tracks it.

Criteria changes in this amendment (2026-10-28):

  • Changed AC-1: it keeps both refusals and now states them for both outcomes. Reason: the outcome now has two text rules, and the refusal holds in each.
  • Replaced AC-2: the per-bypass-line refusal list of option D, with its non-executing allowlist rule, is removed. Reason: the operator chose narrowed option (c), which removes every name-based exemption. The strict branch refuses every listed bypass line in the tightened outcome. The baseline keeps the line's rule, so the bypass lines stay text-bypassable there, as A6 states. The new AC-2 is the invariant that no line refusal is lost.
  • Replaced AC-3: the installed-build journey of cd src && python3 tool.py ../.claude/settings.json is covered by the new AC-1 in both outcomes. The new AC-3 pins retry recognition, which this outcome adds.
  • Added AC-4 to AC-8, for the triggers, doctor, measurement, policy key and hardening of design D Part A.
  • Changed AC-2 after the Codex 16 and Fable 01 reviews: the exception is the H-3 class, checked by a predicate, where it was four listed rows. Reason: the exception is a class, and a row list would let a widened predicate pass unnoticed. The corpus gains the review's three class rows.
  • Changed AC-4 after the same reviews: an absent Codex or Grok configuration tightens a call identified as that harness. Reason: without it the shipped profile is not in force, and the call cannot be shown contained.
  • Changed AC-5: doctor prints one text-rule line per harness, decided by the hook's function. Reason: one host line could disagree with what the hook decides for a given harness.
  • Changed AC-4 after Codex 17 and Fable 02: the per-trigger fixtures become attestation fixtures (each customised, unknown or unreadable form tightens; each listed narrower form stays the baseline), and an unidentified payload tightens. Reason: the trigger list could not be made sound; the union rule let a payload of no single harness reach the baseline.
  • Changed AC-5 after the same reviews: a harness the project does not configure is a note, and doctor no longer claims the state root unwritable. Reason: its write set left out grants it cannot compute.
  • Changed AC-7 after the same reviews: a Claude call also reads the session project's policy, failing closed. Reason: strict set in the session's project was lost when the call ran in another repository.

Criteria changes for option 2 (operator, 2026-10-29):

  • Changed AC-1 and AC-2: "baseline" and "tightened" become relaxed and strict. Reason: the outcomes are renamed for what selects them; the refusals and the invariant are unchanged.
  • Changed AC-3: a payload without the retry field takes the rule the landed policy selects, and the note that an unmarked retry follows the baseline now says it follows the relaxed rule. Reason: there is no configuration-selected baseline.
  • Replaced AC-4: the attestation fixtures are removed; the new AC-4 states the default and where relaxed is honoured. Reason: attestation is removed (Codex 18 findings 1 to 4 and Fable F3-1 showed it could not be made sound).
  • Changed AC-5: doctor prints one text-rule line, strict with its reason or relaxed by operator choice with its ref, and no longer judges harness configuration. Reason: nothing is attested any more, so a per-harness verdict would claim what the guard does not check.
  • Changed AC-7: the values are strict (the default) and relaxed; auto is dropped. Reason: auto selected attestation; relaxed is the operator's explicit choice.
  • Changed AC-8: H-3's cd ~ && cd "$p" and cd / && pushd "$p" pass the startup check in both outcomes and pass the guard under relaxed; strict refuses their run-time operands. Reason: issue 342's line is allowed only where the operator chose relaxed.

Criteria change after merging the line at 31f7df8f7 (2026-11-01):

  • Changed AC-4: relaxed is read only from the remote's default branch. Reason: TSK-1077 made the default branch the one local policy authority, so a declared line no longer supplies policy and the strict-wins merge across sources has nothing to merge.

Criteria change after merging the line at 59f134771 (2026-10-30):

  • Changed AC-2: the line column is the binary built from the line this branch last merged, where it was the binary at 5f2fe3827. Reason: relaxed is the line's rule, and the line moved. The line at 59f134771 (TSK-1002 among others) refuses 167 corpus rows the 5f2fe3827 binary allowed and allows 5 it refused, each run from the checkout root against an ordinary settings.json. Against the old column the invariant cannot hold for any build that keeps relaxed equal to the line. The invariant itself is unchanged.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Release scope amendment (2026-10-18)/An opt-in infrastructure preset refuses commands that change live cloud state

An opt-in infrastructure preset refuses commands that change live cloud state

TSK-400todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue: #171, its defect portion. exec-guard has no way to refuse commands that change live cloud state: terraform apply, tofu apply, mutating gcloud verbs, kubectl writes and flux pass at security.outward_actions: block, because crates/codeflow-core/src/security/outward.rs knows only the shipped families. The adopter's workaround is its own deny rules in the Claude permission preset and Codex command rules, to be removed once a release refuses these commands.

This task ships the opt-in infrastructure preset that TSK-320 first planned (operator decision 5 of 2026-10-13): security.project_action_presets: ["infrastructure"], off by default. When on, it refuses exactly decision 5's forms, as recorded in TSK-320's description: tofu and terraform apply, destroy, import, state rm, state mv, force-unlock, taint, untaint; gcloud verbs create, delete, update, deploy, set-iam-policy, add-iam-policy-binding, remove-iam-policy-binding, enable, disable; kubectl apply, create, delete, patch, replace, scale, edit, rollout, drain, cordon, taint; flux as a whole program; helm install, upgrade, uninstall, rollback; pulumi up, destroy, import, refresh. They are refused at the outward_actions level, through the shipped unwrapping, and update reports a changed preset.

The preset is a list-valued security key, so it must survive policy composition. Today crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/landed_policy.rs starts from the default branch's policy (:77) and folds in each declared integration target through stricter (:108), which composes levels and level-like enums (:342) and unions only git.protected_branches (:360). A main policy with the preset off would erase an integration target's opt-in. This task adds a bounded union for security.project_action_presets in that function, across every default-branch candidate and declared target, so any applicable landed authority that turns the preset on keeps it on. It does not wait for TSK-322's typed composition API and adds no edge to it. If TSK-322 is already on the integration line when this task lands, this task routes the preset union through that typed API; otherwise TSK-322 does so when it lands. In both cases the later task reruns this task's AC-5 against the combined implementation and cites the result in its PR.

Project-declared commands (project_actions) remain TSK-320 in EPC-023 (4.1.0), which now depends on this task and adds its declarations beside the preset.

Outcome: an adopter that turns on the infrastructure preset has these commands refused by CodeFlow and can drop its own deny rules.

Context

Issue: #169, its defect portions. Two adopter workarounds:

  • A carry of one landed, reviewed task change to another integration line has no checked route. A carry pull request fails work.stable_planning_anchor because the task's record lives on its home line (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:1466-1530), so the adopter lands carries by a gated merge outside every check.
  • The cleanup rule deletes a pushed branch only when its PR is MERGED and the tip equals the PR's recorded head (assets/base/rules/worktrees.md:93-110). A branch whose content landed by ancestry, with no merged PR (a carry merged into its destination line, or a closed PR whose head is an ancestor of main), can never be deleted.

This task gives both a checked route that exists today. A carry is a merge of the task's reviewed head (or its home line) into the other line, which codeflow integrate --no-ff (TSK-293) can make; codeflow ci judges it by the source task's binding, which TSK-339 establishes for imported completions. A pushed branch may also be deleted when its tip is an ancestor of its destination line, as an alternative to the matching merged PR, with the existing checks kept: an inactive owner, a clean worktree, and the recorded tip SHA still shown by the remote. The proof is recorded in the cleanup step. Patch equivalence (git cherry) is never a deletion proof: it compares diffs with whitespace and line numbers removed, so a patch-equivalent lead is evidence to investigate, as TSK-319's rule already states.

The one-commit carry class with byte comparison (TSK-318), and the remote branch inventory with compare-and-swap deletion (TSK-319), stay in EPC-023 (4.1.0); both now depend on this task.

Outcome: an adopter can carry a landed task to another line through a pull request that codeflow ci checks and accepts, and can clean up a pushed branch whose content provably landed.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Release scope amendment (2026-10-18)/A resolved update conflict does not come back on the next update

A resolved update conflict does not come back on the next update

TSK-405complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue: #74, its comment of 2026-10-13 only. When codeflow update hits a conflict in a managed file the project customised, it writes <file>.new and a report note, but keeps the old shipped baseline and manifest hash (crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/update.rs:818, the ManagedStep::Conflict arm; the clean-merge arm at :809 records the new shipped hash and baseline). After a person resolves the .new and replaces the file, the next update merges against the old base, sees the previous release's upstream changes as project changes and conflicts again on the same hunks. The adopter's workaround is to re-resolve the same conflict on every update; a project that customises its CI workflow hits it every release.

The Codex review of PR 249 reproduced it with this worktree's binary (target/review-PR249-update-conflict-02.txt in the planning worktree): after a simulated resolution the second update exits 2 and recreates the same conflict. In a control, setting only the existing baseline and manifest hash to the pristine candidate, with the person's file kept, made the next update exit 0 and keep the project's change, with no format change.

Outcome: a person's accepted resolution of an update conflict is recorded against the correct shipped base, so the same conflict does not return on the next update and later upstream changes still merge.

Invariant: the baseline and manifest hash keep describing shipped content, never the person's merged file. The existing formats stay. The baseline replacement and codeflow update --plan stay in 4.0.0 and carry this regression test forward.

The builder chooses how the resolution is recorded (for example, the conflict arm writes the new shipped baseline beside the .new and records the resolution as pending, and the next update accepts it only when the .new is gone and the file holds no conflict markers; or an explicit resolve step) and records why. Whatever the route, an unresolved or mismatched resolution is never accepted silently.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18 after the second Codex review of PR 249 (target/review-PR249-codex-02.md, R10), under the operator's rule that every defect that forces an adopter workaround belongs in 3.2.0.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Shell expansion and link amendment (2026-10-18)/Shell expansions cannot hide a checkout from the guards

Shell expansions cannot hide a checkout from the guards

TSK-406complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Sources: the security reviews of PR 246 (TSK-377) on 2026-10-18, findings SEC-377-14, SEC-377-15 and SEC-377-16, and Grok 4.7's rounds 4 and 5 of the same PR, finding R4-1 and the round 5 git worktree move case. TSK-377's Closeout names this task as their owner before it had an ID. All are pre-existing: the released 3.1.0 binary also allows R4-1 and SEC-377-16, judged with the commands never executed. The Codex review of PR 255 (round 1) added the cd case and corrected the fail-before cases below.

Reproduced on the line at 236e9d08b with that tree's built hooks, payload cwd the main checkout and <w> a registered worktree under .worktrees/, the commands judged and never run. Each case names the guard that owns its route:

Route and owning guardAllowed today (fail-before case)Refused today (literal or preservation case)
interpreter argument, exec-guardpython3 tool.py $PWD/.worktrees/<w>, W=.worktrees/<w>; python3 tool.py $W, python3 tool.py "$(printf %s .worktrees/<w>)"python3 tool.py .worktrees/<w>; python3 tool.py $PWD/.claude/settings.json
interpreter code, exec-guardpython3 -c "import shutil; shutil.rmtree('$PWD/.worktrees/<w>')"; the same shutil.rmtree("$PWD/.worktrees/<w>") in an unquoted heredocpython3 -c "open('$PWD/.claude/settings.json','w')", the same open in an unquoted heredoc
static substitution, exec-guard (R4-1)node -e "$(printf %s 'require("fs").rmSync(".worktrees/<w>",{recursive:true,force:true})')"the same form naming .worktrees/<w>/.claude/settings.json
shell writer, git-guard (SEC-377-15)rm -rf $PWD/.worktrees/<w> with the hook process's PWD elsewhere; cd docs && rm -rf $PWD/../.worktrees/<w>rm -rf .worktrees/<w>; cd docs && rm -rf ../.worktrees/<w>
same-line worktree, git-guard (SEC-377-16)git worktree add -b t .worktrees/n && printf x > .worktrees/n/.claude/settings.jsonnone

The refused enforcement-file forms already refuse because exec-guard judges opaque and composed text against enforcement-path tails (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/arguments.rs:130-157); they stay as preservation tests. The checkout-root forms have no such fallback, which is the defect. git-guard has no interpreter route: exec-guard owns every interpreter refusal, and this task does not add one to git-guard.

The defects:

  • Interpreter arguments and code (SEC-377-14). The interpreter checks in crates/codeflow-core/src/security/outward.rs and security/interpreter.rs do not resolve shell variables for checkout reach: $PWD, ${PWD}, $(pwd), $HOME, an assignment earlier on the line, and the same words inside double-quoted interpreter code or an unquoted heredoc.
  • Static command substitution (Grok R4-1). A command substitution whose output is fixed by its literal text, such as $(printf %s '<code>'), hides the code body from the checkout check.
  • git-guard's $PWD (SEC-377-15). environment_value (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:4030-4047) reads PWD from the hook's own process environment. Replacing it with the payload cwd alone is not enough: after cd docs, the shell's $PWD is <checkout>/docs, so cd docs && rm -rf $PWD/../.worktrees/<w> reaches the worktree while the literal cd docs && rm -rf ../.worktrees/<w> already refuses.
  • A worktree made earlier on the line (SEC-377-16, Grok round 5). A path created by git worktree add <path> earlier in a command is not protected later in it, and git worktree move .worktrees/<w> <outside> && rm -rf <outside> also passes. Today git worktree add -b t .worktrees/n && git -C .worktrees/n status is refused by git-guard under git.policy_authority, because the new path does not exist when the line is judged; after this task it passes.

Outcome: a path the shell would expand to a checkout root or an enforcement file gets the verdict of the literal path, an expansion the guard cannot resolve is refused where a registered checkout or enforcement file is reachable, and a checkout created or moved earlier on a line is protected for the rest of it.

Two pieces of shell state are tracked at every command position and kept apart. The working directory starts at the payload cwd and changes only through cd, pushd and popd; every relative filesystem operand (a writer target, an interpreter argument, a link name or target) resolves from it. The PWD parameter starts equal to it and follows each successful cd, but it can also be assigned (PWD=/private/tmp), which changes what $PWD expands to and not where commands act. $PWD expands from the parameter; a relative path never resolves from an assigned PWD. Scope follows the shell: a brace group { ...; } runs in the current shell, so its cd and assignments reach the commands after it; a subshell ( ... ), a command substitution and a background job (&) keep their changes to themselves; a pipeline element runs in a subshell, except the last element where the shell runs it in the current shell (zsh, or Bash with lastpipe), and when the shell or that option is unknown the guard keeps both states. &&, ||, ; and newlines carry the state to the next command. Where the guard cannot know which state holds (a cd that may fail on an || branch, a cd to an unresolved word, CDPATH), it keeps every reachable state and judges the command against each. $HOME comes from the payload environment the guards already read. The directory set TSK-397 narrows after cd is the same working-directory state; whichever task lands second reuses the other's model.

Scope: assignments earlier on the line (plain and export), $PWD, ${PWD}, $(pwd), pwd , $HOME and ${HOME}, and static command substitutions such as $(printf %s '<literal>'), in interpreter argv, in double-quoted interpreter code and in unquoted heredoc bodies (exec-guard), and in shell writer targets (git-guard). A path named by git worktree add <path> (with or without -b, -B or --detach), and both the source and the destination of git worktree move <src> <dst>, are treated as registered checkouts for the rest of the command.

Interface with TSK-407: this task provides the expansion resolver (assignments, static substitutions, PWD and HOME as command-position state). TSK-407 depends on this task and reuses that resolver for link names and link targets; neither task carries a second resolver.

Residual, kept by the operator's decision of 2026-10-15 (workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md, the TSK-302 scope decision): a path built by interpreter code at run time (adjacent literals, +, chr(), formatting, encoding) stays a stated residual; the OS sandbox and the permission preset are the backstop. Quoted heredocs (<<'EOF') and single-quoted code are literal and keep their current verdict.

Non-goal: a full shell evaluator. A command substitution whose output depends on anything other than its literal text (a file read, another program's environment, a network call) is unresolved and is judged under the unresolved rule above.

Added by the second EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18, under the operator's release rule of that day that every security gap belongs in 3.2.0 (workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md, 2026-10-18 operator decision).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Release scope amendment (2026-10-18)/A link created earlier on a command line is refused like an existing link

A link created earlier on a command line is refused like an existing link

TSK-407todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: the security review of PR 239 (TSK-373) on 2026-10-18, severity medium, shipped in both guards. A link that already exists is followed and refuses, but a link created earlier on the same command line is not seen, because the guards judge the line before it runs and the link is not on disk yet. Reproduced on the line at 236e9d08b with that tree's built hooks, the commands judged and never run: git-guard and exec-guard both allow ln -s .claude/settings.json s2 && python3 tool.py s2, ln -s .claude/settings.json s2 && cp x s2 and ln -s .claude/settings.json s2 && printf x > s2, while exec-guard refuses python3 tool.py .claude/settings.json.

Decision: the residual is refused, not accepted. A link created earlier on the same line is part of the shell grammar the guards model (operator decision of 2026-10-15 on TSK-302's scope), so it is judged like an existing link. Decided by the primary on 2026-10-18 under the operator's direction of that day to decide from evidence (workspace RELEASE-PLAN.md, "Settled under it the same day", item 2).

Outcome: a writer or interpreter that names a link created, or possibly created, earlier on the same command line gets the verdict it would get if the link already existed, and a link whose target the guard cannot resolve is refused.

Rule: the guards model the filesystem state that earlier commands on the line produce, and resolve every later word through it.

  • Link-creating commands read: ln (symbolic or hard, with -s, -f, -n, -T and -t <dir>), link, and cp -s, cp -l, cp --symbolic-link and cp --link.
  • Names and targets: a link's name and target are resolved through TSK-406's expansion resolver (assignments, static substitutions, PWD and HOME as command-position state), so L=l; ln -s .worktrees/<w> "$L" creates l. This task owns expanded link names and targets and their propagation to later writers and interpreters; it reuses TSK-406's resolver and carries no second one.
  • Where the link lands: a relative link name resolves from the command's working directory, never from an assigned PWD parameter (TSK-406 keeps the two apart): after PWD=/private/tmp, ln -s .claude d still creates d in the checkout. For the last operand, a real directory and a symbolic link to a directory are treated differently. A real directory receives the link inside it under the target's base name, with or without -n (ln -sn ../.claude docs creates docs/.claude, whose target resolves to .claude). A symbolic link to a directory is followed the same way without -n (ln -s docs a && ln -sf ../.claude a creates docs/.claude); with -n it is treated as a plain name, so -f replaces it (ln -s docs a && ln -sfn .claude a makes a point at .claude) and without -f the command fails. -T never treats the operand as a directory: it replaces a file or symbolic link with -f, and against a real directory the command fails, because a directory cannot be replaced by a link. A link command can fail after creating some of its links: with several targets each operand is linked in turn, and a later operand's failure does not remove the links already made (ln -s ../.claude ../src docs, with docs/src present, creates docs/.claude and then fails). So the guard keeps every possible filesystem effect of a link command, including the links of the operands that succeed when the command as a whole fails, for every later word reached through &&, ||, ;, a newline or any other separator. Only a failure known to happen before any change creates nothing (a single-target -T against a real directory, a destination directory that does not exist); where the guard cannot tell, it keeps all the possible states. The same holds for ln -t <dir>, cp -s and cp -l with several sources. -t <dir> places each target in <dir>.
  • What a symbolic link points at: its target text is kept as written and resolved when a later word consumes it, relative to the link's own parent directory, not the command's directory (ln -s ../.claude docs/l points at .claude). Resolution walks component by component through the line's links and the disk, as the existing walk does for links on disk (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/edit_guard.rs:490-513). So a chain resolves through links created after the first one (ln -s a b && ln -s .claude a, then b/settings.json is .claude/settings.json). A hard link, cp -l or link, names the file its source resolves to when it is created.
  • Verdict: a later writer or interpreter word that resolves to an enforcement path or a checkout root refuses with the rule the target itself gets: git-guard owns shell writers (redirects, tee, copy and move destinations, in-place editors, rm), exec-guard owns interpreter arguments and code. A word whose resolution meets a cycle, more links than the OS follows, an unresolved expansion or glob in a link's name or target, or a path under a link the guard cannot read refuses as cannot-verify. A word that resolves to an ordinary path keeps its ordinary verdict, so ln -s src/app.py app.py && python3 app.py passes.
  • Order: "later" covers every list and pipeline separator (&&, ||, ;, |, &, newline), subshells, brace groups and command substitutions. Where a link may or may not exist (a link command on an || branch), every reachable state is judged. Filesystem changes made inside a subshell, brace group or command substitution persist for every later command; only the working directory and shell parameters are scoped, as TSK-406 defines.

The startup-file judgment already reads ln and cp -s or cp -l as link-creating commands (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/startup.rs:2848-2867, copy_judgment); this task reads the same commands for enforcement paths and checkout roots and carries the resulting state to the later words on the line.

The partial-failure behaviour was established by the Codex review of PR 255, round 3, with /bin/ln and GNU ln on a harmless temporary fixture (both returned 1 and left the first link in place); the hook verdicts below are judged strings, and no exploit was executed. Reproduced on the line at 236e9d08b (Codex review of PR 255, rounds 1 and 3, and the drafter), payload cwd the main checkout, the commands judged and never run, both guards allowing each case through cp -s and the named owning guard allowing each partial-failure case (judged by Codex round 3; the docs/src condition held only in its native fixture, not in the checkout the hooks judged): L=l; ln -s .worktrees/<w> "$L" && python3 tool.py l; ln -s a b && ln -s .claude a && printf x > b/settings.json; ln -s ../.claude docs/l && printf x > docs/l/settings.json; ln -s docs a && ln -sf ../.claude a && printf x > a/.claude/settings.json; ln -s docs a && ln -sfn .claude a && printf x > a/settings.json; ln -s .claude a && cp -s a b && printf x > b/settings.json; ln -s ../.claude ../src docs || printf x > docs/.claude/settings.json and the same line with ; (git-guard), and ln -s ../.claude ../src docs || python3 tool.py docs/.claude/settings.json (exec-guard). The ordinary controls ln -s src/app.py app.py && python3 app.py, L=l; ln -s src/main.rs "$L" && python3 tool.py l, ln -s a b && ln -s src a && printf x > b/new.txt and ln -s ../src docs/l && printf x > docs/l/new.txt pass today and must keep passing.

Non-goal: a link created by interpreter code (os.symlink, fs.symlinkSync) is runtime-built and stays the stated residual of the 2026-10-15 decision; the OS sandbox and the permission preset are the backstop. A link name or target written with a shell expansion is not that residual: it is in this task's scope.

Added by the second EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-18.

Widened on 2026-10-20 (EPC-022 amendment) by the primary under the operator's rule that every security gap belongs in 3.2.0, with finding F-HL of Grok 4.7's review of PR 260 (TSK-379) at 7156ae3ec, severity high, confirmed (.worktrees/tsk-379/target/review-TSK-379-grok-01.md). A hard link shares the inode of an enforcement file, so a write to the new name rewrites the original, and the guards see only the name. ln, cp -l and cp -al of .claude/settings.json or .git/config to a name outside the enforcement set are allowed today by both guards, whether the link already exists or the line creates it, and a later redirect, interpreter argument or native Write of that name is allowed by git-guard, exec-guard and edit-guard. The reviewer proved it on one volume in a scratch fixture, the original restored afterwards: a link of repo/.claude/settings.json to a name under the temporary directory (same inode), then printf PWNED > <name> passed both guards and the file held PWNED; a link of repo/.git/config, then an appended core.hooksPath line passed both guards, and a following git commit --allow-empty in the scratch repository honored the planted hooks path (the hook marker file held hooked). A link across volumes cannot share an inode, so the class is same-volume only; an in-repo destination on the checkout's volume always is.

The widening rule: a destination that shares device and inode with an enforcement file or a checkout's git pointer is a write of that file. It is judged twice: on the creating command (ln, cp -l, cp -al, link, and ln without -s, which AC-2 already lists for the same-line case), which refuses as a write of the source it links, and on every later write to the name, in a later command on the same line or in a later tool call, which the guards resolve through the filesystem (device and inode) to the file it is, before the path rule runs. A plain cp makes a new inode and stays allowed. Reading device and inode is one stat of the operand per judged word, so the cost is bounded by the words the guards already resolve. The same identity rule covers a startup-class file as a direct operand: a name that is a hard link of ~/.zshrc (tee notes, printf x > notes, with notes sharing that inode) is outside F1 of PR 264 below, which judged only the directory walk, and the enforcement-file wording above did not cover it, so it is added here as one spelled case: exec-guard, which owns the startup class, refuses the write as a write of the startup file, and the creating ln ~/.zshrc notes refuses as its link does today.

The same identity rule applies to a writer that walks a directory tree, added by the primary on 2026-10-20 from F1 of Grok 4.7's confirm review of PR 264 (TSK-380), round 2 at 1e1965723 (.worktrees/tsk-380/target/review-TSK-380-grok-02.md), severity major, confirmed live. rg --pre tee truncates every file it searches. The --pre root walk that PR 264 adds refuses a startup file name and a symbolic link that leaves the root (startup.rs, reaches_below, at that head), and git-guard refuses a root that is a path prefix of an enforcement file (preprocessor_write_violation at that head calling holds_enforcement_files, crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/edit_guard.rs:1125 on the line), but a regular file under the root that is a second name of a protected inode passes both: rg --pre tee needle <dir> with <dir>/notes a hard link of ~/.zshrc was allowed by both guards and the live run emptied the startup file; rg --pre tee needle docs with docs/alias.json a hard link of .claude/settings.json was allowed by both and emptied the settings file. A symbolic link in the same place is already refused. Requirement: in the rg --pre root walk (startup.rs, reaches_below, as PR 264 lands it) and in the native walk holds_enforcement_files (edit_guard.rs), a non-directory entry whose device and inode match a startup-class file or an enforcement file is treated as that file. Refusing every entry with a link count above one is the wrong test: ordinary files can be hard-linked, and the identity compare is exact. The scope is those two walks. The content a recursive copy or sync moves (cp -R, rsync, ditto) is TSK-408's judge, not this rule: a plain cp allocates a new inode and stays allowed, and no copy-source walk treats a matching inode as a write.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Release scope amendment (2026-10-18)/A recursive copy or sync is judged by the enforcement files it creates, replaces or deletes

A recursive copy or sync is judged by the enforcement files it creates, replaces or deletes

TSK-408todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: finding F6 of the cf-security-reviewer round 1 review of PR 260 (TSK-379) at 7156ae3ec, severity high, confirmed, predating that PR and outside its diff (.worktrees/tsk-379/target/review-TSK-379-security-01.md). It is a 3.2.0 security gap under the operator's release rule of 2026-10-18.

git-guard's copy judge reads a copy or sync by its destination path: the copies check (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:5296-5309) hands copy_destinations (:5388-5417) the destination, the sources as spelled and, for a copy into a directory, each source's base name inside it, and refuses when one of those words is an enforcement path. It never reads what the source tree holds, so a recursive copy whose source contains .claude/settings.json or a hook lands it on the checkout unjudged, and it never reads what a sync would delete under its destination. Allowed today by both hooks and by the base binary, the commands judged and never run except where the reviewer says so:

SpellingEffect in the reviewer's scratch run
cp -R /src/.claude .overwrote .claude/settings.json
cp -R /src/ .worktrees/wlands /src's .claude and .git content in a checkout
rsync -a /src/ ./the same onto the current checkout
ditto /src .the same
rsync -a --delete /empty/ .worktrees/w/deleted the worktree's settings and its .git pointer
rsync -a --remove-source-files .claude/ /dst/removes every file under .claude after copying it out
rsync -a --remove-source-files .git/hooks/ /dst/removes the hooks

F5 of the same review, the --remove-sent-files and --remove-source spellings of the last two, is repaired inside PR 260 and is not this task.

Outcome: a recursive copy or sync is refused when any file it would create, replace or delete under its destination is an enforcement file or a checkout's git pointer, and a copy or sync that touches none of them passes as it does today.

Rule: the guard judges the content a recursive copy or sync moves, not only the destination word.

  • Commands read: cp with -R, -r or -a, rsync (its archive and recursive forms, any option whose name starts with --delete plus --del, --remove-source-files and its aliases) and ditto, in every launcher and separator form the guards already read for cp, on both hooks: git-guard's copy judge (copies, above) and exec-guard's (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/startup.rs:2795-2807, ExecWriter::copies), which for a directory copy judges the source and destination words and does not read the tree either, so each F6 spelling passed both hooks.
  • What is judged: for each source, every path the command would write under the destination, mapped by the command's own rules (cp's copy into an existing directory under the source's base name, rsync's and ditto's trailing-slash rules); for a deleting sync, every path under the destination that the source lacks; for a source-removing sync, every source file. A path in that set that is an enforcement file, a .git file or directory of a registered checkout, or a checkout root refuses with the rule that file gets, and the message names the file and the source it comes from.
  • Reading the source: the guard reads the source tree on disk at judgment time, bounded by the same walk limit the repository reader uses (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/repo.rs). A source it cannot read (missing, unreadable, an unresolved expansion or glob, a remote host: or rsync:// spelling) or a walk past the bound refuses as cannot-verify, naming the source, when the destination is inside a checkout or the guard cannot tell. A destination outside every checkout and enforcement set keeps its ordinary verdict without reading the source.
  • Plain copies unchanged: a non-recursive cp of a single file keeps the destination-path verdict it has today. A copy whose destination is outside every checkout (cp -R .claude /scratch/backup) stays allowed; it writes nothing the guards protect, and TSK-407's hard-link rule covers the one case where a copy shares an inode with the original.

Non-goal: archive extraction (tar -x, unzip, git archive) whose member names are inside the archive and not on disk; it keeps the destination-path check and the OS sandbox as its backstop, and the builder records it as the residual in the policy reference. Modelling what a copied script does when run later is TSK-378's and TSK-406's ground, not this task's.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-20 under the operator's release rule of 2026-10-18 that every security gap belongs in 3.2.0.

Context

Issue #250. On 2026-10-18 an adopter's pre-push gate (CodeFlow 3.1.1, source 48104f48b) blocked a push with push set failed for: [empty] after the push set took 578.5 s against its 60 s budget on a machine with load averages of 20 to 33. Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/The commit-time secret scan can run the pinned gitleaks rules

The commit-time secret scan can run the pinned gitleaks rules

TSK-412complete

After this merges, a project that sets `git.secret_scan_engine.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a project that sets `git.secret_scan_engine: gitleaks` can have the pinned gitleaks rules refuse a staged match at commit time, and every project has the merges Git concludes itself scanned for secrets.

Context

Issue #251. The pre-commit hook scans the added lines of the staged diff with a fixed set of high-signal credential shapes (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_hook.rs:110-152 calls scan_staged, which runs crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/scan.rs scan_line). The managed CI secret scan runs gitleaks 8.30.1 with its default rules, which include the entropy-based generic-api-key. A match that only the CI rule sees is found after the commit exists and other work is built on it; the adopter's only fixes are a history rewrite or a permanent .gitleaksignore fingerprint, each needing a person's reviewed commit. In the reporting monorepo, 7 of 23 exemptions are one spec line that passes the hook on every edit, and a file's SHA-256 recorded under its path name cost two permanent exemptions. The adopter measured gitleaks git --staged at 0.03 s for an empty stage and 0.06 s for a merge commit's range, so a staged scan fits the pre-commit budget.

Outcome: a project can opt in to running the pinned gitleaks binary on the staged content at commit time, with the same rules and ignore files the managed CI scan reads, so a match is caught while it can still be reworded; the built-in patterns stay the floor, and at block a missing or mismatched binary fails closed.

Decisions recorded here:

  • Opt-in, not default. A new policy key (provisional name git.secret_scan_engine, values builtin and gitleaks, default builtin), placed by TSK-280's placement rule and read by the hook (TSK-363 refuses a key with no reader). The built-in scan runs in both settings; gitleaks adds the binary's verdict.
  • Same pins as CI. The hook runs the gitleaks version the managed workflow pins (assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml) and checks its checksum; at block, a binary that is missing, unpinned or mismatched refuses the commit and names codeflow doctor and the install route. At warn it warns once and runs the built-in scan.
  • Ignore files. The working tree's .gitleaksignore and .gitleaks.toml are read, as the only copies available before a commit exists; a commit cannot weaken CI, which reads them from the trusted base. The pull request records what a staged fingerprint looks like (the issue's open question) and documents that an existing commit-bound fingerprint never covers a staged finding, so a known false-positive file is allowlisted by path in .gitleaks.toml.
  • The scanner makes no network request. The hook never downloads the binary, and the scan and its gitleaks runner never fetch (a partial clone's missing object is a failed scan); codeflow doctor reports where it looked and the pinned version. The hook's policy-authority step may ask the configured remote once, as AC-5 (amended) states.

Non-goals: a local run of the full managed scan over a range (TSK-430 in EPC-024), the dependency audit, and making gitleaks the default.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-22 under the operator's release rule of 2026-10-18 (a defect that forces an adopter workaround belongs in 3.2.0).

Widened 2026-10-26 for issue #296 (CodeFlow 3.1.1; unchanged at this line's 0f08dd7f8). The staged secret scan never runs for an automatic merge commit: Git runs pre-merge-commit on that path and not pre-commit, and pre_merge_commit (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_hook.rs) checks protected branches and the root checkout only, so a merge driver that writes a key neither parent holds commits it. Git writes MERGE_HEAD after pre-merge-commit runs (git v2.54.0, builtin/merge.c:930 and :963), so the scan runs in commit-msg, which Git calls with MERGE_MSG for an automatic merge and with COMMIT_EDITMSG for plain and hand-concluded commits that already ran pre-commit. The built-in floor and, when chosen, the gitleaks engine both run there. This is a security gap in the default, so it rides with this task's scan work in 4.0.0 rather than waiting for the opt-in engine's users.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/An inline interpreter program's git calls are read by the language's grammar

An inline interpreter program's git calls are read by the language's grammar

TSK-413todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #253. exec-guard reads the source text of an inline python3 -c '...' program as if it were shell git arguments. In subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(source), "status"]) the guard takes the literal str as the -C repository path, fails to discover a repository at <cwd>/str, and refuses the whole command under git.policy_authority with the remedy "restore the command repository and its readable policy authority", which names no route that fits. The -C value is a Python expression evaluated at run time to a throwaway clone path. The adopter's workaround is to move the snippet into a file and run python3 -I -B <file>, which the guard does not read at all, so the current parse is both wrong in its explanation and easy to step around. Seen 2026-10-18 on CodeFlow 3.1.1 (48104f48b) in a Codex builder seat. The reader is the interpreter judge TSK-302 added (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/interpreter.rs); TSK-378 widens it to more interpreters and TSK-406 gives it the shell-expansion resolver.

Outcome: a git call inside an inline interpreter program is read by that language's grammar: a string literal operand gets the literal's verdict, any other expression is unresolved and is refused only where a checkout or enforcement file is reachable, and the refusal names the expression and the sanctioned route (a literal path, or a reviewed script file). The issue's command from a checkout is therefore still refused, with the right explanation; the guard never evaluates interpreter code to decide.

Rule: a -C, --git-dir, --work-tree or path operand of a git call in interpreter code is judged as a literal only when the language's grammar makes it one (a plain string literal, or a concatenation of literals); a name, call, f-string with a placeholder, or other expression is an unresolved word, judged by the same rule TSK-406 gives an unresolved shell expansion: refused where a checkout or enforcement file is reachable from the working directory, with the expression quoted in the message, and allowed otherwise. The refusal names git.policy_authority only when a literal path names a repository the guard cannot read.

Non-goals: reading a script file the interpreter is given (a stated residual of TSK-302, unchanged here); executing or evaluating interpreter code.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-22 under the operator's release rule of 2026-10-18 (a defect that blocks work belongs in 3.2.0).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/The sed judge reads quoted delimiters and judges only sed's own writes

The sed judge reads quoted delimiters and judges only sed's own writes

TSK-415todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #258, two cases on CodeFlow 3.1.1 (48104f48b), which already holds TSK-290's sed reader (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/sed_script.rs):

  • sed -i '' 's#b#c#' "$TMPDIR/sedprobe.md" is refused under git.hook_integrity as editing "repository enforcement files", while the same edit with / as the delimiter passes. The scratch file is outside any repository. The likely cause, not confirmed in source, is that # inside the quoted expression is read as a comment start, leaving the sed -i target unresolved and the rule failing closed.
  • sed -n "/## Closeout/,$ p" <record>; rg -n "..." DOC-INDEX.md; rg -n "mode|quick" .codeflow/project.toml, a read-only line, is refused with "sed takes a word the shell fills in, and the command line names the enforcement path .codeflow/project.toml" (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:4462). The $ is a sed address followed by a space, which the shell does not expand, and the enforcement path is an operand of a separate rg read. The check combines "some sed word is unresolved" with "an enforcement path appears anywhere on the line".

Outcome: git-guard refuses sed under git.hook_integrity only when a path sed itself could write (an -i target, or a w or W command or flag) resolves to a hook, policy or settings path; a quoted # or a $ that the shell does not expand is part of the argument, and a path named by another command on the line never counts against sed.

Rules:

  • The shell word reader keeps a # that is inside quotes, or not at the start of a word, as text; a $ followed by a space, a quote or the end of the word is text, not an expansion.
  • The unresolved-sed check judges only the words sed could write: the -i operands and the targets of w, W and the s///w flag, resolved by TSK-290's reader. A word the shell fills in among those stays refused where an enforcement file is reachable (TSK-406's rule). Another command's operands on the same line are judged by that command's judge alone.
  • The second case's sed -n with no -i and no w is a read and passes.

Non-goals: sed forms TSK-290 marks unproven (they stay refused), and the shell segmenter defects TSK-417 owns (newlines and braces inside quotes, variable tee paths).

Readiness and completion checks judge a line by the reference they report

TSK-416todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #262 and the 2026-10-22 comment on issue #278, the same cause in two commands. codeflow work claim reports readiness "on origin/<line>" (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/readiness.rs:1236) but checks a dependency's research pin against target_reference(repo, &line) with the dependency's bare integration_target, and target_reference_names (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:3039-3058) tries refs/heads/<target> before refs/remotes/origin/<target>, so a stale local branch of the line decides readiness and refuses a pin that is on origin's tip. codeflow task status <id> complete judges a waiver's planning commit "on the target" the same way: with local main stale at a commit before the planning pull request merged, completion refused "waiver names <planning sha>, which is not on the target" although origin/main held it. In both cases the agent cannot repair the local branch: git fetch origin <line>:<line> is refused by git-guard as a policy-authority change, and fast-forwarding a protected local main is refused by git.merge_to_protected, so a person has to update the checkout. TSK-398 fixed the same local-first lookup for codeflow ci and pre-push anchors only (cmd/ci.rs).

Outcome: every readiness and completion check that reports a reference judges against that reference: a bare target resolves to the remote-tracking ref when the remote has it, a local branch of the same name never decides, and when only a local branch exists the message says which reference was read.

Rule: target_reference_names for a bare name tries refs/remotes/origin/<target> first and refs/heads/<target> only when the remote-tracking ref is absent, and every caller that reports a reference prints the one it resolved. Callers found by a search of target_reference and target_reference_names are each covered by a test. The fetch work claim performs stays; it updates the remote-tracking ref the check now reads.

Non-goals: moving a local branch for the user; the chain semantics TSK-341 decides; the reopened-task waiver rule TSK-340 now carries (the body of #278).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/The shell reader keeps a quoted argument whole across newlines and braces

The shell reader keeps a quoted argument whole across newlines and braces

TSK-417todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #273 and its comment, on CodeFlow 3.1.1 (48104f48b) with the Claude Code Bash tool. git-guard refuses L=/private/tmp/scratch; echo x | tee $L/probe5.log; python3 -I -c "\nprint(1)\n" under git.hook_integrity, naming the later quoted Python text as part of the tee target ("targets the integrity path the registered worktree <worktree>/ (through print(1))"). The same line with a literal tee path, tee $L/x.log alone, or a quoted string with no newline each pass. With braces in the quoted text the refusal shows the text brace-expanded, or says "a brace expansion too large to read" (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:2091). The reader appears to split the command into lines, or brace-expand it, before it accounts for quoting, so a later quoted argument attaches to the unresolved variable path. The comment adds a message defect: a list that combines a sed -i on a variable path with grep -c -E '^[0-9a-f]{64} l1' $R is refused (expected, for the sed -i), but the message names the quoted regex quantifier {64} as an enforcement path and claims a directory read of more than 4096 entries.

Outcome: inside quotes, a newline and a brace are part of one argument: they never end a command, change another command's target or expand; a tee to a path assigned earlier on the line resolves as it does when no multi-line string follows; and a refusal names the operand that caused it, never a quoted pattern from another command.

Rules:

  • The segmenter reads quoting before it splits on newlines or expands braces: a newline or {...} inside single or double quotes is text. An unquoted newline ends a command as today.
  • Brace expansion applies to unquoted words only, and a quoted word whose text contains a brace is never read as a path glob or counted against the directory-entry limit.
  • A refusal under git.hook_integrity names the writing command and the operand the judgment rests on (here sed -i $R), with the unresolved-word reason TSK-406 states; other commands' quoted arguments on the line do not appear in it.

Non-goals: the sed delimiter and address cases (TSK-415); making an unresolved sed -i target pass (it stays refused where an enforcement file is reachable).

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-22 under the operator's release rule of 2026-10-18 (a defect that blocks work belongs in 3.2.0).

Widened 2026-10-26 for issue #342 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). git-guard refused a read-only cd <worktree> && grep -c -e ... -e "externally_modified\") is True:" ... -e "ord(c) > 127" ... /dev/null under git.hook_integrity, saying "redirect would overwrite the integrity path repository enforcement files". The only > is inside a double-quoted pattern, after an escaped \" in an earlier pattern. The issue's exact line is refused by the installed 3.1.0 binary in this repository and allowed by the line's binary at 0f08dd7f8, where TSK-380 (search patterns are never write targets) and TSK-406 have landed. AC-7 pins the line as a regression test and adds the message rule the issue asks for: a line whose quoting the reader cannot settle is refused as unparseable, never as a named redirect. The issue's comment of 2026-10-26 (a |-delimited sed -i program) still fails at 0f08dd7f8 and is the sed reader's case, TSK-415 AC-7.
