Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/A records-only editorial change lands wording changes to many closed records

A records-only editorial change lands wording changes to many closed records

TSK-418todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #277. A full-tier project adopted a rule that tracked content must not name internal sessions or local paths, and must rewrite that wording across closed task and epic records while keeping every criterion id, tag, status, criterion outcome and reviewed commit. codeflow ci 3.1.1 refuses the edit in every pull request shape: a records-only PR naming the cleanup task (37 work.acceptance_binding, 24 work.criteria_frozen, 7 work.records), a plan/ branch naming the open epics (binding, amendment and records refusals remain), one PR per completed standalone task under ADR-0080 (criteria text only, 64 PRs), and a cancelled epic, which Task: cannot name. The issue cites each rule's source lines at 48104f48b and shows that the binding refusal depends on unrelated history after the landing, not on the edit. ADR-0084 on this line (TSK-278) covers one task record per PR and only its criteria and acceptance blocks, with the review field frozen. The project leaves closed records unchanged and registers the workaround.

Outcome: one reviewed pull request can change only the wording of any number of closed task and epic records, across epics, standalone tasks and cancelled epics, while codeflow ci proves that every status, criterion id, tag, criterion outcome, reviewed commit, waiver commit and superseded-block count is unchanged and prints a per-record wording delta for the reviewer; such a record is not rebound, not read as reopened and not judged as a criteria change.

Decisions recorded here, from the issue's suggested fix:

  • Class. A planning-records-only range on a plan/ branch whose body declares the class with one Records: editorial line beside Task: TSK-NNN, the cleanup task, so the Task: line keeps one meaning. The cleanup task is an ordinary task (standalone or in an epic) whose own record may be in the range.
  • What CI proves per changed record, against the merge-base copy: same path, kind and status; frontmatter identical except the annotation ADR-0084 defines; same criteria ids, order and tags; same number of active and superseded acceptance blocks; in each block the same reviewed, every criterion outcome, every waiver sha, the journey outcome and the verdict. Prose sections, criteria text, block evidence and notes text, a superseded block's reason and - reopened: lines may change. A review field may change only when the pull request records the original as ADR-0084's digest does.
  • Exemptions. A record that passes these checks is not rebound, not read as reopened and not judged under work.criteria_frozen; each prints a wording delta as a note. A record that fails any check gets today's refusal, naming the field that changed.
  • Remedy text. The waiver clause leaves the binding remedy unless the refused block holds a waived result, and a wording edit is pointed at this class.
  • The decision extends ADR-0084 and is recorded as a new ADR drafted in this task's PR (Tier-3: a CI class that exempts closed records from three checks).

Non-goals: changing any result or outcome through this class; the single-record redaction of ADR-0084 (unchanged); cancelling or reopening a task.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-22 under the operator's decisions of 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-22 (an adopter workaround, and a project-management change, belong in 3.2.0).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/Epics are sized to one value line and built one at a time per stream

Epics are sized to one value line and built one at a time per stream

TSK-419todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #280, items 1 and 4 and the comment of 2026-10-22. A full-tier project on 3.1.1 runs 17 integration lines; several epics hold 22 to 69 tasks, and after three weeks almost no product work has reached main, because an epic finishes only when all of its tasks finish and each work stream held several open epics at once. cf-method "Planning an epic" warrants an epic by the standalone test and names no size; cf-plan step 5 partitions tasks by outcome and dependency. Nothing says how small an epic should be, when to open the pull request to main, or how many epics a stream builds at once.

Outcome: the managed guidance says an epic is the smallest set of tasks that gives a reviewer something usable on main, stated as one value line ("after this merges, X can do Y"); an epic that will not fit that line is planned as two or more epics with their merge order; the pull request to main opens when a usable set of finished tasks is ready, with unfinished user-facing work switched off; and a work stream builds one epic at a time to completion.

Rules the guidance states, each in plain words with an example:

  • The value line. cf-plan and the epic template ask for one value line in the epic's ## Outcome section (TSK-435); cf-method "Planning an epic" adds it to the clarity checklist. Size numbers, where given, are an orientation range, never a cap ("Only the operator adds process").
  • Split, with merge order. A brief whose outcome needs more than one value line becomes two or more epics; the plan names which merges first and the edge between them.
  • Early pull request to main. Open it when a usable set of finished tasks is ready, not only when the epic is done; unfinished user-facing work stays off on main behind a flag, a disabled default or an unwired entry point, named in the PR, so a partial merge never shows half-built work. The epic's remaining tasks continue on the line. The precondition is TSK-433: until it lands, codeflow ci judges a line's own reopened and amended completions as foreign in a pull request into main (18 blocking findings on the 3.2.0 line head 29a217556), so the guidance names TSK-433's class and this task is dispatched after it lands.
  • One epic at a time per stream. A stream builds one epic to completion (all tasks landed, closed, PR to main); the next epic's planning and reviews may run alongside, and the next build starts only while the current epic waits on something outside the stream. The managed map's "shape a request" and "land a batch" rows carry the rule.

Non-goals: a cap on epic size; a status view of streams (TSK-420 shows line drift; the per-stream view is TSK-311's in 4.1.0); changing how epics close.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-22 under the operator's decision of that day (project-management changes go in 3.2.0). This amendment applies the rule to EPC-024.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/orient reports each integration line's drift from main

orient reports each integration line's drift from main

TSK-420complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #280, item 2. In the reporting project, integration lines sit 12 to 1,201 commits behind main; a change on main stays missing on every line until someone syncs each one by hand, and nothing shows which lines have drifted. codeflow orient prints the session digest (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/orient.rs, crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/orient.rs) with branch, worktree and work counts and no line view; the program report that would show every fetched line (#166, TSK-311) is 4.1.0 work.

Outcome: codeflow orient and the SessionStart digest show, for each integration line the remote advertises, how many commits it is behind the protected target, when the target was last merged into it, and the age of its oldest unlanded task, and flag a line that has gone longer than a project-set interval without a sync.

Rules:

  • The lines are the remote-tracking integration/* refs as last fetched, because orient is a read command and never fetches (SPC-013 R-103); with no remote or no fetched integration refs, the local lines, marked as local.
  • "Behind" is git rev-list --count <line>..<target>. The line's own commits are its first-parent chain down to, and excluding, the merge base with the target; commits at or below the merge base are inherited and never count as the line's events. A sync event is an own merge commit whose other parent is on the target; "last sync" is the newest such event by its commit date (the date the merge was made, not the merged tip's age). The line's creation is reported only from real evidence of the ref's creation (the remote's branch creation record where the provider gives one, or the local reflog entry that created the ref); without it, creation is unknown. The oldest own commit may be shown, labelled oldest divergent commit, as the historical fact it is, and never stands for creation: a line named today over month-old divergent history has an old divergent commit and an unknown creation. A line with no own commit shows fresh, no own commits. A line whose creation is unknown and that has no sync event gets no time-based flag. A timestamp alone establishes neither a ref's creation nor a sync event; the commit date is read only for a sync merge identified independently by its parents. "Oldest unlanded task" is the earliest created among the line's tasks whose records on the line are not terminal.
  • The interval is a policy key (provisional git.line_sync_interval, placed by TSK-280's rule, read by orient, default off) ; past it the line is flagged with the sync route TSK-421 names.
  • The facts are exposed through one reader the sync route (TSK-421) and the program report (TSK-311) reuse; the view stays read-only.
  • Streams are the coordination ledger's WS-NNN (EPC-025, TSK-439); this view does not read the ledger and lists epics only.

Non-goals: syncing or closing a line (TSK-421); the program report's per-record view (TSK-311, which reuses this reader for its line rows).

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-22 under the operator's decision of that day (project-management changes go in 3.2.0).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/A line is synced from main and closed by one checked route each

A line is synced from main and closed by one checked route each

TSK-421todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #280, items 3 and 5. Syncing a line from main is a hand-run merge today (cf-method "Managing a body of work", drift control); each sync trips record checks that judge main's completed tasks again (#176, #181, #197, #217, #218, #240, owned by TSK-306, TSK-339 and TSK-340), and a sync that carries a .github/workflows/ change needs a person to push it, because the guards refuse agent writes there (TSK-325). Nothing closes a line: a dormant or empty line keeps collecting drift.

Outcome: one command merges the protected target into a line, runs the line's pre-push gate, and reports which merged paths a person must push, and is safe to run whenever the target changes; and one command closes a line after checking that nothing on it is unlanded, recording the closure.

Rules:

  • Sync (provisional codeflow line sync <line>): fetches, merges origin/<target> into the line's checkout in a linked worktree with a no-fast-forward merge, refuses on a conflict naming the files, runs the quick gate through the same path the pre-push hook uses, and reports the merged paths under .github/workflows/ and other person-pushed paths with the exact push a person runs. With no such paths it pushes the line as a durability push. A sync that lands no new commits is a no-op that says so. A clean sync produces a range codeflow ci and the pre-push hook accept without a waiver, which is what TSK-339 and TSK-340 deliver; this task adds the fixture that proves it on the sync route and returns any remaining re-judge to the plan as a finding. The epic or checkpoint pull request the synced line then opens into main is judged as TSK-433 states.
  • Close (provisional codeflow line close <line>): refuses while any task whose integration_target is the line is not terminal, any pushed task branch targets the line with a tip not on it, or the line holds commits not on the target; otherwise writes the closure (date, final tip, the epic's PR to main where one exists) into the epic record's planning notes through a planning commit on the target, and lists the branch deletion TSK-402's cleanup rule then allows. It never deletes the branch itself.
  • Both are agent-runnable under the guards: they use the sanctioned fetch, merge and push forms and never touch a protected branch.

Non-goals: deleting branches (TSK-402's cleanup rule); carrying one task's landed change to another line (TSK-402); the drift view (TSK-420).

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-22 under the operator's decision of that day (project-management changes go in 3.2.0).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/The epic line's pull request into main judges the line's own completions as its own

The epic line's pull request into main judges the line's own completions as its own

TSK-433complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Found by the primary on 2026-10-22 while rehearsing the 3.2.0 release pull request. codeflow ci --base origin/main --head 29a217556 --branch integration/EPC-022-the-3-2-0-milestone-fixes --into main, run with the binary built at the line's tree, gives 18 blocking findings, all work.acceptance_binding, two for each of nine tasks that were reopened and amended on the line (TSK-275, TSK-276, TSK-278, TSK-280, TSK-304, TSK-305, TSK-306, TSK-307 and TSK-352):

  • "refs/remotes/origin/integration/EPC-022-the-3-2-0-milestone-fixes (commit 29a217556) records a completion of this task, but it is not the target this run is judged against, so its criteria stay as they were" (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/landing.rs:129);
  • "a reopened task keeps its criteria as the anchored target has them; change them in the epic's batched amendment, a planning pull request on the target" (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:2795, REOPENED_CRITERIA).

When the epic line itself is the head of a pull request into main, the anchored target is main, so the line's own landed completions and the planning amendments that changed those tasks' criteria on the line are judged as foreign: the line is the home that TSK-339 says a completion is judged at, but here it is also the head. Every epic pull request to main, and every early checkpoint pull request (issue #280 item 4, TSK-419), fails the same way, so the release pull request itself is blocked. No open task owns this direction: TSK-339 judges a completion imported into a receiving line at its proven home, TSK-306 settles competing record versions at unordered judged points, TSK-340 settles the reopened completion sequence, and TSK-308 counts adopted direct commits; none of their criteria names the line-into-target pull request.

Outcome: when a pull request's head is an integration line and its target is the protected branch, codeflow ci judges each task whose integration_target is that line against the line's own history: a completion landed on the line is bound at its line landing, criteria amended by a planning amendment on the line are the task's criteria, and a reopen and re-completion on the line is one valid sequence; and codeflow ci for the EPC-022 line's pull request into main is clean on the line head.

Rules:

  • The pull request class is the epic PR (Task: EPC-NNN, head an integration/ line, target the protected branch). For it, the anchored target for a task whose integration_target is the line is the line head, with main as the base of the range; a task whose target is main keeps today's judgment.
  • The line's authority is proven the way TSK-339 proves a home: the completion's landing merge on the line, the reviewed commit on the line, and the planning amendments on the line, each through the guarded history reader. A task whose line history cannot be read, or whose record on the line differs from the record at the head, stays refused.
  • A checkpoint pull request from the line to main before the epic closes (TSK-419) is the same class and gets the same judgment.
  • An epic line that joined the judged line, whose tip the range head contains and which passes the epic-line proof itself, is judged the same way for the tasks that declare it (amended 2026-10-28: route A joined the EPC-025 line into this line through TSK-1000). A joined line that fails the proof keeps today's refusal.

Non-goals: changing how a task pull request into the line is judged; waiving any task's binding; closing the epic.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-22 under the operator's release rule of 2026-10-18 (a defect that blocks work belongs in 3.2.0). It must land before the epic's pull request to main is opened.

Widened 2026-10-26 for issues #320 and #341, both from one adopter's codeflow ci --into main runs on an integration line (CodeFlow 3.1.1). An integration branch can be deleted only after it is merged

TSK-434todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Operator decision of 2026-10-22: agents should be able to delete an integration branch, but only after it is merged. Today codeflow hook git-guard allows git push origin --delete integration/EPC-099-test (exit 0) with no merge check, and the pre-push hook's deletion rule covers protected refs only (git.delete_protected, crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:8681-8688 and git_hook.rs:890-895); the only thing that stops the deletion is the deletion rule in GitHub's "Integration hosted gates" ruleset, a remote setting outside the guards. The cleanup rule TSK-402 widens is instruction text (worktrees.md), not enforcement, and TSK-421's line close lists a deletion without performing it.

Outcome: git-guard and the pre-push hook refuse deleting a remote or local integration/ branch unless the branch is fully contained in its target, there is no open pull request from or into it, and it is not a protected branch; a refusal names the missing proof, an allowed deletion names the proof it checked, and protected branches and release tags stay refused.

Rules:

  • Containment is ancestry on the fetched target: the branch tip is an ancestor of origin/<target>, where the target is the epic's protected branch (main) for an epic line, read from the epic record or, with none, the repository's default branch. A target the guard cannot fetch or read is a missing proof.
  • No open pull request from or into the branch, read through the remote provider where one is configured (codeflow remote); where the provider cannot be asked, the proof is missing and the deletion refuses, naming the route (ask a person, or configure the provider).
  • Protected branches and release tags (main, master, the policy globs, and tags the release policy names) keep today's git.delete_protected refusal whatever the proofs say.
  • The same judgment covers git push --delete, git push :<ref>, git branch -d/-D of a local integration/ branch and the refs/ spellings, on git-guard (the Claude, Codex and Grok planes) and on the pre-push hook; the message lists each proof with its result.
  • Once this task lands and is reviewed, the operator removes the deletion rule from the GitHub "Integration hosted gates" ruleset; that ruleset change stays the operator's and is not part of this task.

Non-goals: deleting task branches (TSK-402's cleanup rule and TSK-319 in 4.1.0); closing a line's records (TSK-421).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/Records state their Outcome and epics their Deliverables

Records state their Outcome and epics their Deliverables

TSK-435complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Operator decision of 2026-10-22, part of the issue #280 work: an explicit Outcome on records, and Deliverables on epics. Issue 280 asks that an epic state one value line ("after this merges, X can do Y"); today the task template has no home for it (records put an "Outcome:" sentence in the Description by convention), the epic template has no Deliverables section, and codeflow validate --docs checks a task's Deliverables (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/record_text.rs:581-596) but no Outcome anywhere.

Outcome: after this lands, a task or epic record created with the templates carries an ## Outcome section with one line saying what someone can do once it lands, an epic carries a ## Deliverables section like a task's, codeflow validate --docs requires the Outcome section on records created after the change, and existing records stay valid: closed records are never changed or flagged, and an open record created before the change gets a warning, not a refusal, and gains the section when next amended.

Rules:

  • Templates. assets/base/pm/task.md.tmpl and epic.md.tmpl gain ## Outcome (one line, in the form "after this merges, X can do Y") between the Description and the Deliverables; epic.md.tmpl gains ## Deliverables with the task template's comment. codeflow task new and epic new write both.
  • Validation, adoption-aware. The compatibility boundary is the project's own adoption of this release, identified by record identity, never by a calendar date: when codeflow update first brings a release that has the section, it writes the adoption marker into the project's configuration (provisional records.outcome_required_since in .codeflow/project.toml) with the adoption commit (the project's HEAD at that update) and the uid of every task and epic record present in the working tree at that moment, committed or not. A record is "present at adoption" when its uid is in that list; every other record is "later". A later non-terminal record whose Outcome section is missing or empty is refused by validate --docs; a present-at-adoption record without it gets a warning naming the section and gains the section when next amended, whatever its created date, so a record made with the old release the morning of a same-day upgrade stays valid; a record whose status is terminal (complete, cancelled, archived) is never flagged. A fresh codeflow init writes the marker with an empty list, so every record of a new project needs the section. With no marker (a project updated by hand, or one that has not yet run codeflow update), every missing section warns and nothing refuses, and codeflow doctor says the marker is missing and how update writes it.
  • Compatibility. No existing record is edited by this task; the "Outcome:" sentence convention in Descriptions stays valid for old records.
  • Guidance. cf-plan and cf-method "Planning an epic" name the section as the home of the value line; TSK-419's sizing guidance points at it, so TSK-419 depends on this task.

Non-goals: rewording existing records (TSK-418's class covers that when a project wants it); any new field in frontmatter.

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-22 at the operator's direction of that day.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/A task criterion can record a deferred result proved after merge

A task criterion can record a deferred result proved after merge

TSK-436todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #287. A task's acceptance block accepts only verified or waived per criterion; deferred exists only for an epic's after-release criteria (cf-method/references/project-organization.md, the deferred | owner; window; follow-up form, read by crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/record_text.rs:1533-1546), and a waived result needs a planning amendment of that criterion inside the reviewed commit. Some criteria can only be proved after the merge: an adopter's dependency-admission check runs as pull_request_target, so the base's checker judges the head's data and a pull request that adds a new exception kind cannot go green until it is merged; the first push scan of main after the merge is the real proof. The author must reword the criterion to match local evidence, or the maintainer merges on known reds with no record that a check is owed.

Outcome: a task's acceptance block can record a criterion as deferred, naming the event that will prove it, who checks it and a follow-up, with no planning amendment because the criterion does not change; codeflow ci and orient show the owed follow-up until someone records the result as verified, or as failed with a linked task.

Rules:

  • Form. The task result reuses the epic form: AC-n: deferred | event: <the proving event>; owner: <who checks>; follow-up: <TSK-NNN or another permitted durable record, an epic criterion or a feedback item>. The event is free text, the owner a role or seat, the follow-up a tracked record that exists in the repository. A tracked record never cites a coordination ledger id (FU-NNN, LN-NNN, WS-NNN): the ledger is clone-local and absent in CI (ADR-0086), so a ledger item may link outward to the task's deferred criterion, and the durable reference stays in the record.
  • Binding. A deferred result binds like a verified one: the task can complete and land, and the block names the reviewed commit. The task stays complete; the deferred criteria are listed in the task's Closeout as owed.
  • Resolution. codeflow task status <id> defer-resolve AC-n --verified <evidence> or --failed --task TSK-NNN (provisional verb) appends the result under the block as a dated line, a records-only change codeflow ci accepts in a planning amendment or a task PR, judged like the amendment note of SPC-013 R-50. A failed result must link an open task.
  • Surfacing. codeflow ci prints each owed deferred result of the tasks in its range as a note, and orient lists every owed deferred result of the project with its event and owner, from the records alone; neither blocks and neither reads the ledger.
  • An epic closes only when every deferred task result is resolved, or the epic's own block defers the criterion as today.

Non-goals: changing waived; deferring a journey criterion; a hosted check that records the result by itself.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Open issues and project-management amendment (2026-10-22)/Each seat reaches only its own lane's sockets and never the container runtime

Each seat reaches only its own lane's sockets and never the container runtime

TSK-437todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #286, item 1. Parallel lanes each run local helper services (a browser automation server, a dev database, a preview server), and anything that can connect to a lane's service can act through it; a browser server can read files the browser reaches and take raw DevTools commands. Every seat, hook and tool runs as one OS user who also owns the container runtime socket, so a project cannot keep one lane away from another's service by changing the service alone. The shipped postures set dangerously_allow_all_unix_sockets = false for cf-guard and cf-builder (assets/base/codex/config.toml:205, :242) with no per-seat allowance, and the Claude presets carry no allowUnixSockets list; the container runtime socket is not denied by name on any plane. Two research passes agreed the criterion "no other process under the same host user may connect" cannot be met on a single-user host; this task delivers what the seat postures can.

Outcome: a seat's sandbox can be given access to its own lane's unix sockets only, through a documented and tested per-seat launch override (Codex unix_sockets rules, Claude allowUnixSockets), and every seat denies the container runtime socket by default, with unsandboxed retries off for a seat that holds a socket allowance.

Criteria to establish first, recorded in the task's pull request (the issue's "not verified" items): whether a per-lane Codex unix_sockets rule works as a launch override on the supported release, and Claude's allowUnixSockets default and merge behaviour on macOS. Each AC below states what the answer changes.

Non-goals: the optional supervisor and the separate-account guidance (TSK-438 in EPC-024); the services themselves, which stay the project's (unix socket, peer credentials, per-run secret).

Added by the EPC-022 amendment of 2026-10-22 under the operator's rule of 2026-10-18 (a security gap in the seat postures CodeFlow owns).

not recorded

Context

Operator decision of 2026-10-22. In a project that uses CodeFlow, explaining something visually defaults to cf-present; the harness's own artifact (a Claude Artifact page, an inline widget) is used only when the operator asks for it or the content must be shared, since cf-present is local and cannot be shared. Today the managed instructions say the opposite: the "show something complex" row of the Claude harness table (assets/base/CLAUDE.md.tmpl:44, installed as CLAUDE.md:45), the managed-block row of the same name (assets/base/AGENTS.md.tmpl:75) and .codeflow/rules/writing.md "Figures by surface" (assets/base/rules/writing.md:147) send a page people will comment on or share to the harness's page publisher, and the cf-present skill trigger describes it as a review surface for when one materially helps.

Outcome: in a CodeFlow project, a figure or explanation that needs more than an inline reply goes to cf-present by default, and the harness's artifact or widget is the stated exception, used when the operator asks for it or the content must be shared; every home that says otherwise is changed, with its asset sources, managed mirrors and the skill trigger.

Rules the text states: an inline figure in the reply stays the default where the surface renders one and the answer is short; beyond that, cf-present; the harness page or widget only on the operator's ask or for sharing; fenced ASCII in Markdown files, records, PR bodies and terminals; never Mermaid. The exception is stated in each home in one sentence so a reader cannot take the harness page as an equal option.

Amended 2026-10-23: the outcome also covers the review-session lifecycle of the present runtime, from the operator's incident of that day on macOS: an End review control, a plain window close that keeps the session while the isolated browser quits after a short grace, and codeflow present show reopening a window in a running browser. These are runtime and CLI code in crates/codeflow-present/ and crates/codeflow-cli/ with real-browser tests, so the work is code and not instructions only (AC-6 to AC-8).

Non-goals: the Comment, figure and tabs runtime fixes (TSK-443), the design direction (TSK-444), the skill method (TSK-445) and the docs portal (TSK-446). This task first carried all five outcomes; the operator had them restructured on 2026-10-22 into one task each, and this id keeps the default-surface outcome.

Operator direction of 2026-10-22. The operator reports that cf-present figures look monochrome: tokens.json gives each of the six skins (Graphite, Slate and Sage, light and dark) grey ink plus accent, warn and stop only, and the grammar maps most marks to grey, so a figure with no governing path renders nearly grey. The operator's renders also show an inverted type scale: comparison column titles and the decision title render larger than a ### section heading and about as large as ## , so options outrank the section that contains them; and the document summary is shown only by present list, never on the page. Figures may use the existing colours or added ones that harmonise with them; there is no hard restriction, but the result must show strong aesthetic judgment, elegant and coherent across the three skins in light and dark, and taste is the operator's.

Outcome: a cf-design pass led by the Claude design primary settles, from options shown to the operator as rendered pages, the page anatomy (document title and summary at the top, the anchor, a section heading with its lead, the figure sheet), one type scale in which the document title is larger than a section, a section than a subsection, and a subsection than a block title, and the figure colour (the governing path in accent-bearing marks, and whether harmonious category hues are added per skin and mode), across Graphite, Slate and Sage in light and dark; the operator signs off on the direction and a fresh-context design reviewer checks the result against it (operator decision, 2026-10-24); and the tokens, the present styles (header, hierarchy) and the portal token sheet change together with the palette drift test.

Push and CI gates stop rerunning unchanged work

TSK-449complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

The push and hosted CI rerun checks on unchanged work. Pre-push runs codeflow validate --docs and every quick target at HEAD on each push (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs:235-237), the git rules ask for a durability push after every unit, and no target declares input_class, so the skip in crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/delivery.rs:559-566 never fires; run_everything includes *.md. Hosted CI builds the release binary in six jobs, reruns fmt, clippy, rustdoc and doctests on Windows, and fails the verdict jobs on purpose for a draft to integration/ (.github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml:109, 445, 727). Source: the operator approved process audit of 2026-10-23 (line numbers at c9993bcf3).

Scope: (1) pre-push keeps codeflow ci, the conflict check and the secret scan; validate --docs (already run by codeflow ci as work.valid_graph) and the quick targets leave it, and the quick gate is cited in the PR Testing section when the PR is made ready. (2) The input declarations (input_class, narrower run_everything, per-target inputs) belong to open TSK-353, not this task: reuse stays conditional on complete matching check identity from a qualifying run, and documentation-reading targets such as docs-validation keep running on docs edits. This task adds only the pre-push and tier changes. (3) prose-exhaustive, read-benchmark, present-browser and present-binary-delta move from the landing-candidate full gate to the weekly schedule and the release candidate. (4) The release binary is built once per workflow. (5) Windows drops fmt only. (6) Draft PRs get a neutral verdict and ready_for_review runs the exact head. (7) The shipped template runs essential on PRs and full on the protected branch and schedule.

Dispatch contract: TSK-449 depends on TSK-331 (it removes the quick targets from pre-push after TSK-331's heavy-work admission and pre-push wait criteria have landed, and amends those pre-push criteria as moot in its PR). The Testing-citation check at ready is TSK-451's (AC-8). The shipped template's dependency-audit step is TSK-450's; this task owns the rest of assets/base/ci/. push_set.rs is this task's alone; the release-impact preflight call there stays unchanged because the evaluator interface does not change (TSK-451).

Non-goals: the full gate on the landing candidate, its lock, the coverage floor, the secret scan, gitleaks, the trusted codeflow ci job and the human merge are unchanged. Risk: a neutral or skipped check passes a required-check rule, so a ready PR needs its run at the exact head (AC-6). This task owns the test_gate_on_push entry (its meaning changes with (1)) in both policy files and its row in docs/policy-reference.md; TSK-450 owns every other line.

Effect on adopting projects: shipped hooks stop running the test gate on push (a push is backup, not a gate); the shipped workflow runs essential on PRs and full on the protected branch and schedule; a project that relied on the pre-push gate runs codeflow test --mode quick itself.

Owned files: push_set.rs, the pre-push stage of crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/git_hook.rs and crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_hook.rs, testing/delivery.rs, .codeflow/test-config.json, assets/base/testing/, .github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml (all but the dependency-audit step of the security review job, which TSK-450 owns), .github/workflows/codeflow-policy.yml, assets/base/ci/ (except the dependency-audit step, TSK-450), scripts/gate-parity.py, scripts/ci-reuse.py. Guidance that tells builders to cite the quick gate is TSK-452.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Process cuts amendment (2026-10-23)/Commit and PR style rules warn and the audit weighs severity

Commit and PR style rules warn and the audit weighs severity

TSK-450todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Style rules and the dependency audit cost retries and stalls without protecting a boundary. The description limit, body shape and count, unlisted trailers, en and em dashes and the PR Summary shape refuse commits and PR edits (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/standards.rs:172-200, 266-350, 546-590; crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/pr_body.rs:1160-1270); only the type, the breaking marker and the subject length feed a machine. The dependency audit fails the security review job on any advisory with no severity threshold (.github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml:1372-1485); a medium advisory in a dev lockfile and the tokio advisory each stopped every PR. Seven policy keys (security.script_bypass, interpreter_scan, enforcement_baseline, workflow_pushes, sandbox_retry, sandbox_retry_allow and git.clean_regenerable) have no consumer in the crates and docs/policy-reference.md:891 says the sandbox keys are not read yet. Source: the operator approved process audit of 2026-10-23, including the operator's decision of that day on the dependency audit (line numbers at c9993bcf3).

Scope: (1) Move to warn: description over 50, body shape and count, unlisted trailers, policy_characters and the PR Summary shape (a level for the description limit may need a new key; place it per policy_key_placement). Stay at block: commit type, the breaking marker, subject 72, ai_attribution (an AI trailer is still refused, though other unlisted trailers only warn), emoji, secrets, branch prefix, the Task: line, required PR sections and the release-impact job. The ai_attribution refusal message names the Claude setting that turns the host's trailer off (includeCoAuthoredBy and attribution), and the shipped settings keep both off. (2) The dependency audit follows one precedence table, used here, in the criteria and in EPC-022 AC-126. An advisory is "new" when its identity (advisory id, package, ecosystem) is in the head scan and not in the base scan. Rows apply in order: (a) a scan that fails or is incomplete is missing evidence and fails the job at both block and warn; (b) an advisory matched by a trusted suppression that has not expired passes and is reported; (c) a new advisory of any severity, low and informational included, fails; (d) a critical or high advisory fails unless a trusted triage entry (owner, rationale, expiry) states that it is not reachable, and unknown or missing reachability evidence counts as reachable; (e) a medium advisory fails unless a trusted triage entry (owner, rationale, expiry) exists and has not expired; (f) a low or informational advisory that is not new is printed and passes. There is no dev-only exemption. Composition: security_review and dep_audit share the one table and the effective level is the stricter of the two; at block a failing advisory row fails the job; at warn the same advisory rows print as warnings and the job passes; a failed or incomplete scan fails the job at both block and warn; at off the audit does not run. Suppressions and triage entries are read from the base commit only. The same table is mirrored by the shipped template step (this task owns assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml's audit step). (3) The seven unread keys leave the shipped policy, the schema and docs/policy-reference.md; a policy file that still sets one keeps loading. (4) codeflow policy prints a report of effective values.

Non-goals: no hook, guard, secret scan or remote rule changes. Protection lost by (2): a low or informational advisory that is not new, a medium advisory with a valid trusted triage entry, and a critical or high advisory with a trusted not-reachable triage entry no longer stop a merge; all are still printed on every run and the weekly scan. A medium advisory without a triage entry still fails, and so does any new advisory.

Effect on adopting projects: shipped style defaults match the intent (advisory style, blocking semantics); adopters that set the seven removed keys see them ignored with a notice, and the shipped template's audit follows the same severity rule when dep_audit is block.

Owned files: assets/base/policy.json and .codeflow/policy.json (all lines but test_gate_on_push, which TSK-449 owns), hooks/standards.rs, hooks/policy.rs, hooks/policy_schema.rs, security/privilege.rs where it names a removed key, crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/policy.rs, the Summary shape and policy_characters hunks of ci/pr_body.rs and ci.rs, docs/policy-reference.md (but the test_gate_on_push row), the dependency audit step of the security review job in codeflow-ci.yml, osv-scanner.toml, the shipped audit step in assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml, a new audit script under scripts/ with its test, the shipped Claude settings under assets/base/settings/ and .claude/settings.json. The last-release fixtures are not edited. The Reviews and release-impact hunks of pr_body.rs are TSK-451.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Process cuts amendment (2026-10-23)/One record per completed fact

One record per completed fact

TSK-451complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

One fact is recorded in several places and then cross-checked. Criteria and evidence live in the task record, the acceptance block, the PR Testing section, the verdict and an evidence ledger; the review verdict is in the PR Reviews row, the acceptance block and the verdict text, and codeflow ci blocks when the Reviews row and the acceptance block differ (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:975-1090). Release impact is judged by codeflow ci, by scripts/release.py check-pr and by the pre-push preflight (pr_body.rs:1395-1495, push_set.rs:177-183). A task PR cannot amend its own task's criteria without a separate planning PR (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/amendment.rs:385-454). Source: the operator approved process audit of 2026-10-23 (line numbers at c9993bcf3).

Scope: (1) The acceptance block is the completion record. codeflow ci derives the Reviews row from it, prints it, and warns when the PR body names something different. (2) No separate evidence ledger in any template, check or record (the guidance text is TSK-452). (3) A task PR may amend its own task's record (criteria, follow-ups), with a reason per removed criterion in the PR body; any change to another task, an epic or a status that is not its own still needs a planning PR. (4) validate --docs runs once per codeflow ci invocation, as work.valid_graph; the separate pre-push step and quick-target copy are TSK-449. (5) Release impact has one generic evaluator, the policy-controlled reading in ci/pr_body.rs (git.pr_release_impact, enforced at the level the project sets, including block), which every caller uses. This repository's duplicate invocations are deduplicated through an explicit configuration: scripts/release.py check-pr and the release impact job call that evaluator (codeflow ci --read-release-impact) and judge nothing of their own, and the pre-push preflight in push_set.rs keeps its existing call because the evaluator's interface does not change. An adopter without scripts/release.py or a release workflow keeps its enforcement from codeflow ci. (6) At ready, a code PR's Testing section cites codeflow test --mode quick for the head tree; a draft owes none (the Testing hunks of ci/pr_body.rs are this task's, and TSK-452 owns the guidance that asks for it). (7) The PR template and the task and PR templates shrink to match. Research and review-only work needing no durable record is guidance (TSK-452).

Non-goals: the acceptance block's binding to the reviewed commit, the journey criterion, the Task: line and the human merge do not change. Protection to keep: weakening a criterion inside the PR that is reviewed must stay visible, so a removal without a reason is refused (AC-3).

Effect on adopting projects: a smaller PR template and fewer codeflow ci refusals over duplicated facts; adopters that wrote a Reviews row keep passing when it agrees with the acceptance block.

Owned files: crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs (the acceptance cross-check and work.valid_graph hunks), crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/acceptance.rs, the Reviews, Testing and release-impact hunks of ci/pr_body.rs, ci/classification.rs, crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/amendment.rs, acceptance.rs and record_text.rs, scripts/release.py and scripts/test_release.py, .github/workflows/codeflow-release.yml, .github/pull_request_template.md, assets/base/ci/pull_request_template.md, assets/base/pm/. TSK-450 owns the Summary and character hunks; TSK-449 owns push_set.rs.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Process cuts amendment (2026-10-23)/Review cadence and guidance state each rule once

Review cadence and guidance state each rule once

TSK-452complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Guidance repeats work and repeats itself. Every review round rereads the whole unit "not only the delta" (findings.md:64-66), a security change can get five or six passes over one diff (cf-security-reviewer.md:12-34), cf-reviewer is mandatory in one file and optional in another (cf-develop step 4b, workflow-discipline.md:265, cf-model-orchestrator SKILL.md:381-383, cf-reviewer.md:138-139), rounds 6 and 7 found sibling cases one at a time, the routed required reading is about 150 KB, batch landing is stated in four files and the plain-writing rule in eight. Source: the operator approved process audit of 2026-10-23, including the operator's decision of that day on the security review stack (line numbers at c9993bcf3).

Scope: (1) Review cadence at four stages: plan settlement (epics only), PR ready, landing candidate (hand-resolved hunks only), epic close. Between stages the finder confirms a fix on the delta plus the affected tests; one final holistic pass on the final substantive revision precedes approval. (2) The builder's sibling sweep, with file:line per site, precedes the first review on a class fix; a reviewer who finds a sibling returns the unit to the sweep. (3) Security: the one other-lineage whole-unit review runs with the security checklist as the attacker lens; the Claude side triages scanner output inside its integrated judgment; cf-reviewer runs only when no other-lineage seat exists, stated once; the "high complexity" and "material depth" triggers for an extra family are dropped from routing-policy.json, the security and irreversible triggers stay. (4) Only material findings block; nits get a disposition. (5) Estimates come from planned throughput (cf-estimate, "Durations"). (6) Lane and queue rules: lanes sized from host memory and CPU, cheap targeted checks run freely while heavy work takes TSK-331's admission, and only the primary runs the full gate. (7) Research, review and consult work gets no durable record unless it produces a durable artifact; the evidence ledger text goes; one findings record linked from the PR (resolving the conflict between completion.md and pr-evidence.md). (8) Dedupe: batch landing in one home (cf-method "Managing a body of work"), the plain-writing rule once in .codeflow/rules/writing.md, the delivery flow once, one editorial-review trigger, cf-present loads specimens on demand, and the orchestrator preflight is printed by codeflow doctor (configured versus observed values, with unavailable evidence reported) and read, with the live observation still made.

(9) Planned work is delivered at speed (operator direction of 2026-10-23). Exploration, research and planning stay deliberate; once work is planned into an epic and tasks with criteria, builders execute without re-planning, re-litigating settled decisions or confirmation work for its own sake. Throughput expectation, set by the operator as an explicit decision of 2026-10-23 (which satisfies "Only the operator adds process"): each build lane delivers at least one planned task to ready-for-review per hour, preferably two. Quality is not traded: criteria, the tests that prove them and real security stay. Speed practices: targeted tests in the worktree, the quick gate once before ready, no local full gate, one push at ready, no reruns on an unchanged tree, lean PR bodies carrying criteria with file:line and test evidence, any stop over 15 minutes reported at once, reversible choices decided by the builder. Coordinator duties: start every task whose edges allow, up to host capacity; measure each lane's time on its task at every sweep; act on any lane past an hour. One canonical home: cf-method's workflow lifecycle reference holds the full rule; cf-develop, cf-model-orchestrator, the managed map's build row and cf-estimate (estimates from planned throughput, never extrapolated from a slow pace) point to it. The durability-push rule in the git rules changes to match "one push at ready" for the pre-push cost TSK-449 removes.

Non-goals: no hook, guard, CI or policy change, and no change to what the protections are; the deterministic scanners, the secret scan and trusted CI are untouched. Protection lost by (3): one fewer independent security pass per security-sensitive unit; both lineages still read the diff with the security checklist.

Effect on adopting projects: the managed kernel grows from 12,561 to 13,023 bytes and the per-task reading chain from 132,428 to 134,597 bytes, both within their guidelines, because the cadence, speed and preflight text outweighs the dedupes; codeflow update rewrites the managed files (AGENTS.md block, rules, skills, agents) and the baseline; adopters keep their own rules outside the managed markers.

Owned files: the managed block of AGENTS.md and assets/base/AGENTS*.tmpl, CLAUDE.md and its templates, .codeflow/rules/* with assets/base/rules/*, the skills cf-method, cf-develop, cf-ship, cf-plan, cf-estimate, cf-model-orchestrator, cf-present and cf-editorial-review in .claude/skills, .agents/skills, assets/base/claude/skills and assets/base/agents/skills (byte-identical mirrors), the agents cf-reviewer and cf-security-reviewer in .claude/agents and their asset copies, routing-policy.json, crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/doctor.rs (the preflight output), and the resynced .codeflow/.baseline for those files. TSK-452 depends on TSK-331 (the lane and queue guidance names the admission lock and codeflow reserve as built). Other open tasks edit some of these files (TSK-419, TSK-423, TSK-435, TSK-441, TSK-387); dispatch keeps one writer at a time.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Untracked issues amendment (2026-10-26)/Estimate outcomes find a deleted line's landing and report open-task age with idle claims

Estimate outcomes find a deleted line's landing and report open-task age with idle claims

TSK-1012todo

after this merges, `estimate outcomes` times a task whose integration ref was deleted after its line merged.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

after this merges, `estimate outcomes` times a task whose integration ref was deleted after its line merged, measures a line before deletion with `--ref`, and lists each open task's start, blocked spans, current age less blocked time and idle claims, in the `ongoing` category beside TSK-1171's.

Context

Issue #334 items D and B and its comment of 2026-10-25. Two measurements are lost today:

  • D, deleted lines. A task's landing is found through its integration ref; when that ref is deleted after the epic merges, the run says the target "does not resolve in this clone" (history.rs:472-477) and the task's start is lost. In the adopter's run, 39 of 41 completed tasks without a start had a deleted line whose tip survives on main as a merge's second parent.
  • B, open-task age. No report shows an open task's start, blocked spans, current age and idle claims.

The claim record (item F) is TSK-1173's; this task reads it. The profile, bands and the clock's end are TSK-1013 to TSK-1172. Each of D and B has a manual route (record outcomes before deleting a line), so this is a 4.1.0-grade feature carried in EPC-022 so the method runs on the work now in flight.

Outcome: after this merges, estimate outcomes times a task whose integration ref was deleted after its line merged, measures a line before deletion with --ref, and lists each open task's start, blocked spans, current age less blocked time and idle claims, in the ongoing category beside TSK-1171's.

Rules:

  • Landing from HEAD keeps the first-parent base the current reader uses; a deleted line is found through the merge on the target that brought it, never by a branch name.
  • Every started task stays in the report in its own category (completed, ongoing, cancelled, reopened, superseded, unknown start). An unknown start is never filled.
  • An idle claim (a claim with no later commit) is flagged with its age and handed over, never released automatically, never deleted. No idle threshold is set here; any threshold is set later from the measured claim-to-first-commit gaps and needs the operator's approval (D3).

Non-goals: bands, hit rates and the profile (TSK-1013, TSK-1171); the claim record (TSK-1173); grouping by class (TSK-313).

Criteria removed from this record by the 2026-11-01 cut, each moved and not copied (AC-n removed: <reason>):

  • AC-3 removed: the recorded claim time and the idle claim are TSK-1173 AC-2 and AC-4
  • AC-5 removed: the one-step claim and the adopted-branch start (D4, D1) are TSK-1173 AC-1 and AC-2
  • AC-6 removed: the idle flag with its age is this task's AC-9; the handover text and the no-release rule are TSK-1173 AC-7

Coverage defaults apply to targets that set no rules of their own

TSK-1014todo

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #299, its defect half. The shipped test-config schema says defaults.coverage holds "Default coverage rules applied when targets omit them" (assets/base/testing/test-config.schema.json, defaults), but the engine never applies them: crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/config/mod.rs reads defaults.coverage only for its glob check, and collect_coverage_reports in crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/gate.rs skips a target with no coverage configuration and judges a target's own rules only. A project that writes its floor once in defaults.coverage, as the schema invites, gets no floor at all and must copy the rules into every target, a workaround the release rule of 2026-10-18 places in 3.2.0. Codex's review of PR 343 separated this from the issue's feature half (a mandatory 80 floor with recorded exemptions), which stays TSK-1006 in EPC-024.

Outcome: the rules a project writes in defaults.coverage are applied to every target that collects coverage and sets no rules of its own, and a test target that cannot be covered by them (no coverage producer) is named in the gate output rather than passing silently.

Rules:

  • Defaults carry rules only, not a producer (format, artifact, the mode command that writes it). A target with a coverage block and no rules inherits the default rules; a target's own non-empty rules replace them, as "applied when targets omit them" says.
  • A target with no coverage block while defaults.coverage is non-empty gets a warning naming the target and the missing producer; it is not failed, since no floor applied to it before and the mandatory floor is TSK-1006's decision.
  • The inherited rules are enforcing exactly as a target's own rules are: a missing artifact fails the gate.
  • No minimum is imposed and no default value changes; the schema text is kept and now true.

Non-goals: the mandatory 80 floor, exemption records and essential evaluation (TSK-1006, EPC-024); changed-files scope.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Issues 351 to 358 amendment (2026-10-27)/git-guard allows read-only git commands it cannot place

git-guard allows read-only git commands it cannot place

TSK-1024todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #357 and its comment (CodeFlow 3.1.1). git-guard refuses read-only git commands in common shapes, so agents split or rewrite harmless inspection lines, and the guard's own advice (cd /path/to/repo && git …) is a form it then refuses.

Rechecked on 2026-10-27 through codeflow hook git-guard --contract 3 with the 3.2.0 binary built at TSK-397's head caf728c70, payload cwd a worktree of this repository:

Issue caseResult on 3.2.0
1: git -C <repo> branch --list 'task/TSK-643-*'still refused, git.discard_uncommitted, "the pattern in task/TSK-643-*"
2 and 2b: cd <repo> && git remote -v | head -2, the same with git worktree liststill refused, git.policy_authority, "a directory change on a line the guard does not model", after a note advising cd /path/to/repo && git …
comment: cd $S; git remote show originstill refused, git.policy_authority, "$S"
2c: cd <repo> && git status -sb | head -2allowed with the "judged it as a protected branch" note
3: git -C <repo> worktree add <new> task/x && git -C <new> status -sballowed with a note: no longer reproduces
comment: cd $TMPDIR && rm -rf cfsrc && …allowed: no longer reproduces
comment: gh issue comment … --body "… git remote show …"allowed: no longer reproduces

Causes, read on the line tip 7172229aa:

  • Case 1: discard_intent (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard.rs:20146) expands every operand with expand_word before it parses options; a glob fails there (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_target.rs:244), although the branch arm (git_guard.rs:20268) treats only a forced delete as a discard.
  • Cases 2 and the comment: on a line flat_top_level does not model (a pipe, ||, a group), moves_for (git_guard.rs:8561-8569) makes every git command's directory unknown when the line changes directory, and an unknown target is allowed only for the subcommands of discard_readonly_git (git_guard.rs:20466): status, diff, log, show, rev-parse, ls-files, ls-tree, merge-base, for-each-ref, show-ref, cat-file, check-ignore, help and version.

Outcome: a git command that cannot change refs, the index, the work tree, configuration, hooks or a remote is allowed with a note wherever git-guard cannot place it, and a refusal's advice names a form the guard accepts.

Design, fixed here:

  • The guard does not start modeling cd. The operator decided on 2026-10-25 (TSK-397's amendment) that narrowing directories cannot be made sound against shell state the guard cannot see; the issue's suggestions 3 and 4 (model a leading cd, model paths created earlier on the line) are therefore not taken. An unknown directory stays unknown; what changes is which commands are safe there.
  • One read-only classifier replaces discard_readonly_git. It decides from the subcommand and its parsed options, not from the subcommand name alone, and serves the unresolved-target block in check_git, may_change_discard_state, an early exit in discard_intent and check_discard, so discard intent is decided before any operand is expanded, and check_authority (git_guard.rs:8635, run first for every git command from check_git at :8722). There, a command whose -C target is a worktree created earlier on the same line takes its source's authority only for status (:8674), so git -C <new> log -1 still loads policy from a directory that does not exist yet and is refused (:8679-8685). The classifier replaces that status-only test; a mutation still needs a readable target and every branch check.
  • Read-only forms it accepts: the current list; branch with only listing options (--list/-l with patterns, --show-current, -a, -r, -v/-vv, --contains, --no-contains, --merged, --no-merged, --points-at, --format, --sort); worktree list; remote with no subcommand, -v, show, get-url; config read forms (reusing config_only_reads, git_guard.rs:10716); stash list and stash show; tag with --list/-l only; describe, name-rev, rev-list, shortlog, blame, count-objects, var, and symbolic-ref with no new value.
  • Never read-only: any form that creates, renames, deletes or sets something (branch <name>, -m, -c, -d, -u, tag <name>, remote add, config without a read flag), and any option that runs a program or writes a file: a git -c setting, --exec-path, --output, grep -O/--open-files-in-pager, --upload-pack and --receive-pack. grep joins the list only without those options.
  • The advice printed with an unresolved target says why the guard could not place the command (a pipe or || on the line, an unresolved cd) and suggests git -C <literal path> …, never cd /path && git ….

Severity: medium. No refusal of a write is removed; the cost is agent turns and confusing advice on every read-only inspection line with a pipe after cd.

Outcome

A standalone task files its own follow-up record in its pull request

TSK-1025todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #354, item 1 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, an adopter's standalone task TSK-643). The task's pull request carried its own record and a new follow-up task record that its AC-6 waiver names, and codeflow ci refused it under work.classification: "a task PR may add only its own standalone task record". Removing the follow-up record after completion then forced a reopen, which led to the issue's other two items. Those are placed elsewhere: the waiver refused after a reopen is TSK-340 AC-7, and work.criteria_frozen counting the task's own remote branch is TSK-350 AC-5.

Read on the line tip 7172229aa:

  • the refusal: crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/classification.rs:1055-1066 refuses any added record that is not the PR task's own, and any second added record;
  • the documented route: docs/cli.md:118 (--follow-up-of) says a standalone task's follow-up is "a standalone task, filed on a task branch cut from the target, with its record filled in and committed, then claimed with work claim". That is the follow-up's own task pull request, which carries its code, so the record reaches the target only when the follow-up's work lands, after the source task that names it;
  • the issue says work claim needs the predecessor complete on the target. Not confirmed: task new --follow-up-of writes only follow_up_of and no depends_on edge (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/light_paths.rs:200), so a claim is held back only when someone adds that edge by hand.

Outcome: a standalone task can file the follow-up its own acceptance names in the same pull request, and the docs give one route that works before the source task lands.

Design: a standalone task pull request may add, besides its own record, only the follow-up records its own acceptance block names in follow_ups: new standalone tasks whose follow_up_of is the pull request's task, at status todo, with no product path of their own. Every other added record stays refused, as does a follow-up record that is complete, names another source, belongs to an epic, or is changed by a later commit in a way that would bind work to it. The alternative, docs only (file the follow-up first in a records-only pull request), keeps classification unchanged but adds one pull request and one merge cycle per follow-up, which is the cost the issue reports; the bounded allowance is chosen because the added record carries no work and is reviewed with the source task that names it.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Issues 351 to 358 amendment (2026-10-27)/The managed CI cancels superseded runs and skips a proven repeat

The managed CI cancels superseded runs and skips a proven repeat

TSK-1026todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #352, items 1 and 2 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). The managed workflow assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml has no concurrency group, so a new push to a pull request leaves the superseded run going to its end, and a push whose tree an earlier hosted run already passed runs the whole gate again. An adopter edited the managed file to add both and recorded it as a workaround. The issue's item 3, sharded gates, is TSK-384 AC-5 and AC-6.

Read on the line tip 7172229aa:

  • the template has no concurrency key (none in its 1,079 lines); this repository's own .github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml:30-32 already uses a group per workflow and ref with cancel-in-progress only for pull_request events;
  • the template runs on pull_request, on pushes to main and master, weekly and on dispatch (codeflow-ci.yml:26-35), and since TSK-449 a pull request runs the essential mode and a push the full mode (:170-198);
  • this repository skips a repeated push run through scripts/ci-reuse.py; TSK-359 is hardening that lookup's binding (the exact merged pull request, base, tested merge tree, workflow blob and required jobs) and states "changing the shipped template" as its non-goal.

Outcome: the managed workflow cancels a superseded pull request run, and a push to the protected branch whose tree a bound pull request run already passed reuses that verdict under TSK-359's binding, with the secret scan and every security job still running.

Design and tradeoffs:

  • Concurrency: a pull request run is superseded only when a run for a newer head of the same pull request starts. Proposed, for AC-6 to confirm: a group per workflow and pull request, cancel-in-progress true only for a synchronize event (the one pull_request event that brings a new head), and the queue mode TSK-1040 adopts (queue: max), so a same-head event (opened, reopened, a re-run, a repeated arrival) neither cancels a running run nor replaces a pending one; it waits and completes. If AC-6 finds that expression unsound, each run first checks whether its head is still the pull request's head and stops when it is not, and same-head runs share no cancelling group. Push, schedule and dispatch runs are never cancelled, so a protected-branch verdict is always completed. Cost: a cancelled run shows as cancelled on the superseded commit, which only matters for a commit nobody merges; a queued same-head run costs one more run.
  • Reuse: the managed workflow gets the same binding TSK-359 proves here, read from the run's recorded provenance and executed from the trusted base's copy of the helper, never from the pushed tree. A full-mode push that reuses an essential-mode pull request verdict would weaken the full gate, so reuse is allowed only when the reused run's effective mode equals the push's effective mode. A project may opt in to running essential on push, which changes the push's effective mode; it never waives the equality. Unproven reuse runs the jobs.
  • Never reused: the secret scan, the gitleaks canary, the security review and CodeQL, as in TSK-359.

Issue #355 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, macOS, a Codex review seat in Herdr). Under the managed cf-guard profile, Chromium does not start: both the system Chrome and Playwright's headless shell exit with bootstrap_check_in org.chromium.Chromium.MachPortRendezvousServer: Permission denied (1100). A UI review that needs the reviewer to drive a browser then falls back to a capture the author's host runs, which the reviewer can only recheck by hash, so the live checks are not independent.

Read on the line tip 7172229aa: the limitation is known and stated in the shipped config (assets/base/codex/config.toml:13-18: Playwright's Chromium did not start under cf-guard, cf-builder or :workspace because the sandbox denies its Mach port rendezvous; it starts unsandboxed). No managed guidance gives a review seat a sanctioned route to run browser checks. The issue's observation was not re-run here.

Outcome: a review seat on macOS can drive a browser against the reviewed head itself, through one documented route that does not widen the seat's file or network access, and a review that cannot use it says so as reduced assurance.

Options and the choice:

  • Allow the Mach registration in cf-guard. Not chosen as the default: whether a Codex permission profile can express a Mach allowance is not established, and a Mach service allowance in a read-only reviewer sandbox is an IPC surface outside the file and network rules the profile states. AC-1 establishes the facts; if a narrow, named allowance exists and the security review accepts it, it may be the route.
  • Run the browser outside the seat's sandbox as a lane-owned browser server started for the reviewed head, which the review seat drives over its own lane socket. This reuses TSK-437's per-seat socket allowance, and the reviewer issues every interaction itself. Chosen unless AC-1 finds a sound profile allowance. A lane socket controls who connects, not what the connected browser can do (TSK-437 states that a browser server can read files the browser reaches and take raw DevTools commands), so this route needs its own boundary: the browser process runs in its own sandbox, or behind a broker that passes only the automation commands the review needs, with file reads limited to the served reviewed head and a scratch profile, network limited to the local server under review, and downloads and file writes refused. The seat's own denies being unchanged does not prove that boundary; AC-2's negative canaries do.
  • A host-executed capture with a hashed report stays the documented fallback and is recorded as reduced assurance, never as an independent live check.
Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Issues 351 to 358 amendment (2026-10-27)/The scaffold ships a useful status line and leaves effort to each person

The scaffold ships a useful status line and leaves effort to each person

TSK-1028complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #351 and its two maintainer comments of 2026-10-27 (07:38Z and 21:04Z), CodeFlow 3.1.1. The scaffold writes personal preferences into the shared project settings, where they replace each contributor's own choice: a branch-only statusLine and effortLevel: "high" in .claude/settings.json, and model_reasoning_effort = "high" in .codex/config.toml.

The 21:04Z comment states the status line both consuming repositories now carry as their workaround, and asks that it, or a configurable equivalent, be the scaffold default, with a contributor's own line in .claude/settings.local.json. Quoted from the comment:

It reads Claude Code's status JSON on stdin and prints the model display name and id, the Claude Code version, the output style, the folder name, the git branch when there is one, and the context used as tokens out of the window and as a percentage: green below 50, yellow below 80, red from 80. It needs jq.

Read on the line tip 7172229aa:

  • the three Claude presets set both keys: assets/base/settings/default.json:7 and :576-579, and the same in acceptEdits.json and bypass-sandboxed.json (:7, :577); the shipped line is printf '%s' "$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo codeflow)", unchanged since fe644c345 (2026-06-12) per the 07:38Z comment;
  • codeflow update adds any shipped top-level key a project's file lacks and keeps any value it has (crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/settings_merge.rs:200-207), so a project that deletes statusLine or effortLevel gets them back on its next update, and a project still holding the old shipped line never receives a new default. env and permissions have a baseline-guarded rule; these keys do not;
  • assets/base/codex/config.toml sets model_reasoning_effort = "high", and the file is managed (assets/base/scaffold-manifest.toml:278-282);
  • every seat launch already passes its effort (cf-herdr/SKILL.md:104-107: Claude --effort, Codex -c model_reasoning_effort=…, Grok --reasoning-effort), so the effort pins set only what a person gets when they start a session by hand;
  • the effort pins are a recorded decision: ADR-0056 says "Codex project settings pin high. Claude settings provide effortLevel: high as a starting default";
  • .claude/settings.local.json outranks the shared file (cf-customize/references/claude-context-policy.md:47-49) but is per checkout (gitignored, assets/base/gitignore:17). Corrected during review: since Claude Code v2.1.211 a worktree session uses the main checkout's file, with stated exceptions such as Windows, so one personal file serves every worktree there. Codex has no per-project personal file; the issue says its only per-person override is a -c flag (not verified here).

Outcome: the scaffold ships a useful project status line that degrades cleanly without jq, effort is the contributor's own unless a project opts in, and the docs say where each person sets their own values.

Change and tradeoffs:

  • Status line: ship the comment's line, or a configurable equivalent that shows the same fields, as the default in the three presets. Without jq it prints a short fallback (folder and branch) instead of an error or an empty line. A long inline command is hard to review; the builder may ship it as a managed script the setting calls, if update keeps that script current. On update, a project whose statusLine is exactly a value CodeFlow shipped, proved by the recorded baseline, moves to the new default; a line the project changed stays and is reported. The shared line still outranks a person's user settings, so the docs name .claude/settings.local.json as the personal route and state its per-checkout limit.
  • Effort: effortLevel and Codex model_reasoning_effort become opt-in, offered by cf-customize and documented, and are no longer shipped. On update, a key whose value is exactly what CodeFlow shipped is removed; a project's own value stays. The cost: a person who starts a session by hand without their own effort setting gets the harness default, which may be lower than high; primaries launched through cf-herdr still enter at high.
  • The effort change supersedes ADR-0056's settings-pin sentence, which is the operator's call; that part waits for the approval, recorded in this task's pull request.
