Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Issues 351 to 358 amendment (2026-10-27)/The Claude compaction point is a documented project choice

The Claude compaction point is a documented project choice

TSK-1029complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #358 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). Every scaffolded .claude/settings.json sets CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=1000000 and CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=50, so sessions compact at about 500K tokens, and the shared value sits above each contributor's own settings. The adopter reports long orchestrator sessions running near that point, and is measuring 50, 40, 35 and 30 percent on cost per session and on whether a session still knows its task, branch and next step after compaction.

Operator decision of 2026-10-27: 35 percent of the 1M window (compaction at about 350K), replacing 50; the operator proposed it ("how about 35% (350k)"). The value is revisited once the adopter's measurement lands.

Read on the line tip 7172229aa:

  • the presets set both keys (assets/base/settings/default.json:3-6, acceptEdits.json:3-6, bypass-sandboxed.json:3-6), shipped by 3adda9b44 (2026-10-03);
  • the issue's "undocumented" claim holds only in part. cf-customize/references/claude-context-policy.md states the values, the thresholds (about 500K against Claude Code's default of about 967K on a 1M-window model; about 100K on a session limited to 200K), how to change or opt out, and the per-person override in .claude/settings.local.json (:47-49). It does not say why the value was chosen or what it costs, and it is reachable only through cf-customize;
  • codeflow update keeps every env value a project has (crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/settings_merge.rs:227-290), so a changed shipped default reaches only fresh installs unless update learns to move a value that is exactly the old shipped one;
  • the qualification kit pins the percentage at 100 in .claude/settings.local.json for its compaction fixtures (cf-evaluate-model/scripts/eval_kit.py:396-403), so it does not depend on the shared value.

Token-cost tradeoff, stated for the record:

  • every turn sends the whole context as input; with prompt caching most of it is billed as cache reads, but per-turn input still grows with the context: a turn near 350K carries about 0.7 times the input of a turn near 500K, and about 2.3 times one near 150K;
  • without these keys a 1M-window session compacts near 967K, so any pin lowers the peak against the harness default;
  • a lower point compacts more often; each compaction reads the full context once and writes a summary, and detail the summary drops is lost. The orient digest that SessionStart prints after a compaction (ADR-0013) gives context and pointers to the durable records, and rereading those records recovers task, branch and next step, which limits that loss;
  • the percentage also applies to sessions limited to 200K, which compact at about 70K with 35 percent;
  • some models price input above a size threshold at a higher rate; the current rate for the model in use is checked, not assumed (not verified here).

Outcome: scaffolded sessions compact at 35 percent of the 1M window, the docs explain the cost and context tradeoff and where a project and a person change it, and the value is revisited from the adopter's measurement.

The keys stay in the shared file: the compaction point is a team cost policy and also applies to subagents.

Corrected during the build: AC-3 first gave the personal file a per-checkout limit. Since Claude Code v2.1.211 a worktree session uses the file at the main checkout's root, except outside git, with the repository root at the home folder, on Windows, or under another owner (TSK-1028 corrected its AC-6 the same way), so AC-3 now asks where the file lives for a worktree. The AC-4 revisit is TSK-1049 (EPC-023).

Added during review (Codex rounds 2 to 5): moving a shipped value made codeflow update --diff and update's report show settings values, so this task also makes them show no project content.

Display contract, stated identically in TSK-1029 and TSK-1051: a diagnostic, report line or export never contains a value, key, heading or line a project wrote, in its text, its Debug form or any error it wraps. It may name a path, a line and column, a count, and a schema name or heading CodeFlow defines. A version is shown as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, plus a prerelease only in CodeFlow's own release form (alpha.N, beta.N, rc.N); any other prerelease, and any build metadata, is shown as (with a suffix), and a value that does not parse as a version is not shown.

Ownership:

  • TSK-1029 owns everything codeflow update and codeflow update --pin print and write to the --diff export. The export is judged only against the assets embedded in the binary (scaffold/diff_redact.rs). Report lines name step positions, keys and paths. The readers and wrappers they reach are covered: the project metadata and state files (scaffold/state.rs, registry.rs and its locked read in file_lock.rs), the version check and version display (scaffold/version.rs), pending update records (scaffold/update/pending.rs), the PR template diagnosis, whose project headings are named by position or count (scaffold/pr_template.rs), the workspace policy load (hooks/policy.rs Policy::load_file), the remote policy read (remote.rs), the CI pin checks that codeflow doctor shares (scaffold/release_pin.rs, doctor/ci_pin.rs: an unreadable digest line is named by number, a duplicated key only when CodeFlow defines it), and release downloads, named by artifact and failure category, never by URL or curl output, with an invalid --pin named without its value. TOML and JSON errors become a ParsePlace (scaffold/mod.rs): format, a fixed kind, line and column. ScaffoldError never keeps a parser error as its source.
  • The boundary is a type (Codex rounds 5 and 6). Every line those commands print or export is a Shown (scaffold/shown.rs), whose text is private and which has no conversion from a string. Its fixed-text constructors take only &'static str; runtime values enter only as a count, a path, a parse place, an I/O category, a version under the rule above, a date, a hash the binary computed, or a slice of a Shipped text (scaffold/assets.rs), which only the asset reader or compiled-in text makes. shown! takes a literal format and Shown arguments only. Report, ScaffoldError and the --diff sections hold only Shown; the pin report keeps its versions as strings and formats through Shown (PinReport::shown). Their Debug writes the same text, and ScaffoldError keeps no source. A catalogued remedy is filled in one pass over its own text, so a brace in a filled path is copied as text. The other public report and error types update reaches (PinReport, PinnedDigests, Unparseable, RootUnreadable, Diagnosis, KeptTemplate) have a Debug that shows no project text. Everything update prints after its report (the workspace hint, the cf-present state warning, the registry warning, the PR template prompt, update --pin) goes through the CLI writers say, warn and prompt, which take a Shown; a failed git read is named by the step and its exit code. Because Report and ScaffoldError are shared, codeflow init and the docs portal setup build their lines the same way; TSK-1051 still owns their review, and init --workspace's git step output (git_run). tests/update_display_boundary.rs checks in the core and CLI sources what the type cannot see: no leak, each runtime-text constructor call listed with what feeds it, and no print outside the writers in the CLI functions update and update --pin call. It reads source, not expanded code, and follows calls by name, so it is not a proof that every route crosses the boundary; its limits are in its header. codeflow-present is out of its scope: update calls only provision_state_root there and prints a fixed line on failure. tests/update_canary_sweep.rs plants one canary in every input update and update --pin read (every installed file and baseline, the registry, a kept PR template, a pending record, task and epic records with and without a migration baseline, the version, the pin argument, the release URL and a served release), five ways each, and checks stdout, stderr and the export. These two tests and the adversarial helper tests are the contract.
  • TSK-1051 owns every other reader and printer in the three crates and in every shipped asset that runs, including error types outside ScaffoldError that keep a parser error as their source, semantic validation messages (such as hooks/policy_schema.rs) and codeflow init's report.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality asks amendment (2026-10-27)/The shipped instructions say what belongs in a repository

The shipped instructions say what belongs in a repository

TSK-1030todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #279 and its comments of 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-27. Agents under CodeFlow treat the repository as the place to keep everything they produce, and nothing in the shipped instructions or the reviewer's verdict asks whether a new file belongs there. One shipped row invites the opposite: cf-method references/project-organization.md:670 (the issue cites :560 at 3.1.1; the row moved) names docs/verification/<task>/ as the home of "retained comparison evidence" that lands on protected branches. One adopter's main grew to 492 files (26 MB) in 61 per-task folders under docs/verification/, and the adopter copied the row into its own rules.

The operator placed the instruction fix in 3.2.0 on 2026-10-27; the gate stays in TSK-428 (EPC-024, 4.2.0), because it needs TSK-424's exemption register and baseline. This task takes TSK-428's former AC-1 (the instruction) and AC-2 (the review question), which are instruction and review-question changes small enough to ship alone.

Outcome: the shipped instructions state what belongs in a repository and what stays out, required evidence lives in the PR body or the task record, the project-organization.md row that names docs/verification/<task>/ is replaced, and cf-reviewer asks of every added file whether it is needed long term and in its smallest form.

Rules:

  • What belongs: product or authority content, code with its tests and config, and evidence a live record cites that the PR body cannot carry, in summary form. What stays out: run output and per-run logs, review records and verdict files, superseded iterations, build and cache output, copies kept for reference, scratch and session working files, duplicate copies, and per-task verification folders. Git history keeps removed evidence, so a clean-up does not lose it.
  • Vendoring gets one rule (the 2026-10-27 22:46Z comment): a copy a runtime needs is admitted through the project's dependency rule; a copy kept for reference is not.
  • The replaced row points to cf-ship/references/pr-evidence.md for required evidence and keeps prototypes out of protected branches as the table already says.
  • Consumer-facing examples that cite CodeFlow's own docs/verification/ paths are dropped or reworded, so the folder stops looking expected.
  • The block and warn tiers, citation safety for removed evidence and exceptions are TSK-428's (gate), not this task's.

Non-goals: the gate and its tiers (TSK-428); CodeFlow's own managed-copy footprint (TSK-429); deleting what adopters or this repository already hold (AC-1 records this repository's state and routes it).

First-pass survey (planning, 2026-10-27, line tip 5f2fe3827)
  • The row: assets/base/claude/skills/cf-method/references/project-organization.md:670, mirrored in .claude/skills, .agents/skills and both .codeflow/.baseline trees.
  • Examples citing CodeFlow's own evidence paths: assets/base/agents/skills/cf-present/resources/figure-grammar.md:153 and utility-presentation-system.md:29, the same two in cf-docs-portal/resources/, assets/base/rules/writing.md:287 and :334, and cf-model-orchestrator/resources/grok-host.md:56.
  • Defaults that treat the folder as standard: assets/docs-portal/starter/portal.config.json:11 and three fixtures in cf-evaluate-model/resources/fixtures.json (exclude: ["docs/verification"]).
  • Nearest existing rules: assets/base/rules/workflow-discipline.md:145 "Write only what earns its keep" (code, not files); cf-ship/references/pr-evidence.md (the PR body's evidence, no rule on files); cf-model-orchestrator/resources/quality/evidence.md (evidence quality, no home rule); the managed assets/base/gitignore (secrets, editor files, worktrees; no build or run output); cf-reviewer (assets/base/claude/agents/cf-reviewer.md) has no added-file question.
  • This repository: docs/verification/ holds 91 MB in 60 folders, and 79 records under project-management/ cite paths in it.

The shipped instructions hold project tooling to the tests product code gets

TSK-1031todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

The operator's quality asks of 2026-10-27, tests and coverage (D2). Issue #299 asks that every test-running target meet the coverage floor; TSK-1006 (EPC-024) builds that floor as a default, and TSK-1014 (this epic) fixes the ignored defaults.coverage. Neither says that a project's own tooling (scripts, build helpers, code generators, release and CI helpers, hook scripts) is code held to the same tests and floor. The shipped coverage rule speaks of "aggregate production-code coverage" and lets generated, vendor, fixture and test code be excluded, so an agent can read tooling as outside the rule, and adopters' tooling went untested and unchecked (issue #275's evidence: 59 JSON loaders and 21 git wrappers in one repository's tooling).

This task is the instruction half, small on its own; the default floor for tooling targets needs TSK-424's register and stays in TSK-1006.

Outcome: the shipped instructions say that project tooling is code that ships with tests, runs in a test target and counts toward the coverage floor; cf-stack wires a test target for the project's tooling when it has any; and cf-reviewer treats an untested tooling change as it treats untested product code.

Non-goals: the floor as an enforced default and its exemptions (TSK-1006); the defaults fix (TSK-1014); this repository's own untested scripts (AC-1 records them and routes them).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality asks amendment (2026-10-27)/The shipped instructions require typed code and typed data at every boundary

The shipped instructions require typed code and typed data at every boundary

TSK-1032todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #275 (items 1 and 6 and its comments of 2026-10-22) and the operator's quality asks of 2026-10-27, strict typing (D3). Three shipped texts steer agents away from strictness: cf-model-orchestrator/resources/quality/design-implementation.md:24-33 (types "where they prevent material errors"; no "stricter-compiler or language migrations merely to satisfy this rule"), cf-develop/SKILL.md:41-44 ("never force a stricter compiler") and cf-stack/SKILL.md:32-35 ("Do not mandate TypeScript, a validator library"). Under them, reviews passed Python at 5% annotated, hundreds of dict[str, Any] and hand-written validators, and TypeScript never type-checked as a whole.

This task takes TSK-427's former AC-1, AC-2, AC-4 and AC-5 (the texts, the review check, qualification and the journey), which are instruction and review-question changes small enough to ship in 4.0.0. The tooling per language (TSK-426), CodeFlow's own code passing the defaults and relaxations through the register (TSK-427) stay in EPC-024, because they need TSK-424's register and baseline.

Outcome: by default the shipped instructions require new and changed code to be fully typed, every escape type and suppression to carry an inline reason, and data crossing any boundary (files, network, process, environment, database, user input, another module's untyped output) to be parsed into a typed model that also validates it, with the language's standard library for it (for example Pydantic models in Python, zod schemas in TypeScript, serde types in Rust, structs with a validator in Go); a typed representation alone (a plain Python dataclass or a TypeScript interface) does not validate its input, so the instructions name both parts; TypeScript is the default for new projects and new files, and an existing JavaScript codebase type-checks its JavaScript in place; adding the project's type checker, linter and typed-model library is in scope for cf-develop; and cf-reviewer checks it.

Rules:

  • A project opts out of the default only by stating its reason in the project-owned part of AGENTS.md (its Stack standards) until TSK-424's register ships in 4.2.0, when TSK-427 moves the route to a register entry (the operator's decision of 2026-10-27).
  • TypeScript is the default for new projects and new files. An existing JavaScript codebase type-checks its JavaScript (for example checkJs with JSDoc types) instead of being rewritten (the operator's decision of 2026-10-27); AC-1 confirms the mechanism per toolchain.
  • The proportionality wording that remains applies to how much a boundary model holds, never to whether code is typed.

Non-goals: per-language tool setup and gate targets (TSK-426); CodeFlow's own code passing the defaults and the register route (TSK-427); rewriting adopters' existing code.

First-pass survey (planning, 2026-10-27, line tip 5f2fe3827)
  • assets/base/agents/skills/cf-model-orchestrator/resources/quality/design-implementation.md:24-33: types "where they prevent material errors"; trust-boundary parsing only for untrusted input ("Trusted internal values do not need redundant runtime validation").
  • assets/base/agents/skills/cf-develop/SKILL.md:41-44: points to that rule and adds "never force a stricter compiler, dependency, language, or stack migration merely for compliance".
  • assets/base/agents/skills/cf-stack/SKILL.md:29-35: reuse an existing type checker; "Do not mandate TypeScript, a validator library".
  • assets/base/claude/agents/cf-reviewer.md:40: already asks for meaningful type contracts, flags unchecked casts and other bypasses, and requires runtime parsing and validation at trust boundaries with invalid, absent and unexpected values tested. The gap is the default: it applies "where they prevent material errors", so it does not require new code to be fully typed or data at every boundary to be modelled. The extension keeps its runtime-validation requirement.
  • assets/base/testing/templates/example-node.json: no type-check target.

not recorded

Context

Issue #274 and the operator's quality asks of 2026-10-27, declare once (D4). Two adopting repositories held hundreds of hand copies of names, ids, team slugs, paths, settings and closed sets of strings, most bypassing a home that already existed (an exported constant nothing imports, a declared tuple compared against raw literals, a required-check guard covering two of six names), and 12 copied helper families (21 git wrappers, 59 JSON loaders, 82 repository-root lookups); a team rename needed 122 lines in 50 files edited by hand, and both reviews checked only that the edit was complete. The shipped instructions say "keep business rules single-sourced" and "stay DRY with judgment", but say nothing about declaring each value once as an enum, constant or type, and the reviewer is not asked about copies.

TSK-425 (EPC-024) is the define-once gate; it needs TSK-424's register and baseline. This task is the instruction-level part, small on its own.

Outcome: the shipped instructions require each value with meaning (names, ids, paths, settings, closed sets of strings, limits) to be declared once as a constant, enum or type that every use reads, generates from or checks; shared shapes and helpers to have one home that callers import; and code to be DRY and modular in that sense; and cf-reviewer asks whether a change copies a value or code that already has a home, a new unchecked copy being a material finding.

Rules:

  • The rule covers values across languages and file types (code, workflows, policy, infrastructure, config); where one language cannot import another's value, the copy is generated from or checked against the home.
  • A copy kept on purpose (a test's independent oracle, a stable protocol constant, documentation) is allowed with a stated reason; the instructions say which cases count.
  • This task delivers the review question that TSK-424 AC-5 first named ("whether a change copies a value that has a home"); TSK-424 AC-5 keeps only the exemption question.

Non-goals: the gate, adapters, the known-values file and exemptions (TSK-425, TSK-424); rewriting copies that adopters already hold.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality asks amendment (2026-10-27)/A non-trivial project uses its standard framework, in proportion

A non-trivial project uses its standard framework, in proportion

TSK-1034todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

The operator's quality asks of 2026-10-27, frameworks (D5); no issue or task existed. Adopters' agents build non-trivial user-facing surfaces as hand-written vanilla JavaScript, HTML and CSS (issue #275's evidence: about 450 plain JS and MJS gate and prototype files in one repository), and nothing in cf-stack or cf-design says when a project should use its type's standard framework instead. CodeFlow's own runtimes point both ways: the present web is Preact with TypeScript and esbuild, the docs portal is Astro with Starlight, but the shipped cf-present and cf-docs-portal design-system kits are a 1,357-line hand-written chrome.js that works with no build step, and an agent may read that kit as the model for product code.

Outcome: cf-stack and cf-design tell an agent to use the project type's standard framework (and its component, routing, state and build tooling) for a non-trivial project instead of hand-written vanilla JavaScript, HTML and CSS; a proportionality rule says when plain code is right (a one-page tool, a trivial script, a static page with no interaction); and the guidance states CodeFlow's position on its own bounded runtimes such as cf-present.

Rules:

  • "Standard framework" is chosen per project type and stack from current practice and the project's existing choice; the guidance names the decision criteria and examples, not one framework for everyone. An existing framework in the project is reused.
  • Adopting a new framework in an existing project is a stack decision the owner approves (cf-stack step 1); the guidance says so.
  • The position on CodeFlow's own runtimes says why each is built the way it is (for example, a reference kit that must open from a folder with no build step) and that it is not a model for product code, or changes it where AC-1 finds no such reason. Rebuilding a runtime is out of scope and becomes a tracked item if AC-1 recommends it.

Non-goals: the strict typing defaults (TSK-1032, TSK-426); rewriting adopters' existing surfaces; rebuilding cf-present or the docs portal.

First-pass survey (planning, 2026-10-27, line tip 5f2fe3827)

  • CodeFlow's own products: crates/codeflow-present/web/package.json (Preact 10, TypeScript 5.9, esbuild); assets/docs-portal/starter/package.json (Astro 7, Starlight).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality asks amendment (2026-10-27)/A doubled slash in a path is judged like its plain spelling, and the essential gate passes

A doubled slash in a path is judged like its plain spelling, and the essential gate passes

TSK-1035todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Found by TSK-435 (PR 364), diagnosed by its Codex review (.worktrees/tsk-435/target/review-TSK-435-codex-01.md, GPT-6 Astra, session 01a17fcb-712f-7450-901f-d6a412fbb4bc, "TMPDIR assessment") and reproduced for this record. This repository's essential gate target creates its run directory with mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cf.XXXXXX" and exports it as TMPDIR (.codeflow/test-config.json:151). On macOS the default TMPDIR ends in /, so the exported path holds // (.../T//cf.ab12cd). Under such a TMPDIR, 12 essential tests fail; with a plain path they pass. Every local essential run on a macOS host is red, and the failures hide real regressions in the same suites.

One of the 12 is a real protection miss, not a spelling difference: security/outward.rs:549 normalizes the candidate path, while security/interpreter.rs:152 (secret_path_spelling) strips an unnormalized HOME prefix, so a HOME spelled with a doubled slash can let a secret path read through the guard (refusal_journey/secret_paths.rs:67). Paths the guards compare reach adopters from their own environment, so this is a security defect wherever a root is spelled with //.

Codex's split of the 12, confirmed by the reproduction below:

GroupTestsCause named by the review
Absent-worktree handling (5)4 checkout_identity, remedy_clearing guards::clears_absent_worktreecrates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/repo.rs:993 rejects repeated separators, then canonicalization fails at hooks/git_discard.rs:224; git-guard refuses git worktree prune under git.discard_uncommitted instead of printing the absent-worktree remedy
Path-spelling assertions (6)3 target_repository, 3 test_gate_clitests compare the original spelling with normalized diagnostics: hooks_cli/target_repository.rs:682, :771, test_gate_cli.rs:1276, :1602, :1658
Secret path (1)refusal_journey secret_pathsthe unnormalized HOME prefix above

Reproduction (2026-10-27, line tip 5f2fe3827, test binaries built in the planning worktree, run outside the sandbox because one test file's name holds secret):

Outcome: a guard judges a path with a doubled slash, in the candidate or in the root it compares against (HOME, a checkout, a worktree, a configured store), exactly as its plain spelling, failing closed when it cannot; absent-worktree handling accepts a repeated separator; the tests compare normalized paths; and the essential gate's run directory holds no //, so the essential suite passes on macOS.

Rules:

  • Both sides of every prefix or containment comparison are normalized the same way before comparing; a path that cannot be normalized refuses.
  • The sibling sweep covers every comparison against HOME or another root in crates/codeflow-core/src/security/ and src/hooks/, not only the sites above.
  • The test-config fix (no // in the run directory) does not replace the product fix; a regression test sets a // root directly.

Order: build after TSK-1002 (PR 346), which reshaped the same guard code in security/interpreter.rs. TSK-1002 landed in PR 346 on 2026-10-30 and the depends_on edge is recorded. Before unblocking, the planning amendment rechecked TSK-1002's landed code for the HOME comparison (security/interpreter.rs:1447-1451 still strips an unnormalized HOME prefix); whatever it finds, this task keeps a regression case for the doubled-slash HOME miss (AC-2), even if TSK-1002 already repairs the mechanism.

Non-goals: other spellings the guard tasks already own (symbolic links, case, ~ forms).

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality asks amendment (2026-10-27)/A blocked task can be unblocked in its own pull request

A blocked task can be unblocked in its own pull request

TSK-1036complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #365 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, 48104f48b). A task whose record is blocked on the target cannot be moved to todo, or on to complete, by a pull request that names it. The only range that passes is a planning amendment on a plan/ branch whose Task: line names some open epic, even one the range does not touch. The documented route says otherwise: cf-method references/project-organization.md:320 says a status change "rides in the task's PR", and its table (:328) lists "blocked to todo | codeflow task status TSK-NNN todo". Blocking is asymmetric: todo -> blocked passes in the task's own pull request, because the merge-base still holds todo.

Sites, read on the line tip 5f2fe3827 (the issue cites 3.1.1 lines; the lifecycle.rs lines were refreshed on 53749287c on 2026-10-29):

  • crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:1874 check_task_anchor reads the status at the merge-base and projects only a reopen of a complete task (:1904-1931); start_gate (:2310) then refuses the blocked base record. This holds for epic tasks as well as standalone ones (code reading; the issue ran the standalone case).
  • crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/lifecycle.rs:1148 refuses blocked -> complete, and judge_range_against (:2197) judges the range whole, so a separate unblock commit does not help.
  • The refusal is raised at crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:1715 and crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/classification.rs:986; its remedy, crates/codeflow-core/src/remedy.rs:244-248, says to commit the record on this branch, which a record already on the target cannot satisfy.
  • crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/amendment.rs:10 lists a standalone task's change in an amendment ("listed, never refused"), but the planning class needs at least one Task: EPC-NNN.

Issue #400 (CodeFlow 3.1.1) is the same range judgment seen from a sync merge. judge_range_against compares each changed record only between the merge-base copy (:2209, one old copy at :2260) and the head copy, so a merge of main that carries blocked -> todo -> complete is read as blocked -> complete and refused (:1148). The triage of 2026-10-29 reproduced it on the line with codeflow ci: the sync merge range is refused, each of the two commits alone gave no work.records finding, and the plain two-commit range is refused too. The issue itself reports that pushing the sync in two steps passes; the pre-push hook was not run in the triage. The endpoint rule has a gap in the other direction: todo -> cancelled -> todo in one range nets to todo -> todo and passes, although its second step alone is refused because a cancelled task is terminal. Judging each step on its own commit closes both. As an argument about status transitions only, it accepts nothing that two separate pushes would not already accept; it proves transition legality, not review or authorship, which TSK-1066 owns. AC-7 carries it, because the fix is one change to the same function as AC-3.

TSK-1022 (this epic) is blocked on TSK-1002. Its unblock does not wait on this task: it rides in the EPC-022 batched amendment that adds depends_on: [TSK-1002] once PR 346 lands, a graph change that belongs in an amendment anyway, and the issue shows that route passes.

Widened 2026-10-30 for issue #424 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, by an adopter, the same root as #400). On main a record went blocked -> todo and then todo -> complete in two commits; a line holding it at blocked merged main in one step, and work.records refused the range as blocked -> complete. Merging main in two stages, one per step, passed each time and ended at the identical tree. The verdict on a status change shall not depend on how the same history was split into merges. AC-7 already requires the one-merge sync to pass; AC-8 adds the reporter's two shapes as fixtures and the same-tree comparison.

Outcome: a task's own pull request can move it from blocked to todo, and on to complete when its work is done, with the Blocker removal shown to the reviewer; the remedy names a route that works; and the documented status route matches what CI accepts; and a range is judged step by step, so a sync merge that carries legal steps passes and a hidden illegal step is refused.

Rules:

  • The unblock is judged on what the range does: the head record has no Blocker and the status passes through todo, so the start gate judges todo, as a reopen is projected today. Every other planning input still comes from the merge-base.
  • A head that unblocks a task whose blocker names an unfinished predecessor is judged by the ordinary depends_on rules; the unblock never admits work the graph does not.
  • A planning amendment that changes only standalone records needs no epic on its Task: line, or the docs say why one is required; AC-1 decides.

Non-goals: the repeated-closeout sequence (TSK-340), which this task builds on.

Outcome

Context

Issue #370, its work next part. codeflow work next trusts each task record's status, so a task whose work has landed but whose record was never completed is offered as ready, and a session may start finished work again. The backlog already holds the fact that would stop it: crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/readiness.rs backlog (:774) splits each record's claim branches into open and landed (split_landed, :638, proving a landing with git cherry in landed, :446), then marks the task Ready when no open branch remains (:846-847), so a task whose only branch has landed shows as ready. The landed names reach Backlog::landed but work next (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/work.rs:100) never prints them.

Planning found no live instance on this line: no ready EPC-022 task had a remote task/ branch merged into the line (checked on 2026-10-28 with work next --json and git branch -r --merged), so the defect is shown by code reading and AC-1 reproduces it on a fixture.

This is a defect in an existing command, reporting finished work as ready from facts it already computes, so it is placed in 4.0.0. The full audit of every drift class is TSK-1042 in EPC-023 (4.1.0).

Outcome: codeflow work next never offers as ready a task whose branch has landed in its target while its record is still open; it lists such a task as landed with the suggested codeflow task status command, and work claim refuses it with the same reason.

Rules:

  • A record-only branch (one that only filed or amended the record) does not count as landed work; AC-1 settles how that is told apart.
  • Nothing changes a status; the command reports and refuses.

Non-goals: the other drift classes (blocker cleared, idle claims, abandoned, owed completion, epic out of step), which are TSK-1042 in EPC-023.

A quick gate with no comparison base explains its full run

TSK-1039todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #371 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, 48104f48b, opened 2026-10-28 01:16Z). With targets that declare narrow paths and a complete green full run recorded at the merge base, the 3.1.1 pre-push hook runs every quick target on every push with the reason "no proven comparison base", about 550 to 580 seconds a push in the reporting repository, and the adopter is building its own selection map as a workaround. At 3.1.1 the hook reaches run_gate_exact(root, "quick") with default options (the issue cites git_hook.rs:1278 and gate.rs:152-153), and the selector has no base when --since is absent.

That path no longer exists on the 4.0.0 line. TSK-449 (complete, PR 325, 2026-10-24) removed test-config targets from the push on purpose: the push set is codeflow ci over each pushed range and runs no target (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs:5, docs/policy-reference.md:75, the test at crates/codeflow-cli/tests/hooks_cli.rs:5537, EPC-022 AC-125). The adopter runs 3.1.1, before TSK-449, so 4.0.0 removes the reported cost, and nothing in this task returns a test target to the push.

Issue #494 (filed 2026-11-01, also 3.1.1, 48104f48b, tag v3.1.1, merged 2026-10-12) is the same mechanism on two more pushes: the 3.1.1 push ran the quick gate (push_set.rs at that commit, lines 6 and 195), so one intermittent test at the tip refused a records-only push and the push made by codeflow work claim, and the task that fixes the flaky test could not be claimed. PR 325 (TSK-449, 2026-10-24) is after that release, so neither push can fail on a test on this line. This task owns the regression test for both shapes (AC-2). The issue's third ask, a recorded pre-existing failure, has no push to attach to here; a failure of the cited quick gate stays the builder's to report at ready.

What remains is the quick gate that a pull request cites when it is made ready. TSK-352 (complete) gave codeflow test a default base: comparison_base in crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/delivery.rs:388 takes an explicit --since, else the merge base of HEAD with the declared target of the task the branch carries. With no task on the branch (plan/, chore/), a detached head, or a task with no declared target (:405, :413, :416), it runs every target and prints only "no comparison base: ..." (:465-467), without saying that --since <commit> narrows, the route the issue itself found working.

Outcome: issue #371's push cost is confirmed gone on the 4.0.0 line and stays gone (a push runs no test-config target), and a quick or essential gate with no comparison base runs every target and states its reason; it names --since <commit> as the way to narrow only where --since can narrow (row A below), and otherwise says that local narrowing is unavailable (row B).

Credit rows (TSK-1044 settles which one holds; every criterion below that narrows, skips, reuses or recommends --since is checked against both):

RowWhenRequired behavior
Athe operator adopted a protected recorder in TSK-1044the positive journeys: selection narrows, skips and reuse happen only from attested executions
Bno protected recorderevery requested target runs and the reason is reported; no output recommends --since where it cannot narrow; positive narrowing, skip and reuse journeys are marked deferred in the epic's planning notes

Rules:

  • TSK-449's push contract holds: a push neither runs nor waits for a test-config target.
  • The base stays TSK-352's rule: an exact commit from --since or the carried task's line, never a mutable branch name and never the push's old tip; an unproven base runs everything and names why.
  • A default base for a branch with no task is out of scope: --since is a working manual route, and an automatic one would be a feature (4.1.0) with its own planning.

Non-goals: result reuse (TSK-355); the push budget itself.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality follow-up amendment (2026-10-28)/A pull request body edit never cancels the required policy check

A pull request body edit never cancels the required policy check

TSK-1040todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #373 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, opened 2026-10-28 01:17Z). The generated .github/workflows/codeflow-policy.yml runs on pull_request_target with types opened, synchronize, reopened, edited, ready_for_review, in one concurrency group per pull request with cancel-in-progress true for those runs (assets/base/ci/codeflow-policy.yml:40-53). When the body is edited seconds after a push, the edited run cancels the push's run; the required "commit standards" check on that head then shows once cancelled and once passed, and the adopter's PR stayed blocked until someone re-ran it (runs 40613620628 and 40613623003, 2026-10-28; five more cancelled runs on three branches on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27). Turning cancel-in-progress off alone does not fix it: with the default single-slot queue GitHub keeps one pending run per group and cancels it when a newer one arrives. The shipped comment (:29-36) states the cancellation as intended, reasoning that the surviving run reads the current body from the API; the required check on the pushed head is what it loses. This repository's own .github/workflows/codeflow-policy.yml carries the same block.

Outcome: no pull request event cancels or replaces the run that judges a pushed head's required "commit standards" check; every queued run completes; a run that judged a body, head or base that changed while it ran fails with its own message so the run queued by that change decides; and the body is logged by digest, never as text.

Rules (the issue's proposal, to be confirmed by AC-1):

  • Concurrency keeps the per-PR group and the per-run group for push, schedule and dispatch, with cancel-in-progress: false and the queue mode that keeps every pending run (queue: max, GitHub changelog of 2026-05-07), if AC-1 confirms the key and its limits.
  • A last step reads the pull request again and fails if the head SHA, the base branch or the body changed while the run judged them, and fails closed when the read fails. The base commit is not compared, since a push to the base fires no pull request event.
  • The body is logged as a sha256 digest.
  • Limits are documented: the queue's 100-run cap (past it a newest push fails closed), the window after a run's last read, two API calls per run on the shared token's rate limit, and linter support for the new key.

Non-goals: codeflow-ci.yml's cancellation of superseded runs (TSK-1026, which builds on this task's rule).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality follow-up amendment (2026-10-28)/Gate evidence cannot be redirected or forged by an agent session

Gate evidence cannot be redirected or forged by an agent session

TSK-1044complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Source: the Codex security review of TSK-337 (PR 375) on 2026-10-27, findings 1 and 2 (.worktrees/tsk-337/target/review-TSK-337-codex-01.md, session 01a18068-1704-7682-a9e8-322c84d7164f). Both concern the durable gate evidence under ~/.codeflow/gate-runs/<repo>/<run-id>/, which any process running as the user can write, an agent session included.

  • Writes follow planted links (CWE-59). A full gate copies its run directory into the durable root with copy_evidence (crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/gate.rs:513, :629), which uses create_dir_all and fs::copy and rejects no link at a destination ancestor, directory or final file. The run directory is visible before the targets finish (:345). A process that can write gate-runs can plant a link there, and a later gate, possibly run with wider file access, writes through it outside the evidence directory. The reviewer reproduced the link following with a scratch harness of this copier; no end-to-end privileged attack was run. The run directory itself is already created through the anchored helper crate::contained::Tree (gate.rs:533).
  • Skip credit from records anyone can write (CWE-345). green_base (crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/delivery.rs:330) accepts a run.json by Git tree, config digest and claimed successful, clean and complete execution; target_covered (:617) checks consistency of the record's own claims, and a match removes an opted-in content target from a quick or essential run (:557). Records are not authenticated or bound to a commit SHA, and the ownership and permission check (read_owned_record, :236) cannot tell an agent from the real recorder, since both run as the same user. A writer of gate-runs can forge local skip credit in an adopter project that opts into reusable content targets.

Scope of each finding:

  • Link-following writes affect every gate that writes evidence, default full runs included: a full run with a revision writes its durable copy (gate.rs:506, copy_evidence at :629), and the copier has no platform exclusion, so containment is needed on macOS, Linux and Windows (where the threat is junctions and other reparse points).
  • Forged selection credit does not reach hosted CI (--all, .github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml), a default full run (all targets forced when --since is absent, gate.rs:186), integration (integrate.rs:585) or Windows (no local selection credit). It does reach every selection-capable run: quick and essential runs and a full run with --since, which reaches the same record-based selection (delivery.rs:557). This repository declares no reusable content target today.

Who can write gate-runs today: Claude sessions, through the shipped presets' sandbox write grant (assets/base/settings/default.json:368, acceptEdits.json:369, bypass-sandboxed.json:447, and this repository's .claude/settings.json:488), which full gates in a sandboxed session need for the evidence preflight (gate_guard.rs:241) and the durable copy (gate.rs:513). Codex builders would have had the same access; TSK-337 (PR 375) drops that grant from cf-builder and amends its AC-5.

Outcome: no gate writes outside the durable evidence directory whatever links or special files are planted in it, and no record a session or a candidate's tests can write removes a requested target from any gate run; the shipped Claude presets keep, narrow or drop the gate-runs grant by the operator's recorded decision, which states what it means for running full gates in an agent session.

Rules:

  • Secure by default (the operator's rule of 2026-10-24): fail closed when a check cannot be sure; bind trust to identities a requester cannot forge, never to file contents, names or ownership the requester controls; and remove a feature that cannot be made sound rather than patching its bypasses.
  • Evidence writes use anchored traversal (the existing crate::contained::Tree, or its equivalent for the home directory): every component is opened without following links, links and special files are refused at ancestors, directories and final files, and files are created without following an existing name.
  • Skip credit comes only from a recorder whose authority the agent session and the candidate's tests cannot exercise. A key or token they can read does not count. If no such recorder is sound on a platform, local selection credit from these records is withdrawn there and every requested target runs.
  • Ordinary run reports stay writable and readable; cited run ids for landing evidence keep working. Readable is not trusted: a record written before this change, or by any process the session can run, stays report-only and is never promoted to credit.
  • Any uncertain case (an unreadable, unauthenticated, pre-upgrade or replayed record, or authentication that is unavailable) runs the requested target or refuses; it never grants credit.
  • Decision owner (cf-method/references/autonomy.md: a material security boundary the brief does not fix is the operator's): the operator decides whether the shipped Claude presets keep, narrow or drop the ~/.codeflow/gate-runs grant, and whether a protected recorder is adopted. The builder investigates and brings the options with the full-gate route for each. Until the operator decides, the interim state holds: writable reports earn no credit; an unresolved grant or recorder authority authorizes nothing that depends on it (TSK-353's skips, TSK-355's reuse, TSK-1039's --since narrowing); and the containment repairs of AC-2 proceed, since they do not wait on the decision. The decision clears when the operator's choice is recorded in this task's Closeout and in the epic's planning notes.

Non-goals: result reuse itself (TSK-355, which follows this task's trust rule); the Codex profile's grant (TSK-337); hosted CI.

First-pass survey (planning, 2026-10-28, line tip after PR 374)
  • Writers: testing/gate.rs:345 (run directory, through crate::contained::Tree), :498 (the local run.json, written by pathname with std::fs::write), :513 and :629 (durable copy); testing/gate_guard.rs:241-243 (the evidence write probe: create_dir_all follows ancestor links, then a create_new file).
  • Readers: testing/delivery.rs:56 (durable_root), :236 (read_owned_record: O_NOFOLLOW on the final file only; ancestor directories are followed), :317 (credit_home), :330 (green_base), :557 and :617 (credit).
  • The anchored helper crates/codeflow-core/src/contained.rs refuses links and Windows reparse points at every component but does not isolate hard links or Unix mounts (:18), so choosing it is not by itself proof for a leaf.
  • This survey is a start: AC-1 sweeps the whole codebase.
  • Docs and guidance that cite the durable home: assets/base/rules/worktrees.md:138, assets/base/agents/skills/cf-ship/references/pr-evidence.md:124, docs/delivery.md:142, docs/capabilities.md:370, docs/harness-posture.md.
  • Grants: the three shipped Claude presets and this repository's settings above; assets/base/codex/config.toml:264 (comment) and the cf-builder grant TSK-337 removes.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Away session amendment (2026-10-28)/An away session's charter, decisions and owed actions survive compaction and render as one report

An away session's charter, decisions and owed actions survive compaction and render as one report

TSK-1045todo

After this merges, a session left to run without its user keeps one activation per clone that admits every claim, seat, replacement.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a session left to run without its user keeps one activation per clone that admits every claim, seat, replacement, landing and job renewal before it happens, and a user can read one report of what happened and what they must do.

Context

The operator asked on 2026-10-28 for a standard command or skill a user sets when away, so work keeps going without stalling, is tracked, and ends in one consolidated report with action items (things to run, review or approve, and anything else). The operator widened it the same day: the capability is generic, never tied to a time of day; it adapts to how and when the user engages and to what the user uses it for; and it covers keeping the work going, doing it right, following the cf-* procedures and rules, tracking, and the report. This task is the engine half: the durable state, the admission of every effect, the effects' commands and the report. TSK-1046 is the skill that runs the session on it; the field trial and harness research are recorded there.

Why CodeFlow code is needed: a session's working memory does not survive compaction, a restart or a usage-limit stop, and nothing CodeFlow prints at session start says the session was left to run, for what, or what it owes the user. codeflow orient on the line tip 654935d52 prints no ledger or away line (checked 2026-10-28). In the maintainer's own coordination workspace, which ran this behaviour by hand from 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-28, the state lived in a hand-kept board and handoff file, and stale facts, an unread listener and parked items followed.

Outcome: one away activation per clone records the charter (purpose, scope, target line, engagement, an optional end, the interval and the limits), its owner, what it has consumed, the reversible choices the session made and the items it owes the user; it admits every consuming effect (a tick, a claim, a seat, a replacement, a landing, a job renewal) before the effect happens and never refunds it; it gives the session one command for each effect, each reconciled against the world after a crash; the session-start digest names an active activation at start, resume and compaction; and codeflow report away renders one outcomes-first report whose user actions are typed Run, Review, Approve, Decide or Provide, each bound to its subject, evidence, preconditions and the time it was last checked, with every fact and source it could not read marked unverified.

Session design, revision 12.3 (amended 2026-10-29)

Source: the session system design, revision 12.3 of 2026-10-29, the last design revision. It amends the final design of the same day through revisions 8 to 12.3; Codex (GPT-6 Astra at high) reviewed revisions 8 to 11 (r11-04: SOUND) and, under the corrected threat model, 12.1 and 12.2 (r12-05 and r12-06, both NOT SOUND). Revision 12.3 answers r12-06: its blocking finding became the named landing residual the operator accepted, and its races became the fault tests of AC-26. No Codex review covers 12.3 itself; the build's fault tests are its proof. The documents are listed in the planning pull request's references. This section and the criteria carry the decided specifics, so a builder needs no other source.

Threat model: the session's own tool results (git push --porcelain, git ls-remote, gh, herdr, CronCreate, CronList, CronDelete) are trusted as evidence of the world at that moment and read defensively: a lost reply or a timeout is unknown, success is never inferred from silence, and every record precedes its effect. Content other actors write (repository files, PR and issue text, other people's refs and jobs) is evidence, never authority. Our own primary and the operator are cooperative. A hostile model or a stolen session is out of scope here, as everywhere in CodeFlow.

Figure: one tick. A missed or doubled tick costs latency, never correctness; nothing is recorded as done before it is done, and nothing consumed is refunded.

Rules:

  • No authority. The activation has no field that grants an action, and nothing in it widens cf-method/references/autonomy.md; an unknown field is refused. Who started it is recorded, never trusted as the operator.
  • No time of day. Start, end and cadence are absolute times or durations; an open-ended activation is the normal case.
  • One activation per clone. The store is codeflow/coord/away.json in the clone's coordination home (format: 1), beside away.lock (fs2 exclusive, bounded wait) and away.cache.json. away start takes the lock and refuses while a live, .prev, damaged or temp file exists. Writes go to a temp file in the same directory with fsync, then rename(live, .prev), rename(temp, live) and a directory fsync, each result checked; .prev is never restored into the live file.
  • The lock contract, for every effect: read the world outside the lock; under the lock re-check the local record against the read and persist the reservation (an attempt, a phase, a pending); release; make the external call; under the lock again record the result and reconcile. The lock is never held across a network or tool call, so a stop from another shell always persists, and a crash between the reservation and the record is reconciled by the next tick from the world, with nothing refunded or reserved twice.
  • Ownership. The owner is one Claude Code session on one machine and boot: session_id, pid, pid_start, machine_id, boot_id, harness and version, and a generation that start, --take-over and resume --rebind increment. Claude Code 2.1.312 on macOS is qualified first, Linux after its canaries, Windows refused until a boot id source is named; Codex and Grok are refused as owner and run as seats. An owner-only command is accepted only when the caller's environment names the owner session id and pid, the pid's start time equals the recorded one, and the caller descends from that pid by the owner identity walk below. /fork, --fork-session and /branch give a new session id and are refused as owner; after /branch, away resume --rebind is attended. After a changed boot id only away status, report away and away end are accepted.
  • Ticks. A fire carries the watcher nonce in its prompt; a retired, unknown or missing nonce consumes nothing. Admitted ticks are at least half the recorded interval apart. The nonce only refuses: a caller-supplied value never grants more than a hand tick would.
  • Claims follow the cooperative claim contract: a claim branch is created once at a claim commit, an object only this activation produces, and no CodeFlow clone writes to a branch it did not create. Under it, ls-remote settles an unclear push: our claim commit at the tip is ours; an absent branch is retried, three pushes in all; any other value is lost and the unit is skipped. Someone who recreates the branch at our exact commit reads as us, a boundary the contract accepts.
  • Seats are admitted, dispatched once by the owner and acknowledged once by the seat. A lost seat is replaced only on recorded evidence, on a fresh branch and worktree; the old branch, worktree and pull request are quarantined and never reused, so two seats never share a target. 4.0.0 has no qualified process-containment guarantee, so a quarantine is released only by the attended away seat --terminated, and its cost is reported every tick.
  • Landing into an integration line is unattended under its admission checks; landing into main or any protected branch is refused by name and stays the operator's. GitHub's merge API pins the head, not the destination, so a retarget between the pre-merge read and the merge lands elsewhere and is caught by verification after, which blocks every further landing on the clone until the attended unblock (the named residual for C4, E1 and E2).
  • The scheduled job is created by the user at start and renewed and cleaned by the activation: one pending renewal at a time, resolved by one atomic promotion or abandoned before anything is deleted, and only jobs this activation owns are deleted. The exact-copy watcher contract: a job whose prompt carries a nonce this activation issued is reconciled as this activation's job, whoever created it, because the nonce is random and appears only in prompts the activation wrote.
  • Security paths. A unit whose diff touches an entry of the governing security_paths list (AC-25) lands only on a full-assurance approval from another lineage at its exact head; until one answers it waits, unattended, and each tick re-probes.
  • Time. Every activation with an end has deadline_mono on the suspend-inclusive counter (Linux CLOCK_BOOTTIME, macOS mach_continuous_time, Windows QueryInterruptTime), never extended.
  • Owed items and decisions live in the activation (design decision 5): id-scoped keys and per-item revisions; the ledger's follow-ups (TSK-422) are read with a budget and listed beside, never written. A fulfils link closes an item when the fact changes, so the report never lists an action already done. A Note is shown but is not an action. Each reversible choice stays in its home as autonomy.md "While a question is open" says; the activation holds one entry per choice with that pointer, its status and what reverses it.
  • Limits are the ones CodeFlow counts: an end time or duration, units claimed, seats admitted (a total-attempt budget: every admitted seat, replacements included, counts for the rest of the activation) and admitted ticks. Usage, tokens and spend are advisory telemetry where a harness reports them; a configured usage, token or spend limit is refused at away start (design decision 3).
  • Live or marked. The report observes the forge through the ledger's bounded observer (coord/observe.rs) unless --offline, prints each forge fact with its observation time, and lists every source it could not read. Exit 0 means the command ran; completeness is reported separately in text and JSON.
  • Stages are named apart: implemented, reviewed, landed on a line, merged to main, released.
  • The cadence default is 30 minutes, read from [sweep] interval_minutes in .codeflow/project.toml, which this task or TSK-1037, whichever lands first, defines as the one interval key for scheduled sweeps, attended or away.
  • CodeFlow schedules nothing and runs no agent (docs/product.md:70-71). The harness fires the ticks; the activation records the jobs it owns and never claims a trigger can wake a sleeping host or restore quota.
  • The saved report and its JSON never use the NEED YOUR ATTENTION heading (.codeflow/rules/writing.md:141-143 keeps it for replies); they label the section "Your actions". Ledger display ids (FU, LN, WS) stay out of tracked records and PR bodies.

Non-goals: a scheduler or daemon; sending the report outside the machine (a hard gate, autonomy.md:79); the sweep checklist (TSK-1037); an open-PR classifier (TSK-1041); and, each tracked once in EPC-023 with its revisit event, away mode on another harness's route (Codex-owned activations and job kinds with no list surface, TSK-1074), cross-clone claim arbitration for the title-slug case (TSK-1075) and usage as a stop trigger (TSK-1076). The delegate heartbeat and Stop lifecycle stay with TSK-440 (EPC-025).

Owner identity walk

Figure: the walk carries each hop's whole tuple, so a process that exits and whose pid is reused between iterations fails on its ppid or start time. Two reader limits stay: an intermediate hop is indistinguishable only when pid, ppid and start all repeat within the reader's resolution, and the owner, identified by pid and start time alone, when both repeat. Descendants of the owner are the owner's processes by design, a cooperative boundary.

Preconditions and residuals: accepted by the operator on 2026-10-29

The operator accepted the design's ten residuals and its four preconditions, as listed in the revision 12.3 summary, on 2026-10-29 (relayed to this planning PR by the coordinator). The residuals: the landing destination is not bound at the merge (C4, E1, E2: a retarget in the final window is caught after and blocks, not prevented); an effect dispatched before a stop can complete (A18); a reboot ends the activation (O2); an escaped seat is outside the activation's reach (P2); and the deferred rows E9, H2, H3 and H7. The preconditions:

  • Ruleset C on integration/, strict and with no bypass actor for the merging identity. TSK-1080 (EPC-022, the content-policy design's unit U5) writes it through codeflow remote protect; on this repository it exists once the operator's enablement run follows TSK-336 and TSK-1080 on main. Amended 2026-10-29 by the content policy amendment, which filed TSK-1080 (until then this note said the unit's task was not yet filed and an amendment would add it as a predecessor of the landing journey). No task edge is added: the dependency is of the landing journey on a forge where ruleset C exists, not of this task's code on TSK-1080's, and until the ruleset is in place the activation refuses every landing and owes the user an item to configure it (AC-22(a)), so this task builds and tests without it.
  • The cooperative claim contract (Rules, AC-14), stated in the docs.
  • The exact-copy watcher contract (Rules, AC-21), stated in the docs.
  • security_paths as a new policy key with the default list, fail closed and guarded against weakening (AC-25). No other record owns the key, so this task adds it.
Amendment of 2026-10-29 (session design revision 12.3)

The record is amended to the reviewed design. Removed, each with its reason:

  • The work-stream and coordinator-lease keying, and the edge to TSK-439: the activation is keyed to the clone and owned by one session identified by session id, pid with start time, machine id and boot id; it holds no ledger role, so a fresh adopter can record an activation through the shipped CLI before TSK-439 lands (design decision 4). The edges are now TSK-1047 and TSK-1038.
  • The tick claim with an idempotency key: replaced by admitted ticks under the clone lock, with the nonce and spacing checks (AC-15).
  • Reconciling an uncertain effect against live state before a retry, as a general rule: each effect now has its own reconciliation (the claim read of AC-14, the seat evidence of AC-17, the landing phases of AC-23, the watcher listing of AC-21).
  • The ledger schema change and the action fields on follow add: owed items live in the activation file (design decision 5); the ledger is read, never written, so no schema version changes.
  • The heartbeat refresh and the heartbeat-timeout warning: the activation holds no coordinator lease, so it has no heartbeat to keep fresh.
  • The usage, token and spend limit: no harness reports usage in a qualified form (design decision 3); usage as a stop trigger is TSK-1076.
  • Cancelling the armed route when the fire limit is reached: job cleanup follows AC-21's ownership rules instead.

The criteria keep their numbers; a removed clause is marked in place with its reason, and AC-14 to AC-27 are new.

Canaries owed before "supported" on a platform
  • Parent-chain readers with sub-second start times per OS (macOS libproc PROC_PIDTBSDINFO; Linux /proc/<pid>/stat fields 4 and 22 with CLK_TCK), each qualified to return one process incarnation per tuple, with the two indistinguishable reuse cases recorded with the platform's resolution.
  • Machine id (macOS IOPlatformUUID, Linux /etc/machine-id, Windows MachineGuid) and boot id (macOS kern.bootsessionuuid, which could not be read from the planning sandbox; Linux /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id; Windows unnamed, so Windows ownership stays refused).
  • gh pr merge, CronCreate and CronDelete running in a scheduled turn without a permission prompt; --match-head-commit refusing a moved head and the strict ruleset refusing a stale head at a scratch forge; the claim commit through the real hooks and CI; the exact gh JSON field names; Herdr's pane process fields.
  • Sleep across a tick on each OS; Windows rename under a held reader; scheduled jobs firing in a conversation after /branch.
Planning survey (line tip 654935d52, 2026-10-28)

The Roles bullet below is superseded by the amendment of 2026-10-29; the rest stands as read on that day.

  • Ledger: codeflow follow records holder, done_when, --awaiting-operator, --next-check and typed links (docs/cli.md "Remember"); only a fulfils link closes an item (crates/codeflow-core/src/coord/due.rs:10, :503-519); its home is the clone's common git directory (ADR-0086); follow snapshot --output refuses to overwrite (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/follow.rs:232). It has no action type.
  • Roles (superseded): a writing verb acts as the role in CODEFLOW_COORD_ROLE with an instance and generation, checked against the log, and a caller with no role only reads (docs/coordination-ledger.md:278-290). This made TSK-439 a predecessor while owed items were ledger follow-ups.
  • Session start: session-orient runs at startup|resume|clear|compact|fork in Claude (assets/base/settings/default.json:544-553) and at startup|resume|clear|compact in Codex (assets/base/codex/hooks.json:18-20), so a digest line survives compaction on both.
  • TSK-440 (EPC-025, 4.0.0) adds the ledger to the start digest, a turn-end overdue check and observations only through coord/observe.rs, never unattended (its AC-4, AC-8). This task does not wait for it: its digest line reads the activation only, offline. Whichever of the two lands second folds the away line into the stream section, so the digest shows owed operator items once, and makes coord status show the typed actions as report away does. Operator items have one renderer, TSK-440's coord/surface.rs: whichever of the two lands first creates it with the action types, and the digest, coord status and the report's "Your actions" all render owed items through it. The Claude preset gets one Stop entry, TSK-440's turn-end check; this task adds none.
  • codeflow report ceremony (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/report.rs:18) is the existing report namespace, so the report is codeflow report away, adopted from the Codex discovery.
  • Shared files: hooks/orient.rs with TSK-423, TSK-440 and TSK-1037; work.rs and readiness.rs with TSK-1047 and TSK-1038; the policy schema with every task that adds a policy key.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Away session amendment (2026-10-28)/A session set away keeps the work going and on its procedures, and hands back one report

A session set away keeps the work going and on its procedures, and hands back one report

TSK-1046todo

After this merges, a user can tell a session to carry on without them, and it keeps in-scope work moving on its procedures.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a user can tell a session to carry on without them, and it keeps in-scope work moving on its procedures, lands reviewed units into integration lines, leaves `main` and the other attended steps to the user, and hands back one report.

Context

The operator asked on 2026-10-28 for a standard command or skill a user invokes or sets when away, so work keeps going as far as it can without stalling, is tracked, and ends in one consolidated report with action items (things to run, review or approve, and anything else). The same day the operator widened it: the capability is generic, never tied to night or any time of day; the agent adapts to how and when the user engages and responds, and to what the user uses it for; and it covers keeping the work going, making sure the work is done right, making sure the cf-* procedures, skills and rules are followed while the user is away, tracking, and the report. The operator also set the base rule TSK-1047 enforces: new work starts from the live tip of the branch that holds the work it needs (main when main has it, else the line that has it), and the target's current tip is merged in before review.

This task is the session half: a managed skill (working name /cf-away) and its wiring. TSK-1045 is the durable activation, decision index, owed actions and report it runs on.

Outcome: a user tells a session to carry on without them, for any purpose and any length of time; with the user present, the session records the activation (TSK-1045) and arms its first scheduled job; at each admitted tick it claims ready in-scope units, opens one builder seat per claimed unit and one reviewer seat per revision, replaces a lost seat on a fresh branch through the orchestrator's fallback, lands reviewed, gated units into integration lines, renews and cleans its own scheduled job, checks that each unit is on the cf-* procedure and rules its stage needs, rechecks changeable state live, records the reversible choices it makes, and lists as items for the user only the steps that stay theirs (landing into main, a landing mismatch, a quarantined worktree, a security-path unit's wait, decisions); it adapts when and how it asks to how the user engages, keeps one report current, ends on the user's word or the activation's end, and hands back the final report. (Amended 2026-10-29 to the session design, revision 12.3.)

Design (session design revision 12.3, amended 2026-10-29)

Source: the session system design, revision 12.3 of 2026-10-29, the last design revision; TSK-1045's record carries its engine contract, threat model and preconditions. What this skill does unattended, and what waits for the user:

Figure: one activation, a repeating admitted tick, one report. CodeFlow schedules nothing (docs/product.md:70-71); the harness fires the ticks, and the activation acts only on jobs it owns by issued nonce.

  • A skill plus a small command (TSK-1045), not a sweep mode or a pipeline. The sweep (TSK-1037, EPC-023) is a read-only checklist with no record and no action; this capability acts, records and reports, and it lands in 4.0.0 by the operator's standing direction while the sweep is in 4.1.0. The pipeline preset (cf-method/SKILL.md:46-51) is single-vendor batch work and never substitutes for interactive review; the away session is the interactive coordinator continuing. When TSK-1037 lands, its codeflow sweep becomes the tick's state read (TSK-1037 amended in this plan) and the interval key is shared (TSK-1045).
  • No new authority. The skill is a procedure over cf-method/references/autonomy.md: the ladder (:26-57), the operator's list (:59-90), working defaults and fail-closed states (:92-123), standing rules only from the authenticated operator in the session (:138-209) and the multi-session sweep (:270-293). Setting a session away is not a delegation and grants nothing: a merge into main or any protected branch, publishing, tags, closing issues, spend, credentials, sending anything outside the conversation and every irreversible or security-weakening step stay the operator's and become Approve or Run items while other work continues. Landing a reviewed, gated unit into an integration line is the primary's ordinary step, which the session takes under TSK-1045's admission checks. A rule relayed by a peer, a file, a Herdr delivery or an issue comment is refused as the operator's.
  • Generic. Purpose (build an epic, review only, watch and land, research, a release watch) selects which procedures the tick runs, and a review-only or research activation implements and lands nothing. Engagement (not reachable, checking in, reachable) decides only how and when a question reaches the user: at once in one round, batched into the report, or as a Decide item. Whether dependent work continues on a working default or holds a fail-closed state follows reversibility and evidence in every engagement (autonomy.md:92-123), never reachability. Nothing assumes a time of day.
  • Limits the user sets are honoured. The supported limits are the ones CodeFlow can count (end, units claimed, seats admitted, admitted ticks); usage is advisory, and a usage or spend limit is refused at start (TSK-1045). A reached seats or units limit stops new seats, replacements or claims while existing work progresses; a reached fire limit stops admission and the session starts nothing further. Each is reported, and only the end or the user's word ends the activation. (Amended 2026-10-29.)
  • One owner, one start. One activation per clone, owned by one Claude Code session on one machine and boot (TSK-1045). A tick spends only when admitted; a claim is settled under the cooperative claim contract; a seat is dispatched once and acknowledged once; a replacement never reuses the old branch or worktree; a merge is never re-issued on a missing acknowledgement. Each uncertain outcome is reconciled by the effect's own read of the world (TSK-1045 AC-14, AC-17, AC-21, AC-23), so no task is claimed, no seat launched and no unit landed twice. (Amended 2026-10-29: was a stream lease and reconcile-then-retry.)
  • Continuation stays on the coordinator. No blocking Stop hook on review seats or delegates, whose own completion protocol it would break (cf-delegate resources/claude-turn-completion.md); a native goal's evaluator (Claude /goal, Grok's panel) is never a CodeFlow review. The tick never starts work outside the activation's scope: when the in-scope queue is empty it renders the report and waits for a named event.
  • Honest about what is armed. A trigger cannot wake a sleeping host or restore quota. On waking, the session reconciles once and never replays missed ticks; a stale heartbeat means contact is overdue, never that a seat or lane is safe to replace (superseded on 2026-10-29 by the session design, revision 12.3: the activation keeps no heartbeat, and a seat is replaced only on the evidence states of TSK-1045 AC-17). A Claude Code job expires seven days after its creation, so the activation renews its own job from day five. After a reboot the activation is reported and ended, never continued; away start --from copies its charter forward with the user present.
  • Attended only (amended 2026-10-29). Landing into main; clearing a landing mismatch block; releasing a quarantined worktree; starting the activation and arming its first job; a second activation in the clone; rebinding after /branch; after a reboot, anything but status, report and end; irreversible or security-weakening steps and the operator's decisions. A security-path unit whose review has only one lineage waits, unattended, and each tick probes for another. Away mode on another harness's route and usage as a stop trigger are tracked in EPC-023 (TSK-1074, TSK-1076).
  • Working name /cf-away and codeflow away (reversible; naming is the operator's taste and is asked).
Reconciliation with the Codex discovery (session 01a180b0-a76b-7393-9f2b-a4a31a945c15, GPT-6 Astra at high, 2026-10-28)

Codex discovered independently on the same line tip and reached the same shape: a cf-away skill, the ledger for commitments, a generated report, native goals or schedules waking the interactive coordinator, no daemon, no headless runs, no new permission mode, and autonomy.md as the only authority policy.

Adopted from it: the report verb in the existing report namespace (codeflow report away); the activation's owner, trigger, permission mode and resource limits, with a repeated start reconciling instead of arming a second trigger (superseded on 2026-10-29 by the session design, revision 12.3: a second away start in the clone is refused, AC-13(a) and TSK-1045 AC-2(c)); the Provide action type and the Note that is shown but not counted; per-action preconditions bound to repository, branch and SHA, so a moved head shows the item as stale; "Your actions" in saved reports, since writing.md keeps NEED YOUR ATTENTION for replies; exit 0 kept apart from completeness; the failure-replay, crash and concurrency tests (TSK-1045 AC-9); the stance on goal evaluators, stale heartbeats, sleeping hosts, delegate Stop hooks and empty queues above; Grok production and building staying unqualified (cf-model-orchestrator/resources/routing/transport.md, the seat table); and TSK-1038 as a predecessor, so an unattended session never restarts landed work.

Where this plan differs, and why:

  • Placement. Codex would add no away feature to 3.2.0 and would build it after TSK-1037, TSK-1041 and TSK-1042 in EPC-023. The operator's standing direction is that features land in the current release, and the request was for now, so the coordinator placed it in 3.2.0. The first unit is shaped to wait on no 4.1.0 work: TSK-1045 reads the landed ledger, local git and the ledger's observer, and the tick reads state by hand until TSK-1037's sweep lands and replaces that read (TSK-1037 amended). No 4.1.0 task is pulled forward; whether to pull TSK-1041, TSK-1042 and TSK-1037 into 4.0.0 is asked of the operator, who also confirms the placement itself when back. Codex's review of PR 379 agreed the 3.2.0 shape works without those three.
  • Ledger adoption. Codex ordered TSK-439, TSK-440 and TSK-423 before the report. Its review of PR 379 showed TSK-439 is a true prerequisite: TSK-422 binds roles only through test fixtures, and a caller with no claimed role only reads (docs/coordination-ledger.md:278-290), so TSK-1045 now depends on TSK-439 and keys the activation to its streams and leases. TSK-440 and TSK-423 stay off the path: whichever of TSK-1045 and TSK-440 lands second folds the away line into the stream digest, and this task carries its own guidance. Superseded on 2026-10-29 by the session design, revision 12.3: the activation is keyed to the clone and its owner session, owed items live in the activation file, and TSK-1045 depends on TSK-1047 and TSK-1038 instead of TSK-439.
  • The base rule (TSK-1047) and the generic, adaptive scope came from the operator after the discovery brief, so Codex did not cover them.

Recorded for others: Codex found ADR-0086's statement that Grok has only PreToolUse hooks outdated against current Grok docs (Stop, SessionStart and compaction events exist; only PreToolUse blocks). That belongs to TSK-440's Grok adapter criterion (AC-3), not to this task.

Field trial (the maintainer's coordination workspace, 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-28)

The maintainer ran this behaviour by hand: a coordinator session swept lanes every 30 minutes, kept a board and a handoff file, and ran shell scripts for a push queue and a landing loop. Each failure below maps to a tick step and a qualification case (AC-10):
