The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a maintainer can ask the line's binary for the exact shipped bytes of any managed file at any published release, and a release cannot be prepared without adding its own bases to that pack.

Context

Source: the operator's retention decision of 2026-10-17 (every published release's bases in the binary, about 0.6 MB then, advisory 2 MB budget) and SPC-015.

A three-way merge in codeflow update needs the pristine shipped copy of the file at the version the project installed it from. Today that copy is the project's own .codeflow/.baseline/<dest>. This task makes the binary the source instead: it embeds the shipped scaffold of every published release (v2.0.0 and v2.1.0 with 44 asset files each, v3.0.0 with 194, v3.1.0 and v3.1.1 with 199, at their tags) as one compressed, read-only pack, with an index that names each retained release, and gives the engine a reader that returns a shipped file's bytes at a named version. The release tooling adds the release being prepared to the pack and refuses a release whose bases are missing. Nothing reads the pack in update, init or doctor until TSK-1087; this task is its own unit because the pack's layout and the release step are a contract TSK-1087 consumes and the two together are too large for one thorough review.

Non-goals: rendered copies (templates filled with project values), which SPC-015 places in the sparse pack; any change to how a project is updated.

After this merges, two pull requests that change different managed files merge without touching `.codeflow/manifest.json` or a baseline, and an adopter on 3.x moves to 4.0.0 with one `codeflow update` that rewrites the manifest and removes `.codeflow/.baseline/` from their repository.

A topic branch that carries only a line's own commits is judged as the line

TSK-1089todo

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a maintainer can split an epic line's pull request into `main` into topic pull requests, each carrying only the line's own commits, and `codeflow ci` judges each one as it judges the line.

Context

Source: issue #423 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, filed 2026-10-30 by an adopter). No open task covers it; TSK-433 (complete) gave a line's pull request into main the line treatment of the line's own completions.

An adopter splits an epic line's pull request into main into topic pull requests, each from its own branch carrying a slice of the line's merges. For the same base, head and flags, codeflow ci refuses the topic branch with work.acceptance_binding (the task's reviewed commit is not on the head's first-parent chain) and passes when --branch names the line. The only difference is the branch name.

The line treatment is keyed on the branch name in several places, read on the line tip b7ae7c6a6:

  • crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/classification.rs:236 (a Task: EPC-NNN body on an integration/ head becomes Class::EpicLine), :259, :352, :382 and :639 (the epic-line proof is run only for an integration/ head);
  • crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/acceptance.rs:324 (a run without a body makes the criteria amendable only for an integration/ head that passes check_epic_line);
  • crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci/context.rs:390;
  • the line bases in crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/acceptance.rs (:4071, :4081), which mark the judged line only when its name is the line.

Rule: a branch gets the line treatment only when its commits show it carries the line's own judged history: every commit in the range is a commit of the line, or a merge made on the branch whose result is the clean re-merge of its parents, each parent being a line commit, a commit of the target, or an earlier merge on the branch that itself meets this rule. So the rule applies recursively, and every eligible merge's ancestry outside the target is rooted in line commits: a topic branch can merge main with line commit A, then merge that result with line commit B. A branch name, or an explicit flag naming the line, only selects which line to check; neither grants the treatment alone. A picked commit (a new commit with a line commit's patch) is not a line commit. A branch with any other commit keeps today's judgment.

What counts as the line is fixed by authorities the requester does not control, separately from the structural epic-line proof, which can take the epic and the target declaration from the candidate head (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:713, :728) and does not judge merge commits (line_adoption.rs:193):

  • the line is the one the target's own records bind to the epic the pull request names (epic_line_binding, work_start.rs:883, read at the target tip, never at the head);
  • the line's tip is the one the destination advertises for that exact ref, resolved once to a commit at the start of the run (the remote-tracking ref as fetched for a local run), never a local branch or a commit the requester names;
  • a commit counts as a line commit only when it is reachable from that tip, so it reached the line through the line's own landing route.

How far that tip is judged rests on the hosted protection of lines (ruleset C, TSK-1080): until a line requires reviewed pull requests on the host, a requester who can push to the line can place commits on it, and this task trusts the line no more than codeflow ci already does when --branch names it. The task neither widens nor narrows that.

This binds trust, so the review carries the cf-security-reviewer checklist.

Non-goals: changing what the line itself is judged by; the line-to-main criteria report of TSK-350 AC-9.

Outcome

After this merges, a maintainer can rely on every Windows test partition of this repository's CI finishing inside its stated margin run after run, and on a partition that is drifting toward its limit being named on a green run before it overruns.

Context

Source: the coordinator's reading of PR 426's dispatch run 41110375672 on 2026-10-30. The other eleven partitions passed in 9.5 to 16.6 job minutes. The planner on the line plans every partition at about 9.2 minutes (python3 scripts/windows-partitions.py plan).

The job log's slowest tests were near the end of the partition, each running past 180 seconds while it overlapped the others: installed_cli_journey repeated_update_changes_nothing_and_restores_a_managed_file_changed_out_of_band (371.6 s), release_line_cli the_release_rule_table_is_a_one_time_bridge (264.0 s), init_e2e a_fresh_standard_project_prints_steps_that_clear_each_finding (223.0 s) and seven remedy_clearing tests (185 to 230 s). TSK-1063's run check (windows-partitions.py check) runs after the partitions and reads their reports, so it names an overrun only once it has happened; a cancelled partition writes no report.

The cause is not established: stale timing data, a slow runner, the overlap of long tests at the end of one partition, or tests that grew since TSK-1063 measured them. AC-1 measures it.

The anchor refusal names the branch shape a new standalone record needs

TSK-1091todo

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an author whose standalone record is refused for its branch name is told the branch shape the record needs and how to get there, from `codeflow ci`, `codeflow work start` and the pre-push hook alike.

Context

Source: issue #430 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, filed 2026-10-30 by an adopter), triaged the same day. No open task covers it; TSK-414 (complete) covers only a cancelled standalone record landing through a plan/ branch.

A pull request adds a standalone task record on a branch whose name does not carry the task (chore/close-tsk-nnn-record), with Task: TSK-NNN in its body. codeflow ci refuses it with work.stable_planning_anchor: "task TSK-NNN is not present at the merge-base; land its epic planning record, or carry its own standalone record on this task branch", and the remedy says to run codeflow work start. The record is on the branch, and work start only checks the anchor, so neither tells the author what to change. The same range passes on a branch named chore/TSK-NNN-<slug>.

The cause, read on the line tip b7ae7c6a6: standalone_at_head (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/work_start.rs:2232) accepts a record that is not at the merge-base only when the branch's work suffix starts with TSK-NNN-, and otherwise returns TaskNotAnchored, whose text (work_start.rs:69) does not mention the branch. Its remedy, WORK_START_MERGE_PLANNING (crates/codeflow-core/src/remedy.rs:340), names codeflow work start. TaskNotAnchored also covers a record missing from both the merge-base and the head, and an epic task whose planning has not landed.

The verdicts stay as they are: the rule is right, and only its text and remedy change. Non-goals: accepting a record on a branch that does not carry the task.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Issue and review follow-ups amendment (2026-10-30)/A refused interpreter that names an enforcement path says what it found and names the read route

A refused interpreter that names an enforcement path says what it found and names the read route

TSK-1092todo

After this merges, an agent refused for naming an enforcement path in an interpreter is told whether the code or an argument named it and.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an agent refused for naming an enforcement path in an interpreter is told whether the code or an argument named it and how to read the file instead.

Context

Source: issue #431 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, filed 2026-10-30 by an adopter), triaged the same day. A reviewer computing the digest of a managed workflow with python3 -I -c "...open('.github/workflows/codeflow-ci.yml','rb')..." was refused under git.hook_integrity with the remedy "the enforcement hooks and their policy are not agent-editable", which speaks of an edit the reviewer never tried. A read of .codeflow/policy.json the same way got the same text.

The verdicts stay: an inline program cannot be shown to be read-only, so the guard keeps failing closed. What changes is what the refusal says. Read on the line tip b7ae7c6a6, whose binary already differs from 3.1.1 here (TSK-302 landed):

  • interpreter.rs runs TSK-302's argument reader first (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/interpreter.rs:38, arguments::evaluate), which reports every word after the interpreter, a -c code string included, as "an interpreter argument <path> may reach repository enforcement files" with the INTERPRETER_ARGUMENT remedy (crates/codeflow-core/src/security/arguments.rs:197, crates/codeflow-core/src/remedy.rs:461), which names cat, jq, grep and a stdin redirect.
  • The broader literal scan that follows (interpreter.rs:94-110) reports "interpreter code names the enforcement path" with the edit-only HOOK_INTEGRITY remedy (remedy.rs:457), but exec-guard keeps the first finding of equal strength for one rule (crates/codeflow-core/src/hooks/exec_guard.rs:322, merge_strongest), so on the line the argument finding is the one printed. The issue's digest command, fed to the line binary on stdin and never run, prints the argument text and the read routes.
  • 3.1.1, which the issue ran, has no argument reader for this case and prints the code finding with the edit-only remedy.

So the line's defect is attribution: a path inside -c code is called an argument, and the edit-only text is still reachable wherever the argument reader does not fire first. The read routes are a plain reader (cat, jq, grep, shasum, git show <ref>:<path>) and a redirect into the program's stdin, where the shell opens the file read-only.

Non-goals: judging an obvious read in code as a read (the issue's second option, which a later reopen of the path defeats); any verdict change.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Issue and review follow-ups amendment (2026-10-30)/Work claim adopts the agent's own checked-out task branch and publishes it

Work claim adopts the agent's own checked-out task branch and publishes it

TSK-1093todo

After this merges, an agent that built a task on its own unpushed task branch ahead of the claim can claim the task from that branch and.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an agent that built a task on its own unpushed task branch ahead of the claim can claim the task from that branch and publish it as the claim, while every other carrier still refuses.

Context

Source: issue #433 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, filed 2026-10-30 by an adopter), triaged the same day. An agent built an epic task ahead of its claim on the local branch task/TSK-150-<slug>, never pushed. Run from that worktree, codeflow work claim TSK-150 refused: "TSK-150 is already claimed by a visible branch: task/TSK-150-...", naming the branch the agent was on. No remote branch carried the task, the name was the one the claim would create, and the branch contained the target's tip. The refusal names no route, so an agent either stops or works around the claim's create-only push.

Read on the line tip b7ae7c6a6, in crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/readiness.rs:

  • visible_work_branches (:350) counts local branches as claims, as .codeflow/rules/worktrees.md:66 documents.
  • claim_on (:1743) drops the current branch from the carriers only on the standalone route (standalone_claim_base, :1709; the retain at :1787), which renames a branch holding a new standalone record. An epic task, or a record already on the target, never takes it.
  • Every other carrier that has not landed refuses (:1793).
  • work start already reports other carriers as information, not a refusal (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/work.rs:408).

Rule: work claim adopts the current branch only when all of these hold, and refuses otherwise with the reason and a route:

  • the branch is checked out in the worktree the command runs in;
  • it is the only carrier of the id among local branches and every remote the claim reads; any remote carrier refuses;
  • its name is the name the claim would create;
  • it is not a protected branch;
  • it contains the claim's base: the stack base of the --on pins when they are given (stack_base, the base a new claim is cut from, readiness.rs:1756), otherwise the target's tip; with valid pins the target may have moved past the branch;
  • readiness is judged on the target's record, as for a new claim.

With an origin remote it then publishes the branch with the existing create-only push (--force-with-lease=<destination>:, readiness.rs:1815) and prints "adopted" instead of "created"; a lost push race refuses and leaves local and remote refs unchanged. Without origin it adopts the branch locally and says the claim is visible only in this clone, as a new claim does today (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/work.rs:292).

The claim is the mark other agents trust to see who holds a task, so the review carries the cf-security-reviewer checklist. Today's refusal stays when another clone has pushed a branch for the id or a second local branch carries it.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Progress report amendment (2026-10-31)/codeflow status --json gives percent complete, location, order, lanes, windows and issues for any scope

codeflow status --json gives percent complete, location, order, lanes, windows and issues for any scope

TSK-1095todo

After this merges, anyone on an adopting project can run `codeflow status` with a scope and get, for a task, an epic or the whole line.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, anyone on an adopting project can run `codeflow status` with a scope and get, for a task, an epic or the whole line, the percent complete at each level with its basis, what is on `main` and what is not with the path to `main`, the order of work, the lanes carrying it, a window per item and milestone with its basis, and the issues per item, each fact live or marked unverified, as text and JSON.

Context

The operator asked on 2026-10-30 for a command or skill that reports the status of work properly each time it is asked, in any project that adopts CodeFlow: what is being worked on with just the right context, the epics and tasks involved, percent complete at each level (the epic, the task and the overall scope), the lanes a coordinator runs and the overall across them, the order work is done in, the expected time to completion for each item, and the issues for each item. On 2026-10-30 (20:40) the operator added that timing must read at a glance on a real time axis, and that work landed on an integration line counts as done while the report makes clear what is on main, what is not, and when it gets there. Nothing computes this today: codeflow status prints counts from the working tree with no JSON (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/status.rs:7-17), work next prints readiness (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/readiness.rs:27-48), and report ceremony is the only report (crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/report.rs:17-22). Every session writes its own status by hand, with the stale facts the writing rule warns about.

This task is the engine: it extends codeflow status, the command an adopter already reaches for, with the facts and a JSON form. TSK-1098 renders them as the figure-led cf-present document (--present) and the plain-text form (--md); TSK-1099 is the cf-status skill that answers a status request with them. TSK-312 (status --json on TSK-311's fact model) is merged into this task on 2026-10-31 and cancelled; every TSK-312 criterion is kept below (AC-2, AC-7 and AC-11). Shape decided in planning, open to the builder's investigation (AC-1):

Figure: the scope selects records, git and the optional forge, ledger and session file supply facts, and the percent, location, order, lane, window and issue views are derived from them; nothing is stored.

Decisions, each reversible and disclosed here:

  • Command and flags. codeflow status keeps its text view unchanged with no flag. New: --json; the scope flags --task TSK-NNN, --epic EPC-NNN (repeatable) and --line <integration branch>, with the default scope every open epic whose home is the current target; a scope flag with no output flag prints the progress text view. --json, --present <path> (TSK-1098) and --md (TSK-1098) are mutually exclusive output choices over the same facts; --session <file> and --since <previous facts file> are optional input modifiers: this task defines the --session schema and merges its facts into the lanes view, and reads a previous --json output through --since to emit what changed (landings, new red checks, tasks added, blockers opened or cleared, decisions recorded) with their times. "Overall" is the named scope, so a task report shows the task, its epic and that epic's place in the scope. The coordinator recommended this shape on 2026-10-30 over a new report verb; the operator confirms the names at plan approval.
  • Stage ladder. A task's percent is the highest stage it has reached on a fixed ladder printed with every report: not started 0, in progress (a claim or a task branch with commits) 20, in review (an open pull request) 50, reviewed (an approving other-lineage review on the head) 75, landed on its home target 100; cancelled tasks are excluded from every denominator and listed. Criteria verified against criteria total is shown beside the stage percent from the acceptance block when one exists, never mixed with it, labelled criteria, bound to the reviewed SHA the block names and marked stale when the head has moved since; a block or count that is absent is not recorded, never 0 of N. An epic's percent is the mean of its open and complete tasks' stage percents, with the count of tasks per stage beside it; the scope's percent is the same over its unique tasks, never a mean of epic percents. An empty denominator or an unreadable record is unknown, never 0 or 100.
  • Location and the path to main. Landed on the integration line is done for the task percent, and each task and epic also carries a location from its own landing evidence: main (its landing commit reachable from the trusted remote's default branch), line (reachable from its integration line only), pull request (an open pull request into the line or into main), branch (a task branch with commits and no pull request) or none; a checkpoint merge of the line into main moves only the tasks whose landing commits it carries, never the epic as a whole. A task whose record is on the line but whose work has not started is none with the note record on line, never line. A pull request location carries its substate (draft, open, approved at <sha> with the reviewed SHA named and marked not the head when the head moved); "ready" is never a location, it is the next step's word. The open pull requests into main are listed with the task state of each, so a lead can say "no 4.0.0 pull request into main is open; the only open one is for a cancelled task" rather than an absolute none. Every remote claim is bound to the fetched ref identity it was read from (the SHA and the fetch time) and marked unverified when that ref is older than the sweep interval or could not be fetched. The epic's path to main is the remaining steps on the landing route the project records (land the open units on the line, the line's full gate, the pull request to main, the operator's merge, release when the project has a release step); an agent-owned step carries a window from the scenarios; an operator-owned step is two events, ready for the operator (a window) and done by the operator (undated, awaiting the operator), and every step after it is conditional on it and says so. The hop to main always carries its condition in words and, when the scenarios give one, the earliest conditional end under the intake-stops scenario ("after the epic is complete on the line, earliest about N days if intake stops and capacity holds; then the operator's merge"), so "when does it reach main" has an answer beyond "no date"; this is a read of record and git state, never a promise.
  • Named sets. The fact model defines each named set once and every view reuses it: the landing chain (the open pull requests into the line in landing order, with the landed ones and their times), each lane's tasks, the path to main; a count of a set is the count of that one definition.
  • Order. A topological order of depends_on among the scope's open tasks, authoritative: a task never precedes its predecessor. Among tasks with no dependency between them the state decides the place: active first (claimed or started, through the readiness core work next uses, after TSK-1038 never offering landed work), then ready, then waiting with the predecessor waited on, then blocked with the reason; so a blocked predecessor sits before its waiting successor, and the state is printed on every row. The critical path is the chain whose planning-scenario durations sum highest, marked, and the longest chain by count is reported apart as the dependency depth, never called critical.
  • Lanes. When the coordination ledger has lanes (TSK-439, when landed), each lane with its scope, attempt, seat kind and the task's percent; otherwise observed lanes: each claimed or started task with its worktree, branch, open pull request and head age, labelled observed, with no seat and no owner invented. A --session <file> of session-only facts (lane, task, builder, reviewer, seat, verdict in flight, blocker, each with its observation time) is validated against a shipped schema, merged into the lanes view labelled session, and never changes a percent or a stage. A project with no ledger and no session file shows "lanes: observed only".
  • Windows. Every open agent-owned item and every agent-owned step on the path to main carries one window: the earliest and latest end as durations from the snapshot time (the as-of moment), with the planning value inside it, and a start that is the as-of moment or its predecessors' latest end, so a renderer can place it as a band on one time axis with the as-of rule. A blocked item's window is conditional on its blocker clearing and says so; an item whose window has no honest basis (an unknown predecessor, an undated operator step before it, a cancelled or unreadable predecessor) is not yet estimable with the reason, never a number. When the project has adopted cf-estimate and a forecast record covers the scope, the windows come from it, bound to the scope and revision it estimated and marked stale when criteria changed since. Otherwise the window comes from the planned throughput rule (cf-method/references/workflow-lifecycle.md "Planned work moves at speed": at least one task per build lane per hour, preferably two): earliest at two tasks per lane-hour with one review and landing cycle of one hour per unit, planning at one per lane-hour with one review cycle and one repair round, latest at one per lane-hour with two review rounds and one landing cycle per batch, over the open tasks along the order with the number of lanes observed. Every window carries a basis_kind: forecast (an adopted forecast record), observed (the planned rate over the lanes observed) or assumed (no lane observed, so one lane is assumed and the window is labelled assumed one lane wherever it is drawn, never mixed with an observed window). The scope's finish is forecast under two named scenarios in one place: intake stops (the open tasks at the planning rate) and intake continues at the rate observed over the last seven days (which may give no finite finish, said in words). Each window prints its basis and computation time, is a duration from the as-of moment and never a calendar commitment, and the planned-throughput rate is never lowered to an observed slow pace.
  • Issues. Per task: blocked (reason, owner, revisit), waiting (the predecessor), an open pull request whose required check is red, missing or pending (read through the ledger's bounded observer crates/codeflow-core/src/coord/observe.rs, unverified when offline), stale (claimed with no commit for longer than the sweep interval [sweep] interval_minutes, default 30), a deferred acceptance result owed (TSK-436), and a follow-up awaiting the operator when the ledger is present. Each issue names its unblocker (an agent lane, a CI run, a predecessor, the operator) and the window in which it is expected to clear when the scenarios give one, so a renderer can draw a blocked list and an explicit "needs the operator" set. The operator set is none owed only when every source that can name an owed item (records, the ledger when present, the away activation's owed items and decisions when an activation exists (TSK-1045, read with its own coverage result and never written), the forge through the observer, the session file when given) was checked at this snapshot; otherwise it is not established with the unchecked or unreadable source named, never an all-clear. Per lane: a seat with no progress since the last tick, from ledger or session evidence only.
  • Pace and intake. Over the scope's history the fact model gives, per day for the last seven days and in total, the tasks landed on their home target, the tasks added to the scope (from record creation dates and merge times, each named) and the open count at the end of each day, with the lane count observed, so a reader can see whether intake outruns landing. Two rates are given and labelled: the scope's own observed landing rate, and the planned capacity rate over the lanes observed (the planned-throughput rule); the finish forecast names which rate each scenario uses, and the intake-stops count names the tasks added since the previous snapshot as intake. This is the basis line of the windows and is printed with them.
  • Fact model. JSON with schema_version, a snapshot time with its zone, and every field present with unknown or unverified rather than omitted or zero, frozen by a schema test; each measure (percents, locations, order, lanes, windows, issues, pace) carries an evidence entry naming its source (records, git, the forge through the observer, the ledger, the activation, a forecast record, the session file), its check time and whether it was checked, so a renderer can draw the evidence matrix. Every forge observation keeps its read time and is never overwritten by a later one without its own read time; every time in the model carries one zone, the snapshot's, and a check state is the value read (skipped and missing stay so, never rewritten as running). Every snapshot carries the repository identity TSK-311's envelope defines, so a --since file from another repository is refused even when its display ids match. TSK-311's report program reuses this model for the records it adds cross-line home and currency to, and its AC-4's "schema test that TSK-312 reuses" reads as this task's schema test. This task reads records through the existing readiness core and record store (crates/codeflow-core/src/status.rs, workgraph/readiness.rs) and never adds a second record reader.
  • Report facts the operator asked for on 2026-10-31. The operator's standing requirements for every report (deliverable and overall percent; each epic or topic with what it is, done and not done, the reasoning and the percent; blockers with a recommended action, why and alternatives; operator inputs with context, options, recommendation and reasoning; commands that run from any folder) need facts the model did not name. The fact model carries, per scope, the deliverable (the epic's ## Outcome line, or the task's, not recorded when absent) beside the percent; per epic, what_it_is (its Outcome line), the done and not_done task lists and a reasoning line (the stage counts and the basis the percent is computed from); themes grouping an epic's tasks by the record section that introduced them (the amendment heading, which is how this repository's epics group asks) or by a theme: line in the task record when present, ungrouped otherwise, so a renderer can drill from the epic to a theme to a task; per issue, recommended_action, why and alternatives filled from the record (the ## Blocker reason, owner and revisit, the follow-ups, a decision note) or from the --session file labelled session, and not recorded when neither has them, never invented; per operator item, a decision with context, options, recommendation and reasoning from the same sources with the same rule; and per task the context facts a drill-down needs (outcome line, location, lane, state, window, last moved, open pull request). Every command the model cites (a check to rerun, a pull request to open, a log to read) carries the repository's absolute path or a git -C <path> form so a script assembled from them runs from any folder; the renderer (TSK-1098) assembles the script.

Non-goals: rendering (TSK-1098); the skill and its wiring (TSK-1099); cross-line home and currency (TSK-311); a scheduler, daemon or stored report; writing to any record or ledger; a check or verdict (the report never fails a gate); tracked class and lane vocabulary (TSK-313, TSK-314, EPC-023).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality enforcement into 4.0.0 amendment (2026-10-31)/Present and portal tables encode state, extent and emphasis from one grammar module

Present and portal tables encode state, extent and emphasis from one grammar module

TSK-1096todo

After this merges, an author or a generator can show state, magnitude.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an author or a generator can show state, magnitude, grouping and emphasis inside a table on the present surface and the docs portal, readable at a glance and without colour, with every exact value still present as text.

Context

The operator's clarification of 2026-10-30 (20:15, relayed by the coordinator): avoiding text tables does not mean banning tables; it means that when a table is the better shape, it is presented visually, with colour encodings, inline bars, status marks, grouping and emphasis, never as plain text. The feedback of the same day (20:40) added that a table must be easy to consume and look good, elegant and restrained, never cheesy or overdone, and that a disclosure must open to content presented as well as the first reading path, since layering information is not sweeping text into a box the reader fears to open. Neither surface can do this today:

  • the present table block holds string cells rendered as Markdown in plain <td> elements (crates/codeflow-present/src/render.rs:406-425; schema .codeflow/schemas/present/document-v2.schema.json, table), with no state, bar, tone or group a cell can carry;
  • the present status block draws pass and fail with the same filled mark and pending and not-run with the same outlined mark, told apart by colour alone, and hides the mark from assistive technology without emitting the state as text (crates/codeflow-present/src/render.rs:425-440, crates/codeflow-present/web/src/styles.css, the .state-mark rules), against the two-channel rule the figure grammar sets for every pair of states (figure-grammar.md section 2, rule 3);
  • the portal renders Markdown tables as Starlight tables and its generated capability table prints status as plain text (assets/docs-portal/starter/scripts/adapter.mjs:422, scripts/lib.mjs:1150); the lookup wrappers in portal.css:688-762 change layout at phone width only;
  • the figure twin is an exact textual fallback, which must stay as it is (crates/codeflow-present/web/src/figure-grammar.mjs, the twin renderer).

Outcome: one encoded-table vocabulary, drawn by the grammar module both runtimes load, lets an author or a generator give a table cell a state mark from the mark vocabulary, an inline extent bar against a declared maximum, a tone (accent, cat1, cat2) or an emphasis, and a row a group, so the present table block and a declared portal table read as visuals with their exact values kept as text; the present status block meets the two-channel rule with an accessible state name; and the figure twin stays the plain fallback.

Figure: one vocabulary and one module serve both surfaces; each surface keeps its own carrier and shell.

Decisions, each reversible and disclosed here:

  • A cell is a string (as today) or an object with text and any of state (a mark from figure-grammar.md section 4, drawn with its two non-hue channels and its name as accessible text), bar (value, max, optional unit and label naming what is measured, such as criteria; drawn to length on the table's one declared scale per column, the value kept as text beside it; a value of null draws no bar and the text not recorded, never zero), tone (accent, cat1, cat2; hue only, never the only carrier) and strong; a row may carry group, drawn as a group heading. A legend lists every state and tone used, as figures do. The present table block gains these fields under schema_version: 2 without breaking a string-only table.
  • The portal carrier is a declared table bound in portal.config.json like a figure (tables, with route and panel or anchor), drawn by the adapter from a declaration file; a Markdown table in a source stays a Markdown table. The builder confirms in AC-1 that a declaration beats a cf-table fence in sources under the content contract, and records the choice; the vocabulary is the same either way.
  • An encoded table is a primary carrier when a comparison or lookup is its better shape; the method text that puts tables in disclosures (TSK-445 AC-3) applies to reference detail, and TSK-1097 restates the rule.
  • No new colours: the --cf-fig-* roles and the mark vocabulary draw everything; a status cell is the cov, part, notrun, na, nc, done, todo, blocked or stop mark, and the status block's four states map to done (pass), stop (fail), todo (pending) and notrun (not run), each with the state name in the accessible tree.
  • Restraint is part of the vocabulary: a column carries one encoding (a mark, a bar or a tone), a table uses at most two tones beside the accent, bars share one scale per column, row striping and borders come from the kit's chrome.css table rules and never from the declaration, and the legend lists only what is used; the renderer refuses a cell with two encodings and a table with more than three tones. The kit's table rule in chrome.css sets the quiet surface (hairline rules, tabular numerals, a group heading one step heavier), so an encoded table looks the same on both surfaces.
  • An encoded table and the figure families are the carriers inside a disclosure too: the present disclosure block and the portal's details panels accept the same blocks as the first reading path, and the twin of a figure stays the exact accessible fallback and writes every mark as its human word (checked, partial, not run, not applicable, not claimed, unknown), never its identifier. The runtime's own figure Details panel, which today opens to the description paragraph and the plain twin (crates/codeflow-present/web/src/figure-grammar.mjs, the Details renderer near line 722, and the portal's copy), is the disclosure the operator met: it opens instead to a one-line lead and the twin drawn as an encoded table (states as marks, values with bars where the figure drew extent), with the plain twin kept beneath for assistive readers and copy, on both surfaces. A disclosure's closed summary line may carry a state mark and a count chip, so a closed disclosure says what is inside and how much (the design brief revision 2, gap 8).
  • The vocabulary gains an unknown mark (a hatched ring with the word), distinct from na (faint, not applicable) and notrun (hatch), so a generator can draw a value it could not establish without calling it inapplicable or zero.

Non-goals: new figure families; a table that replaces a figure where a relationship carries the point (the altitude contract stands); the portal page rewrites (TSK-446); the method text beyond the block selection table (TSK-1097); product or brand design.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality enforcement into 4.0.0 amendment (2026-10-31)/The present and portal craft meets the immediately obvious bar, with the artifact guidance adopted

The present and portal craft meets the immediately obvious bar, with the artifact guidance adopted

TSK-1097todo

After this merges, an author of a present document or a portal page has one checkable bar for information that is immediately obvious.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an author of a present document or a portal page has one checkable bar for information that is immediately obvious, both runtimes warn on the parts a machine can measure, and the figure guidance carries the chart lessons the utility was missing.

Context

The operator's principle of 2026-10-30 (20:15, relayed by the coordinator) for cf-present and cf-docs-portal alike: information that is immediately obvious, visual plus supporting text, with the right context, a leading anchor and an order that spares the reader from connecting the dots; visuals and colour used in useful ways that convey things faster without losing detail or the real complexity. The operator also asked for Anthropic's artifact guidance (artifact-design, artifact-diagramming and dataviz, read on 2026-10-30) to be compared with the two skills and its good parts adopted. TSK-445 (PR 344) already carries the method's anchor, section leads, figure-first order and the artifact-design and diagramming lessons; TSK-446 fixes the portal's page order. This task closes what neither covers and writes the principle as a checkable bar in both skills. The operator's feedback of 2026-10-30 (20:40) sharpened the bar on three points, all of which apply to cf-present, cf-docs-portal and the status report alike: a detail section is layered information and opens to content presented as well as the first path, never text swept into a box; a table that is needed is elegant and restrained; and a document or page answers the questions its reader brings, in the order they arise, so the reader never connects the dots.

Gap list against the artifact guidance, paraphrased (no text copied):

ItemThe guidanceThe skills todayDecision
Numeralstabular figures where digits line up in columns; proportional on a large standalone numberno rule; figure.css and chrome.css set noneadopt: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on table cells, the twin and extent value labels in the kit sheets; proportional elsewhere
Palette validationcompute colour safety with a script (simulated colour-vision deficiency separation, lightness band, contrast), never by eyeruntime checks 4.5:1 text and 3:1 focus contrast of imported project tokens (document-authoring.md "Utility tokens"); the shared palette test checks drift and the two-channel rule carries stateadopt: a simulated-deficiency separation measure between the figure ink roles (accent, cat1, cat2, warn, stop, line, line-mid, line-soft) per skin and mode in the kit palette test, and on an imported project palette at runtime, as a warning naming the two-channel rule as the mitigation

Outcome: both skills state the immediately obvious bar in checkable terms in their composition gates and review rubrics, with the encoded table (TSK-1096) admitted as a primary carrier where a comparison or lookup is the better shape; the adopted items above are in the kit, the runtime checks and the figure guidance; and present check and the portal gate report the measurable parts.

The bar, as both skills will state it:

Figure: the order of a document or page under the bar, from the anchor to the reachable detail.

Decisions, each reversible and disclosed here:

  • The bar's checkable items: (a) the first screen carries the anchor and an orienting visual; (b) every section opens with a lead line and carries a figure or an encoded visual that answers it, or says in its lead why none applies; (c) a table in the first reading path encodes state, extent or emphasis; (d) every state differs on two non-hue channels and has an accessible name; (e) a cold reader names the overall state and the main blocker or relationship in a few seconds, recorded as an answer; (f) every summarised value keeps its exact value and source reachable; (g) a disclosure or details panel opens to a lead line and a figure or an encoded table, never to a bare paragraph with a plain table or to a wall of text, so the layered detail is as clear as the first screen, and its closed summary says what is inside with a mark or a count where one applies; (h) a table is restrained: one encoding per column, at most two tones beside the accent, the kit's quiet surface, a legend of only what is used, and no decoration beyond the vocabulary (TSK-1096 AC-8 holds the renderer to it); (i) the author names the reader and records the questions that reader brings, in the order they arise, and the sections follow that recorded list with each lead naming its question; the bar fixes no universal sequence, since a status report (TSK-1098's list) and a capability page bring different readers; it requires that the list exists, is recorded in the document's or page's summary, and is followed; (j) (added 2026-10-31, the operator's feedback on consistency) a recurring piece uses the catalog's component set, adds a new section kind once with a specimen rather than improvising it in an html stage, and differs from its predecessor only where the facts differ, so consecutive versions look alike; for a present document of a recurring kind (a status report, a design review) this means the shell's layout contract and view-kind registry (TSK-1120), a topic so a repeat revises the same document with change marks (TSK-1121) and stable block ids; a portal page keeps its committed source and route identity under the portal content contract (cf-docs-portal/references/content-contract.md) and takes only the composition and consistency guidance, never a topic or a session (Codex round 8, F3). Items (a) to (d), (g) and (h) are mechanical and the checks report them; the mechanical half of (j) is reported by the checks TSK-1120 (an html stage where the registry kind names a catalog carrier, a custom view) and TSK-1121 (a missing topic on a registry-kind document) own, this task stating only the guidance; (e), (f), (i) and the rest of (j) are the reviewer's judged evidence, with (i) checked against the recorded list. Two further rules of craft, from the four reviews of the status report of 2026-10-30: every state or location word is defined where first used (a subtitle, a lead or a caption), and a caption carries one new fact (the last event, the basis) and never restates the figure or describes the table.
  • The method text's sentence that puts tables in disclosures (TSK-445 AC-3) is superseded: a plain table is reference detail and sits only in a figure twin, never in the first reading path and never alone in a disclosure; an encoded table may lead a section when a comparison or lookup is its better shape. This task lands after TSK-445; TSK-445's own criteria are unchanged.
  • The portal's rule that a Technical table never stands in for its figure (cf-docs-portal/references/visual-craft.md) stays for plain tables; an encoded table bound as a declaration may be a panel's carrier when the altitude contract's families do not fit, with the reason in its caption.

The operator's design decisions of 2026-10-31 (about 14:58 to 15:0x, 16:35, 18:37, 18:4x and 18:5x, recorded in the coordinator's handoff, section 5, with the 2026-10-27 typing row) extend the bar to the shared design system and the figures, on both surfaces: one token system, Mode separate from Theme, Graphite as the neutral default with the accent the operator settles (TSK-1162 AC-2), a curated set of accents per theme, no thick left-border callouts, stage colours held to measured floors, no text overflow, figures that explain visually, pills on one line and a generic surface. The plan elaborates them with tokens declared once in a typed source, inline SVG with Mermaid refused under the workspace rule, and a visual-coverage check. AC-9 to AC-18 carry them. The display control and the side menu are TSK-1120's, the entity page content TSK-1098's and the layered portal TSK-446's. The design seat's working prototype dashboard-v2 (a session scratchpad of 2026-10-31, not committed; TSK-1122 commits the approved prototype) is the design reference for these decisions, never shipped code: its token build (tokens/tokens.json, scripts/build-tokens.mjs, scripts/color-math.mjs) and its browser tests (tests/smoke.mjs, menu.mjs, states.mjs, fit.mjs, axe.mjs) show how each criterion below can be checked.

Sample set (moved 2026-11-01): the ten present report specimens and the three portal layer samples, with their captures, are no longer this task's. The operator approved the move on 2026-11-01 so the bar, the kit, the checks and the token system reach TSK-1120 and TSK-446 without waiting for the authoring and review of thirteen documents. TSK-1127 now authors the set once, on the approved shell, topic and portal frame (its AC-6 carries the former AC-19). This task keeps the bar, the kit, the token system and the checks, and proves them on fixtures, planted failures and the two reference pages. Where a criterion below names the specimens or the sample pages, its proof over the sample set is TSK-1127 AC-4 and AC-6, and this task proves the same check on fixtures and the reference pages.

Text and navigation rule (added 2026-11-01): the operator decided at 19:25 on 2026-11-01 ("in general the design is better", but the nav rail and peek keep regressing and cards carry walls of text; source: coordination/coordinators/visual-docs/DESIGN-DIRECTION.md, "Navigation and text") that prose is the last resort and that navigation is one component with a test, not care. AC-20 and AC-21 are the text rule and its check. The one navigation component, its spec and its browser test (the operator's navigation rule of the same decision) were first planned here as AC-22 and AC-23 and moved on 2026-11-01 to TSK-1160, because the task became Very Hard with them. This task owns the text rule and its checks; TSK-1160 builds the component on this task's token source; TSK-1127 holds the shipped samples to both (its AC-7 and AC-8).

Second split (2026-11-01): with the component gone the task still held the token system, its themes, modes, accents and colour floors beside the bar, the figure guidance and ten check families, which graded Very Hard. The token source and its floors (former AC-4, AC-9, AC-10 and AC-12) moved to TSK-1162, which this task now depends on; the bar's guidance, the check warnings and tests, the text rule and the reference pages stay here. Other records that say "TSK-1097's token system" mean TSK-1162.

Non-goals: the encoded-table runtime (TSK-1096); the portal page rewrites and page order (TSK-446); the anchor and method text itself (TSK-445); a new figure family; a stat tile block; product design.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Progress report amendment (2026-10-31)/codeflow status --present renders the figure-led progress document and --md its plain-text form

codeflow status --present renders the figure-led progress document and --md its plain-text form

TSK-1098todo

After this merges, one command turns the status facts of any adopting project into a present document a reader grasps in a few seconds.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, one command turns the status facts of any adopting project into a present document a reader grasps in a few seconds, in the order a reader asks its questions, with every value reachable in visual detail, and into a plain-text form for terminals and pull requests.

Context

The operator asked on 2026-10-30 that status be presented in a visually rich way with supporting text on cf-present, and added on the same day (20:40): timing must read at a glance on a time axis; it must be clear what is on main, what is not and when it gets there; a details disclosure must open to well-presented visual content, never a dense paragraph and a plain table ("layering information, not sweeping text there"); a table that is needed must be easy to consume and look good, elegant and restrained; and the report must answer, in a logical progression, what someone expecting a report would want to know. TSK-1095 computes the facts; this task renders them so the same facts open as a cf-present document on any adopting project with no agent, and print as a plain-text form for terminals, pull request bodies and chat. The rendering is in the binary so it is deterministic, tested and the same everywhere; the skill (TSK-1099) adds only the session's context and session-only facts through --session.

The reader's questions, in the order the document answers them, from the status report design brief revision 2 (the design lead's, revised 2026-10-30 21:05 EDT, section 2), generalised for any adopting project:

Figure: the eight reader questions and the carrier that answers each, in reading order; a reader who stops after question 4 has the decision picture; every number appears first as a mark and stays as text.

The operator's feedback of 2026-10-31 reshaped the carrier: the report is a dashboard, not one long page. It is organised by outcomes first, every outcome drilled into for its detail (13:15), with a side menu, tabs for aspects and drill-down from the release to an epic to a theme to a task with the task's context, built on the shell cf-present gains in TSK-1120, revised in place with change marks through TSK-1121, and conforming to the design the operator approves on TSK-1122's clickable prototype. The eight questions keep their order inside the overview and the views that answer them.

Figure: the view tree; the outcomes are the first menu group and the primary path, the other entries cut across them, and every fact is reachable from the outcomes path alone.

Decisions, each reversible and disclosed here:

  • codeflow status --present <path> (with the scope flags and --session <file> of TSK-1095) writes a schema_version: 2 document the skill opens with codeflow present open; --md prints the plain-text form with the fenced ASCII chat forms of the same families (figure-grammar.md section 7) and the ladder, for a terminal, a PR body or a reply; the text views of TSK-1095 are unchanged.
  • The document follows the bar of TSK-1097 and the design brief revision 2 (its reader model, page outline, mark set, chips, timing design, location design, layered detail rule and table style), with the brief's repository-specific numbers and rows replaced by the facts of the scope at hand, and with every html stage the brief fell back to replaced by the figure families and the encoded table the grammar now has (TSK-1096, TSK-1100): anchor first, each section a titled narrative with a lead line naming its question, the figure or encoded visual, short acting text; a disclosure opens to an encoded table or a figure with its lead, never a bare paragraph and a plain table, and its summary carries a mark or count. The anchor's lines are the as-of time with its zone, the owed items (or none owed, or not established with the unchecked source), the next operator moment with its window, the scope and the location summary on one denominator (so many on main, on the line, in a pull request, not started); the skill may prepend one context block, and the document carries a summary. The order is the recorded reader's question list above, named in each section's lead; TSK-1097's bar requires that an author record the reader and the questions, and this list is the one this document records.
  • Carriers: the overall and per-epic percent as an extent figure with max 100 and limit ticks at the stage boundaries; location as a flow figure of four stations (branch, pull request, line, main) with the task count under each on one denominator, the arrows labelled with what moves work along and their windows, the arrow into main in the accent as the governing path with the pull request and its state or no PR, no date in words, and an extent per location beside it; timing as the schedule family (TSK-1100) on a clock axis with the as-of rule: the next landing, the chain, the operator step as a readiness window ending in the ring with the merge undated off the axis, and the hop to main, stopped work hatched with its condition, dependencies drawn, the critical path in accent, and the per-item windows in a disclosure as an encoded table; the blocked list as an encoded table (state mark, item, cause, unblocker chip, window); the operator set as a status block, a success callout of one line only when the facts say none owed with every source checked, and a pending status item naming the unchecked source when not established; the since strip as an encoded table of events with times when --since was given, and one lead line saying no previous report was given otherwise; lanes as an extent per lane with the session facts (seat, verdict in flight, blocker) as marks and the overall row, each lane with a disclosure opening to its encoded task table (criteria bar, checks as marks, review round, location chip, next milestone and window, last moved); tasks as the encoded table of TSK-1096 grouped by epic with the stage mark, a bar for the percent, the location chip, the planning window and an issue mark; pace and intake as extent rows per day (landed against added, with the open count at the end of each day) with the finish under the two named scenarios (intake stops; intake continues at the observed rate, a non-finite finish said in words), the two labelled rates and the windows' basis as the lead, the only home of the finish forecast; evidence as a coverage figure (measures by sources, the five cell marks) inside a disclosure with an encoded table of refs and commands. No html stage, no callout per task, no stat tile, no table without an encoding outside a figure twin. Craft rules from the four reviews of the hand-built report (2026-10-30 21:42 EDT): each lane's disclosure follows its own lane row, never collected at the end; a lane's lead is tasks landed of total, with criteria verified second and the word criteria on its bar, stale when the reviewed SHA is not the head, not recorded when absent; the location chip says open PR or draft, the state says what it waits for, the next step says then the operator's decision; every named set (the chain, a lane, the path) is defined once from the facts and the same count appears everywhere; the anchor defines on main (the merge is in main's history), on the line (landed since) and complete where first used, and says that neither is a release; the since strip is one column in time order with a neutral event mark and the stop mark only for a stop; a caption carries one new fact and never restates its figure.
  • Governing path in accent: the critical path, the arrow into main and the scope row; location in the cat1 and cat2 companions through the chips; warn for a window marked stale or an adverse run; stop for a blocker; never hue alone; the legend drawn once per figure as the grammar requires.
  • A scope with more than 24 open tasks groups the table by epic and draws the schedule for the critical path and its neighbours only, saying so in the caption; the full order and every window stay in a disclosure as encoded tables.
  • Every figure fact names its source in the facts JSON, so the twin and the description hold the exact values; nothing is drawn that the facts do not state; unknown draws as the unknown mark (TSK-1096) with the word, unverified as the notrun hatch with the word, and neither as na (not applicable), which keeps its own meaning, nor as zero.
  • The derived binding: the schedule, flow, extent and coverage declarations carry source entries into the facts JSON (the field per drawn value), so codeflow present check can compare a figure against the facts file beside it and refuse a drawn value the facts do not hold.
  • The view tree (2026-10-31). --present writes a views document (TSK-1120) with topic status:<scope key> (TSK-1121). The root overview opens with the anchor (deliverable, overall percent, as-of, owed items, next operator moment, location summary) and lists the scope's outcomes first, one row per epic or theme from the facts' deliverable and what_it_is lines, each with its percent, state and next step and a view reference into its topic view; the eight questions' decision picture follows in the overview. Each topic view (an epic, then each theme under it) carries what it is, done, not done, the reasoning line and the percent, with tabs Progress, Order and Issues, and references into its item views; each item view (a task) carries the context strip from the facts' context (outcome, location, lane, state, window, last moved, pull request), its criteria bar, checks, issues and evidence. Cross-cutting menu entries follow the outcomes: Epics, Lanes, Order, Decisions, Evidence, Script. The approved tree is written here by TSK-1122's PR; until then this paragraph is the plan.
  • The operator's report items (2026-10-31). Blockers render as an encoded table with recommended action, why and alternatives columns from the facts (not recorded drawn as its word, never blank); operator inputs render in the decisions view as decision and form blocks (document.rs:69 and :83) with the context, options, recommendation (marked) and reasoning from the facts, answered through the present session's responses so the skill (TSK-1099) reads them back; the commands view holds one labelled code block (TSK-1113's label and copy button where landed, a plain code block otherwise) carrying every cited command assembled into one script that runs from any folder, since each command carries its repository path (TSK-1095 AC-15); every narrative block in a view is short points (the present check lead rule of TSK-1097), never a paragraph wall.
  • Reuse across reports (2026-10-31). Block and view ids derive from the facts (scope key, view kind, item id, section kind), so a second run on the same scope writes the same ids for the same things and the runtime's change marks (TSK-1121) show only what the facts changed; the skill updates the topic's open session (present update) rather than opening a new one, so the report's version history is the session's revision history; a --since run also fills the since view.
  • Split with PR 449. TSK-1113's stats block may carry the pace basis tiles (landings per day, CI minutes, review rounds) where it has landed; otherwise they stay extent rows, and the document never adds a stat tile of its own. The earlier note that a stat tile block is not in this release is superseded by TSK-1113.

Non-goals: the facts (TSK-1095); the skill, its wiring and its context prose (TSK-1099); the schedule family (TSK-1100) and the encoded table (TSK-1096) themselves; the shell (TSK-1120), the topic and change marks (TSK-1121) and the approved design (TSK-1122); opening the browser (the skill does); a stored or scheduled report.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Progress report amendment (2026-10-31)/A cf-status skill answers every status request from codeflow status in any adopting project

A cf-status skill answers every status request from codeflow status in any adopting project

TSK-1099todo

After this merges, anyone on an adopting project who asks a session for status gets the same figure-led progress document with the session's.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, anyone on an adopting project who asks a session for status gets the same figure-led progress document with the session's lanes, seats and context drawn in, in a few seconds, with every number from the command and every unverified fact marked.

Context

The operator asked on 2026-10-30 for a command or skill that knows how to report the status of things properly each time it is asked, in any project that adopts CodeFlow. Today the rules say how a status reply reads (.codeflow/rules/writing.md "Replies and status": outcomes first, live-checked facts, operator items once) and the map's "report status or hand off" row says what to check, but every session composes the report by hand, and the hourly report of a long run has no fixed shape. TSK-1095 computes the facts and TSK-1098 renders them; this task is the managed skill that runs them on every status request and adds the facts and context only the session has: which lanes the coordinator runs, which builders and seats carry them, which verdicts are in flight and which blockers it knows that no record holds yet.

Outcome: a session asked for status in any adopting project at the standard or full tier runs /cf-status: it picks the scope from the request (a task, an epic, the line, or the lanes it coordinates), writes its session-only facts to a --session file in the shipped schema (lane, task, builder, reviewer, seat, verdict in flight, blocker, each with its observation time), runs codeflow status --present <path> --session <file> and opens the document with cf-present, prepends one context block with what is being worked on and why it matters in a few plain lines, replies in chat with the handoff line and the anchor only, uses the --md form where no browser can open (a terminal-only harness, a PR body, a hand-off file), never computes a percent, an order or an estimate by hand, and marks every fact the command marked unverified as such; the orchestrator's status and hourly report guidance, the map row and the away report point to it instead of restating a shape.

Figure: the skill adds scope, session facts and context around one command and one surface; the numbers never come from the session.

Decisions, each reversible and disclosed here:

  • Name cf-status, matching the command it runs; trigger on a request for status, progress, where things stand, an hourly or hand-off report, or "report" in a coordination session; the operator confirms the name at plan approval (the earlier working name was cf-report).
  • Tier: standard and full (it needs cf-present); the minimal tier's map row keeps its text and gains a pointer to the command's --md form.
  • Session facts are observations, never state: the skill writes what it saw and when (a Herdr pane, a subagent id, a verdict file, a blocker it met), the command labels them session in the lanes view, and they never change a percent or a stage (TSK-1095 AC-4). The skill checks each changeable fact live before writing it, as the map row requires, or writes it with its last check time.
  • In chat the reply is the handoff line, the anchor's lines and, once, NEED YOUR ATTENTION for the operator-owned items the issues view names (a merge into main, a hook trust, a decision); counts and tooling come last, as the writing rule orders.
  • In a project with no project-management/ tier the skill says so, reports what git and the forge show through the command's unknown fields and never invents tasks, lanes or percents.
  • The hourly report of a long run (the coordinator's sweep, the away tick of TSK-1046 when it lands) is this skill with the same scope and a fresh session file each time, passing the previous run's facts file through --since so the since strip is filled; the skill keeps the last facts file per scope under the present state directory, never in the repository. The away report (codeflow report away, TSK-1045) stays the activation's own report and links the progress document.
  • The live cf-present session is the handover surface; an export is a review capture of the session at a time and the skill says so beside any export it hands over (the four reviews of 2026-10-30 found the export clipping stages; TSK-1101 fixes it).
  • Reuse, with versions (the operator's feedback of 2026-10-31). The skill keeps a topic register per scope under the present state directory (the topic key status:<scope key>, the open session id, the last facts file, the last context block); a repeat request on a scope with an open session runs the command with --since the kept facts file and applies the new document with codeflow present update <session> <file> --expected-revision N, so the report's history is the session's revision history and the runtime's change marks (TSK-1121) show what moved; it opens a new session only when the register has none or the operator asks for a fresh one, and says which it did. The context block is carried forward from the register and revised only where the session's facts changed, never rewritten; the reply names the revision and the change line ("since revision 3: 2 views changed, 1 new"). The session file also carries the session's judgment where the command cannot read it from a record: a recommended action, why and alternatives per blocker, and context, options, recommendation and reasoning per operator decision (TSK-1095 AC-15, labelled session), each with its observation time; the skill reads the answers the operator gives in the document's decision and form blocks through codeflow present feedback <session> --wait --format v2 in the existing acknowledge-and-deduplicate loop (cf-present/SKILL.md section 4 and references/feedback-loop.md; the v1 default delivers no answers) and acts on them as review input (SKILL.md section 4: an answer is an operator choice, never authority to bypass a gate), recording a durable decision in its real home.

Non-goals: the facts and the rendering (TSK-1095, TSK-1098); scheduling (the harness schedules, as TSK-1037 and TSK-1046 record); writing to any record or ledger; replacing codeflow status's text view, work next or orient.

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality enforcement into 4.0.0 amendment (2026-10-31)/Figures draw expected windows on a time axis with now, dependencies and the path to main

Figures draw expected windows on a time axis with now, dependencies and the path to main

TSK-1100todo

After this merges, a present document or a portal page can show when each item starts and is expected to end, what each waits on.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, a present document or a portal page can show when each item starts and is expected to end, what each waits on, where it is on the way to `main` and when it is expected there, on one time axis a reader grasps in a few seconds, with the exact windows and bases in the twin.

Context

The operator's feedback of 2026-10-30 (20:40, relayed by the coordinator) on the hand-built status presentation: the lane figure "still doesn't seem to convey certain things like the timing aspects clearly"; timing must read at a glance, on a real time axis with now, the expected windows and the dependencies; and the report must make clear what is on main, what is not, and when it gets there. The figure grammar has nine families and none draws time: the method says a series over time is "a table and one sentence naming that boundary" (explanation-method.md stage 3), the extent family draws reach from a baseline on one scale, and the layering family draws planes over one shared axis of moments with no durations (figure-grammar.md section 1). The hand-built report drew expected completion as extent bars from zero, so a reader could not see when an item starts, how windows overlap, or which dependency sets the end.

Outcome: a tenth family, schedule, drawn by the grammar module both runtimes load, places items as windows on one time axis (a band from the earliest to the latest end with a soft fill and a dashed outline, no solid part, the planning value a thin tick inside), marks the as-of moment as a vertical rule labelled as of, draws a completed event as a filled disc at its time, writes each dependency in words beside its band (after 426) and draws a connector from a predecessor's latest end to a successor's start only for a dependency the declaration marks governing, labelled with the predecessor's name, groups rows by lane or by location (main, integration line, pull request, branch), draws an agent-owned milestone such as the line's gate as a diamond at the end of its window, draws an operator-owned step as a readiness window ending in the human ring with the done event undated and written in words (your decision, no date) off the axis, hatches a stopped item's band with its condition (after the issue clears), writes not yet estimable with the reason for an item with no window instead of drawing it, and keeps the twelve rules (two non-hue channels per state, a legend, a one-sentence caption, a table twin with the exact windows and bases, a narrow recomposition that stacks rows and keeps the axis).

Figure: rows are items grouped by lane or location, bands run from the earliest to the latest end with the planning tick inside, a disc is a completed event, hatching is a stopped item with its condition, connectors show dependencies, the diamond is an agent milestone, the ring is the operator's decision, and the undated merge is written off the axis.

Decisions, each reversible and disclosed here:

  • The axis reads as a clock when the declaration's as_of carries a timestamp with its zone: ticks show the clock time with the zone named once in the axis title and the offset from the as-of moment (+2 h) beneath, at a cadence chosen from the span and the available width (two hours for a span up to a day at wide, six hours at narrow, one day for a span over two days, with the first and last tick always labelled and never more than one tick per 80 units), midnight carries its date, and the span starts before the earliest completed event so every disc sits in a labelled past; without a timestamp the axis is hours from the as-of moment, then days when a window passes 48 hours. A conditional or stopped band is drawn in relative units with its condition beside it and never as clock times, since its start is unknown. The renderer prints the basis of the windows beside the legend and a local legend of at most four entries under the figure. A second panel with a days scale may follow the same label column when a milestone lies beyond the hours span, and a lane figure that draws windows reuses this family's axis header rather than bare ticks.
  • Location gets a shared chip vocabulary in figure-grammar.md section 4, drawn by the module wherever an item appears (schedule rows, encoded table cells, flow stations): main (the layer-remote square with a check inside and a heavier outline, cat2 tone), line (the plain layer-remote square, cat1 tone), pull request (the node ring with the number), branch (the optional dashed outline), each with its word, so every pair differs on two non-hue channels (glyph and outline weight for main against line) and no page defines location by tone alone (the design brief revision 2, gap 4 and its marks section).
  • Marks reuse the vocabulary: optional (soft fill, dashed outline) for a window band, done for a completed event disc, blocked hatching for a stopped band, trans for a dependency connector, merge for an agent milestone diamond, human for the operator ring, limit for the as-of rule, with the accent tone on the critical path and cat1 and cat2 as lane companions; a new mark is added only if the builder shows the vocabulary cannot carry a state.
  • The declaration takes axis (unit and span), as_of, rows (item, group, state, a window with earliest, planning and latest, completed events with times, dependencies, kind item or milestone, owner agent or human, a condition for a stopped or conditional band, a reason for an item with no window). The field names follow the window shape TSK-1095's record specifies (earliest, planning and latest end as durations from the as-of moment, a start, a condition, a basis), so TSK-1098 can bind the facts without a translation layer; the derived binding itself (source into a codeflow status --json file) is TSK-1098's, since it needs the landed facts.
  • The chat form is the fenced ASCII above, under 78 columns.

Non-goals: a daemon or scheduler; computing the windows (TSK-1095); the progress document (TSK-1098); a Gantt editor; a calendar.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Quality enforcement into 4.0.0 amendment (2026-10-31)/The present export sizes each stage frame from its content and waits for stages to paint

The present export sizes each stage frame from its content and waits for stages to paint

TSK-1101todo

After this merges, an exported present page shows every stage the live session measured whole and declares every unmeasured stage with a.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an exported present page shows every stage the live session measured whole and declares every unmeasured stage with a notice at the fixed height, never a silent clip, so a review of a document with `html` stages reads what the live page shows or says where it cannot.

Context

Four reviewers of the status report design brief (Fable, Codex GPT-6 Astra, Grok 4.7 and a fresh Claude Opus reader, consolidated on 2026-10-30 21:42 EDT) read the exported page and all saw the same defect: the live session hosts each html stage inline (crates/codeflow-present/src/render.rs:591, .cf-stage-host), but the export puts each stage in a sandboxed frame with a fixed height (crates/codeflow-present/web/src/styles.css:651-654, .block--html iframe { block-size: 28rem }), so a stage taller than the frame is clipped (a nine-row lane board showed seven rows) and a shorter one leaves a blank gap, and at phone width the frame clips again. A static capture of the export taken before the stages' script has painted shows them blank. The reviewers ruled the export a review capture only and the live session the handover surface until this is fixed, and named the fix: size the frame from the stage's rendered height. Inlining the stage, their other option, is ruled out by the ADR-0049 boundary, so the height is measured on the live page in the export's geometry; an unmeasured stage keeps the fixed height with a notice, never a silent clip.

Outcome: an exported present page shows every measured html stage whole, at the height the live session measured for the export's own geometry, in light and dark and at phone width, with no clipping and no blank gap, declares any unmeasured stage instead of clipping it, and a capture of the export taken after the page reports ready shows every frame loaded.

Figure: the live page and the export today, and the export after the fix, for a tall stage and a short one.

Decisions, each reversible and disclosed here:

  • The runtime boundary of ADR-0049 is unchanged: the export keeps the sandboxed iframe with srcdoc, sandbox="", no allow-scripts and no allow-same-origin (crates/codeflow-present/src/export.rs, the export_html_stage_keeps_content_and_sandbox test), no script runs inside a frame, and the stage is never inlined in an export. The height comes from the live session instead, measured in the export's own geometry: the live page renders each stage a second time in a hidden measuring host that reproduces the export frame's layout (the export's content width in CSS pixels, its padding, no review rail), at each content width the export produces (its wide and narrow columns), and reports the rendered height (stage id, revision, export content width, the export rendering contract it measured under, height in CSS pixels) to the session store over the existing session channel; the live page's own inline host, whose width changes with the review rail, is never the source. The export rendering contract is a digest the binary computes over the inputs that decide a stage's rendered height in an export: the export stylesheets it embeds (export.rs:186, styles.css, figure.css, export-fallback.css), the root font size and type scale, the bundled fonts and the frame geometry; the live page reports the contract its measuring host ran under, and the export writes a stored height as the frame's block size only when the stored revision, content width and rendering contract all equal the ones it renders under, with a floor of one row and no ceiling (Codex round 8, F5: TSK-1109 of PR 449 changes the root scale and stage typography, so a height measured before it is wrong after it at the same revision and width). A stage with no matching measurement (a document never opened live at that revision, an export at another width, or a measurement under another rendering contract) is not measured: it keeps the present fixed height and shows a visible notice, "height not measured at this width; open the session", never a silent clip; opening the session re-measures under the current contract. The outcome is therefore: every measured stage whole, every unmeasured stage declared.
  • The reported height is validated input: numeric, bounded, bound to a stage id, a revision, a content width the store knows the export produces and the rendering contract digest the binary knows; a report for another revision, an unknown stage, an unlisted width or an unknown contract is dropped; a later report for the same stage, revision, content width and contract replaces the earlier one.
  • The export marks the document ready (data-cf-ready on the root) only after every frame has fired load or failed within a bounded wait, from the host page's own script, with a visible notice on a frame that did not load, so a capture tool can wait on one signal.
  • The export's chrome says what it is: a review capture of the session at a time, with the session the handover surface.

Non-goals: a change to the ADR-0049 boundary (no script in a frame, no inline stage in an export); the figure grammar; a new block or a schema field for height.

Outcome
