Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Push judging split amendment (2026-11-01)/A push is judged against the line its task record targets

A push is judged against the line its task record targets

TSK-1161todo

After this merges, an adopter whose task branch passes `codeflow ci --branch` is no longer refused by pre-push.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an adopter whose task branch passes `codeflow ci --branch` is no longer refused by pre-push, or judged against the wrong base, because of a target-line mismatch; a push to a destination that does not advertise the line is still refused. <!-- One line saying what someone can do once this lands, in the form "after this merges, <who> can <do what>". `codeflow validate --docs` refuses an open record created after the project adopted this section when the line is missing (`outcome_present_uids` in `.codeflow/project.toml`), and warns for an older open record. -->

Context

Judge a task branch's push against the line its record targets when the destination advertises that line, and treat an empty range whose head the line already contains as no change. Today the hook takes its policy and commit-history authority from the destination's default branch tip (judged_by, crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/push_set.rs:1016; --policy-from and --commits-from at :334), and that stays. The target it hands codeflow ci is the branch's declared line only when declared_bounds allows it (ci_target, :366-383; declared_bounds, :1475-1485, which sets aside a protected line whose advertised tip differs from the default branch's); --into is omitted when the range is empty (base == r.local_sha, :346-349); and target_base uses the declared line's advertised tip only on some paths (:1544-1559). codeflow ci --branch takes the work target from the head's task record (work_target_at, crates/codeflow-cli/src/cmd/ci.rs:1822-1830) and checks work admission against it (work.stable_planning_anchor, ci.rs:1840-1870). The two therefore diverge on some heads: a push can be refused, or judged against the wrong base, though ci on the same head passes. Found in TSK-1124's work; the issue 454 family, whose criteria half is TSK-350 AC-13. Non-goal: the default branch stays the policy and commit-history authority (TSK-350 requires it); this task changes only the target line and range base the push is judged against, not --policy-from. after this merges, a project with the profile on sees every completed, cancelled, reopened, superseded or unknown-start task compared with the band and profile revision frozen at its breakdown, as hit, miss, breach or no band, apart from forecasts, with each task's clocked time (blocked spans removed) and elapsed time (blocked included) printed; a project without the profile sees no change.

Context

Issue #334 item A, plus the Estimate block warnings of item G and the history rules of the method. A project with the profile on needs each finished task compared with the band it was given at breakdown. This task is the reader and the warnings. The templates, profile file and ADR are TSK-1013's; the end of the clock is TSK-1172's; open tasks are TSK-1012's.

Outcome: after this merges, a project with the profile on sees every completed, cancelled, reopened, superseded or unknown-start task compared with the band and profile revision frozen at its breakdown, as hit, miss, breach or no band, apart from forecasts, with each task's clocked time (blocked spans removed) and elapsed time (blocked included) printed; a project without the profile sees no change.

Rules:

  • No profile means no change. A task planned before the profile's effective date is "no band", never back-filled.
  • A malformed block warns, never fails. A breach never blocks.
  • A re-planned or split task keeps the parent's band and breach; cancelled stays in the denominator and is shown; unknown start is its own category.
  • A band moved after breakdown carries its reason. A band set by an approved planning amendment before the task's start is read as frozen (decision P2.6).

Non-goals: ongoing tasks and their age (TSK-1012); the clock's end rule (TSK-1172); class grouping (TSK-313); any default band set.

Design to settle in the PR (recommendation): both points ride in the acceptance block beside reviewed (the block is already bound to the reviewed commit and written by task status complete), not in the ledger: git holds them, ADR-0079's "derive from git" stands, and squash landings keep them. Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Estimation cut, TSK-336 split and issue 502 amendment (2026-11-01)/A claim is one step that records the task's start

A claim is one step that records the task's start

TSK-1173todo

after this merges, `work claim` creates the task branch and its worktree.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

after this merges, `work claim` creates the task branch and its worktree, commits `claimed:` and `claim_base:` into the task's record as one commit, pushes the branch with that commit and runs the start preflight; `estimate outcomes` takes the `claimed:` time as the start when it is the task's own claim; `work start` stays the read-only re-entry check for a resumed session and CI; and a claim with no later commit reads as an idle claim with its age.

Context

Issue #334 item F and section 1.5 ("claim and start are one step"), under operator decisions D1 and D4 (2026-11-01). Today work claim pushes an empty branch and prints "check it out and run codeflow work start". The task's start is only the first later commit, and a squash landing loses even that (ADR-0079:42-44). This task makes the claim the one step that starts the clock.

Outcome: after this merges, work claim creates the task branch and its worktree, commits claimed: and claim_base: into the task's record as one commit, pushes the branch with that commit and runs the start preflight; estimate outcomes takes the claimed: time as the start when it is the task's own claim; work start stays the read-only re-entry check for a resumed session and CI; and a claim with no later commit reads as an idle claim with its age.

Design (settle in the PR; recommendations from the start-clock research):

  • One commit on the task branch writes claimed: <RFC3339> and claim_base: <40-hex sha> into the record frontmatter (the one-line edit task status already makes, status_verb.rs), using git commit --only on the record path. In git, so ADR-0079's derivation holds and a squash or rebase landing keeps the start; the record's own PR may change its record (ADR-0076). Rejected: a ledger event (not in git, lost on a clone) and the pushed branch's creation time (not stored in git).
  • Order for a fresh claim: branch, worktree, the claim commit through status_verb::replace_if_unchanged, create-only push, preflight, with an attempt file in the worktree's git directory. The record is restored before any rollback; only a verified-disposable worktree and branch are rolled back, and never after the claim commit exists.
  • Order for an adopted (TSK-1093) or renamed branch: push as it is, create-only, so a lost race leaves the local branch unchanged; then write the two lines in the worktree where it is checked out, commit with --only, and push that commit with a lease. A staged or modified record file refuses the claim. A re-run resumes only on the two cases the attempt file proves; a lost race never resumes.
  • Start rule: the claimed: time; for an adopted or renamed branch the earlier of that and the first commit after claim_base, with provenance known, declared (the line readable, the commit or base not) or unknown. A hand-written line is read as declared, not as a claim. refresh_claim keeps the first time.
  • codeflow ci classification is not changed. The task's own claimed: edit selects Tracked and meets no new admission requirement (read from classification.rs:217-230 and :926-1067; this task proves it with fixtures).
  • Hotspots read first: TSK-1093, TSK-1125, TSK-1047, TSK-341, TSK-416 and TSK-1105 (both this task and TSK-1105 edit readiness.rs and work.rs; one writer at a time, the Coordinator's call; this task first, since it sets the shape).

Non-goals: an idle threshold or automatic release (D3, decided: flag and hand over only); a new verb (ADR-0057:48); changes to classification.

Outcome

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Estimation cut, TSK-336 split and issue 502 amendment (2026-11-01)/A pull request summary opens with enough context for anyone to know what it is and why

A pull request summary opens with enough context for anyone to know what it is and why

TSK-1174todo

after this merges, the shipped PR instructions tell every author, with one good and one bad example.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

after this merges, the shipped PR instructions tell every author, with one good and one bad example, that the first paragraph of the Summary states what the PR changes and why, in plain words and before any file name, identifier or detail; and `codeflow ci` warns, never fails, on the two cases it can recognize without judging meaning.

Context

Operator direction, 2026-11-01 (relayed by the Director): a pull request summary must open with just enough context for anyone to know what the PR is and why it exists, whether or not the change is functional, before any detail. Today the shipped instruction says the Summary "anchors a reader with no context in a few lines" (assets/base/rules/git-rules.md:150), and codeflow ci checks only the Summary's block shape: one prose paragraph, a list or table, at most one closing paragraph (pr_body.rs:1284-1325, summary_problem at :1222-1262). Nothing says what the first paragraph must hold, and nothing shows a good and a bad one.

Outcome: after this merges, the shipped PR instructions tell every author, with one good and one bad example, that the first paragraph of the Summary states what the PR changes and why, in plain words and before any file name, identifier or detail; and codeflow ci warns, never fails, on the two cases it can recognize without judging meaning.

What codeflow ci can and cannot enforce (read at line tip, 2026-11-01):

  • It cannot judge whether a paragraph states what changes and why. That is meaning; a check that guessed would fail closed on prose it cannot read. Review and cf-editorial-review judge it.
  • It can recognize two proxies from the Summary's visible lead text, which summary_blocks already collects per block (OpenBlock.text, pr_body.rs:1056-1066): a lead under 12 words, and a lead that opens with an identifier label (TSK-NNN, EPC-NNN, #NNN, or a path) before any words. Both are warnings only. The rule key stays git.pr_summary; the finding is raised at warn whatever the configured level, and not at all when the level is off (pr_body.rs:1292). No policy key is added, so the policy schema fixtures do not change.

Non-goals: judging meaning mechanically; a new policy key or level; a change to the block shape rule; any change to the sections other than Summary.

Outcome

Secret scanning cannot be replaced or evaded by the pull request

TSK-1176todo

after this merges, a pull request cannot replace, weaken or evade the secret scan that judges it, and a secret introduced by any commit is found.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

after this merges, a pull request cannot replace, weaken or evade the secret scan that judges it, and a secret introduced by any commit is found.

Context

Issues #279 and the PR 231 follow-ups (SEC-03, SEC-06, SEC-07). Split from TSK-336 on 2026-11-01. The whole-PR review of PR 479 graded TSK-336 Very Hard (9: S2 2, S6 1, S7 1, C 2, X 1, R 2), and a Very Hard task is split before claim. TSK-336 keeps the foundation (the default branch's code judges every pull request); this task takes one outcome with the criteria that prove it, moved and not copied, each marked with its old number. The five pieces are TSK-336, TSK-1175, TSK-1176, TSK-1177 and TSK-1178.

A pull request's secret scan runs the head's own copy of the workflow, so the head can change the scan that judges it; SEC-03 asks that the scan, like the policy verdict, come from trusted authority. SEC-06 (a replace ref hides a planted secret) and SEC-07 (an octopus merge's additions are not read) are scan-reading gaps in the same job. SEC-05 (low: legacy-fingerprint advice still covers a clean two-parent merge amended to add content) is advice only and suppresses no finding; disposition: tracked once here, revisit when this task edits the legacy-fingerprint advice (moved from TSK-336, where the revisit event was the same edit), where the fix is to require a remerge CONFLICT header naming the path. The scan job lives in the trusted verdict workflow that TSK-336 sets up, hence the edge.

Files shared by the five pieces (codeflow-ci.yml, codeflow-policy.yml, their installed copies and baselines, ci.rs): one writer at a time, as TSK-336's contract says; the Coordinator orders the writers. File sharing adds no scheduling dependency.

Outcome: the trusted: secret scan verdict runs the authority's scan logic over the range as data, finds a secret introduced by any commit (a replaced object or an octopus merge included), and no head-run secret scan job exists.

Non-goals: the other verdict jobs (TSK-336); who creates the authority check (TSK-1177).

Release/The 4.0.0 milestone fixes/Estimation cut, TSK-336 split and issue 502 amendment (2026-11-01)/Codeflow ci admits an append-only waiver annotation on a reopened task's criterion

Codeflow ci admits an append-only waiver annotation on a reopened task's criterion

TSK-1179todo

after this merges, `codeflow ci` accepts a reopened task whose completion landed when its own PR completes it with `AC-n.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

after this merges, `codeflow ci` accepts a reopened task whose completion landed when its own PR completes it with `AC-n: waived | <40-hex sha>`, where that commit appends a waiver annotation to criterion n, keeps its original text unchanged, cites the superseding commit by its SHA, and changes only planning records; any other change to a frozen criterion, and any unprovable condition, is refused with the cause named and the planning route.

Context

Issue 502. After a task's completion has landed and the task is reopened, work.criteria_frozen refuses any edit of its criteria in its own PR, and work.acceptance_binding accepts a waiver only when its commit amends that criterion. Together they leave a planning amendment as the only route, even for a one-line ruling. The report gives three attempts, each refused: rewrite the criterion text, a records-only note that does not amend the criterion, and a waiver note appended to the criterion's line.

This task opens one route inside the task's own PR, the second of the issue's two options, tightened: an append-only waiver annotation on the criterion's line, bound to the waiver commit's content and SHA. The original criterion text stays byte for byte, which is what the freeze protects, so the freeze is unchanged for every other edit. Neither a name nor a branch decides it.

Outcome: after this merges, a reopened task whose completion landed can complete in its own pull request with AC-n: waived | <40-hex sha>, where that commit appends a waiver annotation to criterion n, keeps its original text unchanged, cites the superseding commit by its SHA, and changes only planning records; any other change to a frozen criterion, and any unprovable condition, is refused with the cause named and the planning route.

Rules (fail closed; authority bound to content and SHAs):

  • Content, not claims. The waiver commit's diff for criterion n must be a pure append: the pre-image of the criterion block is an unchanged prefix of the post-image, and the added text matches the annotation form Waived <date>: <reason>. Superseded by <40-hex sha>. No other line of any criterion changes, and no criterion is added or removed.
  • SHA-bound. The waiver value is a full 40-hex commit id. A branch, tag, abbreviated id, PR number, person or role name is refused. The commit must be in the head's own range, after the reopen commit and strictly before reviewed (the existing ordering rules), and must be the commit that adds the annotation (not a later or earlier record commit).
  • The superseding commit is named by SHA and resolved. The annotation's SHA must resolve to a commit reachable from the head's history; it is recorded, and review judges whether it supports the reason. The check proves existence and reachability, never meaning.
  • Authority from the trusted side. The rule runs under the policy authority the run pins (--policy-from, the pre-push hook's default branch tip), never the head's copy: a head that edits the policy cannot admit its own waiver.
  • Paths. The waiver commit changes only the task's own record, judged by the planning-only test TSK-1129 gives both waiver routes (no product code, policy, harness instruction, hidden file, adopter-facing path, symbolic link or submodule).
  • Verb and CI agree. codeflow task status <id> complete and codeflow ci reach the same verdict and print the same refusal.
  • Scope. Only a task with a landed completion that was reopened is affected. Other tasks' criteria, a task that was never completed, and a criterion text rewrite keep today's refusals.

Non-goals: letting a reopened task rewrite criterion text; accepting a waiver by role or name; changing work.acceptance_binding for a task that was never reopened; the planning-amendment route, which stays.

Security task. It changes policy authority, the rule that decides who may change or waive a frozen criterion, so it carries the cross-lineage Codex security review set out in the Execution contract.

Split on 2026-11-02 after the cross-lineage review of the cut: with the waiver annotation scored as a changed persisted shape (S1 3, as TSK-1173 scores its claimed: line) the task graded Very Hard (9), and a Very Hard task is split before claim. This task keeps the CI side: the freeze exception, the annotation form, the pure-append proof and the controls. TSK-1180 takes the task status complete verb, the parity of the two, the refusal text and the docs, and depends on this task. Until TSK-1180 lands the verb still refuses, which fails closed.

Dependency on TSK-1129 (PR 478, issue 465): TSK-1129 gives the own-range waiver route its planning-only test and shares waiver_problem with this task. Its record is not on this line yet, so depends_on cannot name it without a dangling reference. The dependency is recorded here; the revisit event is PR 478 merging, and the planning amendment that follows it adds TSK-1129 -> TSK-1179 to depends_on and the EPC-022 graph. Until that edge exists the task is a root in the graph but must not be claimed.

Outcome

Release/Quality defaults, local scan parity and seat capacity/Strict evidence defaults amendment (2026-10-26)/One exemption register and relaxation report serves every managed check

One exemption register and relaxation report serves every managed check

TSK-424todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issues #274 (item 2 to 5), #275 (items 4 and 5) and #279 (item 5) each ask for the same mechanism: a project that relaxes a default check, or exempts one occurrence from it, records why, who owns it and when it is revisited, in one format every check reads, and codeflow ci reports the register's health in the pull request evidence. CodeFlow 3.1.1 has no waiver or exemption concept, so each adopting project invents its own register, field set and refusal rules.

Outcome: one exemption register format under .codeflow/ serves every managed check this epic adds: each entry carries id, kind, rule, paths, value where it applies, reason, task id, owner role, date, expiry and revisit trigger; the register also holds permanent admissions (admitted, frozen-tree, provenance and removed rows); for every blocking class an entry applies only when the default-branch authority holds it; a check refuses a missing field, a malformed task id, an exception past its expiry, a head-introduced entry that matches nothing, a class-wide entry and an inline suppression that cites no register id, and reports a stale base entry for retirement in that pull request; admitted debt, admitted once in the pull request that introduces the check and compared against the previously admitted baseline by stable occurrence identity, can only shrink; and codeflow ci reports entries, expiring entries, baseline size and its change in the PR evidence.

Rules:

  • The register (provisional .codeflow/exemptions.json) and the baseline (provisional .codeflow/baseline/<check>.json) are project files. The default-branch authority (TSK-1077) governs the check's own configuration and level, so a head can never turn a check off or lower it (as the secret-scan exemptions are judged, TSK-292, TSK-336). For a blocking class, an entry applies only when the authority holds it; a pull request that adds only register entries is the exemption-PR class (docs/policy-reference.md:301-308) generalised to the register file, and lands through the operator's merge. For warn-tier and report-only consumers, an entry introduced or amended at the head applies only with every required field and is listed in the PR evidence as a new or changed exemption, never silent. An entry retired at the head is accepted when its occurrence is gone at the head (the ordinary same-PR repair-and-retirement); a base entry that matches nothing at the head is reported as stale and retired in that pull request, never refused; a head entry that matches nothing is refused. A setting max_exemption_days bounds the expiry of exceptions.
  • Admitted debt is separate from exemptions and has its own lifecycle. The baseline records stable occurrence identities (path, rule and a content hash of the occurrence, never a line number), each naming its fix task. The ratchet compares the head's occurrences against the previously admitted baseline, the one at the default-branch authority, never against a baseline the head edited: a pull request passes only when every head occurrence is in the admitted baseline by identity, so growth and replacement debt (one admitted occurrence removed, a different one added) are refused whatever the head's baseline file says; a head may change the baseline only to remove occurrences that are gone (shrinking), and any other head edit of the baseline is refused. Initial admission needs no extra pull request: codeflow baseline admit <check> (provisional) writes the first baseline from the current occurrences, each with a fix task, inside the pull request that first introduces the strict check for that project, and codeflow ci accepts an admission only when the authority holds no admitted baseline for that check and prints the admitted occurrences in the PR evidence; every later head may only shrink it, and widening admitted debt is forbidden by the ratchet (any relaxation is a separate operator-authorized policy change, never a baseline edit). An occurrence with no fix task is refused at admission and at validation.
  • A project-wide relaxation of a default (issue #275 item 5, #279 item
    1. is an entry of kind relaxation naming the setting and its value, with the same required fields; codeflow ci lists each one.
  • Permanent admissions: admitted rows without expiry (allowed lowers; never for secret-name, ignored-path, oversize, frozen-tree or provenance classes, except the per-path size admission of TSK-323's route 3); frozen-tree rows (the tree id equals the authority's; the candidate's final tree is compared, modes included); provenance rows (source repository, commit and digest, checked each run); and removed rows for TSK-428's citation rule. Expiry applies to exceptions only. Task state an entry cites is read from the authority's records.
  • The checks that consume the register are TSK-425, TSK-426 and TSK-428; this task ships the reader, the writer, the schema and the report, with one consumer stub test.

Non-goals: any one check (the consumers); the secret-scan and dependency-audit exemption routes that exist today (unchanged).

Amended 2026-10-27 by the quality asks amendment. The review question on copied values moved to TSK-1033 in EPC-022 (4.0.0), an instruction-level change; AC-5 keeps the exemption question. TSK-428's amendment of the same day records the adopter's admission rule for exceptions (judged from the target branch, so a pull request cannot admit its own) beside this task's AC-4 (a head-introduced entry with every field, listed for the reviewer); AC-7 compares the two before the register is built.

Amended 2026-10-29 by the content policy amendment (design revision 5 for issue #279, decided by the operator that day). The Outcome, the Rules and AC-1 to AC-4 now state the decided behaviour. Until then this record read configuration, level and baseline from "the trusted base" and accepted a head-introduced entry for every consumer once it carried every field. Reasons: TSK-1077 makes the default branch at one SHA the only policy authority (a pull request's base still bounds its range); and a head-introduced exemption for a blocking class lets a pull request admit the file it adds when a reviewer misses a report line (design N-6), which settles AC-7's open question as authority-only. The permanent row kinds serve the frozen, vendored and size cases the operator decided (decision 8, design section 2.6).

Outcome
Quality defaults, local scan parity and seat capacity EPC-024

Release/Quality defaults, local scan parity and seat capacity/Original plan (Planning notes)/A define-once gate refuses hand-copied values and code

A define-once gate refuses hand-copied values and code

TSK-425todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #274, item 1 and the audit behind it. Two adopting repositories held hundreds of hand copies of names, ids, team slugs, paths and settings, most bypassing a home that already existed (an exported constant nothing imports, a required-check guard covering two of six names, workflow branch filters drifted from the policy); a team rename needed 122 lines in 50 files edited by hand, and both reviews checked only that the edit was complete. CodeFlow has no duplication or known-values check, and the project runs its own as a runner: custom target.

Outcome: a define-once gate target type runs the configured language adapters for copied literals and blocks, a stack-neutral known-values check from a project file where each value names its one home and its generated or checked mirrors, and an advisory discovery mode that lists literals appearing in several files; every refusal cites the home and the register route of TSK-424.

Rules:

  • Adapters are configured per stack in .codeflow/test-config.json (for example Biome style/noMagicNumbers, ESLint sonarjs/no-duplicate-string, Ruff PLR2004 and RUF100, jscpd, Regal, tflint); the gate runs the ones the project's stack and installed tools support and reports the rest as not run.
  • The known-values file (provisional .codeflow/known-values.json) lists value, home and mirrors; any other occurrence fails, and a mirror is checked for equality with its home.
  • Discovery mode is advisory and never blocks.
  • An exemption or baseline entry from TSK-424 clears an occurrence; an inline suppression must cite a register id.

Non-goals: adding adapters for languages the project does not use; rewriting the copies the check finds.

Amended 2026-10-27 by the quality asks amendment (the operator's D4 ask). The instruction to declare each value once and the cf-reviewer question on copied values and code are TSK-1033 in EPC-022 (4.0.0), instruction-level changes that ship alone; this gate enforces what that text states and needs TSK-424's register, so it stays here. The first-pass survey for the instruction is in TSK-1033.

Outcome
Quality defaults, local scan parity and seat capacity EPC-024

Strict typing and linting are the default tooling per language

TSK-426todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #275, items 2, 3 and 4 as revised on 2026-10-22 (strict by default, explicit opt-out). In two adopting repositories, three TypeScript projects were never type-checked as a whole (node --test strips types; no gate runs tsc -b), Python was 53 % and 5 % annotated with no type checker or linter, inline workflow shell had no ShellCheck or actionlint, OpenTofu had no tflint and Rego no Regal. No managed gate target or template type-checks a project, and the test-config schema has no notion of a strictness profile.

Outcome: for each language cf-stack detects, it sets up the strict tooling the issue lists at the strictest settings each tool allows, with the checks per profile that AC-8's capability matrix marks applicable, the managed gate runs those targets in quick and CI modes, suppressions without a reason and unused suppressions fail the gate, and a project relaxes a specific setting only through a TSK-424 relaxation entry that codeflow ci reports.

The per-language set (the issue's list, confirmed at build against each tool's current release): TypeScript tsc -b with strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noUnusedParameters and noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature, no allowJs without checkJs, typescript-eslint strictTypeChecked and stylisticTypeChecked with projectService, no-explicit-any as an error and ban-ts-comment with descriptions; Python pyright strict or mypy --strict, Ruff with a broad selection including ANN401 and RUF100, a locked tool environment; Go golangci-lint v2 with a committed config; shell and workflows ShellCheck --enable=all, actionlint and zizmor; OpenTofu tflint preset = "all" with validation on every variable; Rego opa check --strict with schemas and Regal; JSON and YAML config JSON Schema validation. Existing debt enters the TSK-424 baseline, which only shrinks.

Non-goals: the instruction and review changes (TSK-1032 in EPC-022, formerly TSK-427's); typed-model generation from schemas beyond the recommendation cf-stack gives; CodeFlow's own vendored Python (TSK-427).

Amended 2026-10-27 by the quality asks amendment (the operator's D3 ask), adding two outcomes to the tooling:

  • Typed data at every boundary, per profile. AC-8's capability matrix records which boundary checks each profile's tools support, and cf-stack sets up the ones it marks applicable:
    • a typed profile gets a typed-model library that validates on parse (for example Pydantic v2 in Python, zod in TypeScript, serde in Rust, structs with a validator in Go; a plain dataclass or interface alone does not validate) and the strict rules that flag untyped boundary data (for example Ruff ANN401, typescript-eslint no-unsafe-assignment and no-unsafe-member-access, pyright reportUnknown*);
    • a schema-only profile gets its schema check (OpenTofu variable validation, Rego with opa check --strict and schemas, JSON Schema for JSON and YAML config);
    • a profile with neither (for example shell) has the boundary check recorded as unsupported with its treatment, and the gate reports it as not applicable. TSK-1032 states the instruction in 4.0.0.
  • TypeScript is the default for new projects and new files. cf-stack sets a new JavaScript project up as TypeScript, and an existing one with tsc and checkJs (JSDoc types) over its JavaScript in place, without rewriting it (the operator's decision of 2026-10-27, stated in TSK-1032).

First-pass survey (planning, 2026-10-27, line tip 5f2fe3827): assets/base/agents/skills/cf-stack/SKILL.md:29-35 says "Do not mandate TypeScript, a validator library"; assets/base/testing/templates/example-node.json and example-python.json have no type-check target; no template names a typed-model library.

Release/Quality defaults, local scan parity and seat capacity/Original plan (Planning notes)/A repository holds only what it needs long term

A repository holds only what it needs long term

TSK-428todo

After this merges, an adopter's path gate refuses junk that is never wanted in a repository and warns on judgement calls.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an adopter's path gate refuses junk that is never wanted in a repository and warns on judgement calls, judged from the default branch's code and policy, so a pull request cannot weaken the check or admit its own file.

Context

Issue #279, items 1 to 3 and 5. Nothing in the shipped instructions, the reviewer's verdict or the gates asks whether a new file belongs in the repository. Two adopting repositories accumulated 24 MB of tool output as JSON under docs/verification/, a 4.3 MB research file in its fourth draft, a retired prototype with committed dist/ and a vendored minified library, 117 per-run model-checker summaries, a 111 KB manifest of hashes for files not carried, one-off session scripts and byte-identical draft mirrors; every item passed review.

The instruction is TSK-1030's (4.0.0): what belongs in a repository, that git history keeps removed evidence, and that evidence is summarised unless the raw form is what is cited. This task enforces it in the path gate.

Rules (decided 2026-10-29, design revision 5 for issue #279, decisions 7, 9, 10 and 11):

  • Placement. The checks are content classes of path_policy, judged by codeflow ci in the pull_request_target job from the authority's binary and policy, and by pre-commit and pre-push from the landed policy. They are never a testing/ target or a job in codeflow-ci.yml, because those run head code on pull_request and a block tier there would let a pull request change the check that judges it (design N-5).
  • Tiers. Block refuses; warn lists the finding in the codeflow ci PR evidence and passes; a warning acknowledged in the body informs the reviewer and is never a pass. Default tiers (decision 7, hybrid): block per-task evidence folders under the configured root (default docs/verification/, so docs/verification/TSK-001/...), node_modules/, __pycache__/, .pytest_cache/, .mypy_cache/ and .DS_Store; warn dist/, *.log and other run output, single-tool caches, byte-identical duplicates, superseded iterations (an explicit superseded marker outside record frontmatter, or a removed path added again), large files, draft siblings (-r2, -v3, -final), tool-output-like JSON or text, uncited research, and a live record citing a path under the local evidence home. A class moves only by a reviewed policy change on the authority.
  • No review-record class (decision 10: this repository holds 11 legitimate review paths). The superseded marker warns (decision 11: three accepted ADRs would fail a block). No named catalogue and no public fixture format (decision 9).
  • Scope. Junk classes use net scope: a path in the head tree that matches a class and is absent from the base tree. A file added and removed on a line never blocks its pull request, and an existing file is never judged by an unrelated pull request. Audit mode (codeflow ci --audit) lists the final tree and never gates. Secret names and the gitleaks content scan keep history scope, untouched here.
  • Citation safety. When evidence is removed, a live citation of the removed path is refused unless it carries a commit pin that resolves to a commit reachable from the authority the run judges with and holding the file. Managed baseline files and their exact mirrors are exempt from this check only.
  • Exceptions. Every exception is a TSK-424 register entry; for a blocking class it applies only when the authority holds it, so a pull request cannot admit the file it adds (design N-6). No entry exempts a directory as a whole.
  • Exempt inputs. Content classes exempt only .codeflow/policy.json, .codeflow/project.toml and the two policy workflows; TSK-424's register file is not exempt unless a later operator amendment says so.
  • Matchers are declarative only (folder segment, exact name, suffix, name token, root glob, size, duplicate blob, superseded marker), compiled into the binary, with no executable adapters. Name patterns compare whole parts of the file name without its last extension, split at -, _ and ., in lower case, so confirmed does not match confirm.

Non-goals: CodeFlow's own managed-copy footprint (TSK-429); deleting what adopters already hold; this repository's own docs/verification/ clean-up (TSK-1081).

History. Amended 2026-10-27 by the quality asks amendment: the instruction and the review question (former AC-1 and AC-2) moved to TSK-1030, and the gate took three tiers from the issue's comments of that day, as a quick-gate target under crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/ with thresholds in .codeflow/test-config.json, a review-record block class, a superseded-marker block class, and a baseline for existing repositories. Amended 2026-10-29 by the content policy amendment, which replaced each of those with the rules above for the reasons given there (design N-5 and N-6; decisions 7, 10 and 11; net scope).

First-pass survey (planning, 2026-10-27, line tip 5f2fe3827): no shipped gate has a path, name or size rule for added files; the managed assets/base/gitignore covers secrets, editor files and worktrees only; this repository's docs/verification/ holds 91 MB in 60 folders and 79 records cite paths in it, so citation safety decides whether its own clean-up is possible.

Outcome

Context

Issue #234, items 1 and 2. Long multi-seat runs stop when one family's subscription hits its 5-hour or weekly limit; the operator notices, signs in to another account by hand and restarts the seats. Nothing in CodeFlow reads the limit state or knows which account a project uses. The issue rules out automatic rotation between one person's subscriptions, which the vendors' terms forbid, and CodeFlow never reads, copies or stores tokens.

Outcome: a project can keep an untracked account-profile file that maps each family to a config home (and optionally an API-key fallback with a spend cap), CodeFlow launches each CLI with only its own config-home variable set (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME, GROK_HOME), and CodeFlow reads each family's limit state where the CLI exposes it (Claude Code's statusline rate_limits, Codex's app-server rate-limit read and events, Grok Build's limit-hit error) into one structure the routing of TSK-432 consumes.

Rules: the profile file (provisional .codeflow/local/accounts.toml, untracked through the managed ignore, or under the user's home) holds paths and caps, never tokens; the launch table in cf-model-orchestrator/resources/routing/transport.md and the Herdr launch in cf-herdr pass the config home; the limit reader is best-effort and says when a family exposes nothing. The Codex app-server methods come from source and mirrors, not official docs (the issue's not-verified list), so the reader is qualified on the supported release.

Non-goals: the threshold policy, the fallback and resume (TSK-432); any automatic switch between subscriptions.

A target's test report decides its result, and every skip or disabled target is recorded

TSK-1005todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #303, filed against CodeFlow 3.1.1 (48104f48b). The test engine decides a target's result from the command's exit code alone (crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/gate.rs, gate_verdict). A missing, stale or malformed report, skipped tests, tests the report marks flaky, and targets switched off in config (enabled: false, ci_skip without a reason) all pass with no recorded reason. The issue states this is a deliberate tightening of designed behaviour, not a defect, so it is a feature here, beside the other quality defaults of this epic.

Outcome: in essential and full mode a test-executing target passes only when its own report, produced or cache-restored for this run, shows tests executed and every skipped, flaky or switched-off item has a recorded entry; the gate evidence names those items.

Rules:

  • A target that executes tests declares a report. A target that does not (lint or format) declares kinds: ["lint"] and is exempt from the report checks. This task adds the kinds field; TSK-1009 adds the evidence kinds to it.
  • Each allowance (a skipped id, a quarantined flaky id, a disabled target, a CI-skipped target) is an entry in TSK-424's exemption register, of its own kind, with reason, owner and expiry. The issue's per-target skip_allow and quarantine lists become register entries so the epic keeps one register (EPC-024 AC-1); the PR states this choice.
  • No entry makes an absent, unparseable or leftover report pass: the only route to a passing report is one this run wrote or a valid cache restoration. Register entries cover skipped, flaky, disabled and CI-skipped items only.
  • Existing projects get the checks report-only first; block comes through a reviewed policy change, and new scaffolds write it on.

Non-goals: quick mode (format and lint by design, so the pre-push notes stay as they are); CodeFlow's own early-returning tests (TSK-361 in EPC-023); the coverage floor (TSK-1006).

The quality contract states an 80% aggregate production line floor wherever the stack supports it, with exclusions only with an owner, reason and removal condition (cf-model-orchestrator resources/quality/coverage.md). The test engine enforces a floor only when a target carries its own coverage block with at least one rule, accepts any minimum, evaluates it only in full mode, and never applies defaults.coverage (crates/codeflow-core/src/testing/config/mod.rs, parsed but read only by the glob check), although the shipped schema says the defaults are "applied when targets omit them". The changed-files scope is implemented but refused on every target. The issue's defect half, defaults the schema promises and the engine ignores, is TSK-1014 in EPC-022 (4.0.0), placed there by the Codex review of PR 343. This task is the feature half: strict defaults with recorded exceptions, which change designed behaviour.

Outcome: every enabled test-executing target resolves an aggregate coverage floor of at least 80, from its own rules or the defaults, or carries a recorded exemption; essential runs evaluate it, a changed-files floor works against the gate's base, and every exclusion names its reason, owner and removal condition.

Rules:

  • TSK-1014 makes defaults.coverage apply to targets that set no rules; this task makes a floor mandatory. The scaffolded default is one global rule at 80.
  • An aggregate minimum below 80, and every exemption, exclusion and per-file exception, is an entry in TSK-424's register with reason, owner and expiry; plain exclude strings are read with a warning for one release.
  • essential evaluates the floors for the targets it runs; quick stays format and lint. If essential cost is rejected in review, the PR instead names one supported builder route and the skills cite it, as the issue allows.
  • The changed_files scope works against --since <ref> or the landing candidate's merge base and is documented as whole-file; changed-line coverage is a later step, not this task.
  • Existing projects get the checks report-only first; block comes through a reviewed policy change, and new scaffolds write it on.

Non-goals: changed-line coverage; CodeFlow's own coverage evidence per landing candidate (TSK-369 in EPC-023).

Amended 2026-10-27 by the quality asks amendment (the operator's D2 ask): "every test-running target" explicitly includes project tooling, meaning the scripts, build helpers, code generators, release and CI helpers and hook scripts a repository runs to build, check or release itself. Tooling code is held to the floor like product code; only generated, vendored, fixture and test code may be excluded, through the register. TSK-1031 (EPC-022, 4.0.0) states this in the shipped instructions and has cf-stack wire a tooling test target; this task enforces it, because the default floor and its exemptions need TSK-424. First-pass survey (planning, 2026-10-27, line tip 5f2fe3827): the nine test-config templates under assets/base/testing/templates/ have no tooling target; codeflow doctor --check test-config does not look for code no target covers; this repository runs eight scripts/test_*.py files with no coverage (.codeflow/test-config.json:299), and three scripts have no test file.

Release/Quality defaults, local scan parity and seat capacity/Strict evidence defaults amendment (2026-10-26)/Acceptance evidence names its test or command, and a fix proves it failed before

Acceptance evidence names its test or command, and a fix proves it failed before

TSK-1008todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #301, filed against CodeFlow 3.1.1 (48104f48b). The method asks that every criterion is evidenced with file:line or a command, and that every defect fix adds a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after. The acceptance checker accepts any non-empty text as evidence (crates/codeflow-core/src/workgraph/record_text.rs, the <outcome> | <evidence> parse) and has no notion of a test or a fix; acceptance.rs states it proves structure and binding only. The issue proposes a deliberate tightening, so it is a feature of this epic.

Outcome: a verified criterion's evidence names a test path that exists at the reviewed commit, a command with a gate-run id, or a manual: entry that states what was inspected and why no automated test fits; and a fix carries its regression test with a failing run before the fix and a passing run at the reviewed commit, or a recorded regression: none: <reason>. Where the default branch's policy turns it on, a run: command is also rerun at the reviewed commit inside an operating-system sandbox, and the binding fails when its exit status differs from the one recorded; every other token stays a structure and existence check.

Rules:

  • New evidence tokens: test: <repo path>[::<name>], cmd: <command> with a gate-run id, and manual: <what, where, result; why no test>. A bare manual: <reason> is refused.
  • A range holding a fix: commit, or a task whose work_type is fix or hotfix, needs a regression field in the acceptance block: the test reference, fails-at: <sha> <run id> (an ancestor of the fix, inside or outside the PR range) and passes-at: <reviewed sha> <run id>, or none: <reason>, which codeflow ci prints.
  • codeflow test --only <target> can record a run at a named sha in the gate-runs home so the failing result is attributable. Where that home is not readable (hosted CI), ci checks the structure only and the local completion step checks the results.
  • Rules apply only to acceptance blocks first written after the activation commit, recorded as work_records_baseline is; a report-only pass lists active tasks that would fail; block comes through a reviewed policy change, and new scaffolds write it on.
  • Issue #450 adds a rerun. A criterion's evidence may hold a fourth token, run: <command> => exit <code>, where <code> is the exit status the command must return at the reviewed sha (exit 0 for a pass, a nonzero code for a planted failure; a journey that needs setup names a committed script that plants, runs and cleans up). A run: token satisfies AC-1's token rule. With the rerun on, codeflow ci and codeflow task status <id> complete run each run: command against the reviewed sha and fail the binding when the exit status differs from <code> or the command times out. With it off, or for evidence without a run: token, today's behaviour holds. Hosted ci runs nothing: it checks the token's structure only and reports that no result was verified. The security contract below governs every run. AC-6 holds the contract. If the builder finds the rerun too large for one pull request, it is split out as one tracked EPC-024 task that takes AC-6, through the batched epic amendment, and is never dropped.

Security contract for the rerun (Codex review 06 of PR 449, F7). The command comes from a record a contributor writes, so it is untrusted code, and the rerun is a command-execution feature. Each rule names the threat it closes and why its design is the standard one.

  • Activation from the trusted authority. work.evidence_rerun (off by default) and its limits (timeout_secs, network, default false) are read only from the policy at the default branch resolved to one SHA, the authority TSK-1077 defines (ADR-0091), before any candidate input is read. The candidate branch's policy, the working copy's and the exported tree's are never read for these keys. A missing or unreadable authority means off, with a note; it never means on. ci and task status complete use the same resolver. Threat closed: a contributor turning on execution of their own command, or loosening its limits, from the change under review. Standard design: authorization comes from the protected base, never from the change (the trust rule GitHub applies to fork pull requests, and CodeFlow's own ADR-0091).
  • Containment by a named provider, fail closed. The runner launches the command itself inside an operating-system sandbox: Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) on macOS and bubblewrap (bwrap) on Linux, the same mechanisms the harness sandboxes use, with a deny-by-default profile. The existing crates/codeflow-core/src/security/actions.json supplies the action and read-rule catalogue the profile draws on; translating it into Seatbelt and bubblewrap profiles is new work in this task, since no profile generator exists today. The profile allows reads of the exported tree and the system toolchain paths, writes only to the exported tree and one fresh temporary directory, and no network unless the trusted policy's network is true. The command starts with an empty environment plus a fixed allowlist (PATH set to fixed system directories, HOME and TMPDIR set to the temporary directory, LANG); nothing is inherited, so tokens, GIT_*, SSH_AUTH_SOCK and cloud credentials are absent, and the profile denies the home credential paths. If the provider is missing (Windows, no bwrap), cannot start, or any check below fails, the runner refuses before running any command and says why. A timeout and a temporary directory are not described as containment. codeflow test's runner is not the boundary: it inherits the environment and applies no sandbox. The required properties follow; the mechanism is the builder's, settled with the task's security review.
    • Provider floor. The provider executable is resolved independently of the candidate (a fixed trusted path or the trusted policy, never the exported tree, the candidate's PATH or its configuration), and its version is checked against a stated minimum secure version before use; an older or unverifiable provider is refused. For bubblewrap the floor is 0.12.0 or later: earlier versions have a setup-time symlink escape when creating files on attacker-controlled content ([GHSA-pxhw-h44j-8pfx](https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap/security/advisories/GHSA-pxhw-h44j-8pfx)). The Seatbelt floor is the macOS version the builder qualifies and records.
    • Tree fidelity. The exported tree's tracked paths, file bytes, modes and link targets equal the pinned commit's tree exactly, with no attribute processing: export-ignore, export-subst, filters and any candidate, working-copy or local (info/attributes) attributes change nothing. A tree entry the export cannot reproduce faithfully (a submodule, for example) is refused, never skipped. The export keeps no .git link to the repository's object store. A plain git archive does not meet this (it applies export attributes; this repository's .gitattributes:18 drops a tracked file from it), so it is not the named mechanism.
    • Setup never follows candidate links. Exporting the tree and creating every sandbox path (mounts, bind targets, the temporary directory and any file written during setup) never follows a symlink from the candidate tree to a location outside it; a link that would require that is refused before execution. In-tree links are reproduced as links and resolved only inside the sandbox.
    • Trusted probe. The containment probe is trusted launcher code, not the candidate's, run under the same provider and profile as the command. It uses synthetic controls the launcher creates outside the sandbox (a file holding a fresh secret token, a writable file and, when the trusted policy's network is off, a reachable local endpoint), and attempts a read, a write and a connection from inside the sandbox. The probe establishes the outcome of each attempted operation independently and reports it through a channel the candidate cannot write. A read counts as denied only when trustworthy evidence shows the attempt did not obtain the file's content (for example, the launcher checks that the probe's reported read result does not contain the token it wrote); an unchanged file, no output or a generic command failure does not count. A write counts as denied only when the control file is unchanged, and a connection only when the endpoint received nothing. The read and write denials are always required; the connection denial is required only when network is off. A missing control, an unreachable endpoint, a probe error or any required outcome not established refuses the run. The mechanism is the builder's. Threat closed: a command that reads credentials, changes files outside its tree or sends data out, then returns the expected code. Standard design: an OS sandbox with deny by default, an emptied environment and a pre-run probe, as Bazel's sandboxed execution and the harness sandboxes do; refusing when the boundary cannot be shown is the fail-closed rule of 2026-10-24.
  • Parsing as untrusted input. One run: token per evidence field; the token takes the rest of the field. It splits at the last occurrence of => exit (one space either side) that is followed by a decimal code from 0 to 255 and then the end of the field; the text before it is the command. CodeFlow applies no unquoting, escape processing or expansion of its own: quotes and backslashes in the command pass byte for byte to /bin/sh -c inside the sandbox, so a => exit inside quotes is command text unless it is the final delimiter. Refused before any execution: no delimiter, a code outside 0 to 255 or with a sign or leading zeros, an empty command, a newline, NUL or other control character, and a command over 4096 bytes. The reviewed sha, export path, sandbox profile and policy are computed before the command is read, and the command reaches only the sandboxed shell's argument, never a path, a git argument or the policy lookup. Threat closed: delimiter or quoting tricks that change the expected code, or that leak command text into runner setup, export or policy selection. Standard design: a fixed grammar with a single defined split point, and untrusted text passed as one argument, never re-parsed by the host.
  • Distinct failure classes. A provider, probe, export or launch failure is reported out of band by the launcher, never through the command's exit code, and refuses the binding as "rerun could not run"; only a command that ran to completion is compared with <code>. A timeout kills the process group and refuses. Threat closed: a runner or sandbox failure that happens to return the expected nonzero code being read as a reproduced failure.
  • The acceptance block format is shared with TSK-436 (deferred results, 4.0.0), which lands first; this task extends that format, not a copy.

Non-goals: proving evidence honest beyond the structural and existence checks above and the opted-in run: rerun; rerunning test: or cmd: evidence; re-judging completed records.

Each release records the tests and checks behind every managed script

TSK-1043todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #372 (CodeFlow 3.1.1, opened 2026-10-28 01:16Z). CodeFlow installs executable scripts into adopting repositories as managed files. An adopter with strict checks (a type checker, a linter, coverage) must decide whether those scripts are in scope, cannot fix a managed file (the next codeflow update overwrites it), and cannot tell from the repository what CodeFlow checked upstream. The adopter's repository holds 36 tracked Python files from 9 distinct scripts (each in .agents/skills/, .claude/skills/ and twice under .codeflow/.baseline/); cf-evaluate-model/scripts ships 5 scripts with 3 test files, and cf-herdr/scripts/deliver.py, which types prompts into other agents' terminals, ships no test. .codeflow/manifest.json records src, ownership, sha256 and exec per file and nothing about tests or checks. The adopter excludes byte-identical managed copies from its strict checks by a path and SHA-256 manifest, as a recorded workaround.

Outcome: every executable file CodeFlow installs is covered by an upstream test suite and passes the strict checks CodeFlow applies to its own code, and each release ships a machine-readable assurance record per managed executable (hash, covering tests and their result, coverage, type checker and linter with versions, settings and results, the release commit and CI run), which codeflow doctor checks against the installed files, so an adopter can exclude a file from its own checks exactly while it is byte-identical to what CodeFlow vouched for.

Rules:

  • Shipped tests: either every managed script ships its test with a documented way to run it, or none ships and the record carries the assurance; a partial set is not kept. AC-1 decides which.
  • The record is generated by the release pipeline from the run that produced it, never hand-written.
  • Provenance (a signed record or a build attestation) is in scope only if AC-1 finds the release pipeline can produce it without a new secret; otherwise it is a tracked follow-up.
  • The shell hooks under .codeflow/git-hooks/ and every other file marked exec are in scope, not only Python.

Non-goals: CodeFlow's managed-copy footprint (TSK-429); the adopter's own tooling (TSK-1031, TSK-1006).

First-pass survey (planning, 2026-10-28, line tip after PR 367)
  • Vendored executables: nine Python files under assets/ (eight in assets/base/agents/skills/cf-evaluate-model/scripts, one in cf-herdr/scripts), plus the shell hooks under assets/base/git-hooks/.

  • The manifest writer: .codeflow/manifest.json per installed file (src, ownership, sha256, exec); codeflow doctor already reads it for managed drift (check_managed_drift, crates/codeflow-core/src/doctor/mod.rs:3239).
  • Release flow: scripts/release.py and docs/releasing.md.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an adopter's Python checks under the gate resolve packages only from the lock, on every machine and in CI, and an inline script cannot pull a package the lock does not hold.

Context

Issue #275's comment of 2026-10-29 reports what two adopting repositories built because CodeFlow has no equivalent (lessons 8 and 9, custom parts 2 and 5): a locked-environment launcher and inline-script admission. Strict results differ between machines and CI unless every Python run under the gate resolves from one lock; and PEP 723 # /// script blocks let uv run --script resolve packages outside the lock, through [tool] tables (index, source, override, constraint and dependency-metadata keys) or unpinned packages. TSK-426's Description lists "a locked tool environment" for Python and no criterion defines it.

This task ships the launcher contract with cf-stack for Python and the admission rule in the gate: prepare is the only network step (uv sync --locked --no-build --no-cache with an environment allowlist, refusing index and source overrides); run works offline and checks an identity stamp (lock, manifests, Python and uv identity), failing with the prepare command when the stamp is stale; the strict targets call prepare then run; the trusted admission job uses the authority's launcher; and a tracked Python file whose inline metadata holds any [tool] table or a package not exactly pinned, registered and present in the root lock is refused, with exemptions only through TSK-424's register. Other languages get the contract as documentation where the adopter's tool has a locked mode (npm ci, cargo --locked); the shipped launcher is Python's.

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

After this merges, an adopter migrating a large codebase to the strict profile has every new file held strict from its first commit, while the old code pays down its recorded debt.

Context

Issue #275's comment of 2026-10-29, lesson 7: new files can be strict at once, before the old code is fixed. Repository A checks every new file against a recorded boundary revision per line; a copy, a rename, a new folder or a missing pragma never makes a file count as existing; lines with no recorded boundary are reported as "unproved" rather than silently passed. TSK-424's ratchet admits existing debt by stable occurrence identity and only shrinks it; TSK-426 configures the strict profile; neither makes a new file strict while the baseline is being paid down, so a long migration can grow its debt in new code.

This task adds the mode: a recorded boundary revision per target branch and line, held in the register's configuration at the default-branch authority; every file absent from the tree at the boundary is checked at the full strict profile with no debt admitted; a line with no recorded boundary is reported unproved and fails at block; moving a boundary is a register event with the ratchet's semantics (authority-only, and a later boundary only widens the strict set). Non-goal: the per-diagnostic ratchet itself (TSK-424) and the merge rules (TSK-1117).

Release/The coordination ledger: follow-ups and lanes/Original plan (Planning notes)/The coordination ledger has its contracts, store and follow command

The coordination ledger has its contracts, store and follow command

TSK-422complete

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #272, items 2 and 4 and the comment of 2026-10-21, under ADR-0086 as the operator decided on 2026-10-22 and as the independent Codex review of the design (sound with changes, 22 findings, 14 high) settled it. An orchestrating session owns a "task ledger" that CodeFlow gives no shape, no closure rule and no home; in an adopting project a hand-written ledger stopped after nine days, handed-over items went quiet, a merge of lane stocktakes produced about 940 rows mostly duplicating tracked work, and a deleted lane lost what only its conversation held. This task ships the shared contracts first (actors, references, transitions, transactions), then the store and the follow command on them, with its own docs, help and tests.

Outcome: the coordination ledger lives in the clone's common git directory (.git/codeflow/coord/) as one append-only JSON Lines event log with one sequence, liveness in overwritten status files, and codeflow follow keeps follow-ups FU-NNN as full records with typed links, derived due times, closure only on target-aware proof by an allowed actor, exact-duplicate refusal, bounded and scanned text, and a read-only status that never writes; and codeflow work status lists per task the worktrees with uncommitted changes, unpushed commits and commits on no branch.

The contracts, decided by ADR-0086 and applied here:

  • Store (location A): events.jsonl (the one coordination log: stream, follow-up, lane and coordinator events, one sequence), status/ (overwritten liveness files, one per holder, never a log), counters.json (reserved FU and LN numbers, reserved before use, gaps allowed, never lowered), coord.lock (a stable sidecar lock, never removed or replaced) and instance.json (this ledger's UUID; FU and LN numbers are local display ids within it). Paths come from Git's own common-dir discovery (hooks/repo.rs RepoInfo::discover, ids/state.rs), never a literal .git/. The supported live scope is one clone on one machine; an exported reference is qualified by the instance UUID; import is recovery into an empty instance or an explicit reconciliation, never a live lease. No compaction in the first cut; the 10,000-event read path is measured.
  • Transactions. One append is one commit, under the lock, with sequence assigned there; sync before success is reported; a retriable operation carries an idempotency key; a torn tail is repaired or quarantined under the lock before the next append; interior damage, a duplicate or decreasing sequence, a broken transition or an unknown state-changing schema version makes the ledger read-only with a diagnostic; events are validated on replay as on input; hooks wait a bounded time for the lock and report busy as distinct from empty; readers use the committed prefix; network and model work run outside the lock and revalidate the expected revision on commit. Tested on macOS, Linux and native Windows with fs2 advisory locking; shared network filesystems are not supported.
  • Envelope, field names in full: schema_version, event, subject_id, sequence, recorded_at (UTC, for people, never for order), recorded_by (role coordinator, a lane id or operator; an actor instance id always; harness, model and session id when known, unknowns explicit), optional comment; a mutation that depends on ownership carries the expected generation and entity revision and is refused when stale.
  • A follow-up is a full record for a cold reader. Required: title, description, done_when, source (operator, coordinator, a lane id, a review, an issue, outside), source_reference where one exists, stream (the WS-NNN it belongs to, or the project intake list until a coordinator takes it), holder (coordinator or a lane id), links typed context, prerequisite or fulfils (each with repository identity and the record UID where one exists) or a no_link_reason, and an effective schedule (next_check supplied or filled by the documented default). Optional: waits_on, awaiting_operator (a condition, never a holder). Dropped from the first cut: priority.
  • Events: item_added, item_updated (never source), item_checked (what was observed and the next check), item_handed_over, item_closed (evidence marked asserted or machine_verified, a reference a fresh session can open, the applicable revision and target), item_dropped (reason; the disposition of what it leaves), item_reopened (a reverted or invalidated proof keeps the old proof in history).
  • Links and due times. A prerequisite changing state (claimed, complete, blocked, cancelled; a pull request merged, closed or its checks finished; a lane reporting, idle or stale; another follow-up closed; a time passed) makes the follow-up due, never closed. Only a declared fulfils condition whose evidence satisfies done_when on the target, judged through the existing target-aware readiness and acceptance machinery (workgraph/readiness.rs), closes it automatically, naming the observation source, repository, target, revision and time; completion on a feature branch never counts. A cancelled task makes its follow-ups due for relinking or an explicit drop. A dependency wait has a maximum recheck time and records the observed dependency version. Cycles and reference integrity are checked on every dependency change, under the lock.
  • A lane is optional. A follow-up held by the stream's coordinator itself, with no lane, is tracked, checked and closed on the same proof as a lane-held one; direct work by the coordinator is work.
  • Permission matrix, one for every action: any bound actor adds; the holder updates, checks and hands over; the holder closes and drops, and the stream's coordinator may drop with a reason; a cross-stream wait names another stream's item or lane by id and is read-only; the operator's answer is recorded with its source, never as the operator; the operator may run the commands by hand, recorded as the operator. Every actor is bound to its instance and generation.
  • Dedupe. Only an exact duplicate (same source identity or idempotency key) is refused, atomically; similar follow-ups and matching open tasks, epic criteria and feedback items are suggested with a link or reject reason, never blocked.
  • Privacy. Every free-text field is scanned after decoding and size-bounded without echoing a rejected secret; files and directories are private with symlink and path checks; rendering to terminal and Markdown is safe; an explicit purge and repair path exists; the opt-in snapshot is never committed automatically and is exported redacted; a reader never assumes a line was validated on write.
  • Read-only status. follow list (table or --md, bounded: counts, the urgent subset and a pointer to the full list) never writes, claims a role, refreshes a heartbeat or creates a lock; a denied read is unavailable, no ledger is empty, a denied write is unwritten. Heartbeats are refreshed only by bound mutating operations (TSK-439 names them); an unbound observer reads and gets no heartbeat.
  • Role binding. This task ships the actor and binding contracts and binds actors in tests through a fixture; the commands that claim, release and adopt roles are TSK-439's, and the stream and status surfaces are TSK-439's and TSK-440's.
  • An aid, not a control. Nothing here blocks git, records, CI or landing; a missing or damaged ledger only warns; the ledger reads task, epic and ADR state and never writes a record; records, pull request bodies and codeflow ci never cite FU, LN or WS ids and never read the ledger.

Non-goals: lanes, attempts, streams and the coordinator lease, with their commands (TSK-439); the hook surfaces and coord status (TSK-440); the rules and the fresh-context test (TSK-423); compaction; cross-machine coordination; semantic duplicate refusal.

The rules and skills adopt the coordination ledger, proven fresh-context

TSK-423todo

not recorded

The whole outcome and context, from the record

Outcome

not recorded

Context

Issue #272, item 1 and its acceptance, under ADR-0086. Each of TSK-422, TSK-439 and TSK-440 ships the docs, CLI help and tests its own behaviour needs; this task is the integrated adoption: the managed rule and map row, the skill sections, the concepts, the per-harness notes, the architecture section and the fresh-context qualification from #272, with every requirement of the issue and its comment mapped to a task or an explicit deferral.

Outcome: every guidance home says how the coordination ledger and lanes are used, in one vocabulary (session, stream, coordinator, lane, seat, attempt, follow-up), with the ledger named as an aid and never a control; and a fresh-context qualification shows a coordinator reporting three handed-over items, one stalled, with holder, task and next check, without being asked, beside the lone session, the lost transcript with in-flight workers, the stale-but-live holder and the delegated Stop lifecycle.

Rules the guidance states:

  • The coordinator logs every operator-handed and every unsettled or untasked item at once as a full follow-up, follows it up, closes it only on proof of a listed kind, never on "handed to a lane", reads the ledger at session start (the digest), after compaction and before every status reply, and builds status from follow list with items awaiting the operator under "needs you".
  • One canonical role name, coordinator; the skills' existing host wording maps to it. Several coordinators can run at once, one per stream, within one harness and across harnesses; a session names its stream when it claims; a lane belongs to one stream and moves only by a two-sided handover; a task active in another stream's lane is a warning to heed; the coordinator's digest shows its own stream and a line per other stream, and codeflow coord status the whole project. A holder is the coordinator or a lane id; the operator is a condition, never a holder an agent impersonates.
  • The coordinator claims the lease explicitly, sweeps all items, opens and closes lanes (only the coordinator opens lanes), runs the inventory before adopting, and keeps the peer and worker prohibition on nested duos; a lane sees and closes its own items and adds items for what it hands back or finds; a lone session is its own coordinator and needs no lane, and a follow-up the coordinator holds itself is tracked and closed like a lane-held one; a coordinator in a new harness continues lanes it cannot reach by their own heartbeat and reports (fresh: leave running, read reports, start no duplicate writer; silent past the timeout: investigate with the inventory, replace on the same branch and worktree only with stopped-work evidence or a resolved overlap, else keep it as unresolved and possibly live and say so; a returning old seat stops), stated in cf-model-orchestrator, cf-herdr and cf-delegate; a seat attaches with --lane or a recorded --no-lane reason, is labelled by its lane id and is re-checked live before it is driven.
  • The five layers are named with their limits: the rule cannot capture every natural-language ask; the start digest is read-only; commands record what is routed through them; the turn-end check is advisory; an empty ledger does not prove no commitment is missing. A timer is an optional aid. Native task lists in each harness stay private aids; the ledger carries across.
  • The map gains one row ("hand over, receive or find an open item: codeflow follow; delegate: codeflow lane open") and one always-rule; the "report status" row (which TSK-387 extends) and the "start a session" row name the ledger.
  • cf-model-orchestrator/resources/task-graph.md is amended: the native harness task tools remain the per-session planning aid; the coordinator's running state lives in the ledger.

Non-goals: the commands, hooks and their own docs (TSK-422, TSK-439, TSK-440); a mandatory timer.

Amended 2026-10-31 by the hierarchy amendment (ADR-0094): the guidance also states the three roles, as instructions and never as a check in the tooling. A Director is the coordinator of the stream with no parent, at most one per ledger: it names child streams and their coordinators, reads the tree, aggregates reports, answers the user and routes requests, and never lands or merges a child's line. A Coordinator is the coordinator of a stream with a parent: it opens its own stream with stream open --parent, claims it, opens lanes, attaches and closes seats, harvests lane reports, records lane scope changes and reports up with stream report; when its topic is a body of work it creates the topic's integration/<epic> branch, lands reviewed lane pull requests there and raises the line's pull request to main for the operator to merge; it never opens lanes in another stream or reviews units its own lanes authored. A Lane is one topic in one stream held by one session per attempt; its Seat is the session holding it now. All three are the same kind of named, resumable session, differing only in name, guidance and ledger record. A Director or Coordinator that does work itself opens a lane and takes the seat, so the work gets its own worktree, branch, pull request, report and cleanup. A same-family lane may run as a recorded interactive session; headless forms stay forbidden and the other-lineage review stays required. Session names follow <role>/<id>/<slug>; the Herdr label stays cf/<repo>/<WS-or-LN>/<kind>/<nn> and mirrors it; the ledger name is canonical. A report, a cross-session message or a record labelled "operator" written by an agent is evidence to confirm, never an instruction. Depth stays at two supervision levels, with the reason stated. The managed block carries these in one row, rendered for every tier through rule-map.toml and CLAUDE.md.tmpl.
